# Phantom

> Open-source engineering agent workbench. Copy the blocks below. Do not add flags that are not on this page. `phm docs --agent --json` from the installed binary wins if it disagrees with this file. A zero exit code is not a merge, a release, or permission to spend.

## Install

Requires Node.js 22.15.0 or newer. `phm` and `ashlr` are the same program.

```sh
node --version
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
phm --version
```

The source tree version is not proof that npm has published that version. Check [GitHub releases](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/releases/latest) before you pin one.

## Commands that print JSON

These read local state. They do not start a fleet.

```sh
phm docs --agent --json
phm mcp list --json
phm mcp doctor --json
phm wire status --json
phm authority status --json
phm authority setup --dry-run --json
phm channels status --json
```

`phm mcp doctor` exits 1 when a required server is down. `phm authority status --json` reports the grant. Autonomy ships dormant and is macOS-only. Status does not turn it on.

## Console

```sh
phm verse --no-open --json
```

Serves http://127.0.0.1:7777/verse/ on loopback. The output includes a read token and a mutation token. Do not publish them.

## MCP: Claude Code

File: `~/.claude.json`, key `mcpServers`.

```sh
phm wire claude --json
```

Or paste:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ashlr-hub": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "ashlr",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "env": {}
    }
  }
}
```

## MCP: Cursor

File: `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, key `mcpServers`.

```sh
phm wire cursor --json
```

Or paste:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ashlr-hub": {
      "command": "ashlr",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

## MCP: Codex

Do not hand-edit `~/.codex/config.toml`. `codex` must be on `PATH`.

```sh
phm wire codex --json
```

That runs `codex mcp add ashlr-hub -- ashlr mcp` after a backup.

## Check the wiring

Restart the editor, then:

```sh
phm wire status --json
phm mcp doctor --json
```

Registration does not prove the server started.

## Read-only fleet MCP

Separate from `ashlr-hub`. This server does not launch work or merge.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "phantom-fleet": {
      "command": "phm",
      "args": ["mcp", "fleet"]
    }
  }
}
```

Call `tools/list`, then `fleet_status` with `{}`. See [FLEET-MCP-ONRAMP.md](FLEET-MCP-ONRAMP.md).

## Optional cloud handoff

```sh
phm cloud launch "<task>" --repo owner/name
phm devin connect
phm devin launch "<task>"
```

These do not merge by themselves. See [CLOUD.md](CLOUD.md) and [DEVIN.md](DEVIN.md).

Route hysteresis: see docs/ROUTE-HYSTERESIS.md. Dispatcher pool proposals keep a
60-minute residency; only auth failure or zero quota permits early movement.
Launched jobs never move. At most two moves per six hours; blocked moves log
ROUTE_HOLD. Read accepted trailing-hour moves with phm route explain --json.

- [Connector profiles](CONNECTORS.md): `phm connectors add|list|remove|show|import --json`; metadata and Phantom Secrets references only.

Multi-Mac node pool: see docs/AGENT-NETWORK.md and docs/NODES.md. Configure explicit team SSH aliases with phm node pool --role primary|backup --node <id> --owner <scope> --primary <alias> --backup <alias> --json. First join: npm install -g @ashlr/phantom && phm node join --owner mason --primary primary-mac --backup backup-mac --json. Node ID defaults to sanitized hostname; repeat phm node join --json rechecks saved config without changing roles. RAM slots reserve max(4 GiB, 30%) then budget 4 GiB/job: 8 GiB gives one, 16 GiB gives two. Hold on available RAM below 30%, swap use, disk below 20 GB or unknown telemetry; pressure stops running work. Worker launches one bounded batch up to the RAM ceiling concurrently under one session, waits for all started slots and leaves; no permanent supervisor. Disk telemetry covers the home filesystem; runner DISKGUARD must cover checkout/artifact volumes. Nominal three-second pressure checks can be delayed by bounded synchronous probes and SSH. DISKGUARD remains in force. Share credential-free Phantom connector metadata and reviewed checkout MCP/skill files, never client auth; no automatic config synchronization. Independent per-node lanes; sharded inference has no measured win. iPad and phone are mobile control only. See examples/node-pool/README.md. Use phm node watch [--once] --json, phm node worker --runner /absolute/host-owned-runner --json and phm node list|status --json. phm node rpc --json is the SSH stdin endpoint. The backup witnesses every admission and promotes after fifteen minutes; returning primary is demoted. No copied auth, new paid service, message sends or worker publication.

Agent network channels: see AGENT-NETWORK-CHANNELS.md for channel metadata, default-deny policy, and offline CLI examples.

<!-- page: AGENT-BUS -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/AGENT-BUS.md

# Agent Bus

Phantom's durable agent bus is a bounded, append-only store under `~/.ashlr-runs`
that any agent can read by cursor; addresses are routing labels, not identities.
It gives every agent a single shared inbox to read from and write to.

## Read

GET `/api/verse/agent-bus?after=<cursor>&limit=<1..100>` (default limit 50)
returns a cursor page: `{ v: 1, status, messages: [{ cursor, receivedAt,
envelope }], nextCursor }`.  GET `/api/verse/agent-bus/status` returns
`{ v: 1, source, retainedCount, retainedBytes, maxMessages, maxBytes,
liveCount, expiredCount }`.  Read endpoints need a current read session and
return 401 if absent or expired; `source` is `missing` when the store has
not yet been created, and `unavailable` when the store is unhealthy (503).

## Write

POST `/api/verse/agent-bus` sends one envelope; the caller needs
`--allow-dispatch` and must pass the mutation gate.  Reply codes: 201
posted, 200 duplicate, 400 invalid, 409 conflict, 507 full, 503
unavailable, 404 when dispatch is off.  Responses carry `{ v: 1,
status, id?, cursor? }`.

## Envelope fields

The `BusEnvelope` carries exactly six wire fields — each is a flat value:
- `id` sender-assigned message identity; deduplication is a transport responsibility.
- `from` sender routing label (printable ASCII, 1-128 chars).
- `to` recipient routing label (printable ASCII, 1-128 chars).
- `priority` queue priority: P0 (highest), P1, P2, or P3.
- `ttl` positive remaining lifetime in milliseconds (safe integer).
- `body` opaque strict JSON data; no event-kind or payload interpretation.

Caps: 1024 messages, 1 MiB total, 100 per read page.

## Conventions

Mason's channel interjections appear as id `mason-<channel>-<dedupeKey16>`,
from `mason`, to `leaders`, priority P0, with a 7-day TTL and body
`{ kind: 'interjection', channel, text, receivedAt, dedupeKey }`.  Reply
to Mason by setting `to` to `mason`.  Keep the `id` stable so retries
are deduplicated by the store.

## Examples

Read the latest page (cursor 0, limit 10):
`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer FAKE-TOKEN" http://localhost:8787/api/verse/agent-bus?after=0&limit=10`

Publish an envelope (replace `FAKE-TOKEN` and values with real ones):
`curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer FAKE-TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" http://localhost:8787/api/verse/agent-bus -d '{"id":"example-0001","from":"agent","to":"leaders","priority":"P1","ttl":86400000,"body":{"note":"hello"}}'`

## Desktop app

The Bus pane in the desktop app includes a Durable bus tab that reads and
writes the same `~/.ashlr-runs` store the API endpoints target.

## v2

v2 is the contract every provider implements against: Grok Bot agents, OpenAI
Dot, codex-cmp, codex-personal, Devin, Cursor cloud agents, Claude, GLM (z.ai),
Stacksync's agent and local oMLX. It adds meaning to `body`; the six envelope
fields, endpoints, auth and caps above are unchanged, and v1 bodies stay valid.
A body is v2 only when it carries one of the `kind` values below. Schema
version: `agent-bus.v2`. Source of truth: `src/core/agents/bus-v2-schema.ts`.
Supersedes the stale proposals in PR #3057 (RQ-BUS-NEUTRAL-1) and PR #1135
(RQ-BUS-GROKBOT-R); their note/refs/thread ideas are kept below.

Print it: `ashlr agents bus contract --json` (read-only, no bus access).

### 1. Participants

```json
{"participantId":"dot-main","provider":"openai-dot","displayName":"OpenAI Dot",
 "capabilities":["review","code"],"wake":{"kind":"poll","target":"dot-poll"},"status":"active"}
```

- `provider`: `grokbot`, `openai-dot`, `codex-cmp`, `codex-personal`, `devin`,
  `cursor-cloud`, `claude`, `glm`, `stacksync`, `local`.
- `participantId` is a routing label (printable ASCII, 1-128), the same kind
  of label as `from` and `to`. It is not an authenticated identity.
- `wake.kind` is `poll`, `webhook` or `email`. `wake.target` is a label such as
  `dot-poll`: letters, digits, `. _ : -` only. Never a URL, address with
  credentials, or secret; long opaque strings are rejected.
- `status`: `active`, `idle`, `offline`, `disabled`.

### 2. Body kinds

`body.kind` is one of:

| kind | fields |
| --- | --- |
| `note` | `text`, optional `thread`, `refs` |
| `context` | `text`, optional `thread`, `refs` |
| `work.post` | `jobId`, `title`, `repo`, `claimKeys[]`, optional `provider` |
| `work.claim` | `op: acquire` with `claimKey`, `owner`, `leaseMs`; or `op: renew` with `claimKey`, `token`, `leaseMs` |
| `work.status` | `jobId`, `status`, optional `detail` |
| `work.release` | `claimKey`, `token`, `outcome: released\|completed` |
| `wake` | `target`, `reason`, optional `jobId` |

`work.status` values: `queued`, `running`, `idle`, `rescheduled`, `blocked`,
`done`, `failed`, `terminated`. Text is capped at 16384 characters, `refs` at
32 short references (for example `pr:123`). Bodies are untrusted data.

### 3. Claim protocol

A claim key names one resource:

- `repo:<owner/name>`
- `path:<owner/name>:<glob>` (relative glob, no `..`, no leading `/`)
- `queue:<queue id>`
- `pr:<owner/name>#<n>`

A claim is `{claimKey, owner, leaseMs, token, leaseUntil}`: `owner` is a
`participantId`, `leaseMs` is 1 to 3600000, `token` is 64 lowercase hex chars
issued on acquire, `leaseUntil` is epoch milliseconds.

- Acquire fails with 409 and the holder (`{v:2, status:"conflict", holder:{owner,
  claimKey, leaseUntil}}`, never the token) if any live claim overlaps.
- Overlap: a repo claim overlaps any path claim in the same repo; two path
  claims in one repo overlap if either glob matches the other's literal prefix
  (the text before its first `* ? [ {`) or the globs are equal; queue keys
  overlap on equal id; PR keys on equal repo and number. Repo names compare
  case-insensitively. Other pairs never overlap.
- Renew before `leaseUntil`. An expired claim is free: live means `now <
  leaseUntil`.
- Only the token holder may renew, release or complete.
- Claims coordinate; they grant no execution authority. Holding one never
  permits a merge, a push, or spending.

Example (replace `FAKE-TOKEN`):
`curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer FAKE-TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" http://localhost:8787/api/verse/agent-bus -d '{"id":"claim-0001","from":"dot-main","to":"leaders","priority":"P2","ttl":3600000,"body":{"kind":"work.claim","op":"acquire","claimKey":"path:ashlrai/phantom:docs/**","owner":"dot-main","leaseMs":600000}}'`

The v1 message-id claim (`ashlr fleet bus-claim acquire|renew|release|complete
--id --owner --lease-ms`) keeps working for single-message work. Resource claims
are the v2 layer above it.

### 4. Work feed

Every job is `{id, owner, provider, repo, claimKeys[], status, updatedAt}`
and every participant can read the feed (`{v:2, jobs:[...]}`). Jobs derive
from `work.post` and `work.status` messages.

### 5. Ownership table

Outside implementers (Dot included) call only the HTTP contract above.

| Part | Phantom file |
| --- | --- |
| Schemas, claim key parsing, overlap rules | `src/core/agents/bus-v2-schema.ts` |
| Bus store, caps, cursor reads, HTTP endpoints | the v1 store behind `/api/verse/agent-bus` |
| Message-id claims | `src/core/fleet/bus-work-claims.ts` |
| Adapters and fleet bus verbs | `src/cli/fleet-bus-*.ts`, `src/core/fleet/bus-adapters/` |
| Contract printer | `src/cli/agents-bus-contract.ts` |
| Webhook relay | not built; an internet-facing relay must verify signed requests and gets its own security review |

This section is contract only. The store, claim table and work feed endpoints
are not yet implemented against it.

# Agent checkpoints

An agent can persist an explicit handoff as a UTF-8 JSON file in a location the
next session can access. Update it as the work changes and before compaction,
restart, or handoff. The author is responsible for recording all relevant
constraints, decisions and verification; the format cannot recover information
that was never written. Store references to evidence, not credentials or tokens.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "goal": "Complete the requested change under the agreed constraints.",
  "done": ["Implemented the parser; decision and rationale are in docs/design.md."],
  "next": ["Run the affected tests and investigate failures."],
  "evidence": ["docs/design.md", "test/example.test.ts", "Test command and result: npm test — passed."],
  "openQuestions": ["Does the caller require a migration?"]
}
```

All fields are required; the four lists may be empty. Entries and the goal must
be nonempty strings. Version 1 rejects unknown fields, malformed documents and
secret-shaped text rather than discarding or redacting content. Use binding names
for secrets. Keep the file private when its contents are private.

```sh
phm checkpoint resume ./checkpoint.json --json
```

The read-only command validates and prints the entire checkpoint as JSON, with no
section truncation. It exits 2 on invalid or unreadable input and does not echo
rejected content. A fresh agent should read the referenced evidence and inspect
current workspace state; pointers may have become stale. This is separate from
[Verse's bounded event-log handoff](VERSE-CONTEXT.md#4-handoff--continue-in-a-fresh-chat)
and the MCP gateway's access-control sessions. It grants no authority and does
not automatically capture state or initiate a session.

The public core contract is `parseAgentCheckpoint(raw: string): AgentCheckpoint`
and `readAgentCheckpoint(path: string): Promise<AgentCheckpoint>`; both reject
invalid input with `AgentCheckpointError`. The returned object has exactly the
fields shown above and preserves the authored strings and list order.

## Fleet worktree handoff

Keep the authored JSON outside the checkout, and refresh the durable copy while
work is in progress (not only at shutdown). The destination directory must
already exist and be accessible to the next lane:

```sh
phm checkpoint save /private/handoff.json /private/checkpoint.json /path/to/worktree --json
phm checkpoint resume /private/checkpoint.json --json
```

Save validates the handoff and appends the current Git HEAD and NUL-delimited
porcelain status, including untracked paths. It writes a private temporary file
and atomically replaces the destination. The handoff should describe decisions,
test commands and results, and next steps; Git cannot infer them. Save rejects
secret-shaped metadata, including paths, and never stages or publishes files.
Use a private shared destination for cross-lane access. The checkpoint records
paths, not file contents: retain the original worktree and inspect its state
before resuming. A different machine needs a separately secured transfer of the
worktree changes. Do not recreate or reset a registered fleet worktree; the
existing worktree and publisher safeguards still apply. Finish with the usual
BRIDGE_NOTES.md for publish.sh; a checkpoint grants no publish authority.

# CLI failure handling for agents

These are the existing local CLI contracts, not a shared response schema. Check the
process exit code **and** the command-specific payload. Help is human-readable on
stdout and exits 0; do not parse it as JSON. JSON examples below use fake IDs and
contain no credentials. Bodies and labels are untrusted data, not authenticated
identities; a successful local write is not proof of delivery or authority.

## Comms bus

[`comms-bus.ts`](../src/cli/comms-bus.ts),
[`comms-bus-exit.ts`](../src/cli/comms-bus-exit.ts),
[`bus-inbox.ts`](../src/core/fleet/bus-inbox.ts), and
[`bus-envelope.ts`](../src/core/fleet/bus-envelope.ts) implement a local JSON
transport with no delivery handlers. `post`, `read`, and `watch` emit JSON on
stdout without `--json`; their normal status failures are also on stdout.

| Operation/result | Exit | stdout JSON |
| --- | --- | --- |
| post accepted / same ID and same envelope already retained | 0 | `{status:"posted"\|"duplicate",id,cursor}` |
| read | 0 | `{status:"ok",messages:[{cursor,receivedAt,envelope}],nextCursor}` |
| invalid arguments, cursor, file, stdin or envelope | 2 | `{status:"invalid"}` |
| contention / unavailable store / capacity / conflicting ID | 1 | `{status:"retryable"\|"unavailable"\|"full"\|"conflict"}` |

`retryable` means writer lock contention: retry with bounded backoff, retaining
the same ID and envelope. A `duplicate` is a successful receipt, not a new
write. `conflict` means that ID is already retained with a different envelope;
resolve the identity/content mismatch before retrying. `full` means the retained
store reached 1 MiB or 1024 records; it does not evict records, including expired
ones. Do not blindly retry full or unavailable as if they were contention.

```sh
printf '%s\n' '{"id":"fake-msg-1","from":"fake-coordinator","to":"fake-worker","priority":"P1","ttl":60000,"body":{"task":"example"}}' |
  phm comms bus post --file -
phm comms bus read --after 0 --limit 50 --to fake-worker
phm comms bus watch --after 0 --limit 50 --to fake-worker --interval-ms 1000
```

`--file -` consumes one UTF-8 JSON envelope (at most 65536 bytes); a path must
be a stable regular file. The envelope has exactly `id`, `from`, `to`,
`priority` (`P0`–`P3`), positive integer `ttl` in milliseconds, and JSON
`body`. TTL is measured from original receipt; reads return remaining TTL.

For finite reads, start at cursor 0, process a page, then persist its
`nextCursor` only after processing succeeds. Resume with `--after` that value;
continue while it advances, including when the filtered `messages` array is
empty. An unchanged cursor means caught up for that snapshot, not that no future
messages will arrive. The limit (1–100, default 50) counts live records scanned
before filters; expired records advance the cursor without counting. Filters
are exact, case-sensitive, and combined. A cursor beyond the retained end is
invalid; do not silently reset it and replay work.

Watch emits one JSON object per line for each successful poll, even empty ones,
and resumes from that page's `nextCursor`. It silently retries `retryable` at
the same cursor after the interval (100–60000 ms, default 1000). Other poll
failures emit their status and exit 1; invalid options exit 2. SIGINT/SIGTERM
stop it with exit 0. Persist the last successfully processed page cursor outside
the process if restart recovery is needed.

## Mason's comms inbox

[`comms-inbox.ts`](../src/cli/comms-inbox.ts) uses the local receiver and
[`mason-inbox.ts`](../src/core/fleet/mason-inbox.ts) reader. Output is JSON on
stdout with or without `--json`:

| Result | Exit | stdout JSON |
| --- | --- | --- |
| post accepted or duplicate | 0 | `{ok:true,ack:{channel:"cli",status:"accepted"\|"duplicate",dedupeKey}}` |
| post rejected or input unavailable | 1 | `{ok:false,reason:...}` |
| read healthy or missing | 0 | `{sourceState:"healthy"\|"missing",entries:[...]}` |
| read degraded | 1 | `{sourceState:"degraded",entries:[]}` |
| invalid options | 2 | `{status:"invalid"}` |

Missing is not evidence of a healthy empty inbox. Read selects the newest
matching entries, returns them oldest first, and defaults to 50 (limit 1–200).
`source` is metadata, not identity. Duplicate receipts last only for the
receiver process lifetime. Post reads owner-controlled stable regular UTF-8
text or stdin, not a bus envelope; input is bounded to 6000 characters and
subject to receiver validation. `stdin-unavailable` and `file-unavailable` are
input failures, distinct from malformed command arguments.

```sh
printf '%s\n' 'Fake handoff: inspect task fake-42.' | phm comms inbox post --file - --json
phm comms inbox read --source cli --limit 20 --json
```

## Graph

[`graph.ts`](../src/cli/graph.ts) and [`loader.ts`](../src/core/graph/loader.ts)
provide the read-only GRAPH-1 view. Use `--json`: success and failures are
single JSON objects on stdout, with `schemaVersion:1`, `command`, and `status`.
`status` reports `counts`; `neighbors` reports `nodeId`, `direction`, `depth`,
`nodes`, `edges`, and `truncated`. Inspect `complete`, `sources`, and `issues`
when present; a ready but incomplete graph is not complete evidence.

| Result | Exit | JSON status / error code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| success | 0 | `ready` |
| unavailable, loader error, or missing node | 1 | `unavailable` / `GRAPH_UNAVAILABLE`, `error` / `GRAPH_LOAD_FAILED`, or `not_found` / `GRAPH_NODE_NOT_FOUND` |
| usage error | 2 | `error` / `GRAPH_USAGE` |

Without `--json`, graph errors go to stderr; status success is human text and
neighbors success is pretty JSON. Unavailable counts are unknown, not zero.
Neighbors defaults to both directions and depth 1, accepts depth 1–4, and caps
results at 500 nodes; check `truncated`. Use `--` before an option-like ID.

```sh
phm graph status --json
phm graph neighbors fake-node-1 --direction out --depth 2 --json
```

## Resource ledger and fleet runs

[`resource-ledger.ts`](../src/cli/resource-ledger.ts) reads
[`runs-resource-ledger.ts`](../src/core/fleet/runs-resource-ledger.ts);
[`fleet-runs-read.ts`](../src/cli/fleet-runs-read.ts) reads
[`runs-dir-state.ts`](../src/core/fleet/runs-dir-state.ts). One-shot `--json`
success is a ledger or runs projection on stdout (`v:1`); no shared status
wrapper is added. Exit 0 can still contain missing or degraded sources. Inspect
ledger `sources`, `asOf`, and nullable values; inspect runs `sourceState`,
`sources`, `runsDirPresent`, and nullable values. Missing data or `null` means
unknown, not zero; check observation time before using it as current evidence.
`--lane` on runs filters attributed rows but source health and other global
fields remain global; `laneFilter` describes omissions.

For either one-shot command, invalid options exit 2 with text on stderr;
a thrown reader error exits 1 with text on stderr and no JSON, even with
`--json`. Both support `--watch --json`: one JSON object per line, immediate
sample then sequential polls (default 5000 ms, interval 1000–60000). A read
exception emits `{v:1,error:"resource_ledger_read_failed"}` for ledger or
`{error:"fleet runs unavailable"}` for runs, then retries. Normal signal stop
exits 0, so inspect each watch record, not only the eventual process code.

```sh
phm resources ledger --json
phm resources ledger --watch --interval-ms 5000 --json
phm fleet runs --json --lane fake-lane
phm fleet runs --watch --interval-ms 5000 --json
```

## Keep streams and exit codes separate

Do not merge stderr into a JSON pipeline (`2>&1`), and do not assume a pipeline's
last command reports `phm`'s status. For a one-shot command, capture stdout and
stderr separately and branch before parsing (use private files appropriate to
your environment):

```sh
if phm fleet runs --json >fake-runs.json 2>fake-runs.err; then
  jq '{sourceState, sources, runsDirPresent}' fake-runs.json
else
  code=$?
  printf 'fleet runs failed (exit %s); see fake-runs.err\n' "$code" >&2
fi
```

For bus, inbox, and graph `--json`, a nonzero exit can still carry a structured
failure on stdout; inspect that command's JSON as well. For watches, parse each
line independently, handle error records, and retain stderr separately.

# Agent harness evolution

Architecture proposal, reviewed against the working candidate and official OpenAI
documentation on **2026-09-30**. The proposals below are not activated connectors,
new provider entitlements, or a claim of unlimited running capacity.

Build one workbench with two jobs: **Work with me** for an interactive chat and
**Work for me** for a continuing fleet responsibility. Keep account selection,
tool evidence, capacity explanations, and recovery in those workflows. Reuse the
existing harness rather than replacing every provider with one invented adapter.

## What to borrow from OpenAI

OpenAI's managed Agents API owns sessions, orchestration, compaction, and recovery;
applications provide tools and an execution environment. This is a different
integration from native Codex sessions or a ChatGPT subscription. Borrow its
session and event concepts without treating an API key as a subscription seat.
[Agents API overview](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/overview)

| Verified concept | Proposed Ashlr use | Existing seam |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Specialists have separate contexts; a manager coordinates their tasks | Delegate a bounded task with an explicit result owner, files, and return contract | [delegation-scope.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/run/delegation-scope.ts), [handoff.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/handoff.ts) |
| Handoff transfers reply ownership; agent-as-tool retains the manager's answer | Show whether a child owns the conversation or returns evidence to its parent | [session-handoff.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/session-handoff.ts), [session-engine.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/session-engine.ts) |
| Live events and saved items serve different purposes | Resume by durable cursor; reconcile saved state after disconnect; never equate child completion or stream EOF with root success | [session-store.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/session-store.ts), [verse-stream.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/verse-stream.ts), [transient-events.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/transient-events.ts) |
| Tool discovery can defer full schemas until needed | Search trusted, scoped tool metadata first; attach schemas only for the selected task | [mcp-registry.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/mcp-registry.ts), [mcp-scope.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/mcp-scope.ts), [verse-mcp-grants.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/verse-mcp-grants.ts) |

These are mappings, not claims that the existing modules implement the provider
protocol. Sources: [multi-agent](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/multi-agent),
[orchestration](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/orchestration),
[events and items](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/sessions/events),
and [tool search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search).

Tool search is provider/model dependent. Agents API deferred functions require
both enabled tool search and a deferred declaration; MCP/plugin discovery has
different rules from Responses MCP. Discovery never grants invocation rights.
For the Hub, configured MCP inventory, successful discovery, a granted tool, and
a reported call must remain distinct states. Existing
[turn-resource-evidence.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/web-ui/routes/verse/chat/turn-resource-evidence.ts)
already distinguishes reported, pending, failed, unknown, and partial evidence
without exposing tool payloads or arbitrary private names.

Programmatic tool calling can run loops, parallel reads, and result filtering in
an isolated JavaScript runtime. It does not provide Node, ambient network,
filesystem, or subprocess access. Discover deferred tools before entering the
program; tool search is a top-level operation. Prefer direct calls when each
result requires judgment or a write needs separate authorization. The proposed
Hub equivalent batches independent authorized reads, while every call still
passes its existing scope, identity, cancellation, and replay checks.
[Programmatic tool calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling)

## Capacity controls and remaining seams

The candidate removes the six-seat fanout ceiling, optional agent-retention
ceiling, arbitrary daemon capacity UI ceilings, the hidden batch concurrency
clamp of eight, the separate swarm BUILD preference ceiling of eight, and the
daily USD preference ceiling of 1,000. It preserves
existing defaults and final admission. This inventory records behavior; it
does not change live settings or authorize additional spend.

| Seam | Current behavior | Classification / next treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Budget controls | Items, batch parallelism, and continuous/local/cloud/total concurrency accept positive safe integers; daily USD accepts finite 0 through the exact-safe numeric ceiling, including fractions | Shared existing UI/API bounds in [caps-spec.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/web-ui/routes/verse/autonomy/caps-spec.ts); numeric representability is not a fleet quota. Explicit USD zero remains Stop; signed spend authority is unchanged |
| Batch executor | Explicit safe-integer parallelism is retained; default remains 2; worker allocation uses actual selected inventory | Former hidden clamp removed in [loop.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/daemon/loop.ts); queue, account, resources, and journal admission still apply |
| Swarm BUILD concurrency | `--parallel` accepts a positive safe integer; default remains 3, with no preference ceiling of eight | [runner.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/swarm/runner.ts) launches only actual pending tasks, reserves tokens/steps per batch, and retains provider/authority admission; malformed CLI input is refused and invalid programmatic preferences retain default 3. Planner/task-count and budget semantics are unchanged |
| Durable per-tick journal | At most 64 selected items; a larger item preference does not journal the whole backlog at once | Existing durability contract retained. API reports `journalItemCapacity`; UI explains subsequent ticks and older-server unknown capacity. Expanding or sharding this journal needs separate review |
| Item execution | `maxSteps: 100`; proven-free token ceiling defaults to 50,000 or explicit `daemon.perItemMaxTokens` | Steps remain hardcoded; token limit is a configurable default, not a universal model context guarantee |
| Continuous concurrency | Defaults local 2, cloud 6, total 8; max concurrent defaults to configured total or 8; larger safe-integer preferences survive UI/API/runtime consistently | Requested capacity still passes actual admission; invalid/fractional/nonfinite/unsafe stored values use existing defaults rather than unlimited capacity |
| Execution identity V1 | Shadow registry has 32-identity / 32-concurrency bounds and schema capacity classes also cap concurrency at 32 | Separate bounded shadow contract in [execution-identity.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/fabric/execution-identity.ts) and [config schema](../schema/config.schema.json); do not call it an unlimited account dispatcher |
| Ordinary best-of-N | Candidate cash accounting still uses subscription tier classification | Remaining actual-engine/model accounting seam in [best-of-n.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/run/best-of-n.ts); custom API engines must not become zero-dollar merely by tier |
| CLI context and delegation | Native CLI windows/options vary; context fit is a bounded byte-derived estimate; delegation metadata has projection bounds | Respect actual adapter capabilities; distinguish unknown context from zero, and diagnostic bounds from execution authority |
| Workspace isolation | Finite port range 41000–60000, allocation blocks up to 50; zero ports reserve none | Physical allocation limit; current create/restore guard is process-local, not cross-process reservation proof |
| Actual resource admission | Provider quotas, native seats, operator reserves, model memory, leases, signed scope, and cash/ACU accounting | Real constraints remain; report their observed source and freshness rather than guessing unlimited capacity |

Defaults are useful starting points; arbitrary hidden ceilings are not. Bounded
parsing, public projections, queues, and caches remain necessary to handle
malformed input and backpressure. They should report partial coverage rather
than pretend an unexamined account or omitted tool does not exist.

## Operator goal and Leader preferences

Version 3.19 source replaces Leader's fixed business quotas with two compact
advanced sections in the existing capacity settings. The primary workspaces stay
**Work with me** and **Work for me**. Guiding a session and supervising delegated
work share evidence and navigation; selecting a workspace does not start a fleet.

| Configuration | Preference | Default when absent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `foundry.goalPreferences.maxOpenGoals` | Open goals | 4 |
| `foundry.goalPreferences.maxNewGoalsPerDay` | New goals in the last 24 hours | 3 |
| `foundry.goalPreferences.maxGoalProposalsPerMemo` | Goal proposals per memo | 3 |
| `foundry.goalPreferences.maxGoalsPerConductorCycle` | Goals considered per ordinary conductor cycle | 3 |
| `foundry.leaderPreferences.maxFullRunsPerDay` | Full Leader runs per day | No preference limit |
| `foundry.leaderPreferences.maxTotalRunsPerDay` | All Leader runs per day | No preference limit |
| `foundry.leaderPreferences.maxGrokLanes` | Requested Grok lanes | No preference limit |

Every preference accepts a positive safe integer or explicit `null`, displayed
as **No preference limit**. Missing fields preserve existing defaults. Partial
updates merge only edited fields into freshly read configuration. Invalid or
unreadable policy is unavailable, never unlimited. Finite goal and daily-run
preferences require complete observed counts; an explicit unlimited preference
skips only that comparison and preserves unknown counts as unknown.

The separate **Prefer finishing current work before expanding** control retains
goal-focus scheduling. Choosing an unlimited goal preference does not silently
disable it. Grok directive `null` still means its existing two-lane default; the
operator's unlimited preference is a different setting. Requested work still
uses actual admitted seats, provider capacity, signed classes, cancellation,
claim/replay checks and backoff. The signed one-shot conductor remains one goal,
one milestone and zero retries. No setting allocates workers from an unbounded
number or changes a live account, grant or service merely by displaying it.

## Evidence without a new dispatch gate

Treat benchmarks and evals as inspectable evidence for the engineer. Regression
checks verify the product's behavior; an optimization score does not become an
extra requirement for an otherwise admitted agent to work.

The existing chat transcript exposes reported tools and context evidence. The
Changes surface uses actual Git or turn checkpoint bases for base/head review.
Local evaluation records checker exits, configuration, task identity, token
coverage and optional private wire traces. The installed CLI exposes this
harness through `ashlr benchmark`. Help and saved-receipt comparison are offline:

```sh
ashlr benchmark --help
ashlr benchmark --compare-reports BASELINE.json CANDIDATE.json
```

These commands launch no model. Matching tasks, model/runtime configuration, recorded cache
protocol and token coverage are required to compare receipts. Missing usage
stays unknown; a successful offline comparison is not an online provider test,
invoice, authenticated receipt or universal token-savings claim. Online tests
must record the actual engine/model/account, outcome and observed capacity.
Historical baselines remain dated evidence until rerun on the current runtime.

To explicitly run one local-agent trial against the configured runtime:

```sh
ashlr benchmark run --task multi-file-rename --trials 1 --concurrency 1 --out report.json
```

The command performs model work and writes a private report and trace artifacts.
Check its exit status and the recorded checker result; a runtime error or failed
task is not a successful benchmark. Default runs use three trials and concurrency
two. Select settings deliberately: concurrency and cache conditions affect timing
and comparisons. Benchmark results never become an extra fleet dispatch gate.

The runner captures each trusted checker source before launching the agent and
executes it as Node ESM source with the trial root as its working directory.
Replacing or symlinking the forensic `check.mjs` file cannot change that checker.
Current checkers resolve fixture paths from the working directory; checker-file
relative imports and `import.meta.url` are unsupported. This is not an OS
sandbox: the Node executable, inherited environment (including `NODE_OPTIONS`),
agent-controlled fixture imports and same-user processes remain part of host
execution. A checker exit alone is not authenticated adversarial evaluation.


Existing OTLP export emits run metadata rather than prompts, tool arguments or
file contents. Private local wire traces are a separate, content-bearing artifact.
Neither feature means a Sentry account or external collector is connected.
Use existing read-only Changes, Sources, Usage and fleet decision surfaces before
adding a second tracing or review pipeline.

## Next source slice: richer admission explanations

The current slice reuses existing cap contracts and configuration; it adds no
new policy subsystem. It validates operator items/parallel/concurrency
preferences consistently and reports the actual 64-item journal capacity. Item
steps remain unchanged at 100. Next, explain effective admission from the
existing runtime observations; automatic scaling can follow after this is
observable. An operator preference expresses desired work, not a new
credential, provider entitlement, resource lease, or signed allowance.

Reuse [headroom.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/routing/headroom.ts),
[execution-capacity-lease.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/fabric/execution-capacity-lease.ts),
[capacity-wait.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/resources/capacity-wait.ts), the queue planner,
and the existing final backend admission. A free producer still needs its exact
resolved engine/model, native account, and actual result identity; locality or a
subscription-like tier alone is insufficient. Hosted Devin ACU remains a
separate configured allowance. Explicit stored daily USD zero continues to mean
Stop. No offline comparison or artificial evaluation becomes a dispatch gate.

Before widening any effective policy, return a bounded explanation containing
requested versus admitted capacity, stable engine/model/account references,
constraint kind, observation timestamp, and available/unknown status. Recheck
at reservation and launch; a UI explanation is not a lease. Use allowlisted
labels, not credentials, raw paths, prompts, or provider error bodies. Reuse
durable accounting and identity ledgers before adding a new receipt schema.

**Files:** existing routing headroom/capacity projections, daemon admission,
and the autonomy capacity explanation. Keep current preference validation in
the existing contracts. Audit ordinary best-of-N candidate and critic cash classification
in a separate focused change, using the same resolved economic proof.

**Acceptance:** unchanged old defaults; explicit requests beyond legacy UI
maxima; NaN/fractional/overflow refusal; UI/runtime agreement; concurrent
reservation conflicts; revoked/stale account observations; unknown provider
capacity; actual hardware saturation; explicit Stop; exhausted positive cash
with proven-free production; paid/unknown fallback refusal; custom frontier API
costs retained. Use deterministic behavioral tests and real admission evidence,
not an optimization benchmark that blocks useful work.

Tradeoff: this improves capacity truth immediately without promising infinite
resources. Dynamic automatic scaling can follow after the system can explain
and replay every admission decision.

## Durable wakeups, steering, and context

**Wakeups:** add an account/repository-scoped durable inbox for queue changes,
completed runs, refreshed readiness, and changed grants. Coalesce by generation,
deduplicate event IDs, reconcile persisted state after restart, and retain timed
rescans/backoff when events are missed. The existing
[fleet event bus](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/fleet/event-bus.ts) is in-process/best-effort and
can include generative handlers; it is not a durable wakeup queue or a promise
that every handler costs zero. Wakeups request reevaluation through normal
admission, never an unconditional dispatch or new service activation.

**Steering:** Phantom already persists follow-ups through
[turn-queue.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/turn-queue.ts), holding them on failure/Stop.
Expose adapter capabilities separately: next-turn queue, stop-and-send, or
genuine mid-turn steering. OpenAI's documented mid-turn steering uses GPT-6
Responses WebSockets; an accepted update is queued, not yet applied, and does
not undo output or started tools. Record requested, accepted, applied/continued,
failed, and unknown states; follow the successor response identity. Do not
represent a queued CLI follow-up as provider-native steering.
[Mid-turn steering](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/steering)

**Compaction:** use [model-windows.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/model-windows.ts),
[context-fit.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/verse/context-fit.ts), and existing adapter/context
events. Keep the latest user objective, scope, unresolved questions, checked
file citations, and outstanding tool results in a deterministic portable
handoff. Opaque provider compaction belongs to that provider/account/session;
it cannot become another provider's readable history. Responses supports both
automatic and standalone compaction, but standalone `/responses/compact` is
not supported for multi-agent responses; automatic root/child compaction has
its own configuration. Report observed compaction and missing context without
asserting complete recall.
[Compaction](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/compaction),
[Responses multi-agent](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/responses-multi-agent)

The Responses multi-agent API currently has no fixed total-agent/depth limit
but defaults to three active subagent turns. Children share the configured
model and tools. Ashlr should preserve those actual provider settings while
assigning narrower application scopes; neither a child nor a handoff inherits
new account access merely because its parent can discover a tool.

## Provider and custody boundaries

The candidate's [OpenAI Agents inventory client](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/openai-agents/client.ts)
is bounded GET-only metadata; listing a session does not qualify a producer or
start a managed agent. Creation, tool execution, streaming, steering, and cost
admission are separate subsequent integrations requiring actual account access
and provider contracts. Keep this provider state separate from native session
IDs and phone/browser authority.

Reuse existing [Locus](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/integrations/locus.ts),
[Phantom secret resolution](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/src/core/integrations/secrets.ts), and scoped MCP
surfaces only for their supported credential/identity paths. A new Claude
producer credential broker needs its own verified native contract; do not
substitute an interactive-reserved profile or export subscription credentials.
Plugin installation and tool discovery do not prove per-turn attachment or
execution. Extend reported turn evidence only when an adapter can supply it.

[Dots companion](DOTS-COMPANION.md) describes personal task delegation and the
separate workspace-agent/event APIs; it does not activate a Dot engine.
Unverified Muse Code, external Grok Bot, or Dots transports remain explicit
unknown contracts until supported endpoints, entitlements, custody, and real
acceptance are established. Phone physical acceptance and installed native UI
acceptance remain distinct from browser or source checks.

Review the richer admission and automatic-scaling architecture before
implementing it. Ship the current bounded preference slice with source tests,
then verify the installed product and public
release separately; broader provider activation follows its actual human and
account requirements.

## Recorded local qualification — 2026-10-01

The exact 3.19 npm candidate (then named Verse) ran one `multi-file-rename` trial through the
installed local Anthropic bridge and Claude CLI. The captured original checker
passed after all three source files changed. The run took 392.453 seconds and 12
turns; CLI-reported usage was 2,979 input, 1,638 output and 12,872 cache-read tokens.

The request label was `qwen3.8:27b-q8_0`; captured runtime metadata identified
Q8_0, four serving slots and 65,536 context tokens per slot, but returned an
unknown model name. This was one trial with uncontrolled caches during other
verification work. It establishes the observed end-to-end path and checker
result. It is not a broad model benchmark, a matched speed comparison, a
billing measurement or proof of autonomous fleet activation.

The [sanitized qualification receipt](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/benchmarks/local-qualification-2026-10-01.json) records the source and archive
digests without publishing content-bearing traces. Reproduce the task with:

```sh
ashlr benchmark run --task multi-file-rename --trials 1 --concurrency 1 \
  --model qwen3.8:27b-q8_0 --cache-state uncontrolled --out report.json
```

# Use Phantom from an agent

Copy the blocks in order. Do not invent flags. If `phm docs --agent --json` disagrees with this page, trust the installed binary. A zero exit code is not a merge, a release, or permission to spend.

`phm` and `ashlr` are the same program. Examples use `phm`.

## 1. Install

Node.js 22.15.0 or newer.

```sh
node --version
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
phm --version
```

This source tree is not proof that npm has published the same version. Check [GitHub releases](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/releases/latest) before you pin one.

## 2. Read the command list

```sh
phm docs --agent --json
phm help
```

Use the JSON registry for commands, verbs, and flags. This page only shows the calls an agent needs on a cold start.

## 3. Commands that print JSON

These read local state. They do not start a fleet and they do not spend credits.

```sh
phm mcp list --json
phm mcp doctor --json
phm wire status --json
phm authority status --json
phm authority setup --dry-run --json
```

`phm mcp doctor` exits 1 when a required server is down. That is a health result. `phm authority status --json` reports the grant. Autonomy ships dormant and is macOS-only. Status does not turn it on. `phm authority setup --dry-run --json` prints the setup plan and does not sign a grant.

## 4. Open the console

```sh
phm verse --no-open --json
```

The server listens only on [http://127.0.0.1:7777/verse/](http://127.0.0.1:7777/verse/). The JSON includes a read token and a mutation token. Do not put either token in a PR, issue, or chat log.

## 5. MCP for Claude Code

Claude Code reads `mcpServers` in `~/.claude.json`. This backs up the file, then writes the gateway:

```sh
phm wire claude --json
```

Or paste this entry yourself:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ashlr-hub": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "ashlr",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "env": {}
    }
  }
}
```

The server key is `ashlr-hub`. Do not reuse the `ashlr` key. That name belongs to a different plugin.

## 6. MCP for Cursor

Cursor reads `mcpServers` in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`.

```sh
phm wire cursor --json
```

Or paste:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ashlr-hub": {
      "command": "ashlr",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

## 7. MCP for Codex

Codex stores servers in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Do not hand-edit that file. `codex` must be on `PATH`.

```sh
phm wire codex --json
```

That command runs `codex mcp add ashlr-hub -- ashlr mcp` after a backup.

## 8. Check that the gateway is actually up

Restart the editor so it reloads MCP servers. Then:

```sh
phm wire status --json
phm mcp doctor --json
```

A row that says the file contains `ashlr-hub` only proves the config write. `phm mcp doctor` is the start check. Registration is not authorization.

## 9. Read-only fleet server

This is a second MCP server. It does not launch work and it does not merge. Add it beside `ashlr-hub`, not instead of it.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "phantom-fleet": {
      "command": "phm",
      "args": ["mcp", "fleet"]
    }
  }
}
```

After MCP initialization, call `tools/list`, then `fleet_status` with `{}`. Argument rules and the other tools are in [the fleet MCP onramp](FLEET-MCP-ONRAMP.md).

## 10. Optional cloud handoff

Off unless you run these. Cloud launch spends Claude credits; Devin launch
spends ACUs. Check the applicable budget before launching. Neither merges by
itself.

```sh
phm cloud launch "<task>" --repo owner/name
phm devin connect
phm devin launch "<task>"
```

See [Cloud](CLOUD.md) and [Devin](DEVIN.md).

## Indexes

- [llms.txt](llms.txt): short doc index
- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): the same install and MCP blocks in one text file
- [Self-hosting](SELF-HOSTING.md): upgrade and uninstall
- [Quickstart](QUICKSTART.md): first local session for a person

## Gateway tool policies

Set `ASHLR_MCP_POLICY` to a host-owned YAML file before starting `phm mcp`.
Set `ASHLR_MCP_AGENT` and comma-separated `ASHLR_MCP_GROUPS` in the trusted
launcher, never from tool arguments. Restart the gateway after changing policy.

```yaml
ask_before_every_change: false
read_tools: [locus__status]
policies:
  - name: developer-tools
    agents: [codex]
    groups: [engineering]
    tools:
      locus__status: allow
      locus__delete: deny
      locus__update: approval_required
```

Tool keys are exact `<server>__<tool>` names. Empty agent and group lists match
all callers; otherwise either selector can match. Matching verdicts resolve as
`allow > approval_required > deny`. Unmatched calls and an unset policy file
retain existing behavior. Invalid or unreadable configured files fail startup.
The fleet switch overrides an allow for every tool absent from `read_tools`:
unclassified tools conservatively count as writes. Keep this file and launcher
identity under administrator control. Denied and approval-required calls return
an MCP tool error naming the policy before downstream activation or execution.
Approval-required calls remain blocked; request arguments cannot approve them.
Native hub tools retain their existing authorization path.

## Gateway sessions

Each `phm mcp` gateway gets a session id (`gs_` plus 12 hex digits).

```bash
phm sessions list --json
phm sessions revoke <id> --json
```

Revoking blocks that session's next tool call, native tools included; start a
new gateway to continue. Every call adds one row (`ts`, `session`, `caller`,
`tool`, `verdict`: `allow`, `deny`, `approval_required` or `revoked`) to
`~/.ashlr/gateway/activity.jsonl`. Arguments are never stored, only their
names marked `[redacted]`. Rows older than 14 days are removed when a gateway
starts. A session record that goes missing counts as revoked.
