# Dot handoff guide

Evidence checked against official OpenAI sources on **2026-11-04**. This guide
lets an agent hand a bounded task to Mason's personal OpenAI Dot — and read a
result back — without assuming an undocumented API, unlimited usage, or a
model name. No account access, test send, or live Dot transport was performed.
Companion docs: [Dots companion](DOTS-COMPANION.md) (operator workflow),
[Peer interfaces](PEERS-INTERFACES.md) (interface inventory, checked
2026-10-26), [Agent-to-agent](AGENT-TO-AGENT.md) (a2a schema),
[iMessage intake](IMESSAGE.md). Machine-readable summary:
`ashlr fleet dot-handoff [--json]` (offline, read-only; same claims below).

## What official sources establish

### The product

A **dot** ("your dot") is a personal always-on agent inside ChatGPT with its
own cloud computer and browser. It keeps working between conversations, can
pause and wake itself, and delegates work to ChatGPT Work or Codex. One dot
per eligible member. Sources: [Meet dots](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots),
[Getting started with your dot](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001530-getting-started-with-your-dot).

### Task handoff (documented surfaces only)

Work reaches a dot **conversationally** — there is no documented personal-dot
API (see Unverified). Surfaces:

- ChatGPT mobile app, desktop app, or desktop browser (not mobile web); voice
  call; Slack and Teams channels the owner connected.
- **Texting**: iMessage/RCS beta for US Pro users, strictly one-to-one — only
  the verified owner can text the dot, the dot cannot join group texts, text
  other people, or initiate calls. [Message your dot](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/channels)
- A dot delegates outward to ChatGPT Work or Codex: local tasks need the **one
  connected personal computer** online with the ChatGPT app open; cloud coding
  tasks need a Codex cloud environment pre-created in Codex. Delegated tasks
  appear under the dot's **Activity**. [Tasks and memory](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/tasks-and-memory),
  [Computers and apps](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/computers-and-apps)

### Proactive behavior and approvals

Proactive research is **read-only**: it cannot send messages to other people,
change content through plugins, or control a browser or computer. Scheduled
runs and proactive updates appear in the conversation; a schedule needs a
saved task with timezone, end condition and notification destination. An
automatic action review gates account-affecting or sharing actions; optional
custom rules offer act / act-on-request / ask-first / hand-off modes; sensitive
actions (passwords, payments, some deletes) go to the user. Pause, stopping a
delegated task, and canceling a schedule are separate controls.
[Controls](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/controls),
[Privacy/security FAQ](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001529-dots-privacy-security-and-safety-faqs)

### Model

Docs say dots are powered by the GPT-6 family and are expanding to include
GPT-6.1 Terra, with different models for different parts of the work. The
exact model behind any task is **not documented** — never assume or pin a
model name.

### Usage and availability

- Dot conversations do **not** count toward ChatGPT usage limits; Work/Codex
  tasks the dot starts count against those products' limits as usual. The plan
  includes a deeper-work allowance with extended limits the first month.
- Availability: Pro 100/200/500 (18+, outside EEA/UK/Switzerland), Business
  Premium worldwide rollout, Enterprise admin-enabled and off by default; not
  for UAE data/inference residency workspaces. Enterprise preview is free
  2026-11-04 → 2026-11-18, then billing begins for enabled dots.
  [Access section](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots#access),
  [Getting started](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001530-getting-started-with-your-dot)

## Unverified — do not assume

- **Personal-dot API**: no official source documents creating a dot, sending
  it a message, subscribing to its events, polling its tasks, or reading its
  output. Every personal-dot surface is conversational or account UI.
- **Mason's account**: his plan, region, workspace and enabled features are a
  local observation (order t1635u), not documentation. Check the actual
  account before planning capacity.
- **Workspace Agents API**: real but a *separate* product —
  `POST /v1/workspace_agents/{id}/trigger` returns `202` + `conversation_url`,
  beta run-status polling exists, and **agent responses cannot be retrieved
  through the API**. It needs its own workspace agent access token and does
  not address a personal dot.
  [Trigger runs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/workspace-agents/trigger-runs)
- **Plugin MCP events**: an authenticated plugin can expose `events/list`,
  `events/subscribe`, `events/unsubscribe` for signed deliveries on a verified
  public HTTPS callback (user OAuth 2.1 + S256 PKCE). That is an inbound
  surface Phantom could serve, not a way to drive a dot; a delivery
  acknowledges receipt, not completed work.
  [MCP events](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-events),
  [Plugin auth](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/auth)

## Phantom boundary (verified in this repo)

- `openai-dot` in `src/core/agents/bus-v2-schema.ts` is a **routing label** in
  the `agent-bus.v2` contract — not an authenticated identity; claims grant no
  execution authority. Provider recognition ≠ transport.
- `src/core/agents/a2a-schema.ts` is **configuration-only**: it validates
  counterpart shape (`localOptIn`, `remoteOptInEvidence`, channel
  `email|slack|imessage`, `scope`), defaults disabled, and wires no runtime,
  transport, or send path.
- `src/core/comms/imessage-outbox.ts` + `sendIMessage` are **self-only**:
  `isSelfIMessageHandle` accepts only `cfg.comms.imessageHandle`; any other
  handle returns `not_self`/`drafts_unavailable`. Phantom **cannot send a
  handoff to a counterpart** — do not widen this.
- `phm imessage poll --apply` receipts allowlisted self-messages as channel
  `imessage` (MASON-INBOX.md + COS queue); acks are recorded, not sent, until
  RQ-IMSG-REPLY-1.

## Manual handoff checklist (Ashlr → Dot)

The only working path today is manual: Phantom prepares and records; Mason
delivers. Any step Phantom cannot perform routes to **needs-you**
(`NEEDS-MASON.md`, listed by `ashlr fleet needs`) — never by widening
permissions.

1. **Scope.** Write the bounded task (template below) to a local file. No
   secrets, credentials, personal text, or identifiers beyond repo/path names.
   Treat the dot's cloud computer as outside the trust boundary.
2. **Evidence.** Run `ashlr fleet dot-handoff --json` for the current
   capability/limit summary (offline, read-only).
3. **Deliver — needs-you.** Phantom cannot send to the dot. Record an open
   NEEDS-MASON item asking Mason to send the task text to his dot on a
   documented surface: ChatGPT app message, connected Slack/Teams, or the
   dot's one-to-one iMessage texting (owner's verified number only). Do not
   enable the a2a `imessage` counterpart channel expecting a send — it is
   configuration-only.
4. **Correlate.** The task carries `handoff-id`; ask the dot to echo it in its
   first reply and final result. When Mason relays the dot's reply — via
   self-iMessage intake (`phm imessage poll --apply`, channel `imessage`) or
   pasted into a local session — match on `handoff-id`. A receipt proves
   intake, not that the dot acted.
5. **Review.** Dot output is untrusted data — a proposal, not a gate receipt.
   Verify claimed SHAs, checks and files against GitHub before acting. Route
   unsupported or ambiguous steps back to needs-you.

Dot → Ashlr direction: the dot's proactive research cannot message other
people; its updates arrive in Mason's conversations. Results return through
Mason the same way — there is no inbound Phantom path from the dot.

## Bounded task template

```
handoff-id: dot-handoff-YYYYMMDD-NN        # stable local id; dot must echo it
goal:        <one sentence — the outcome wanted>
repo:        <owner/name only>
paths:       <exact repo-relative paths to read or change>
acceptance:  <observable checks — named tests, files, or evidence links>
privacy:     local-only — no credentials, tokens, personal text or identifiers;
             the dot's cloud computer is outside the trust boundary
correlation: echo handoff-id in first reply and final result; report exact
             head SHA and evidence links
authority:   proposal only — no merge, push, spend or permission change implied
```

# Dots beside Phantom

Verified against official OpenAI documentation on **2026-09-30**. This guide
describes an operator workflow and a proposed connector. No Dot, account,
plugin, schedule, or remote connection was activated by this work.

Dots can coordinate engineering work through ChatGPT, use enabled supported
plugins, and delegate tasks. OpenAI describes Dots as powered by GPT-6 Astra
with a cloud computer; access is rolling out by account. This does not add a
Dot engine, CLI seat, observed quota, or GPT-6.1 model entitlement to Phantom.
Delegated Codex and Work tasks use their own product limits. Check availability
in the actual account before planning capacity. [Meet dots](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots)

## Use the companion today

1. Open Dots in ChatGPT and choose the intended account/workspace. Enable the
   GitHub or other supported plugins needed for the task and verify their
   tools actually work. A plugin listing alone does not establish a working
   account connection. [Build plugins](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-plugins)
2. To delegate into this Mac, connect it from **Computers → Your computer →
   Allow access**. The documented limit is currently one connected personal
   computer; the Dot's cloud computer remains separate. Local skills require
   the connected computer. Cloud browser sign-ins do not inherit Mac sessions.
   Do not export native subscription credentials to the cloud computer.
   [Computers and apps](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/computers-and-apps)
3. Give the Dot an exact repository, task, branch, and acceptance criteria.
   Local Codex/Work delegation needs the connected computer online with
   ChatGPT open. Already-configured Codex cloud environments can run new cloud
   coding tasks while that computer is off. Continuing an existing task uses
   its original environment; changing the connected computer does not move it.
   [Tasks and memory](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/tasks-and-memory)

For **Work with me**, use a task such as:

> Continue my existing Codex task named `<exact title>` for `<repo>` at
> `<branch and full SHA>`. Help investigate `<problem>`, propose the smallest
> complete fix, and return the changed files and acceptance evidence. Keep
> the implementation in that task so I can steer it there.

For **Work for me**, make the continuing responsibility concrete:

> Coordinate `<named repo/task>` until `<acceptance criteria>` are met. Use
> the connected computer's Codex tasks for implementation and enabled plugins
> for source evidence. Follow my existing authorization for this task and
> the repository's account, spend, signing, and Stop boundaries. Notify me
> when complete, blocked, or a decision needs me; cite the exact source SHA
> and separate source, installed product, and public release evidence.

Specify any schedule's timezone, end condition, and notification destination;
confirm it was saved. For event-driven work, ask which events the connected
service supports and confirm the subscription. A connected service does not
automatically monitor events. Inspect delegated tasks in Activity. New tasks
receive their assigned context, rather than every prior conversation.
[Tasks and memory](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/tasks-and-memory)

An ongoing scoped instruction can authorize future work within existing
permissions; extra confirmation for every action is not necessary by default.
Custom rules do not grant new access. Pause the Dot, stop delegated Activity,
and cancel schedules separately when stopping the whole workflow. Stopping
does not undo completed actions. [Controls](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots/controls)

## What Phantom currently implements

The [Grok companion guide](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/GROK-BOT-COMPANION.md) documents manual reviews and an
optional provider webhook handoff. It explicitly distinguishes acceptance
from completion and does not implement a two-way Phantom Bot connector. Dots can
serve the same companion role through its supported task delegation; a Grok
webhook URL cannot be reused as a Dot trigger.

| Existing surface | Actual contract | Dots implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phantom agents API | Local workbench reads and operator-gated mutations; no Dot backend | Local Codex tasks may use the workbench under existing permissions; cloud access needs its own connector |
| Phantom agent-tools MCP | Per-turn bearer, live chat scopes, revocation on turn end/Stop | Unsuitable as a persistent external subscription credential |
| Phantom MCP protocol | Lists `2026-07-28`, but handles only initialize, ping, and tool methods | Does not implement `server/discover` or MCP Events |
| Automations webhook | Loopback-only, bounded strict payload, operator mutation gate | Not a public ChatGPT callback or an authenticated cloud ingress |
| Phantom MCP gateway / Ashlr Plugin | Local stdio tool surfaces | Installed tools are not automatically enabled ChatGPT plugins or Dot connections |

These claims come from [agents-api.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/src/core/verse/agents-api.ts),
[verse-mcp.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/src/core/verse/verse-mcp.ts),
[verse-mcp-grants.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/src/core/verse/verse-mcp-grants.ts),
[automations-api.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/src/core/verse/automations-api.ts), and
[mcp-gateway.ts](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/src/core/mcp-gateway.ts). No live Dot transport was tested.

## Supported programmatic paths

The cited personal-Dots guides do not document a general API to create Dots,
send arbitrary messages, poll their conversations, or import their usage.
This is not a claim that OpenAI has no agent APIs: the separate **published
Workspace Agents API** provides a trigger endpoint, idempotency, and beta run
status. It requires its own access token and API channel. Its documentation
currently says agent response retrieval is unavailable. Do not represent a
workspace agent trigger as a personal Dot seat or a completed review.
[Workspace agent runs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/workspace-agents/trigger-runs)

For event-driven coordination, ChatGPT supports **MCP 2.0 Events**. An
authenticated plugin exposes discovery plus `events/list`, `events/subscribe`,
and `events/unsubscribe`. The user requests monitoring; ChatGPT supplies a
callback and signing secret. The server verifies a public HTTPS callback,
persists the scoped subscription, and signs event deliveries. A successful
delivery acknowledges receipt, not completed work. Refresh, revocation,
unsubscribe, replay policy, idempotency, and bounded retries belong to the
connector. [MCP Events](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-events)

## Next implementation slice

Build a separate authenticated **read-only fleet evidence plugin** with
`fleet_status` and `review_evidence` tools and a `fleet.review_ready` event
filtered by repository/PR. Reuse existing projections; report exact head SHA,
check identifiers, and evidence freshness. The ChatGPT-facing connection
requires **user OAuth 2.1 authorization code with S256 PKCE**. Validate token
issuer, resource/audience, expiry, and scopes on every request, and use the
redirect registered for the actual connection. ChatGPT cannot substitute a
customer API key or a machine-to-machine/service-account grant for this user
flow. [Plugin authentication](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/auth)

A dedicated revocable service identity may broker internal upstream reads;
it does not authenticate ChatGPT to the plugin. Exclude phone pairing, UI
cookies, turn/mutation tokens, raw transcripts, grants, and credentials from
this external surface. Event payloads are untrusted data, never authority.
Keep dispatch behind the existing local/signed execution paths.

Acceptance must cover cross-account isolation, callback SSRF/redirect refusal,
signature verification, duplicate/out-of-order delivery, restart/expiry,
revocation, and cancellation. Prove one real subscribed ChatGPT event is
received; separately inspect the resulting delegated task and output. Do not
claim a completed integration from a webhook acknowledgment.

Developer testing can use a configured Secure MCP Tunnel; publication requires
a public HTTPS MCP endpoint. Connect, inspect discovered tools/events, and
exercise both successful and refused requests in the actual account before
showing **Connected** in Phantom. A locally installed stdio server is only the
starting transport. [Connect and test](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/connect-chatgpt)

# Drafts

Mail to anyone other than you waits for your approval. Replies to your own
verified email address still go out directly.

## What happens

1. The email outbox finds a `*.reply.eml` addressed to one person who is not on
   your allowlist.
2. It writes a pending draft to `~/.ashlr-runs/drafts/drafts.jsonl` (mode 0600)
   and moves the file to `outbox/drafted/`. Nothing is sent.
3. The draft shows up as a needs-you item with Approve and Reject.
4. You read it with `phm drafts show` and decide.

Approve records your decision. It does not send. Turning an approved draft into
a send is a separate, security-reviewed step, so until that lands approving a
draft never makes an email leave the machine.

Mail with no recipient or several recipients is refused and stays in the outbox.
Text that looks like a secret is refused and never written to the store. Keep
credentials in Phantom Secrets and refer to them by binding name only.

## Commands

Every command takes `--json`.

```sh
phm drafts list --json
phm drafts list --status pending --json
phm drafts show d-0123456789abcdef --json
phm drafts approve d-0123456789abcdef --digest 0a1b2c3d --json
phm drafts reject d-0123456789abcdef --json
```

- `list` shows metadata only (no body). `--status` is `pending`, `approved` or
  `rejected`.
- `show` prints the full draft including the body and its digest.
- `approve --digest <prefix>` binds your approval to the text you read. Use at
  least 8 characters of the digest from `show`. A mismatch is refused.
- A decided draft cannot be changed. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 not found or already
  decided, 2 bad usage.

## Record format

One JSON object per line. Each decision appends a new snapshot and the last line
for an id wins. A line that is malformed, altered (digest mismatch) or
secret-shaped is ignored.

```json
{"id":"d-0123456789abcdef","status":"pending","channel":"email","to":"client@example.com","subject":"Quote","body":"...","source":"a.reply.eml","digest":"<sha256>","createdAt":"2026-11-04T12:00:00.000Z"}
```

The id comes from the source file name and the text, so a retried pass never
creates a second draft for the same message.

## For developers

- Store, approve and reject, and the needs-you producer: `src/core/cos/drafts.ts`.
- Routing: `sendEmailOutbox({ draftsRunsDir })` in `src/core/comms/email-outbox.ts`.
  Without `draftsRunsDir` a non-allowlisted recipient is refused, as before.
- The needs-you producer exports `needsYouItems()` and `refreshDraftsNeedsYou()`.
  Its items carry no HTTP route, so the decision is taken with the commands above.
  Registering it with the Verse activity route is a separate contract change.

# Mac queue supervisor

`phm drive` runs serial ticks, with a 30 second delay after each completed tick.
It reaps finished workers, publishes successful jobs through the existing
`publish.sh`, and admits READY jobs within pool floors, ceilings and a global
ceiling. STARTING jobs consume capacity. Floors receive priority over surplus
work; floors do not create work or override admission. Job kinds bound which
pools may serve them, and a pool can be capped at a paced daily share — see
[Pool routing](#pool-routing).

```sh
phm drive --once --dry-run
phm drive --once --dry-run --bridge /absolute/path/drive-bridge
phm drive --tick 30 --bridge /absolute/path/drive-bridge --publisher /absolute/path/publish.sh
```

## Integration status

This change provides the supervisor, CLI, subprocess bridge protocol and fake
pool acceptance tests. It does **not** include the Mac-specific bridge executable.
DRIVER-1 and the #1014 admission implementation are absent from this checkout,
but their documented interfaces were inspected locally: DRIVER-1's uncommitted
`docs/QUEUE.md` and `src/core/queue/schema.ts` in the sibling
`RQ-PHANTOM-DRIVER-1-QUEUE` worktree, and `scripts/mac-bridge/MEMORY.md` at local
ref `codex-bridge/RQ-MAC-MEM-ADMISSION`, commit `74bbf659`. These dependency
interfaces inform the bridge contract below; they are not evidence of a merged
dependency or an installed host integration.

Reading `~/.ashlr-runs/queue/README.md` returned `Operation not permitted`.
The live dispatchd status/ledger schemas, actual pool runner and publisher
arguments, and shared scheduler ownership mechanism remain unqualified.

The executable bridge described below must be implemented against those host
contracts before live use. This is a new dependency seam, not a claim that
dispatchd already implements this protocol. A missing bridge fails closed.
Keep dispatchd as the active fallback until Masbot validates the bridge and
coordinates ownership transfer. This command never stops dispatchd, installs
a service, edits runner configuration or changes the sandbox.

The bridge path defaults to `~/.ashlr-runs/queue/drive-bridge`; the publisher
defaults to `~/.ashlr-runs/queue/publish.sh`. These are integration defaults,
not verified host paths. Override them with absolute canonical paths as needed.
Bridge and publisher must be owned regular executable files, with no symlink
aliases, hard links or group/world write permission. Only `publish.sh` is
accepted as the publisher basename.

## Tick behavior

1. Acquire exclusive shared dispatch ownership. A busy or unavailable owner
   returns a hold without reaping, publishing, launching or writing status.
2. Reap through the existing runner, recording durable completion evidence.
3. For each successful FINISHED job, reserve publication durably, invoke
   `phantom exec -- /absolute/path/publish.sh <bridge-supplied arguments>`,
   then record its outcome. No direct Git or GitHub push exists in the driver.
4. Read current queue and capacity. Fill below-floor pools first, then remaining
   capacity by descending priority and queue order. Re-read before every launch.
5. Recheck PAUSE and ask the bridge to atomically verify READY, completed
   dependencies, claim ownership and capacity before launching the existing
   runner with #1014 heavy-step admission wired into its commands.
6. Write native status through the bridge and release ownership in `finally`.

Memory PAUSE blocks launch but permits reap and completion publication. The
default PAUSE convention is `~/.ashlr-runs/PAUSE`, configurable with
`--pause-file`. The driver also treats `~/.ashlr/KILL` as a launch hold.
Unreadable control files and dangling symlinks hold admission. The bridge must
independently check the actual host controls inside its admission transaction;
the CLI check cannot close that race by itself. Native authority and Stop rules
must also guard publication in the host adapter/publisher.

`--once --dry-run` calls only the bridge's read-only `snapshot` and reads control
file metadata. It does not acquire ownership, reap, reserve, publish, launch or
write status. Its plan uses currently known capacity; it does not assume reaping
will free slots. `--dry-run` alone also returns after one tick. Unknown admission,
malformed snapshots and unconfigured pools never become free capacity.

SIGINT/SIGTERM stop new actions and wake the interval sleep. An in-flight bridge
call or publication settles first, with a 120 second command timeout. The driver
does not kill fleet workers. Long-running mode reports a failed tick and retries
after the configured delay; one-shot failures return exit 1. Usage errors return
exit 2. Child stdout/stderr and publication arguments are never printed.

## Dependency integration requirements

### DRIVER-1 queue.v1

The inspected queue contract stores `schema: "queue.v1"` and a `jobs` array at
`~/.ashlr-runs/queue/queue.v1.json`. Queue states are
`READY|CLAIMED|PR-OPEN|BLOCKED|HOLD|DONE|PROPOSED`. They are distinct from the
execution states in this driver's normalized snapshot. The adapter must not
write STARTING or PUBLISHING into `queue.v1` as queue statuses; retain execution
and publication evidence in the host's corresponding records.

Only READY jobs whose dependencies all exist and are DONE may be presented as
launch candidates. Recheck that condition inside the queue claim transaction,
then retain the resulting active claim owner through execution and publication.
Missing dependencies, cyclic dependencies, HOLD, PROPOSED and BLOCKED never
become dispatchable automatically. Imported CLAIMED jobs without ownership
evidence must not be reclaimed or assigned invented owners. Unknown routing
fields such as `unspecified` require review before launch.

Use DRIVER-1's `read`, `claim` and `finish` store seam. Completion and blocking
must use the last active claim's owner. Recording a PR URL yields PR-OPEN and
retains the claim; recording DONE without a PR URL closes it. These are
operator-reported queue states, not proof of merge or required checks. A worker
exit or a publisher's successful invocation does not by itself authorize a
queue DONE transition. Preserve the queue's no-automatic-reclaim rule and never
steal `queue.v1.lock` by age or PID heuristics.

The structural helper
[`projectDriveQueueV1`](../src/core/drive/queue-v1.ts) accepts the documented
QueueDocument shape after the queue store validates it. It maps P0 through P9
to descending numeric priority, preserving P0 precedence and queue order for
ties. READY with incomplete dependencies, unknown priority or unspecified
routing becomes HELD. Imported CLAIMED conservatively becomes STARTING and
consumes capacity even when its owner is unknown. Other queue statuses become
HELD until the bridge overlays independently verified execution/publication
evidence. DONE and PR-OPEN alone never prove worker termination or publication
success. Merge the complete host worker inventory into this projection so no
active worker disappears from capacity accounting.

The helper does not claim jobs or replace the queue's runtime validator. Validate
its translation against the dependency schema before cutover. The queue
transaction lock is not a replacement for shared dispatchd ownership or for
memory admission.

### #1014 heavy-step memory admission

The inspected memory contract provides `with-memory.sh` and
`memory_admission.py`. Preserve the adapter's PATH and gate settings when
invoking the existing launcher. Its shims gate heavy PATH-based cargo, npm,
npx and tsc operations. Absolute executable paths, replaced PATH values and
other package managers need explicit heavy-step wrapping; they must not become
admission bypasses.

Gate each heavy build/test operation, not the whole `phm drive` daemon or the
lifetime of a daemonizing pool worker. Do not use `memory_admission.py run` to
hold a reservation around a daemonizing workload. Configure the existing runner
so its heavy child steps pass through the gate while its sandbox remains intact.
The driver snapshot's `admission` value is a readiness observation, not a heavy
reservation; each heavy step must acquire the real semaphore at execution time.
If the shared gate is absent, inaccessible or unqualified, hold new launches.

All participating worktrees and sandboxes must share the same gate state. The
documented default is `/tmp/phantom-memory-<uid>`, configurable through
`PHANTOM_MEMORY_STATE_DIR` or `--state-dir`, independent of HOME. The gate's
default PAUSE convention uses the OS account home plus `.ashlr-runs/PAUSE`, also
independent of HOME. Configure the driver's `--pause-file` and the gate's
`PHANTOM_MEMORY_PAUSE_FILE`/`--pause-file` to the same actual memguard sentinel;
the convention has not been verified against the installed memguard.

The gate admits at most four heavy reservations, requires at least 30% modeled
free RAM after reservations, and blocks admission when swap reaches 8 GiB or
PAUSE is present. Unknown telemetry queues work. Kernel locks and process-group
liveness retain uncertain reservations without TTL takeover. Never delete its
lock/state files, bypass admission, or relax sandbox access to make it run.
Host acceptance must verify the adapter inside the actual runner sandbox.

## Host bridge protocol: phm-drive/v1

Each invocation is an executable plus two literal arguments: an operation name
and one JSON request object. There is no shell interpolation. Requests include
`"protocol":"phm-drive/v1"`. Replies must be one JSON object of the form
`{"protocol":"phm-drive/v1","result":...}` on stdout. Private diagnostic
logging belongs to the bridge; stdout is bounded to 4 MiB. Do not return secrets,
environment dumps, prompts or auth material in any reply.

| Operation | Additional request fields | Result and required behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `snapshot` | optional `lease` | Normalized snapshot below. Without a lease this must be strictly read-only. Present READY candidates only when every dependency is present and DONE. Include every active worker, including dispatchd and uncertain STARTING work. |
| `acquire` | none | An opaque 16-160 character `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` lease, or `null` when held. Must exclude dispatchd and all other driver instances using the real shared ownership mechanism. Never independently create a second scheduler lock. |
| `reap` | `lease` | `true` after idempotently reconciling completion evidence, updating queue state and appending native `jobs.jsonl` records. A missing PID alone is not completion evidence. |
| `launch` | `lease`, `job` | `"launched"` or `"held"`. Recheck shared ownership, pool/global counts, PAUSE and host memory pressure; on macOS hold unless kernel pressure is known normal and the existing host headroom gate permits launch; other platforms retain their existing admission behavior without macOS telemetry. Recheck inside the host admission transaction immediately before invoking the runner; atomically claim READY with all dependencies DONE using the queue claim owner. Persist STARTING execution evidence before invoking the existing sandboxed runner with #1014 heavy-step gating. Do not reserve a heavy slot for the worker's entire lifetime. |
| `reserve-publish` | `lease`, `job` | `null` if not eligible; otherwise `{"argv":["literal","arguments"]}` after durably recording PUBLISHING. Use the existing publish.sh argument contract. |
| `finish-publish` | `lease`, `job`, `outcome` | `true` after durably recording `published` or `unknown` and its native ledger event. |
| `write-status` | `lease`, `report` | `true` after atomically writing `status.json` in the dispatchd format. Map the normalized report; never replace native schema with the CLI report. |
| `release` | `lease` | `true` after releasing only this owner's lease. Must not release a successor's ownership. |

All mutations must validate the lease, process identity and native authority
before effects. Admission and ownership must fail closed if #1014 or its state
is unavailable. Timeouts or lost replies must retain STARTING/PUBLISHING intent;
never retry a launch or publication just because its acknowledgement was lost.
Ownership recovery must account for in-flight workers and publishers before
transferring to dispatchd. The bridge must support leases across multiple
subprocess invocations, with safe renewal/recovery for long ticks.

The bridge invokes the existing pool runner with its current confinement and
Locus identity checks. Secrets-dependent execution uses `phantom exec --`.
No new credentials, access to `~/.codex` auth, sandbox overrides or non-loopback
local inference endpoints belong in this adapter. The supervisor itself makes
no inference calls and supplies no sandbox flags.

### Snapshot

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "pools": [{ "id": "codex-cmp", "floor": 1, "ceiling": 2 }],
  "maxRunning": 2,
  "paused": false,
  "admission": "open",
  "jobs": [{ "id": "RQ-EXAMPLE", "pool": "codex-cmp", "state": "READY", "priority": 100 }]
}
```

`admission` is `open`, `closed` or `unknown`. Counts are nonnegative integers;
floors cannot exceed ceilings and their sum cannot exceed `maxRunning`. Job and
pool identifiers use ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, start
with a letter or digit, and are at most 160 characters. Jobs have unique IDs and
must reference a configured pool. Priorities are safe integers; higher goes first.

Pools may additionally carry `paused` (boolean) and `admission`
(`open`, `closed`, or `unknown`) from the current lane controls and probes.
Omitted fields preserve the bridge's existing global admission contract; an
explicit unknown probe holds that lane. Refresh these fields with every snapshot.
The atomic launch operation must still recheck lane controls, probes and capacity.

Tick reports include `skipped` entries with job, pool and a fixed reason for
READY jobs blocked by lane pause, probe admission, routing, capacity or paced
share in the latest snapshot. Lane breaker details are reported separately. A tick with no eligible work sets `held` to
the first blocking reason, or `no-ready-jobs` for an empty READY queue. The CLI
logs this report as JSON; the bridge maps it into its native status schema.

States are READY, HELD, STARTING, RUNNING, FINISHED, FAILED, PUBLISHING, PUBLISHED
and PUBLISH_UNKNOWN. HELD is not launchable. FINISHED requires an integer
`exitCode`; only zero is eligible
for publication. A lost/failed publication becomes PUBLISH_UNKNOWN and requires
reconciliation against publish.sh evidence before another attempt. A driver
crash can leave PUBLISHING, which must receive the same reconciliation. Neither
state is selected automatically for publication. Do not infer success from a
worker exit when its completion artifact is missing.

### Claude API lane health

For `claude-api`, every completed job (including FAILED and publication states)
must retain `completedAtMs` (nonnegative epoch milliseconds), integer `exitCode`
and boolean `emptyFinish` (true when completion produced no file changes).
Missing or malformed completion evidence rejects the snapshot. Retain this
history across ticks and restarts; publication must not erase it.

Two code 13 exits or strictly more than 50% empty finishes in a rolling hour
park this lane. The JSON tick log and `write-status` report carry `laneHealth`
with the reason and `probeAtMs`. Five minutes after the latest failed/empty
finish, one eligible queued job may probe recovery; STARTING/RUNNING jobs block
additional probes. A zero exit with changes restores normal capacity and clears
the failure window. Quiet time alone does not prove recovery. Other pools keep
receiving eligible jobs; probes obey all existing admission, routing and capacity
gates. The host bridge must retain the history and map the health report into
its native status schema; no separate inference call is made by the supervisor.

### Pool routing

A job's kind is the uppercase token leading its id after an optional `RQ-`
prefix (`RQ-GEN-…` is GEN, `RQ-REFILL-…-LAND-…` is REFILL). Kind bounds which
pool may serve the line; the driver never re-pools a violating line — it stays
queued (HELD at the queue.v1 seam, never planned at launch) until routing is
corrected, because pool is spend attribution.

- `codex-personal` serves only LAND, FIXUP, DRAIN and DAILYFIX lines. Every
  other kind — including an id with no recognizable kind — is ineligible there.
- GEN, PLAN, SELFOPT and DESK lines go only to `devin` or `codex-local`.
- Kinds the rules do not name keep their declared pool (never
  `codex-personal`).

A pool row may carry an optional `daily` object — the pool's paced daily share
as the bridge reports it:

```json
{ "id": "codex-personal", "floor": 0, "ceiling": 2,
  "daily": { "share": 6, "used": 2, "startMs": 1770000000000, "endMs": 1770086400000 } }
```

`share` dispatches vest evenly across `[startMs, endMs)`; `used` is the
bridge-verified count already spent inside it. The pool launches only while
the vested allowance still exceeds `used`, so it can never be ahead of its
even pace for the day. A malformed `daily` invalidates the snapshot, and an
unstarted or stale window admits nothing — the bridge must present the fresh
window before the share re-opens. Pools without `daily` are unpaced: their
ceiling alone bounds them.

The normalized CLI report contains `version`, `at` (ISO timestamp), `dryRun`,
`paused`, `active`, `ready`, `planned`, `launched`, `published`,
`publicationUnknown` and `held`. This report is for human/machine CLI consumers;
the adapter translates it into the host status format. Native queue mutations
append `jobs.jsonl` through the existing store so dispatchd readers keep working.

## Launchd template for Masbot

This XML is documentation only. Masbot supplies absolute escaped paths and the
actual runtime PATH, validates host compatibility and installs the service after
ownership cutover. No `.plist` file or launchd installation is changed by this job.
Keep the service disabled until the adapter passes the host checks below.

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>ai.ashlr.phantom-drive</string>
  <key>Disabled</key><true/>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/ABSOLUTE/PATH/phm</string><string>drive</string>
    <string>--tick</string><string>30</string>
    <string>--bridge</string><string>/ABSOLUTE/PATH/drive-bridge</string>
    <string>--publisher</string><string>/ABSOLUTE/PATH/publish.sh</string>
    <string>--pause-file</string><string>/ABSOLUTE/PATH/PAUSE</string>
  </array>
  <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  <dict><key>PATH</key><string>/ABSOLUTE/PHANTOM/AND/NODE/BIN:/usr/bin:/bin</string></dict>
  <key>RunAtLoad</key><false/>
  <key>KeepAlive</key><true/>
  <key>ThrottleInterval</key><integer>30</integer>
  <key>ExitTimeOut</key><integer>150</integer>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/ABSOLUTE/PRIVATE/LOGS/drive.out.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/ABSOLUTE/PRIVATE/LOGS/drive.err.log</string>
</dict>
</plist>
```

Before cutover, test the adapter on copied/synthetic native state: native
status/jobs schema compatibility, shared ownership contention against dispatchd,
two drivers, semaphore denial, PAUSE racing a launch, crash recovery around
STARTING/PUBLISHING, publisher argument fidelity, and graceful shutdown. Compare
`phm drive --once --dry-run` with dispatchd's plan. Cutover and rollback must
transfer the same ownership fence; never run both schedulers independently.

Unit acceptance uses a fake pool runner and does not exercise a paid worker,
live publisher, real auth store or active fleet. Run it with an isolated HOME:

```sh
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/drive-supervisor.test.ts test/drive-cli-bridge.test.ts
```

On macOS the built-in driver samples kernel pressure and existing headroom before planning and again at its subprocess launch boundary; unknown macOS telemetry holds. Other platforms retain existing admission behavior without a macOS sysctl probe. These checks do not replace the host bridge transaction recheck. `pauseWorkers` is advisory only; the driver does not pause or signal workers.

# Driver operator runbook

## Availability and operating boundary

`phm drive` is registered in `src/cli/index.ts` and backed by a loaded
implementation. This runbook documents the operating procedure and commissioning
gates. The implemented supervisor contract, CLI flags, host bridge integration
and launchd template are in [Drive and host bridge integration](DRIVE.md).
Refer to that guide for exact flag syntax, defaults and bridge path semantics;
this runbook focuses on operational boundaries, pool policy and recovery.

The existing daemon, resource pools and Leader are separate systems. Their
status does not prove a driver is healthy. See [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md),
[resource pools](RESOURCE-POOLS.md) and the
[source agent operations guide](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/AGENT-OPERATIONS.md#stop-and-pause)
for implemented controls. Driver operation must retain enrollment, authority,
quota, sandbox, review and protected merge gates. A successful job does not
by itself authorize publication or establish acceptance.

## Start and stop

Before the first start, record the installed revision, owner, dispatch scope,
approved budget, existing scheduler, state directory, memguard sentinel path,
pool limits and recovery contact. Obtain paths and supported options from the
landed implementation and its help, rather than guessing a home directory path.
Commission with fixture work before permitting real dispatch or provider costs.

| Action | Procedure |
| --- | --- |
| Start | `phm drive`. Check help and authority first. See [Drive and host bridge integration](DRIVE.md) for flags, bridge path defaults and publisher. Start one instance for the chosen state directory and scope. Verify fresh state and one owned fixture job before enabling more capacity. |
| Pause admissions | Create the memguard `PAUSE` file at the documented path (`--pause-file`; default `~/.ashlr-runs/PAUSE`). Verify admissions cease; record whether running jobs drain or are interrupted. |
| Stop | `phm drive stop` is available. It stops admissions, reconciles running work and reports quiescence before another scheduler takes ownership. See [Drive and host bridge integration](DRIVE.md) for shutdown signal and timeout details. |
| Inspect | `phm drive --once --dry-run` returns a plan without acquiring ownership. See [Drive and host bridge integration](DRIVE.md) for the normalized CLI report schema with version, timestamp, pool counts and admission state. |

Do not infer that closing a terminal stops child work, that deleting a PID file
releases ownership, or that a process exit proves all jobs stopped. Before a
restart, verify the old controller and its children are quiescent and reconcile
any external sessions. If graceful shutdown fails, use the recovery procedure
below and the implementation's documented supervisor controls. No supervisor or
signal recipe is established in this checkout.

## Memguard PAUSE file

The driver checks the memguard `PAUSE` sentinel before admission,
including immediately before launch. The sentinel is an admission hold, not
proof that active workers were terminated and not a substitute for global Stop.
The default convention is `~/.ashlr-runs/PAUSE`, configurable with
`--pause-file`. Unreadable control files and dangling symlinks hold admission.
The bridge must independently check the actual host controls inside its
admission transaction; the CLI check cannot close that race by itself. See
[Drive and host bridge integration](DRIVE.md) for the PAUSE contract and
launch hold semantics.

On a pause, record the cause and time, inspect memory pressure and running jobs,
and reduce concurrency or drain work. Leave a memguard-owned sentinel in place
while pressure persists. Establish who owns removal and whether memguard will
recreate it before clearing it. Resume only after pressure is healthy, ownership
is reconciled and limits are safe. Verify a fresh status and a single admission
before widening capacity. Do not clear unrelated daemon pause or global Stop
markers to resolve a driver pause. Exact path, file format, thresholds, polling
latency and automatic resume policy remain implementation prerequisites.

## Pool floors and ceilings

**Planned policy:** a pool floor is a desired minimum of useful concurrent work
when eligible tasks and safe capacity exist. A ceiling is a hard admission cap.
Neither reserves provider capacity nor authorizes spending. Define the unit
explicitly: running jobs, available seats and tokens are different quantities.

Record each pool's floor, ceiling, active count, eligible queue depth, account
scope and budget. Require nonnegative integer limits with floor no greater than
ceiling. Use a zero ceiling to disable admissions only after that behavior has
been implemented and tested. No configuration keys or numeric defaults are
established here.

Memory holds, Stop, authority, quota and account availability take precedence
over a floor. Never launch duplicate or ineligible work merely to meet a floor.
Count recovered and externally running jobs against the ceiling before filling
new slots. Lowering a ceiling below active work should hold new admissions;
termination policy must be explicit. Raise one pool at a time and observe
memory, queue age, failure rate and accepted outcomes before raising another.

## Reading status.json and jobs.jsonl

**Planned artifacts:** these filenames are intended driver observations, not
existing files with a stable schema. Do not confuse similarly named files from
other subsystems with driver evidence. Implementation must document the state
directory, schema version, atomic snapshot behavior, event durability and
retention before cutover. Never copy raw logs into public reports without
checking for private task content or credentials.

| Artifact | Evidence required before it can support operation |
| --- | --- |
| `status.json` | Schema/revision, controller identity, last update time, admission state and pause reason, per-pool limits/counts, and running job identities. Check freshness against the documented heartbeat interval and controller liveness. A readable stale snapshot is not health. |
| `jobs.jsonl` | One JSON event per line with stable job and attempt identities, pool, event time, transition, outcome and evidence references. Correlate launch, progress and terminal events by identity; count attempts separately from accepted tasks. |

These are required meanings, not field names or sample payloads. Do not build
queries against invented keys. Compare snapshot counts with event history and
actual worker sessions. Missing events, an incomplete final line, invalid JSON,
unknown versions or conflicting terminal outcomes require reconciliation, not a
healthy verdict. Preserve original files and capture a diagnostic copy before
repair. Never truncate the journal, forge a completion or edit a snapshot to
make a job disappear. Any eventual parser must distinguish a partial final write
from corrupt earlier records.

## Recovery from a stuck job

1. Hold admissions using the documented driver pause control once implemented.
   Record the job and attempt IDs, pool, controller, worktree, external session,
   last heartbeat, last progress and timeout policy. Preserve state and logs.
2. Distinguish slow work from a dead controller, a disconnected provider or an
   approval wait. Compare journal events, snapshot freshness and actual worker
   liveness. Elapsed time alone does not prove failure.
3. Request cancellation through the owning runtime's documented control. Verify
   the worker and any external session stopped. If cancellation is uncertain,
   keep the job quarantined and capacity occupied; do not launch a replacement.
4. Inspect the worktree and any existing proposal or PR. Preserve useful changes
   and evidence without committing, publishing or deleting operator data as a
   recovery shortcut. Reconcile external effects before retrying.
5. Use an implemented reconciliation path to record the terminal disposition.
   **Planned:** driver retry and reconciliation commands have no CLI syntax in
   this checkout. Do not hand-edit the journal or invent a retry invocation.
6. After confirmed termination, retry only with explicit attempt identity and
   duplicate-effect checks. Validate one recovered job, ceiling accounting and
   fresh observations before releasing the admission hold.

Escalate unresolved ownership, corrupt state, unconfirmed cancellation or repeated
failures to the operator with evidence. Keep admissions held for the affected
scope. A controller restart must not silently requeue every apparently running
job.

## Parallel run, then cutover

**Planned rollout:** parallel observation must not mean two schedulers dispatch
the same tasks or share one writable state directory.

1. Inventory the incumbent scheduler, queue claims, in-flight work, account
   limits and stop procedure. Name a cutover owner and rollback conditions.
2. Run the driver in a future implemented observation-only mode against recorded
   inputs or fixtures. No shadow-mode flag exists yet. Compare proposed routing,
   pool counts, pause behavior and stuck-job detection with incumbent decisions.
3. If live parallel validation is authorized, partition tasks and account
   capacity explicitly, use separate state directories and enforce exclusive
   claims. Account for the combined ceiling and budget across both schedulers.
   Otherwise keep the driver observation-only until cutover.
4. Require tested Stop/pause, restart reconciliation, ceiling enforcement,
   durable events, stale-status detection and cancellation before cutover.
   Capture fixture results and an agreed observation window with no duplicate
   dispatch or unexplained state differences.
5. Hold new admissions on both sides, drain or explicitly reconcile incumbent
   jobs, and verify no ambiguous claims remain. Transfer ownership once. Start
   the driver at a small approved ceiling and verify one complete job with
   independent acceptance evidence before widening capacity.
6. Roll back for duplicate claims, ignored holds, unsafe memory pressure,
   unexplained accounting or lost observations. Hold driver admissions, reconcile
   its active work, then restore incumbent ownership only after exclusivity is
   established. Retain both evidence histories for review.

Do not disable required CI, review or merge protections for cutover. The external
router's `publish.sh` handoff is outside this driver interface and is not present
in this checkout; it is not a driver command or a package release instruction.

## Cloud task error forwarding

**Planned contract:** cloud tasks (branch namespace `ashlr-cloud/`) deliver work
through the existing PR triage path. When the budget API, activity API, or the
worker session returns structured 503 errors with `{ code, error }` bodies, the
driver must forward them into the task report rather than swallowing them into a
generic failure. Web consumers (`BudgetControl`, `useActivity`) already surface
`ApiError.detail`: the driver should route the same structured detail through the
task's `report.risks` and `stateReason` fields so the operator can distinguish a
capacity hold from a true worker fault.

When a cloud task branch push fails with a remote refusal (protected branch,
missing credentials, or a conflicting ref), the driver must record the refusal
as a terminal disposition rather than retrying blindly. The branch name format
`ashlr-cloud/<taskId>` is the authority for the task-to-branch mapping; never
rewrite it or push to the task's `baseBranch`. The existing `pr-actions.ts`
land/close/update-branch path handles the branch after the driver launches the
worker; the driver's responsibility ends at publication.

### Strategic focus tiers

The whole inventory matters, but it should not receive equal attention. Ashlr wins by making a small core spine outrageously good, then using support repos only when they unblock that spine.

| Tier | Repos | Operating directive |
|---|---|---|
| **Core fleet spine** | ashlr-hub, phantom-secrets, ashlr-plugin, binshield, ashlr-md, ashlr-stack, ashlr-pulse, ashlrcode, ashlr-workbench, lexicon, locus | Keep these moving first. They are the product, execution harness, trust layer, review surface, observability plane, secrets layer, and infra layer that make the autonomous engineering fleet useful. |
| **Core-adjacent candidate** | ashlr-mux | Not present in the local 23-repo inventory yet. Track as cofounder-owned and evaluate as core once the repo is available locally or via GitHub. |
| **Force multipliers** | @ashlr/core-efficiency, morphkit, webfetch, prompt-trackr | Develop when they compound the core fleet: cheaper context, product-building leverage, retrieval/building blocks, or prompt-quality feedback. |
| **Supporting substrate + distribution** | ashlr-auth, ashlr-cli-common, ashlr-config, ashlr-cost, ashlr-mcp-kit, homebrew-ashlr, homebrew-phantom, openclaw-setup | Maintain quality, package boundaries, and distribution. Do not let these pull focus from the core spine unless they are blocking it. |

## The composition flywheel — who provides / consumes what

ashlr-hub is the **conductor**. It enrolls repos' backlogs, dispatches sandboxed agent swarms across multiple backends, and deposits proposal-only diffs into a human-gated Approval Inbox. Everything else either feeds the fleet a capability or is a product the fleet can build. The flywheel: the fleet uses its own ecosystem to make itself cheaper, safer, and more capable, then ships more of the ecosystem.

```
                          ashlr-hub  (conductor: daemon/loop/goal/fleet/inbox)
                              |  consumes capabilities, deposits proposals
        ┌──────────────┬──────┴────────┬─────────────────┬───────────────────┐
   Tier 1 (fix self)  Tier 2 (observe)  Tier 3 (build)   tool layer          substrate
   phantom-secrets    ashlr-pulse       webfetch         ashlr-plugin        @ashlr/core-efficiency
   ashlrcode/workbench stack             morphkit         (40 MCP tools)      (snipCompact/genome/budget)
   core-efficiency    prompt-trackr     ashlr-md
   binshield
```

### Provider → consumer edges (the load-bearing compositions)

| Provider | Provides | Consumed by | Edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| **@ashlr/core-efficiency** | snipCompact / autoCompact / genome RAG / provider budgets / token counting | ashlr-plugin, ashlrcode | The compression substrate under the whole tool layer |
| **ashlr-plugin** | 40 `ashlr__*` MCP tools + genome scribe | every host agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor), ashlr-workbench, ashlr-hub sandboxes | The token-efficient tool surface the fleet routes work through |
| **ashlrcode / ashlr-workbench** | full executor agents (45 tools / 4 wired OSS agents) | ashlr-hub fleet (executor backend) | Real local muscle instead of raw `runGoal` |
| **phantom-secrets** | real API-key injection at the network edge; 25 `phantom_*` MCP tools | ashlr-hub daemon+sandboxes, ashlr-stack (hard dep) | Real secrets never enter config/logs/LLM context |
| **binshield** | dependency-safety scan API + GitHub Action + SARIF | ashlr-hub trust gate | Kills blind dep-bumps; gates autonomous dep work |
| **ashlr-pulse** | OTLP GenAI-span ingest + Fleet Oversight control plane | ashlr-hub (emits telemetry), ashlr-plugin, all coding agents | The fleet's live mission-control dashboard + audit trail |
| **ashlr-stack** | one-command provisioning of 43 providers; 19 `stack_*` MCP tools | ashlr-hub (provisions infra for products it builds) | Wires a downstream project's whole backend |
| **prompt-trackr** | prompt-quality scoring (AES, 6 dims) + SDK/API | ashlr-hub self-improvement loop | Score + iterate the fleet's own prompts |
| **webfetch / morphkit / ashlr-md** | license-first image search / web→iOS / Markdown review surface | ashlr-hub product builds | Tier-3 building blocks for products the fleet creates |

### Composition bets (prioritized)

**Tier 1 — the fleet uses its own ecosystem to fix its own weaknesses:**
1. **phantom → fleet auth.** Inject real engine/API keys into the daemon + sandboxes; phantom tokens stay safe in config/logs/git. Fixes auth-in-daemon directly.
2. **ashlrcode / workbench → executor backend.** Dispatch fleet work to `ac` (45 tools, worktree isolation, real test loop) or the workbench's local-agent pool. Fixes local-execution quality.
3. **core-efficiency / plugin → the fleet's own token cost.** Run strategist/judge/invent prompts through snipCompact + genome + cacheBreakpoints. Slashes burn.
4. **binshield → dep-safety gate.** Scan every proposed dependency change before merge; risk feeds the trust gate.

**Tier 2 — observability + provisioning:** 5. **pulse → fleet telemetry.** 6. **stack → provisioning.** 7. **prompt-trackr → self-improvement.**

**Tier 3 — product-building blocks:** 8. **webfetch + morphkit + ashlr-md** as composable capabilities for products the fleet creates.

## Detailed per-repo capability profiles

These profiles are the higher-confidence, manually expanded capability map for 12 repos. The current inventory above and `ecosystem-index.json` are the count source of truth until the remaining repos get full profiles.

### ashlr-hub — *the conductor*
- **Purpose:** Autonomous engineering fleet (orchestrator at the center of the 23-repo platform): a single Node binary that scans enrolled repos' backlogs, dispatches sandboxed agent swarms across multiple backends, and deposits proposal-only diffs into a human-gated Approval Inbox: proposal-only, sandboxed, gated by model-trust tier. Also a local command center (project index, MCP gateway, spend tracking, ad-hoc run/swarm).
- **Stack:** TypeScript (ESM) on Node >=22.15. Build `tsc` → `dist/` + copy-assets; optional SEA binary. Vitest, ESLint 9. Zero runtime deps except `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`. Sub-surfaces: Raycast extension, Tauri desktop app, terminal TUI.
- **Status:** active / best-in-class-track. Published as `@ashlr/hub` (3.0.1). v1–v5 (M1–M55) shipped; v6 Verification-First (M140+) in progress. 367 adversarial test files, 10 named safety invariants each proven by a test.
- **Key modules:** `src/cli/index.ts` (68KB ~70-case router); `src/api/{index,core,plugin,types}.ts` (public npm surface — `applyProposal` deliberately NOT exported); `src/core/types.ts` (155KB); `src/core/config.ts` (`~/.ashlr/config.json`); `src/core/daemon/loop.ts` (66KB operator loop); `src/core/run/orchestrator.ts` (96KB) + run/router + sandboxed-engine + sandbox/{worktree,confine,policy}; `src/core/swarm/{runner,gate,sign,rollback}`; `src/core/inbox/{store,merge,apply}` (merge 69KB); `src/core/fleet/` (28 files: manager/judge, router, quota, self-improve, regression-sentinel, red-team, taste-critic); `src/core/foundry/provenance.ts`; `src/core/genome/`; `src/core/goals/+vision/+strategy/`; `src/core/ecosystem/map.ts`; `src/core/integrations/`; `src/core/web/` (Mission Control 127.0.0.1:7777); `src/core/plugins/`; `bin/ashlr`; `schema/config.schema.json`.
- **Public API:** CLI `ashlr` (~70 commands: setup, daemon, loop, goal(s), inbox, swarm, run, fleet, manager, vision, invent, comms, serve, eval, verify-safety, doctor, mcp, sandbox gc, tui, …); npm `@ashlr/hub` read-heavy API (loadConfig, loadIndex, buildOrientation, recall, listRuns/Swarms, estimateRun, listProposals/createProposal/pendingCount — **apply NOT exported**, callNativeTool, buildSnapshot); subpaths `/core`, `/types`, `/plugin`; native MCP tool registry + MCP gateway; local HTTP Mission Control at 127.0.0.1:7777; on-disk `~/.ashlr/` contract.
- **Entry / build / test:** `bin/ashlr` → `dist/cli/index.js`; dev `npm run dev` (tsx); build `npm run build`; SEA `npm run build:binary`; test `npm run test` / `npm run test:serial`; typecheck `npm run typecheck`; lint `npm run lint`; install from source `./install.sh`.
- **Composition:** CENTER. Consumes phantom (auth), ashlrcode/workbench (executors), core-efficiency/plugin (token cost), binshield (dep gate), pulse (telemetry), stack (provisioning), prompt-trackr (prompt self-improvement), webfetch/morphkit/ashlr-md (build blocks). Provides `@ashlr/hub` + `ashlr` CLI, native MCP registry + gateway, Approval Inbox / proposal contract, `~/.ashlr/` shared state. Integrates external backends as one-config engines (Ollama/LM Studio, Claude Code CLI, Codex CLI, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs) + GitHub/Vercel/Telegram/iMessage/Raycast/Tauri.
- **Conventions:** ESM with explicit `.js` import specifiers (NodeNext). Layered: `cli/` thin handlers → `core/<domain>/` logic → `api/` curated re-exports (mutating/merge/apply paths intentionally unexported). All shared-state writes go to `~/.ashlr/`; CLI is sole writer. Tests flat in `test/` with milestone-prefixed names (h1.*, m45.*, m54.*), run serially for release. Safety invariants sacrosanct (never weaken a safety test — blocked by M54). Feature work gated behind `cfg.foundry.*` flags defaulting to safe (off / proposal-only).

### @ashlr/core-efficiency — *the compression substrate*
- **Purpose:** Shared token-efficiency primitive library for AI coding agents: genome RAG (self-evolving project specs), multi-tier context compression, provider-aware budgeting/pricing, accurate token counting, Anthropic prompt-cache helpers. Extracted from ashlrcode so it and ashlr-plugin share one implementation.
- **Stack:** TypeScript (ESNext, strict, source-first `.ts` exports). Runtime Bun >=1.0; Node >=20 after `bun run build`. Sole runtime dep: tiktoken. Optional peer: `@anthropic-ai/sdk`. `bun test`. 3-OS CI.
- **Status:** library — active, v0.3.0, MIT, published. Mature (3-OS CI, 55 test files) but several modules carry far more capability than the README documents.
- **Key modules:** `src/index.ts` (root barrel, aliases genome estimateTokens→estimateTokensManifest); `src/genome/` (24-file genetic loop: manifest, retriever V2/Adaptive/Hierarchical, scribe, fitness, embeddings/quantized-ann/reranker-ensemble/distributed-manifest); `src/compression/` (context.ts: snipCompact, contextCollapse, treeCompact, CompressionTier, CompressorLearner; adaptive/regret-learner/semantic-prefilter); `src/budget/index.ts` (PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMITS, PROVIDER_PRICING, ProviderCostOracle); `src/tokens/index.ts` (estimate + tiktoken countTokensAccurate, recalibration); `src/anthropic/index.ts` (withGenome, cacheBreakpoints, ashlrMcpConfig, CacheOptimizer); `src/session-log/`; `src/local/`; `src/types/index.ts` (Message, LLMSummarizer, ProviderRequest).
- **Public API:** subpath exports `.`, `/genome`, `/compression`, `/budget`, `/tokens`, `/anthropic`, `/session-log`, `/local`. compression: autoCompact, snipCompact, contextCollapse, treeCompact, PromptPriority, selectCompressionTier. budget: getProviderContextLimit, systemPromptBudget, rebalanceBudgetOnSwitch. tokens: estimateTokens*, countTokensAccurate, calibratedEstimate. genome: loadManifest, retrieveSectionsV2/Adaptive/Hierarchical, proposeUpdate/consolidateProposals, measureFitness. anthropic: withGenome, cacheBreakpoints, ashlrMcpConfig.
- **Entry / build / test:** main/module → `./src/index.ts` (no bin — library). Build `bun run build`; test `bun test`; typecheck `bun run typecheck`. Install `bun add @ashlr/core-efficiency`.
- **Composition:** Provides the shared efficiency engine to ashlrcode (CLI-coupled layers stay in ashlrcode) and to ashlr-plugin (anthropic/mcp-config.ts auto-detects an installed plugin, emits stdio MCP config). Composes-with `@anthropic-ai/sdk` + claude-agent-sdk as optional peers (never imported directly). Provider-agnostic via the minimal LLMSummarizer `{stream()}` contract. Consumes tiktoken (sole runtime dep) with chars/4 fallback.
- **Conventions:** ESM with explicit `.ts` import extensions; subpath imports preferred over root barrel. Per-file star re-export barrels. Strict TS (noUncheckedIndexedAccess). Tests in top-level `__tests__/*.test.ts` (bun:test). Behavior-preservation contract: provider/budget logic mirrors ashlrcode so the same tests pass against either consumer. Best-effort I/O (catch-and-degrade). Provider-agnostic — depend on LLMSummarizer, not concrete clients.

### ashlr-plugin — *makes every agent cheaper*
- **Purpose:** Multi-host (Claude Code + Codex) token-efficiency layer. 40 MCP tools replacing high-volume Read/Grep/Edit/Bash with compact summarized equivalents (mean −57% tokens), plus 34 slash commands, lifecycle hooks, a genome scribe loop, and a per-session savings ledger.
- **Stack:** TypeScript on Bun >=1.3 (ESM); `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`; tree-sitter (AST edits); postgres + SQLite; optional onnxruntime-node. Sub-packages: server/ (Bun HTTP, Railway/Docker), site/ (Next.js/Vercel), vscode/ (esbuild).
- **Status:** active / best-in-class-track — v1.36.0, 3-OS CI, 202 test files, paid Pro/Team tiers live.
- **Key modules:** `servers/_router.ts` (single long-lived MCP stdio process hosting all 40 tools); `_router-handlers.ts`; `_tool-base.ts` (registry + crash-isolated dispatch); `*-server.ts`/`*-server-handlers.ts` pairs; `_ast-refactor/` (tree-sitter rename/extract); `_llm-providers/` (Haiku default, ONNX/local/cloud Grok); `_genome-*.ts`; `_stats*.ts`/`_accounting.ts`; `hooks/`; `scripts/cli.ts` (read-only stats/codex CLI); `commands/*.md` (34 incl. goal.md/loop.md); `skills/`, `agents/`; host manifests; server/ + site/ + vscode/.
- **Public API:** 40 `ashlr__*` MCP tools (read, grep, edit, edit_structural, multi_edit, savings, bash[_start/_tail/_stop/_list], sql, http, webfetch, logs, diff, diff_semantic, test, tree, glob, ls, orient, genome_propose/_consolidate/_status, issue[_create/_close], pr[_comment/_approve], ask); `ashlr` CLI (stats, tools, mcp, codex-*, genome-refresh); 34 slash commands; 11 skills; 3 subagents; Pro cloud endpoints (/v1/stats/aggregate, /llm/summarize, genome deltas, billing).
- **Entry / build / test:** MCP router `bun run servers/_router.ts`; test `bun test __tests__`; full `bun run check`; typecheck `bunx tsc --noEmit`; benchmark `scripts/run-benchmark.ts`; bins `ashlr`→cli.ts, `ashlr-mcp`→ashlr-mcp.ts.
- **Composition:** Consumes `@ashlr/core-efficiency` (#v0.3.0) for compression + genome primitives. Provides the 40 MCP tools + genome to host agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cline, Cursor, Goose) — the tool layer the ecosystem's agents use. `/goal` and `/loop` shell out to an external fleet conductor CLI that lives in **ashlr-hub** (this repo supplies the sandboxed MCP tool surface the hub routes work through). Pro features call api.ashlr.ai (its own server/). Relates to ashlr-pulse as a tool/telemetry provider.
- **Conventions:** Bun-first; ESM only; `_`-prefix = shared/internal, unprefixed `*-server.ts` = tool entry; every tool = `<name>-server.ts` + `<name>-server-handlers.ts` registered via side-effect import; tools namespaced `ashlr__<tool>`; env-var feature flags (ASHLR_*); tests in `__tests__/`; version synced via scripts; MIT, opt-in privacy-preserving telemetry (SHA-256 session ids, no file content sent).

### ashlrcode (`ac`) — *a full executor in a box*
- **Purpose:** Open-source multi-provider AI coding agent for the terminal — a Claude Code alternative running streaming LLM conversations with tool use, default routed to xAI Grok with auto-failover to Anthropic/OpenAI/DeepSeek/Groq/Ollama. Extensible, provider-agnostic, no vendor lock-in (tools, skills, MCP, KAIROS/autopilot, self-evolving genome).
- **Stack:** TypeScript on Bun (ESM, strict, no build step — `.ts` executed directly; `bun build --compile` for distribution). UI via Ink + chalk. SDKs: `@anthropic-ai/sdk` + openai-compatible router. Biome, bun test. Optional puppeteer.
- **Status:** active — v2.1.0, ~689 tests, 130+ files; MIT, publish-ready but pre-1.x in spirit; active experimental subsystems + known doc-drift + a broken bin entry.
- **Key modules:** `src/cli.ts` (entry: providers, tool registry, sessions, plan mode); `src/repl.tsx` (Ink UI); `src/agent/` (64 files: loop.ts streaming+dispatch, context.ts 3-tier compression, sub-agent, coordinator multi-agent waves, kairos autonomous heartbeat, dream, speculation*, surgical-*); `src/tools/` (39 files, 45+ tools, registry.ts Tool interface + pipeline); `src/providers/` (router failover, cost-tracker shim over @ashlr/cost); `src/genome/` (11 files); `src/commands/` (16 files centralized registry); `src/mcp/`; `src/cmux/`; `src/bridge/` (HTTP /api); `src/config/`; `src/skills/`; `src/persistence/`; `src/autopilot/`.
- **Public API:** CLI `ac` (REPL / single-shot / --continue / --resume / --migrate); 45+ agent tools (Read/Write/Edit/Bash/WebFetch/Agent/Task*/Memory*/EnterWorktree/LSP/Snip/mcp__<server>__<tool>); 42+ slash commands (/autopilot /kairos /coordinate /verify /genome /bridge …); HTTP bridge API (GET /api/status, POST /api/submit, GET /api/history|health); Tool interface extension point; skill markdown format; MCP config in `~/.ashlrcode/settings.json`.

Provides the standalone `ac`/`ashlrcode` terminal agent — sibling to ashlr-plugin + ashlr-workbench; an executor backend the hub fleet dispatches to. Consumes `@anthropic-ai/sdk` + openai (routes xAI/DeepSeek/Groq/Ollama). Composes-with cmux (JSON-RPC) + any MCP server. Imports/migrates from Claude Code (`ac --migrate`). Exposes an HTTP bridge for hub/pulse orchestration.
- **Conventions:** Bun-first TS (ESM, strict, NO build step; explicit `.ts` import extensions). Biome. Every tool implements the Tool interface (name/prompt/inputSchema/isReadOnly/.../call) registered in `src/cli.ts`. Commands in centralized registry (not inline switches).
