# Memory foundation

The source-only memory foundation selects bounded, cited project evidence from a
supplied snapshot. It is a pure local kernel: no store, HTTP route, session
injection, recall worker, model call, filesystem access or execution grant is
wired to it. It does not migrate the existing shared `MEMORY.md`, team context,
lessons or genome stores.

Use [Offline memory evaluations](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/MEMORY-EVALUATION.md)
for the independent synthetic fixtures and measurement limits. Source implementation and offline
contract results do not establish an activated memory service or installed
release acceptance.

## Pure source interface

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/core/memory/types.ts` | Closed version-1 fact, source, snapshot, query, exclusion and pack contracts |
| `src/core/memory/validate.ts` | Exact data shapes, byte/date/control limits, shared-pattern refusal, and a detached recursively frozen snapshot |
| `src/core/memory/scope.ts` | Exact project, owner and audience admission; exact original scope for lifecycle links |
| `src/core/memory/temporal.ts` | Review, valid-time, knowledge-time, lineage, revocation, conflict and tombstone eligibility |
| `src/core/memory/pack.ts` | Deterministic lexical selection, complete quoted evidence, byte limits and receipts |

`buildMemoryContextPack(snapshot, query)` is the supported composition entry
point. It validates unknown inputs, copies the query and freezes a detached
snapshot before selection. Caller changes cannot alter that detached snapshot. To prepare once for several
queries, call `immutableMemorySnapshot(raw)` and pass its returned snapshot to
`buildMemoryContextPack`. The actual detached JSON copy is validated again before freezing. Only
factory-created recursively frozen copies qualify
for reuse, through module-private weak membership; caller-frozen objects or
claimed preparation fields do not bypass validation. Every pack still reruns
query validation, scope, time, lineage, lifecycle, ranking and budget checks.
Preparation caches no query result, observes no live store, and makes no claim
that a supplied snapshot is fresh.
The lower-level temporal projector requires an already validated snapshot; it
is not a storage or authentication boundary.

A fact event identifies an immutable event, logical fact and positive revision;
its project, owner and audience; a subject and slot; text and source references;
observed, effective, recorded and review times; review decision; and explicit
supersession, derivation or deletion links. Every event declares
`authority: false`. Source references contain an ID, a claimed prefixed SHA-256
digest, locator, quotation and optional observation date. Dates are strict UTC
ISO strings with milliseconds; unknown observation dates are `null`.

An approved label requires review metadata. It records a caller-supplied review
decision, not proof of reviewer identity, source authenticity or factual truth.
A claimed source digest is not recomputed against an original archive by this
kernel. IDs, snapshot revision and watermark are supplied by the caller; they
are not signed receipts or a verified live-store revision.

## Scope and time

The caller must supply admitted canonical project IDs and authenticated owner
and audience identities through a future trusted adapter. This kernel compares
those opaque IDs exactly. It does not resolve paths, aliases or same-basename
projects, authenticate the caller, infer personal consent, or fall back to a
global collection. A relevant-looking foreign project or audience is excluded
before lexical ranking. Supersession and deletion cannot widen the target's
original project, owner or audience set.

The two temporal axes answer different questions:

- `time: { mode: 'current', at }` or `{ mode: 'asOf', at }` supplies the
  **validity time**. The caller chooses the clock; no implicit current time is
  read. `validFrom` is inclusive and `validUntil` exclusive. Unknown validity
  is ineligible.
- `knownAt` supplies the **knowledge cutoff**. `null` uses the snapshot's
  `recordedThrough` watermark. Facts recorded after this cutoff are excluded;
  review and observation dates cannot exceed the event's recorded date. A
  cutoff after the supplied watermark is refused.

A historical validity query with the current knowledge cutoff may use a later
import to reconstruct an earlier period. To ask what was known then, set
`knownAt` explicitly as well. Import arrival order alone never chooses a winner.
The receipt records both axes and the supplied watermark; none proves live
freshness.

## Revisions, withdrawal and deletion

Only applicable approved facts can enter a pack. Proposed or disputed records
cannot retire an approved predecessor. Conflicting visible claims in one slot,
unlinked concurrent revisions, missing or invalid lineage, and lineage cycles
fail closed. A derived claim is ineligible when any required parent is
ineligible, including a superseded, expired, conflicted or deleted parent.

Updates retain earlier events and append a higher reviewed revision with
explicit valid-time supersession links. A replacement's expiry or deletion does
not automatically restore its obsolete predecessor. An admitted, effective
replacement whose own lineage is invalid or cyclic does not restore it either:
its predecessors in the same scope and slot are excluded as `conflict`.

A `withdrawn` fact event is an append-only durable reviewed revocation revision,
with a review decision, review date and known effective `validFrom`. It never
enters a pack. Once effective and known, it retires explicit predecessors and
older revisions of the same fact within the same project and owner, whenever
the withdrawal is visible to the querying audience, even if its audience list
differs from the fact's. Preserve the
prior approved events to reconstruct their earlier approved intervals; changing
a previous event's label in place loses that history. Equal-revision approval
and withdrawal decisions conflict and select neither. A genuinely higher
reviewed approval can express a later renewal. A withdrawn tombstone is refused.

Approved tombstones cover their explicit target event IDs and dependent
`derivedFrom` lineage within the exact admitted scope. Each target is applied
independently: a missing, unreviewed or foreign target is skipped and does not
void the deletion of the others. Current recorded deletion
decisions prevent those events from returning through historical validity or
knowledge queries. This is selection invalidation over the supplied snapshot,
not physical erasure. It does not erase original files, backups, provider
contexts or external copies, and does not prevent a new unrelated ID from being
reimported. A future import/store adapter must retain lineage and enforce its
own idempotency and deletion coverage; no broader resurrection guarantee is
claimed.

## Limits and output

| Boundary | Hard cap |
| --- | --- |
| Snapshot | 4,096 events; 32MiB exact canonical JSON bytes |
| Fact text | 16KiB UTF8 bytes |
| Source references | 1–8 per event; quotation 4KiB; locator 256 bytes |
| Lifecycle links | 32 per link array |
| Audiences | 1–32 unique IDs |
| Query text | 4KiB |
| Evidence pack | 256-byte minimum requested budget; 128KiB maximum; 1–64 facts |

Opaque IDs are bounded to 128 characters. Invalid shapes, extra fields,
accessors, sparse or custom arrays, unsupported authority fields, malformed
Unicode, unsafe controls, duplicate event IDs and over-cap inputs are refused.
Snapshot bytes are counted incrementally before allocating a whole over-cap
canonical encoding.

The existing pure `scrubSecrets` and `redactGenericHomePaths` patterns screen
free text and opaque IDs. If screening would change a value, the kernel never
silently rewrites it into the pack. A query, ID or key that fails screening
refuses the whole call. A fact event whose text, source locator or quote fails
is withheld on its own as `screened`, and the rest of the snapshot is still
served. The screened event keeps its lineage effects: it still supersedes its
predecessor and its tombstones still delete, it never contests a slot, and facts
derived from it are withheld. When it touches the query, the pack says how many
facts were withheld for credential-shaped text or a private path.
This shared screening is not exhaustive private-data detection. A successful
pack says `contentSafety: 'screened-with-shared-patterns'`, not that all content
is safe to publish or send to a provider.

After eligibility checks, ranking counts unique query terms that match the
subject, slot and text. Common function words (`the`, `how`, `what` ...) are
ignored unless the query has nothing else, and ASCII words are folded by a small
fixed suffix list, so `builds`, `building` and `build` match. Other scripts are
compared exactly. An empty query gives each eligible event equal score. Ties go
to the event whose matched terms are rarer among eligible facts, then to more
exact-word matches, then to event ID order. A fixed vocabulary of
engineering synonym groups (`src/core/memory/vocabulary.ts`) lets `compile`
match build and `credentials` match secrets; there is no model or embedding,
so wording outside those groups still has to share a stem. Each fact is
canonical JSON whose citations are references: source ID and digest, plus the
quote only when it differs from the fact text. The complete source records stay
on `items[].sourceRefs`. Facts are placed inside a fixed evidence boundary, with angle brackets escaped so quoted text
cannot close that boundary. The view (time mode, time, knowledge cutoff) and the
review disclaimer are stated once on the boundary tag rather than in every fact.
The tag also declares `omitted="observedAt=validFrom validUntil=null"`: a fact
leaves out `observedAt` when it equals `validFrom` and `validUntil` when it is
null, and states either field whenever it differs.
Quoted instructions remain data; `authority: false` never grants tool use,
deployment or account access.

When the query touches a slot whose claims were withheld as a `conflict` or
`revision-conflict`, the pack adds one line naming the subject, slot and number
of withheld claims, and asks the reader to check before relying on it. The
contested text itself never appears. These lines count toward the byte budget;
if one does not fit, the receipt records `conflict-notice-budget`.

### Facts written by independent agents

Agents write memory without coordinating. They pick their own subject and slot
keys, restate each other, cite weak evidence and leave facts behind when code
changes. The pack applies three rules after ranking:

- **Checkable evidence first.** A source is checkable when its locator starts
  with `file:`, `commit:` or `command-output:` and its quote is more than the
  fact restated. Any other source is unverified, such as `chat:`,
  `inference:` or a self-quote. Among relevant facts, checkable ones rank
  first. An unverified fact is withheld as `weaker-evidence` when a checkable
  fact scores at least as well, and it is still served when nothing checkable
  does.
- **One copy of a fact.** A candidate is withheld as `duplicate` of an
  already selected fact in two cases. Either both cite the same source
  (locator and digest) and share a topic stem, or at least half of the smaller
  fact's topic stems appear in the other and one fact's value tokens (numbers,
  versions, paths, dotted or slashed identifiers) are a subset of the other's.
- **Changed sources.** `buildMemoryContextPack(snapshot, query, { changedSourceIds })`
  takes the source IDs whose quote the caller no longer finds at their locator.
  Facts citing such a source are withheld as `source-changed`. When any of them
  touch the query, the pack adds one line saying how many were withheld. The
  argument defaults to `{ changedSourceIds: [] }`. Any other shape is refused
  with `invalid-options`. The pack itself reads no files; the caller does the
  check, and `memorySourceQuotePresent(quote, currentLine)` in
  `src/core/memory/source.ts` is the comparison to use. It ignores whitespace
  next to punctuation, runs of spaces and trailing `//`, `#`, `--` or `/* */`
  comments, so reformatting a line does not withhold a true fact. A quote that
  is only a comment is compared as written.

Facts written under different keys connect through their evidence. A fact is
withheld as `source-changed` when a later fact in the snapshot cites the same
`file:` locator with a different quote of the same statement, a `commit:` diff
that removes a line of its quote, or a commit message that names a qualified
identifier from its quote (or its file, when the message also names its topic).
`memoryQuoteRetiredBy` in `src/core/memory/source.ts` makes that comparison.
Chat remarks and an agent's own reasoning never retire a cited quote.

Facts cited from docs (README, CHANGELOG, `docs/`, Markdown), tests, fixtures,
mocks, examples, samples, benchmarks, vendored code or staging/dev config are
secondary sources. One is held back as `weaker-evidence` when both it and a
primary-source fact answer the query, share a topic word and state different
numbers, unless a primary fact states the same numbers or the query names that
kind of source ("staging", "tests", "README").

The byte budget includes all returned evidence text, escaping, framing and
citations. Facts that do not fit are omitted whole with a reason. The receipt
and item metadata are separate bounded outputs, not included in that text
budget. The token estimate is explicitly UTF8 bytes divided by four, rounded
up; it is not an exact model tokenizer count.

Pack status distinguishes `ready` from `none` (no selected eligible evidence;
the text may still carry conflict lines),
`unknown`, `unavailable` and `refused`. An incomplete available snapshot is
unavailable. `none` may reflect irrelevant evidence or budget omissions; inspect
the receipt rather than interpreting it as proof that memory does not exist.
Receipts record scope, policy version, snapshot claims, temporal axes, selected
IDs and finite exclusion reasons for in-scope events. Events outside the
admitted project, owner or audience are neither identified nor counted.
Receipts do not attest execution authority or
replace authentication and output authorization in an eventual adapter.

## Minimal pure example

This TypeScript example uses fictional supplied records, performs no I/O and
makes no model or provider calls. The digest is deliberately a claim placeholder.

```ts
import { buildMemoryContextPack } from './src/core/memory/pack.js';
import type { MemoryFactEvent } from './src/core/memory/types.js';

const at = '2026-10-14T00:00:00.000Z';
const fact: MemoryFactEvent = {
  schemaVersion: 1, eventId: 'event_build_1', factId: 'fact_build', revision: 1,
  kind: 'fact', projectId: 'project_example', ownerId: 'owner_example',
  audienceIds: ['team_example'], subjectKey: 'build', slotKey: 'command',
  text: 'The project build command is npm run build.',
  sourceRefs: [{
    id: 'source_example', digest: 'sha256_' + 'a'.repeat(64), locator: 'line:1',
    quote: 'npm run build', observedAt: at,
  }],
  observedAt: at, validFrom: at, validUntil: null, recordedAt: at,
  reviewState: 'approved', reviewedAt: at, reviewerDecisionId: 'review_example',
  supersedes: [], derivedFrom: [], tombstones: [], authority: false,
};
const pack = buildMemoryContextPack({
  schemaVersion: 1, snapshotId: 'snapshot_example', revision: 1,
  recordedThrough: at, sourceState: 'available', complete: true,
  events: [fact], authority: false,
}, {
  schemaVersion: 1, projectId: 'project_example', ownerId: 'owner_example',
  audienceId: 'team_example', time: { mode: 'current', at }, knownAt: null,
  query: 'build command', maxBytes: 6144, maxFacts: 8, authority: false,
});
// pack.status === 'ready'; selectedEventIds === ['event_build_1'].
// This is an evidence result, not an agent instruction or execution permit.
```

Run the source-only regressions from a repository checkout with dependencies
already installed:

```sh
npm run test:ci -- --maxWorkers=1 --fileParallelism=false test/memory-foundation.test.ts
```

A structured persistence adapter, live authorization, actual source integrity,
concurrent append protocol, session integration and bounded active recall remain
future work. See the offline evaluation guide for what is and is not measured
before increasing automation.

# Durable memory

`phm memory` keeps Mason's preferences, doctrine and facts so the chief of staff
(COS) intake can start every task with them. Each entry is one markdown file in
`~/.phantom/memory/`, written with owner-only permissions.

- `preference`: how Mason likes work done ("keep replies short").
- `doctrine`: rules that hold across projects ("never force-push").
- `fact`: stable background ("the release branch is master").

```sh
phm memory add "Keep replies short and direct" --kind preference --source chat --json
phm memory add "Outbound sends are draft then approve" --kind doctrine --json
phm memory list --kind doctrine --json
phm memory search outbound --json
phm memory forget pref-1a2b3c4d5e --json
```

`add` returns the entry id. Adding identical text again refreshes `updated`
instead of creating a duplicate. `search` matches every term, ignoring case,
across id, kind, source and text.

## File format

```markdown
---
id: pref-1a2b3c4d5e
kind: preference
source: chat
updated: 2026-11-04T12:00:00.000Z
---
Keep replies short and direct
```

Text is limited to 2000 characters. Files that are malformed, have an id that
does not match the file name, or contain a secret shape are ignored on read.

## Secrets

Entries are refused when they match the secret-shape scan used by connector
profiles (`scrubSecrets` plus the provider token shapes). The error never echoes
the rejected text. Store credentials in Phantom Secrets and refer to them by
binding name only, never by value.

## For the COS intake

`memoryContext({ home?, maxChars? })` in `src/core/cos/memory.ts` is read-only.
It returns a prompt block listing doctrine first, then preferences, then facts
(newest first within each kind), cut off at `maxChars` (default 4000). It returns
an empty string when nothing is stored or the directory is unreadable.


<!-- page: METRICS-ROUTER-FEED -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/METRICS-ROUTER-FEED.md

# Local router metrics feed

```sh
phm metrics ingest --jobs ./jobs.jsonl --status ./status.json --json
```

The command reads two explicit local files and prints JSON to stdout. It never
contacts a provider, GitHub, a URL or a model, writes a store, discovers a home
directory, or dispatches work. `--json` is optional because output is always
JSON. Exit 0 means a valid report or help; exit 2 means bad arguments or refused
input. Input errors produce a controlled diagnostic on stderr, without raw
records or paths. No dependencies or credentials are added.

## Input schema version 1

This is a new, explicit interchange schema. It does not guess the shape of an
unrelated daemon `status.json` or import arbitrary queue logs. Producers must
export the following snapshots. Each UTF-8 JSONL record describes one job:

```json
{"schemaVersion":1,"id":"RQ-example","lane":"codex-cmp","tier":"frontier","outcome":"running","tokens":120,"startedAt":"2026-10-25T10:00:00.000Z"}
```

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `schemaVersion` | Required, exactly `1` on every job row. |
| `id`, `lane`, `tier` | Required, 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens; first character must be a letter or digit. Lane is the queue pool identifier. Tier labels are preserved, not mapped to engines. |
| `outcome` | Optional: `queued`, `running`, `merged`, `empty`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Absent, queued and running jobs are incomplete. |
| `tokens` | Optional nonnegative safe integer: cumulative total tokens consumed by this job, across attempts. An absent measurement is unknown. |
| `startedAt`, `mergedAt` | Optional canonical UTC ISO timestamps, including milliseconds and `Z`. Time to merge is measured from job start. |
| `pr` | Required for merged jobs: `owner/repository#number`, positive number without leading zeros. Case-insensitive identity. No URL is fetched. |
| `reverted` | Optional boolean, a recorded observation. Absence means revert status is unknown. |
| `impact` | Optional finite nonnegative number, at most `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. A producer-supplied score in a common unit across lanes and tiers. No impact score is invented from lines changed. |

`mergedAt`, `reverted` and `impact` require a merged outcome in the combined
snapshot. Each job ID occurs once in the JSONL snapshot. Each merged PR occurs
once across all jobs, preventing double reward. Blank lines are ignored.
Unknown fields are ignored and never copied to the output. Missing fields must
be omitted, not set to `null`. Empty jobs need an explicit `empty` outcome;
missing PR evidence is not proof that a job was empty.

The status file is an explicit overlay on those exact JSONL bytes:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "jobsSha256": "<lowercase SHA-256 of the exact jobs.jsonl bytes>",
  "jobs": [
    {
      "id": "RQ-example",
      "outcome": "merged",
      "tokens": 800,
      "pr": "ashlrai/example#1",
      "mergedAt": "2026-10-25T12:00:00.000Z",
      "reverted": false,
      "impact": 4
    }
  ]
}
```

Status entries replace supplied measurement fields, never add token totals to
the job's previous total. Omitted fields retain their job value. An empty
`jobs` array is valid. Status IDs must be distinct and already present in the
JSONL file. Lane, tier, PR identity, a terminal outcome, and a recorded revert
cannot be contradicted by an overlay. Hash mismatch refuses a mixed snapshot;
publish a new matching pair after changing the JSONL bytes. These hashes bind
content, not producer identity or authenticity.

Both files are bounded to 16 MiB and 100,000 job entries. Readers require
owner-controlled regular files and directories using the existing stable-file
reader. Symlink inputs, unsafe permissions, files changing during a read,
missing files, malformed/truncated JSON, invalid dates, numeric overflow and
contradictory merge evidence refuse the entire report. Replacement characters
(literal U+FFFD as well as invalid UTF-8 decoded to U+FFFD) are refused so the
digests identify the exact accepted bytes. URI and network-share syntax are
rejected. Filesystem paths on OS-mounted volumes follow the OS mount policy;
the command does not resolve or access network services itself.

## Rollup definitions

Output includes `overall`, sorted `lanes`, sorted `tiers`, and sorted
`laneTiers` groups. Sorting is ASCII deterministic. Source SHA-256 values are
included; no current timestamp, path, job ID or PR is copied into output.
Identical input bytes produce identical output bytes. Reordering records
changes source digests but not the rollup values.

Top-level fields: `schemaVersion`, `kind: "router-metrics"`, `readOnly: true`,
`sources`, `overall`, `lanes`, `tiers`, `laneTiers`, `priors`.

Completed jobs are merged, empty, failed or cancelled. Incomplete jobs remain
visible in `jobs` and `incompleteJobs`, but their partial tokens and outcomes
are excluded from every completed-job metric.

| Metric | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| `mergeRate` | Merged PR count / completed jobs. |
| `emptyJobRate` | Explicitly empty jobs / completed jobs. |
| `tokensPerMergedPR` | All completed-job tokens / merged PRs, including failed, cancelled, empty and reverted work. |
| `timeToMergeMs` | Mean of merged time minus job start, in milliseconds. |
| `revertRate` | Reverted PRs / merged PRs. Reverted merges still count as merges. |
| `mergedImpactPerToken` | Retained merged impact / all completed-job tokens. Reverted PRs contribute zero retained impact. |

An empty denominator returns `null`. Zero known tokens returns `null` for
impact per token, never infinity. If any completed job lacks tokens, both
cost-based metrics are `null`. If any merged PR lacks either timestamp,
`timeToMergeMs` is `null`. If any merged PR lacks revert status, `revertRate`
and retained-impact efficiency are `null`. Every non-reverted merge needs an
impact score for efficiency to be known. A reverted merge's retained impact
is known zero even without a score. With positive known cost and no merges,
efficiency is known zero.

Counts expose coverage: `tokenSamples`, `timeToMergeSamples`, `revertSamples`
and `impactSamples`. `knownTokens` is only the known subtotal and must not be
treated as a complete cost when `tokenSamples < completedJobs`. Rates are
fractions, not percentages. No pseudo-counts, confidence interval or
statistical significance claim is added.

## Router integration boundary

`priors` exposes the objective `mergedImpactPerToken` with completed, merged
and empty counts per lane and tier. The `priors` object carries `basis`,
`operationalSteering`, `objective`, `lanes` and `tiers` arrays. Each prior
element has `key`, `completedJobs`, `mergedPRs`, `emptyJobs` and
`mergedImpactPerToken`. `laneTiers` provides joint evidence when lane and tier
observations are correlated. Consumers can use these counts for bandit priors
and known efficiency as an LP objective coefficient, after their own evidence
admission and exploration policy. Null evidence is an unknown arm, not a
zero-reward arm. Compare scores only when impact units match.

This checkout has no queue bandit/LP consumer. The predecessor
RQ-PACE-GROK-BURN at local commit `60975653` also exports advisory pacing only;
its protected routers do not consume pacing yet. Existing operational routers
are Tier-1 protected and existing learned routing requires authenticated
learning authority. Accordingly this feed declares `basis: local-observations`
and `operationalSteering: false`. It does not alter live lane or tier choice.

The remaining authorized router integration must apply existing eligibility,
budget and Grok pacing constraints before optimizing efficiency. In
particular, a high observed Grok score cannot lift a throttle or enlarge the
predecessor's `boxAgentTurnMultiplier` of `0.5` when throttled. Do not use these
local file hashes as learning authority, disable an admission gate, or treat
this command as evidence that the live router is connected.

## Verification

The fixtures in `test/fixtures/router-metrics/` include a status-completed job,
empty and failed jobs, incomplete jobs, a reverted merge and unknown costs.
`test/metrics-ingest.test.ts` checks exact arithmetic, coverage, ordering,
malformed evidence, duplicate credit, path refusal, UTF-8, read-only behavior
and CLI exits. Run tests with a temporary HOME as required by the repository.


<!-- page: MILESTONE-CONTRACT -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/MILESTONE-CONTRACT.md

# MILESTONE-CONTRACT — the Goal Loop runner

> **Recovery note (2026-06-20).** A crash lost the conversation that authored this
> feature. The code on disk survived: `src/core/goal-loop/types.ts` (full type
> contract) and `src/core/goal-loop/parse.ts` (markdown parsers). This document is
> **reconstructed from those surviving docstrings + the existing engine/swarm
> conventions** so the plan is durable on disk this time. Sections marked
> **⟢ RECOVERED ASSUMPTION** carried decisions that lived only in the lost
> conversation — confirm or correct them before they harden into code.

---

## Purpose

The **Goal Loop** is an autonomous runner that executes a roadmap of milestones
**one at a time**, with a **FRESH AGENT PROCESS PER MILESTONE** (a deliberate
context reset between milestones), pausing cleanly at any step that needs a human,
and **resumable cold** from a persisted `state.json`.

The shape that makes this work: a **tiny, durable outer driver** loops over the
roadmap and owns all persistence; each milestone is handed to a **heavy, disposable
agent context** that does the work and returns only a small structured
`MilestoneResult`. The agent's context is thrown away after each milestone — the
driver never accumulates it — so a 40-milestone roadmap costs the driver almost
nothing in context and never degrades from a bloated window.

This is the inverse of one long agent run: instead of one context that grows until
it rots, it is N short contexts, each scoped to exactly one milestone file, stitched
together by a durable few-KB state file.

---

## Inputs — the milestone-file contract (already parsed by `parse.ts`)

### Roadmap index file
Milestones in **dependency order**, one markdown link per line. Two accepted forms:

```markdown
- [M0](M0-bootstrap.md)        ← preferred (markdown link)
- M1: M1-schema.md             ← fallback (`id: file.md`)
```

Order is verbatim = execution order. The runner executes sequentially; later
milestones may depend on earlier outputs. **No parallelism.** Parsed by
`parseRoadmap(dir, roadmapFile?)` → `RoadmapIndex`. Default index filenames tried,
in order, when none is given: `roadmap.md`, `ROADMAP.md`. `README.md` is not
tried, because its `.md` links are usually docs rather than milestones; pass
`--roadmap README.md` to use it. A missing index is an error that names the
files looked for.

### Milestone file
Per-milestone markdown with **atomic steps** and an **acceptance gate**:

```markdown
# M0 — Bootstrap

- [ ] M0.1 create the package skeleton
      Done when: `npm run build` exits 0
- [x] M0.2 add the lint config
      Done when: `npm run lint` exits 0

## Acceptance checklist (gate)
- [ ] build, lint, and test all pass
- [ ] no new runtime dependency added
```

- **Steps** are checkbox lines whose label starts with a stable id (`M0.1`).
  Each carries an optional verifiable `Done when:` check, a `checked` flag, and the
  source `lineIndex` so the runner can tick it back in place byte-faithfully.
- **Gate** items are the bullets/checkboxes under the first heading matching
  `acceptance`/`gate`. Step-id checkboxes inside the gate section are gate items,
  **not** steps.

Parsed by `parseMilestone(path, id?)` → `MilestoneDoc`. `tickSteps(doc, completedIds)`
returns a new `lines[]` with the named boxes flipped `[ ]`→`[x]` (only that
transition; never unticks; rest of the file byte-preserved) plus a `changed` flag so
the driver can skip a no-op write.

---

## The structured result — the ONLY thing that crosses back

A per-milestone agent returns exactly one `MilestoneResult` (JSON):

```ts
interface MilestoneResult {
  milestone: string;          // must match the dispatched milestone id
  status: 'done' | 'needs_human' | 'blocked' | 'in_progress';
  gate_passed: boolean;       // only meaningful with status 'done'
  steps_completed: string[];  // ids verified this run, e.g. ["M0.1","M0.2"]
  blocked_on: string | null;  // precise: what a human must do / what failed
  summary: string;            // short human-readable recap
}
```

Status semantics (verbatim from `types.ts:96-101`):
- **`done`** — every step verified and the acceptance gate passed.
- **`needs_human`** — a human-only step was reached (manual web action, cloud
  GPU/notebook, sign-off, external upload/creds). The agent did **not** attempt it;
  `blocked_on` says exactly what the human must do.
- **`blocked`** — an automatable step failed twice (retry exhausted).
- **`in_progress`** — partial progress (e.g. a dry-run prediction, or a bounded stop).

---

## Persisted state — `state.json` (lives next to the roadmap)

```ts
interface GoalLoopState {
  version: 1;
  roadmap: string;                                  // abs path to the index
  active: string | null;                            // milestone last worked on
  milestones: Record<string, MilestoneStateEntry>;  // keyed by milestone id
  updatedAt: string;                                // ISO
}
interface MilestoneStateEntry {
  milestone: string;
  status: MilestoneStatus;
  gate_passed: boolean;
  steps_done: string[];      // UNION across runs (never shrinks)
  blocked_on: string | null;
  summary: string;
  updatedAt: string;
}
```

Holds **only tiny per-milestone summaries + bookkeeping** — never the agents' heavy
context. **Resume rule:** an entry with `{ status: 'done', gate_passed: true }` is
treated as complete and skipped; everything else is (re-)dispatched, and
`steps_done` is fed to the agent so it skips already-verified steps (the same
skip-done-don't-redo discipline `runSwarm({ resumeId })` uses at `runner.ts:1313`).

---

## Modules to build

### `state.ts` — persistence (no ambiguity; fully determined by the types)
- `loadState(dir, roadmapPath): GoalLoopState` — read `state.json` from the roadmap
  dir; if absent, return a fresh `{ version:1, roadmap, active:null, milestones:{} }`.
  Tolerant of a malformed/partial file (return fresh, never throw).
- `saveState(dir, state): void` — **atomic tmp+rename** (the same write discipline as
  `src/core/inbox/store.ts`), so a crash mid-write leaves the OLD complete file, never
  a partial one.
- `mergeResult(state, result): GoalLoopState` — fold a `MilestoneResult` into the
  entry for its milestone: union `steps_done`, set `status`/`gate_passed`/`blocked_on`/
  `summary`, stamp `updatedAt`. **Merge, never clobber.**
- `statePath(dir): string` — `<dir>/state.json`.

### `result.ts` — parse the agent's structured output (never throws)
- `parseMilestoneResult(raw: string, expectMilestone: string): MilestoneResult` —
  extract the JSON object from the agent's stdout (the `claude --output-format json`
  envelope wraps it in `{ result: "<text>", ... }`, so look inside `result` and also
  accept a bare object), validate the shape, and coerce. On any malformed / missing /
  mismatched-milestone output, return a safe **`blocked`** result with
  `blocked_on` describing the parse failure — the driver turns that into a clean stop,
  never a crash. Mirrors the tolerant, never-throw posture of `parse.ts`.

### `runner.ts` — the driver + the default executor
The driver (pure of any LLM; testable with a fake executor):
1. `parseRoadmap` → ordered milestones; `loadState`.
2. For each milestone **in order**: if state says complete, skip. Otherwise
   `parseMilestone`, set `state.active`, dispatch via the injected `RunMilestoneFn`.
3. On the result: `tickSteps` for `steps_completed` and write the milestone file back
   iff `changed`; `mergeResult` + `saveState`.
4. **Stop the loop** (do not advance) on `needs_human` or `blocked` — print
   `blocked_on` so the human knows exactly what to do; the run is resumable.
   `in_progress` also stops (bounded). Only `done && gate_passed` advances.
5. Return a summary of what ran / where it stopped.

The **default `RunMilestoneFn`** (the real executor): spawn a fresh agent scoped to
**exactly one milestone file** — the context reset. Reuse the existing engine seam,
**do not reinvent spawning**: build the command with
`buildEngineCommand('claude', <prompt>, cfg, { cwd })` → exactly
`claude -p "<prompt>" --model <M> --output-format json` (`engines.ts:104-110`), run
it with `spawnEngine` (which already applies the env-bridge allowlist, optional
phantom wrap, a 5-min wall-clock cap, captures stdout, and **never throws**), then
`parseMilestoneResult(out.output, doc.id)`. The prompt embeds the single milestone
file + the milestone's `steps_done` from state + the strict "return ONLY this JSON
shape" instruction. **Implementations MUST NOT throw** — a failed spawn/parse becomes
a `blocked` result (or `null`) that the driver turns into a clean stop
(`types.ts:178-181`).

> **⟢ RECOVERED ASSUMPTION (executor).** That the per-milestone engine is the
> `claude` adapter via `buildEngineCommand`/`spawnEngine` is inferred from the
> `claude -p` reference in `types.ts:171` + the existing seam. Alternative: route
> through the hub's configured `EngineId` (so `aw`/`builtin` also work). **Confirm:
> hard-wire `claude`, or honor `cfg`'s engine selection?**

### CLI surface
> **⟢ RECOVERED ASSUMPTION (command name).** The CLI name lived only in the lost
> conversation. `ashlr goals` is already taken by M28 (goal *planning* &
> scheduling); this feature *executes* a roadmap. **Proposed:**
> ```
> ashlr roadmap run    [--dir <d>] [--roadmap <file>] [--dry-run] [--json]
> ashlr roadmap status [--dir <d>] [--json]
> ashlr roadmap resume [--dir <d>]          # alias for run; resumes from state.json
> ```
> `--dry-run` maps to `RunMilestoneContext.dryRun` (agent PREDICTS automatable-vs-human
> per step and touches nothing). `--json` emits a machine-readable run summary.
> **Confirm the noun (`roadmap` vs `loop` vs `chain`) and the flags.**

---

## INVARIANTS (and how each is proven)

1. **CONTEXT-RESET** — each milestone runs in a fresh agent process; the driver never
   accumulates agent context. *Proven:* the only value crossing back is a
   `MilestoneResult` (a few hundred bytes); a fake `RunMilestoneFn` asserts the driver
   passes exactly one `MilestoneDoc` per dispatch and stores only the summary.
2. **DURABLE-RESUME** — killing the process between any two milestones loses no
   completed work. *Proven:* `state.json` is written atomically after every milestone;
   a test crashes between milestones N and N+1, re-runs the driver, and asserts
   completed milestones are skipped and the loop continues at N+1.
3. **SKIP-DONE** — a resumed milestone does not redo verified steps. *Proven:*
   `steps_done` from state is handed to the agent and union-merged on return; never
   shrinks.
4. **CLEAN-PAUSE** — `needs_human` / `blocked` stops the loop without advancing and
   without falsely marking anything `done`; `blocked_on` is surfaced. *Proven:* a fake
   executor returns each non-`done` status; the driver halts at that milestone, state
   records the reason, later milestones stay untouched.
5. **BYTE-FAITHFUL TICKS** — ticking step checkboxes changes only `[ ]`→`[x]` on the
   recorded lines; the rest of the milestone file is byte-preserved. *Proven:*
   `tickSteps` round-trip test (already specified by `parse.ts`); driver writes back
   only when `changed`.
6. **NEVER-THROWS** — neither the parsers, the result parser, nor the executor throw
   on malformed input; every failure becomes a clean `blocked`/fresh-state outcome.
   *Proven:* malformed roadmap/milestone/result fixtures yield empty/partial/blocked
   structures, asserted explicitly.
7. **DETERMINISTIC TESTS** — no test spawns a real agent or depends on a model.
   *Proven:* every suite injects a fake `RunMilestoneFn`; the default (spawning)
   executor is unit-tested only at the argv-builder level (as `engines.ts` already is),
   never spawned.

---

## SAFETY POSTURE (inherited from the hub)

- The runner **edits the milestone files and `state.json` only** (tick boxes + persist
  summaries). Any change the *agent* makes to the target repo is the agent's own
  doing inside its scoped process — the driver performs **no `git push` / PR / deploy**
  and no outward action.
- `--dry-run` touches nothing: the agent predicts automatable-vs-human per step and
  reports, matching the existing dry-run posture.
- Non-interactive / CI: same as the hub — detect/predict only unless explicitly run.

# Milestone Index

**Purpose:** a single authoritative lookup from a milestone ID (`Mxxx`) to what
it actually is, whether it shipped, and where the evidence lives. This exists
because milestone IDs in this repo are **not guaranteed unique** — several
numbers were spec'd for one feature and later silently reused by unrelated
shipped work when nobody checked the spec docs before assigning the next ID.
Planning from a spec doc's milestone number alone, without checking this
index, will re-propose work that already shipped under that number for a
different purpose, or worse, believe unbuilt work is done because the number
"exists" in `test/`.

**Ground truth order:** code and tests > this index > `CHANGELOG.md` >
`docs/contracts/CONTRACT-Mxx.md` > spec docs (`docs/SPEC-*.md`). Spec docs
describe *design intent at the time they were written*; they are frequently
stale. If this index and a spec doc disagree, trust this index's cited
`file:line`, or re-verify against the code yourself.

**How this index was built:** every `test/mNNN.*.test.ts` file in the repo
was enumerated (425 distinct milestone numbers as of 2026-08-16, up from 415
the pass before), cross-referenced against `docs/contracts/` for existing
binding contracts and against `docs/SPEC-*.md` for milestone numbers
documented as planned. The M464–M503 range, the M504–M519 range, and every
collision row below were hand-verified against source (see file:line
citations); the full appendix (§4) is otherwise machine-generated from test
filenames — treat its "subject" column as a filename-derived hint, not a
hand-verified description, unless the ID also appears in §2 or §3.

---

## 1. What "M83–M88" numbering gap means

`docs/ROADMAP-NEXT.md` (now retired, see that file) planned M83–M88 as the
*next* work in June 2026. M84, M85, M86, M87, M88 all have `test/mNN.*`
evidence in the appendix below. **M83 (Windows CI lane) has no dedicated test
file** — it shipped as CI configuration only: `windows-latest` appears in the
job matrix at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:42,59,75,87`. This is a legitimate
"shipped, no test/mNN.*.ts" case, not a gap in the appendix's methodology.

---

## 2. Confirmed ID collisions

An ID collision means: a spec doc under `docs/SPEC-*.md` assigned this
milestone number to one feature, and a *different* feature later shipped
under the same number (visible as `test/mNNN.<unrelated-slug>.test.ts`),
without anyone renumbering the spec. In every case below, the spec'd feature
was never built under that number — check the "Unbuilt feature currently sits
where?" column before assuming it shipped somewhere else under a different
number; usually it just never shipped at all.

A prior audit flagged 11 of these (M258, M260–M264, M270, M271, M273–M275).
Re-verification confirmed 10 of the 11 as genuine collisions, found that
**M264 is a collision between two competing spec docs** rather than a
spec-vs-shipped mismatch, and surfaced **one additional collision the prior
audit missed: M259**.

**A thirteenth collision, of a new kind, was introduced on 2026-08-16:**
M470 was already assigned (see §4) to "proposal capture candidate identity."
An unrelated runtime-grant implementation reused the number, but its
self-authorizing trust-root and standing-grant surface was removed during
authority salvage. Production roots remain compiled empty.

<!-- page: MISSION-OS -->

# Mission OS: operator guide

Mission OS turns one strategic briefing into a bounded cross-repository plan,
shows the operator what is dependency-ready, and can record an authenticated
observation of that state. It is designed to make autonomy legible before it
becomes automatic.

This guide describes the current source tree. Source code and passing local
tests do not prove that a packaged binary, resident daemon, Cortex or Locus
connector, release, deployment, or production workflow is installed or active.

## The model

Mission OS separates intent, evidence, and authority:

```text
latest briefing on disk
        |
        v
bounded mission DAG ----> read-only preview
        |                        |
        |                        v
        |                 exact hold reasons
        v
authenticated observation receipt ----> zero-effect shadow suggestion
        |
        +---- explicit `approve` or `reconcile` is still required to create goals
```

**3.10: the Leader replaces the Strategist review.** `ashlr vision review` is
now an alias of `ashlr leader tick --wait`. It never loads the legacy
Strategist and never writes a briefing. A tick applies class-B actions whose
veto window has passed, grades moves that are due, and starts a Leader run only
when one is due (the 06:30 slot, or a trigger: 10 fleet merges, a revert, a
seat window resetting or a high-severity insight; at most three runs a day;
skipped when the evidence has not changed). That run goes to a seat the router
admits under the budget mode, with no cloud fallback. Without a standing grant
it runs on a free local model or not at all, and the memo is a dry run: its
actions are shown, not applied. New direction arrives as
Leader memos (`ashlr leader show`), and every memo action can be undone with
`ashlr leader veto`. Preview, shadow, approve and reconcile below still read the
latest briefing already on disk; nothing in 3.10 writes a new one. See
[Authority](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/docs/AUTHORITY.md) for the Leader's action classes and the nightly job.

The mission graph is a planning DAG. A work node names one exact enrolled
repository and its upstream dependencies. A human-gate node says that a human
decision is required; it cannot supply that decision.

The receipt is an immutable local observation. It records bounded lifecycle and
verification facts while keeping all authority flags false. The shadow
suggestion answers only: "what would the existing planning policy select now?"
It creates nothing and grants nothing.

## Responsibility boundaries

| Plane | Current responsibility | Explicit non-authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ashlr Hub | Enrolled repositories, mission compilation, goal capacity and dedupe, engineering evidence, sandboxed proposal production | No company truth, credential authority, human approval, business outcome, automatic merge, release, or deploy authority from Mission OS |
| Ashlr Cortex | Future governed company intent, accountability, human decisions, and permission-filtered business observations | No current connector; cannot select Hub repositories, verify engineering, or approve Hub proposals |
| Ashlr Locus | Future governed principal, tenant, provider, sealed-session, and credential-reference decisions outside model context | No current connector; identity readiness would not grant Hub planning, execution, merge, or deployment authority |
| Human/operator | Explicitly adopts planning state and separately authorizes consequential actions through their existing gates | A graph, receipt, model answer, or green test never substitutes for this authority |

Cortex and Locus are architectural boundaries in V1, not integrated runtime
dependencies. Hub does not fetch their data, persist their identifiers, resolve
their credentials, or write outcomes back to them.

## Commands and effects

Run installed builds as `ashlr vision ...`. From a source checkout, the
equivalent development invocation is `npm run dev -- vision ...`.

| Command | Reads | Writes | Authority/effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ashlr vision show [id] [--json]` | Current end-state spec (`--json` prints it as one object) | Nothing | Read-only |
| `ashlr vision review [--project <repo>]` | Leader state, fleet digests, ledger, seat headroom | Leader state: due class-B actions applied, due moves graded, and a memo when a run is due | Alias of `ashlr leader tick --wait`; budget-gated; writes no briefing. Memo actions follow their class (A at once, B after the veto window, C to Needs you). `--project` is accepted but not applied: the Leader reviews the whole portfolio |
| `ashlr leader show` / `ashlr leader veto <actionId>` | Leader state | `veto` runs the action's recorded inverse (`--memo <id>` undoes a whole memo) | `show` is read-only; `veto` only lowers what autonomy is doing |
| `ashlr vision preview` | Latest briefing, enrollment, complete goal inventory | Nothing | Read-only; reports exact targets, selections, and hold reasons |
| `ashlr vision shadow [--json]` | Briefing, enrollment, complete goals and proposals, realized-merge authority evidence | One immutable receipt, or replays the matching receipt | Observation-only; emits at most one `would-create` or `hold` suggestion and changes no operational state |
| `ashlr vision approve` | Latest briefing and planning sources | Evolves the spec and adopts selected goals | Explicit planning mutation; still no dispatch, proposal, merge, release, or deployment |
| `ashlr vision reconcile` | Latest briefing and current goal/proposal state | At most one newly dependency-ready goal | Explicit planning mutation; no dispatch or outward effect |

`shadow` is deliberately not filesystem-read-only: its one permitted write is
the private receipt under `~/.ashlr/mission-receipts/`. The suggestion itself
has `maxGoalCreations: 0`, every effect flag is `false`, and the command does not
call goal adoption, agent dispatch, proposal creation, merge, release,
deployment, publication, provider, policy, or budget APIs.

The local Mission Control Goals view is stricter: its Mission Outcome Room
never records a receipt. It requires a complete immutable receipt ledger when
that ledger exists, recognizes an exactly missing ledger without creating it,
selects the newest authenticated receipt for the exact mission key and graph,
recomputes the suggestion from current complete briefing, enrollment, goal,
and proposal snapshots, and displays only a bounded public summary. It shows
`missing`, `withheld`, or `unavailable` rather than treating absent, stale,
partial, malformed, or mismatched evidence as a current suggestion.

## Recommended operator workflow

### 1. Establish bounded inputs

```sh
ashlr preflight
ashlr enroll list
ashlr leader show
```

`ashlr leader show` prints the latest Leader memo and its actions; veto what
you disagree with. `ashlr vision review` (the same as `ashlr leader tick --wait`)
runs a tick now: it spends a seat only when a run is due and the budget mode
admits it, and it writes no briefing. The preview below compiles the latest
briefing already on disk.

### 2. Inspect the exact plan

```sh
ashlr vision preview
```

Confirm the target repository for every work node, dependency ordering,
acceptance evidence, outcome hypothesis, guardrails, and any human gate. A
`create` preview disposition means only "eligible for a later explicit planning
operation." It is not permission to execute.

### 3. Capture the zero-effect decision

```sh
ashlr vision shadow
ashlr vision shadow --json
```

Human-readable success is one of:

```text
Mission reconcile shadow
  WOULD CREATE node <node-key>
  receipt <receipt-id>
  Observation only: no goal, milestone, repository, agent, proposal, merge,
  release, deployment, publication, external mutation, policy, or budget state changed.
```

```text
Mission reconcile shadow
  HELD (<reason>)
  receipt <receipt-id>
  Observation only: ...
```

An abridged JSON success envelope is shown below. The real `suggestion` also
contains its authenticated basis, complete bounds/effects, and stable identity
digests.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "mode": "shadow",
  "authority": "observation-only",
  "state": "would-create",
  "receipt": {
    "disposition": "recorded",
    "receiptId": "<sha256>",
    "receiptDigest": "<sha256>"
  },
  "suggestion": {
    "decision": { "disposition": "would-create", "reason": "would-create" },
    "bounds": { "maxSuggestions": 1, "maxGoalCreations": 0 },
    "effects": { "goals": false, "agents": false, "proposals": false }
  }
}
```

`state` may be `would-create` or `held`. An identical semantic retry reports
receipt disposition `replayed`, keeps the same receipt and suggestion
identities, and preserves the earliest stored observation. The full suggestion
contains false flags for goals, milestones, repositories, agents, proposals,
merges, releases, deployments, publications, external mutations, policy, and
budgets.

After a receipt exists, open Mission Control and select **Goals** to see the
same decision class in the Mission Outcome Room. This dashboard projection is
read-only: it exposes only the bounded disposition and reason, selected node
key and kind, observation-only authority, and an all-false effects summary.
Receipt presence details, timestamps, IDs, digests, HMAC references, source
digests, objectives, proposal or diff evidence, repository paths, tenant
aliases, and the full suggestion basis do not cross the unauthenticated public
API. Refreshing the page does not create or replay a receipt.

Withheld JSON returns nonzero and is intentionally smaller:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "mode": "shadow",
  "authority": "observation-only",
  "state": "withheld",
  "reason": "<fail-closed-reason>",
  "effects": {
    "missionReceipt": "none",
    "outward": "none"
  }
}
```

Failure effects are two independent facts. Before a write, they are
`missionReceipt: "none"` and `outward: "none"`. After a proven receipt write,
`missionReceipt` is `"recorded"` or `"replayed"` while `outward` remains
`"none"`. If receipt publication is conflicted or cannot be proven,
`missionReceipt` and `outward` are both `"unknown"`; the CLI never reports
`none` for an ambiguous persistence result. Receipt details remain alongside
the effects object whenever a persistence disposition exists.

Exit codes are `0` for a verified `would-create` or `held` suggestion, `1` when
evidence or persistence is withheld, and `2` for invalid command usage.

### 4. Make the planning decision explicitly

Choose one, after reviewing the preview and shadow output:

```sh
ashlr vision approve
# or advance only the next dependency-ready node:
ashlr vision reconcile
```

Then use the ordinary goal and inbox surfaces:

```sh
ashlr goals list
ashlr goals status <goal-id>
ashlr goals advance <goal-id>
ashlr inbox
```

Goal creation remains planning-only. `goals advance` is a separate sandboxed,
proposal-producing action. Proposal approval, merge, release, deployment,
publication, resident daemon activation, and external provider mutation remain
separate gates.

## Evidence and privacy

Mission Receipt V1 stores authenticated metadata, not the briefing or raw work:

- briefing, enrollment, goal, proposal, verification, and merge evidence are
  represented by domain-separated digests;
- goal, milestone, and proposal identifiers become HMAC references;
- objectives, rationale, repository paths, diffs, verification commands and
  output, PR URLs, provider payloads, credentials, human decisions, and raw
  business outcomes are not persisted in the receipt;
- exact mission node keys, lifecycle statuses, blocker keys, merge source, and
  realized merge revision remain visible because they are required to explain
  the engineering observation; and
- business outcome is always `not-observed`; human-decision and outcome evidence
  completeness remain false.

The capture adapter accepts at most 512 complete goal records, 4,096 complete
proposal records, and 512 milestones in aggregate. The receipt accepts 1–24
mission nodes, at most 64 milestones per node and 512 total, and at most 256 KiB
of canonical serialized data. Exceeding a bound withholds the receipt rather
than truncating evidence into an apparently complete record.

Receipts use the existing 32-byte host provenance key at
`~/.ashlr/foundry/provenance.key`; Mission OS never creates that key. The HMAC
proves that a process holding the same local key recorded the bytes. It is not
an independent verifier, a remote attestation, or protection against an attacker
who can read the user's key. Do not copy the key into logs, tickets, prompts, or
support bundles.

Receipt reads are bounded and private-store checks fail closed on unsafe
ownership, permissions, links, replacement races, truncation, malformed data,
or missing authentication. A complete missing goal or proposal store is an
authoritative empty source; an unreadable, partial, capped, or degraded store is
not.

Authenticated realized-merge checks may consult read-only Git authority. They
do not run a merge, mutate a repository, push, or contact Cortex or Locus.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom/reason | Meaning | Safe next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `briefing-source-incomplete` | Latest briefing is absent, unreadable, partial, or degraded | Since 3.10 no command writes a briefing (`ashlr vision review` runs the Leader tick), so rerunning review will not repair it. Take direction from the Leader (`ashlr leader show`) instead; do not hand-edit an untrusted briefing into place |
| `enrollment-source-incomplete` or `repository-not-enrolled` | Enrollment authority is degraded or a work node does not bind one exact enrolled root | Run `ashlr preflight` and `ashlr enroll list`; repair enrollment through the enrollment CLI |
| `goal-source-incomplete` / `proposal-source-incomplete` | A bounded authoritative inventory could not be completed | Inspect `ashlr goals list` and `ashlr inbox`; repair filesystem ownership/permissions before retrying rather than treating records as absent |
| `mission-graph-invalid` / `invalid-mission-goal-binding` | The graph digest, dependency DAG, target, or exact goal mission tuple does not validate | Run `ashlr vision preview` and correct the enrollment. The briefing is not regenerated in 3.10; new plans arrive as Leader memos (`ashlr leader show`) |
| `linked-proposal-missing` / `linked-proposal-repository-mismatch` | A mission milestone points at evidence outside the complete inventory or wrong repo | Inspect the linked goal and proposal; never substitute a similarly named proposal |
| `receipt-key-unavailable` | The existing provenance key is absent or unsafe | Do not fabricate or paste a key. Inspect `~/.ashlr/foundry/` ownership and the normal signed-evidence setup that owns key creation |
| `receipt-conflicted` / `receipt-persistence-failed` | Immutable no-clobber publication or exact point verification failed | Stop retry loops, preserve the store, inspect local disk/permissions, and run `ashlr doctor`; do not delete receipt records as a first response |
| `receipt-invalid` / `suggestion-invalid` | Authentication or canonical integrity failed | Treat the output as untrusted, preserve evidence, and investigate the local key/store before any planning mutation |
| `dependency-blocked` / `human-gate-required` / `no-ready-node` | The verified result is a normal hold, not an error | Complete the upstream engineering work or make the required decision through its real authority surface; rerun shadow afterward |

Never "fix" a withheld result by editing a receipt, changing a digest, deleting a
goal/proposal record, or weakening source completeness. The failure is the
safety result.

## Production boundary and roadmap

Current V1 source provides the mission graph, evidence-normalized capture,
immutable authenticated receipt, zero-effect shadow planner, and
`ashlr vision shadow [--json]` integration. Before claiming operational
availability, separately verify that the intended commit was built, packaged,
installed, and invoked; if a daemon is involved, verify the installed artifact
and daemon state independently.

The receipt is one host process's observation, not a lease over the underlying
sources. Concurrent source changes can make it historical immediately after
capture. The explicit `approve` and `reconcile` planning mutations do not yet
append Mission Receipt V1 post-effect evidence, and no automatic daemon
reconciler is activated by this work.

The following are roadmap directions, not present authority or commitments:

1. post-effect receipts for explicit planning mutations;
2. a shared CLI/daemon reconciliation lease with crash-safe recovery;
3. independently authenticated human-decision evidence;
4. permission-filtered Cortex mission-candidate and outcome envelopes;
5. Locus-bound identity references that never expose credentials to model
   context; and
6. a separately activated automatic planning mode only after sustained shadow
   evidence, with merge, release, deployment, publication, provider, policy,
   budget, and business-outcome authority still independent.

Normative details live in the
[Ecosystem Mission Graph source contract](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-hub/blob/master/docs/contracts/CONTRACT-ECOSYSTEM-MISSION-GRAPH.md)
and [Mission Observation Receipt V1 contract](./contracts/CONTRACT-MISSION-RECEIPT-V1.md).

Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/MODEL-INVENTORY.md

# Local model inventory

`phm models inventory --json` measures installed Ollama and oMLX models on a
Mac and writes `~/.ashlr/fleet.json` at `resources.models`. It is disabled by
default. Create `~/.ashlr/model-inventory.json` explicitly:

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "ollama": "http://127.0.0.1:11434",
  "omlx": "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
}
```

Only HTTP origins with literal `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` are accepted. DNS names,
wildcard addresses, credentials, URL paths and redirects are refused. On Mac,
`lsof` must confirm all listeners on each configured port bind to numeric
loopback addresses before each request. Authenticated engines are unavailable;
the command never obtains or sends credentials. Endpoint response bodies and
inference output are not logged or persisted.

Run with idle engines. The command refuses to evict any existing loaded model.
It holds an atomic directory lock for the entire CLI run and processes models
and samples sequentially. An abandoned `model-inventory.lock` is never stolen;
inspect the engines and process before manually removing it.

Admission uses the conservative legacy Mac memguard thresholds: at least 35%
free memory, normal kernel memory pressure, over 10 GB disk headroom, and enough
free memory for 120% of the model's reported size while retaining 25% of total
RAM. Missing telemetry refuses admission. Admission is rechecked before every
sample and tokenizer calibration. This is a local admission check, not a lease
from the bridge scheduler; other clients must keep the engines idle.

Every measured model has three cold samples with a fixed synthetic ` hello`
repetition prompt, calibrated to exactly 512 engine-reported prompt tokens.
Calibration plus measurement is bounded to six attempts. Generation is capped
at 64 tokens, with temperature zero. Each attempt unloads through its engine API
in a `finally` block, and uses at most 20 idle-confirmation polls, with 500 ms pauses between them, before the
next attempt. Unconfirmed unload stops the entire inventory. Cache hits and
missing measurements cannot produce a measured row or tiers. oMLX uses the
inference/tokenizer APIs rather than its benchmark service, which can upload
benchmark results externally.

Ollama reports prompt and decode counts divided by nanosecond durations;
oMLX reports its own prefill and generation rates. Resident memory is the
loaded model's Ollama `/api/ps` size or oMLX admin `actual_size`, never the
on-disk download size. Each reported metric is the median of three samples.
Native context length and quantization come from engine metadata. Unknown
metadata stays null, and cannot satisfy the affected tier threshold. Embedding
and other unsupported models remain in the inventory without invented rates.

## Fleet schema

`resources.models` is a versioned envelope. Existing fleet keys and sibling
resource fields are preserved. A same-directory temporary file and rename
replace the fleet file only after the complete inventory succeeds.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| schemaVersion | 1 | Schema version |
| measuredAt | string | ISO timestamp for the pass |
| promptTokens | 512 | Verified prompt length per measured sample |
| repetitions | 3 | Successful samples required per measured model |
| unavailableEngines | string[] | Engines unavailable or refused before discovery |
| models | ModelInventoryRow[] | All discovered supported model identifiers |

Each row contains `id`, `engine` (`ollama` or `omlx`), `contextLength`,
`quantization`, `residentBytes`, `prefillTokensPerSecond`,
`decodeTokensPerSecond`, `servableTiers` and `status`. Numeric metrics and
quantization are nullable. Status is `measured`, `unsupported`, `unavailable`
or `refused`. Non-measured rows have no tiers. These are capability thresholds,
not model quality certifications:

| Tier | Minimum decode tokens/s | Minimum prefill tokens/s | Minimum context | Minimum quantization bits |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fast | 40 | 100 | 8192 | 4 |
| work | 15 | 50 | 32768 | 4 |
| frontier | 8 | 25 | 65536 | 8 |

Tiers are independent; a model can satisfy multiple rows. Unknown quantization
fails closed. JSON is emitted even for a partial inventory. Exit status is 1
when any engine is unavailable, any model is not measured, or a safety check
fails; otherwise it is 0. An unsuccessful pass can preserve the previous fleet
snapshot, so consumers must check its timestamp rather than assume freshness.

Engine contracts: [Ollama API](https://docs.ollama.com/api) and
[oMLX server](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/blob/main/omlx/server.py),
[oMLX admin routes](https://github.com/jundot/omlx/blob/main/omlx/admin/routes.py).


<!-- page: MODELCAPS -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/MODELCAPS.md

# Refresh the model capability cache

The standalone runner records advertised `/v1/models` metadata in a local
`modelcaps.v1` cache. No router, model catalog, daemon or UI consumes this cache.
A listing is evidence of advertised metadata, not a successful inference call,
an account entitlement or permission to spend.

## Run a refresh

Use a trusted source checkout with Node 22.15+ and its existing dependencies
installed. Use an already configured Phantom Secrets project whose
`phantom exec --` supplies `OPENAI_API_KEY` as a `phm_` placeholder and
`OPENAI_BASE_URL` as its loopback proxy URL. See [companion setup](COMPANIONS.md).
No new credential is required or created by this change.

This command contacts the configured model-list endpoint and replaces the
provider's local cache after a complete successful response:

```sh
node scripts/modelcaps-nightly.mjs --provider openai
```

The runner invokes `phantom exec -- node ...` with a fixed source worker.
It refuses raw keys, remote base URLs, embedded URL credentials, query strings
and redirects. Only a GET request is issued; no completion, generation or
tool call is made. The existing Secrets project selects the upstream provider;
`--provider` only labels the cache and must match that project operationally.
Run from that project's directory with an absolute path to the runner if needed.

Default output is `~/.ashlr/modelcaps/PROVIDER.json`. Override it with
`--output ABS_PATH` using a dedicated private directory. Existing directories
are never chmodded or repaired. Paths must be canonical, with no symlink
ancestors; on macOS this includes resolving `/tmp` and `/var` aliases.
The writer uses the repository's private atomic file helper, a 0600 temporary
file, fsync and rename. Existing symlink or hard-linked cache files are refused.

## Schedule nightly

Use an existing authorized local scheduler. For example, a cron entry in the
configured Secrets project can invoke the runner at 02:00 local time:

```cron
0 2 * * * cd /absolute/secrets-project && /absolute/node /absolute/phantom/scripts/modelcaps-nightly.mjs --provider openai
```

The scheduler needs a PATH containing the trusted `phantom` executable. It must
be able to use the existing Secrets configuration noninteractively. Each
invocation runs once and exits; this change installs no schedule or service.
Do not put credentials in the entry or redirect raw Secrets output into logs.
The wrapper suppresses child stdout and stderr and emits only a fixed status
message. Exit 0 means refresh succeeded; exit 1 means the probe or writer failed.

## Cache contract

`schema` is exactly `modelcaps.v1`. `provider` is the operator-supplied label.
`observedAt` and `expiresAt` are ISO UTC timestamps, with expiry 24 hours after
the completed observation. `source` is `/v1/models`, not a credential-bearing
proxy URL. `models` is sorted by exact model ID, using case-sensitive ordering.

Each model has `id`, `contextWindowTokens`, `maxOutputTokens` and
`capabilities: { tools, vision, reasoning }`. Token counts come only from explicit
positive integer `context_length` and `max_output_tokens` fields. Each capability
is `true`, `false` or `null` (unknown). The parser accepts a capability object
with explicit booleans or a tag array; a recognized tag establishes `true`,
while omitted tags remain unknown. Model names never imply capabilities.
Unrecognized fields and capabilities are discarded, including raw metadata.
This parser does not claim to normalize every provider's extension format.

Valid empty listings are cached as an empty `models` array. Malformed rows,
duplicate IDs, error envelopes, pagination, non-200 responses, invalid UTF-8 or
JSON and responses over 2 MiB fail the entire refresh. The listing allows at
most 10,000 models. A ten-second deadline covers headers and streamed body.
There are no retries or direct-network fallbacks. Probe and validation failures
leave prior cache bytes and timestamps intact. As with other durable writers,
a filesystem failure after rename may report failure after replacement.
Expired files remain on disk as historical observations; no consumer currently
interprets freshness or grants authority from this file.

## Verify offline

Fixture responses and injected transports exercise parsing, persistence and
failure handling without contacting providers or creating credentials:

```sh
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:ci -- --maxWorkers=1 --fileParallelism=false test/modelcaps.test.ts test/modelcaps-nightly.test.ts
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run typecheck
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run lint
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run check:docs
```

# Needs-you Items

The Needs-you drawer in the Phantom desktop console keeps a watch on every lane
and this Mac.  Items from **fleet** (running locally) come from a snapshot of
`~/.ashlr-runs` read by `fleet-needs-you.ts`; items from **release** and
**cloud-triage** (remote) come from the server.  The drawer polls every 15
seconds and flags only problems Mason, a contributor, or an agent can fix.

## Fleet on this Mac

_fleet-needs-you.ts_ items (local snapshot).

| Id | Fires when | Says | Next step | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| claude-lane-down | The Claude lane reports down | "The Claude lane is down" | Run the fix script from the runs bin folder | Fleet ▸ Claude lane (terminal) |
| switches-on | A dispatch switch file exists | "Dispatch is paused by {switch}" | Clear the switch in Fleet ▸ Switches | Fleet ▸ Switches |
| runs-dir-missing | The runs directory does not exist | "The runs directory is missing on this Mac" | Start the dispatcher to create it — Settings ▸ Connection | Settings ▸ Connection |
| stall-incident | Nothing starts and nothing merges for 30 min | "Stall incident" | Check Live runs and the leaders in Ops | Ops ▸ Leader journal |
| merge-stall | Healthy merge evidence shows zero merges and at least three publishes in the last hour | "Merge gate stalled" with recent publishes | Check the merge gate | Fleet ▸ Merges |
| leader-overdue | No leader pass in 30 minutes | "No leader process is running" | Check leaders in Ops and restart the leader loop | Ops ▸ Leader journal |
| lane-held:{lane} | A lane has a hold reason | "Lane {lane} is held" | Check the lane in Ops ▸ Live runs | Ops ▸ Live runs |
| supply-personal-reset | Personal reset hit but lane still held | "Personal Codex has reset; its lane is still held" | Release the hold in Fleet ▸ Lanes, or wait for it to expire | Fleet ▸ Lanes |
| supply-personal-out | Personal limit reached (≥ 100 %) | "Personal Codex is out until {reset}" | Those jobs wait for the reset; leaders should route elsewhere | Fleet ▸ Supply |
| supply-personal-low | Personal usage at 90 %+ | "Personal Codex is at {used} %" | Move new work to Devin and local lanes before it runs out | Fleet ▸ Supply |
| host-disk-low | Disk free < 5 GB (danger) or < 20 GB (warning) | "Disk is critically/nearly full on this Mac" | Free space: empty ~/.ashlr-runs/archive and old clones | Ops ▸ Host |
| host-pressure | Disk < 10 GB or memory < 10 % free | "This Mac is under pressure" | Free disk space or memory on this Mac | Ops ▸ Host |
| lane-idle:{lane} | A lane has queued jobs but none running | "Lane {lane} is idle" | Check the lane's hold and target in Lanes | Fleet ▸ Lanes |
| drop-pending | Leader jobs awaiting ingest | "{n} pending drop file(s)" | Ingest sweeps every few minutes; check in Ops | Ops ▸ Leader journal |

## Release Needy

_release-needs-you.ts_ items (remote, per repo).

| Id | Fires when | Says | Next step | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| release-blocked | A release PR has failing/blocked checks | "Release {version} is blocked" | Open the release PR; Merge Gate reruns after the fix | Fleet ▸ Releases |
| release-ready | A release PR is green, no failures | "Release PR #{num} is green" | Open the release PR; Merge Gate reports all green | Fleet ▸ Releases |

## Cloud Triage

_cloud-triage.ts_ items (remote, per delivery lane).  The drawer's server
response attaches **cloud** or **devin** prefixes to each row.

| Id | Fires when | Says | Next step | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fleet:owner-lane-pr:cloud-{taskId} | A cloud PR gate preview exists | PR title (varies) | Action on the preview (approve / reject / fix) | Fleet ▸ Releases |
| fleet:owner-lane-pr:devin-{taskId} | A Devin session preview exists | Session title (varies) | Action on the preview (approve / reject / fix) | Fleet ▸ Releases |

## Not covered

The drawer does **not** currently flag:

- a single stuck worker (no per-worker health check in fleet-needs-you.ts)
- a lane with target > 0 but only errors (no active item fires)
- a cloud PR that has been idle for many days without checks (covered only when blocking or green)
- a leader with a single old inbox entry (leader-overdue requires 30-min silence)
- a host with disk > 20 GB and memory > 10 % (below all thresholds)

# Node router

Any computer can join Phantom as a node. The box coordinator is just one more
node: it joins, advertises what it can do, and pulls work like the rest. The
router decides which node gets each job, and a lease makes sure a job never
runs on two nodes.

## What the router does

- **Caps.** A node advertises capabilities (`--caps build,gh`). A job lists what
  it needs (`--requires build`). Only nodes with every required cap are eligible.
- **Live usage.** Each node reports load with every heartbeat (`--usage 0-1000`,
  permille). The router sends the job to the least-loaded eligible live node,
  counting jobs the node already holds, and breaks ties by node ID. The same
  state always produces the same plan.
- **Owner scope.** Every job carries an owner. A node declares the owners it
  belongs to (`--owner acme`) and only ever sees, routes or pulls jobs of those
  owners. Another owner's jobs, packs, secret names and nodes never appear in
  its output. A job without an owner is never routed.
- **Leases and fencing.** Pulling a job takes a lease (30 seconds by default)
  and a fencing token that only ever increases. Renew before it expires. If a
  node stalls, the lease lapses and another node can pull the job with a higher
  token; the old holder's renew and complete are then refused. Two nodes racing
  for one job get exactly one claim. Pass the token to every external effect so
  a paused node cannot act after losing the job.
- **Local auth only.** Jobs needing `gh` go only to nodes whose own heartbeat
  reports a working GitHub CLI login (`phm node beat --probe-auth` runs
  `gh auth status` locally and reads only its exit code). Phantom never copies,
  stores or sends a token. Jobs carry secret **names** (`DEPLOY_KEY`), which each
  node resolves from its own custody; values are rejected at enqueue.

## Copy-paste example

```sh
# On each computer (the box coordinator included):
phm node join --node box --owner acme --caps build,gh --json   # prints a session number
phm node beat --node box --session 1 --usage 120 --probe-auth --json

# Anyone in the owner scope queues work:
phm node enqueue --job fix-123 --owner acme --requires gh --pack pack-fix-123 --secrets DEPLOY_KEY --json

# See where it would go, then pull on the node that should run it:
phm node plan --owner acme
phm node pull --node box --session 1 --json

# While working, renew; when done, complete (values come from the pull output):
phm node renew --job fix-123 --node box --session 1 --token 5 --leader-token 3
phm node complete --job fix-123 --node box --session 1 --token 5 --leader-token 3 --result done

# What this owner scope can see:
phm node status --owner acme
```

Add `--json` to any verb for deterministic output:
`{"schemaVersion":1,"command":"pull",...}` on success, or
`{"schemaVersion":1,"command":"pull","error":{"code","message","fix"}}`.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 lease or session lost or store unavailable, 2 bad usage.

## When something is refused

Every error ends with a fix. A job with no taker is shown by `phm node plan`
with the reason: no live node in that owner (join one), no node advertising the
caps (rejoin with them), or no node with a local `gh` login (`gh auth login`,
then `phm node beat --probe-auth`). A `lease-lost` error means stop work on
that job and pull again.

## Limits

State is a private local directory (`~/.ashlr/nodes`, or `$ASHLR_HOME/nodes`)
shared by processes on one host; see [the store notes](../src/core/drive/nodes/README.md)
for the single-host guarantee and failover rules. Fencing guarantees one
accepted completion, not exactly-once external effects, so effect sinks must
reject stale tokens. Owner scope filters what nodes and operators read through
these commands; it is not an access-control boundary against someone who can
read the state directory itself.
