# Local proactive-agent coordination

This milestone adds provider-neutral planning and a durable operator workflow.
It does not connect personal agents or execute provider work. Every command
reply contains `dispatchAuthorized: false`; configured profiles remain unqualified.

## Product direction

The intended product is one self-improving engineering workspace and service.
Ashlr's own service work provides the dogfooding path toward SaaS and autonomous
operations. Users configure goals, assignments and resources across providers:
coding subscriptions, CLI accounts, APIs, cloud funding and local models.
Allocation should improve independently verified outcome value, quality and
time within cost and authority limits; token consumption and activity counts
are not success criteria.

**Work with me** and **Work for me** are a continuum over the same tasks,
context, resources and evidence. A human should inspect priorities and criteria,
interject, approve where required, take ownership and resume delegated work
without losing history or creating duplicate attempts. Moving toward autonomy
does not expand permissions or spending limits. Resource and task views should
agree on identity, observation time, coverage and uncertainty.

These are product acceptance goals, not measured capabilities or completion
claims. The local mechanisms below support planning, manual coordination and
evidence inspection; seamless human takeover, qualified dispatch, independent
live evaluation and multi-user operation remain backlog work. See
[product acceptance](PROACTIVE-COORDINATION-BACKLOG.md#product-acceptance-direction)
and the proposed
[offline team contract](PROACTIVE-COORDINATION-BACKLOG.md#offline-team-contract-proposal).

## Operator workflow

In Proactive agents, add a provider/account/agent identity and declare the
capabilities and planning preferences you want. Multiple profiles can share a
provider or account. The immutable identity is separate from its editable name.
Old profile records hydrate metadata defaults without rewriting storage.

Record a local task with a tenant/project binding, stable task key, goal,
acceptance criteria, recipient and optional deadline/cost ceiling/attempt limit.
The packet endpoint derives a revision-bound local brief with no imported sources;
its coverage stays missing. Project and recipient fields are local planning
metadata, not verified account ownership or cross-account sharing permission.

Assign the reviewed recipient, prepare a handoff intent, record a manual report,
and review that exact result against the acceptance criteria. Operator reviews
are labeled separately from provider or independent verification. A failed review
leaves the task needing attention. A local notice can be acknowledged once.
No step sends work, reads an inbox, grants access, posts messages or spends money.
Canceling an attempt before any persisted handoff intent allows a new local
assignment without inventing a remote cancellation receipt. Once intent exists,
reassignment still requires exact host evidence of no start or confirmed cancel.

## Source contracts

- [Profiles](../src/core/proactive/profiles.ts) keep arbitrary provider slugs,
  account/agent identity, declared capabilities and preferences. Transport,
  entitlement, connection and pricing evidence remain separate prerequisites.
- [Coordinator](../src/core/proactive/coordination.ts) uses an immutable private
  ledger with CAS, request-digest replay, stable task identity, ownership epochs,
  manual report/verification receipts and notification state. Read-only replay
  precedes new-operation preference checks. Changed replay contents conflict.
- [Packets](../src/core/proactive/packets.ts) bind tenant, project, task, explicit
  source accounts, exact destination, artifact revision, scope and limits.
  Host authorization is supplied outside JSON and rechecked; parsing is not
  authorization. The current operator endpoint accepts only a local brief.
- [Planning](../src/core/proactive/planning.ts) ranks declared fit and preferences.
  Every candidate retains `executionEligible: false`. Scores do not measure
  quality, entitlement, quota, connection or spending eligibility.
- [API](../src/core/verse/proactive-coordination-api.ts) sits behind existing read
  session and operator mutation boundaries. It exposes no host reconciliation
  hook or live transport. [Wire references](../src/core/proactive/coordination-wire.ts)
  encode generated digests/IDs explicitly so general secret redaction stays active.

`GET /api/verse/proactive-agents/coordination` returns ledger quality, tasks,
packet recipients and local candidate reasons. `POST .../coordination/packet`
prepares the bounded brief; `POST .../coordination` accepts closed commands:
create, assign, handoff, report, operator-review, cancel and notification-ack.
Writes require the current revision and stable command ID. Preserve a command
after an uncertain response and retry its exact bytes; replay never dispatches.

## Recovery and evidence

Lease expiry blocks a new handoff and never transfers potentially active remote
work. Reassignment requires host evidence of no start or confirmed cancellation.
The optional host-observation port is injected by trusted code; tests use fixtures.
The HTTP API cannot fabricate accepted/running/cancel-confirmed observations.
Reconciliation binds the original command/task/attempt/revision and replays its
persisted result before consulting current host availability or observations.

Reports carry the original packet/attempt/epoch and exact result digest. New
current reports supersede older drafts; stale results remain history and cannot
advance the task. Semantic duplicate reports/reviews preserve acknowledged
notification state. Late reports preserve cancellation and verified terminal state.
Manual verification does not complete an engineering outcome or prove a merge,
deployment, package publication or provider execution.

Credential-shaped result text is refused so an operator cannot verify an exact
digest while its result bytes are hidden by public redaction. Storage is bounded,
private, no-follow and immutable. Hash-chain integrity is local consistency
evidence; it does not defend against a compromised same-user account rewriting
all records. Missing/degraded state cannot silently authorize work.
An independent private watermark chain is reserved and synced before every
ledger revision. Tail truncation, missing ledger/head, or a reservation without
its ledger record is held for explicit reconciliation; recovery cannot turn
that loss into a fresh request. Older unanchored journals are also withheld.
This detects ledger-only loss and interrupted publication. The same OS user
replacing or deleting both custody paths remains outside its guarantee; future
external effects need their own protected, independently bound replay custody.

Null cost means unknown. A stated cost ceiling and deadline are planning limits,
not balances, provider acceptance, timers, execution admission or authority.
No background supervisor consumes these records in this milestone.

## Resource evidence and offline planning

Open **Planning lab** to inspect evidence independently of the task board.
[Resource projection](../src/core/proactive/resource-evidence.ts) accepts public
snapshots through an injected cache getter. It separates identity, connection,
capabilities, entitlement, readiness, usage windows, credits and cost. Percent
usage never becomes tokens or dollars; cost remains actual, estimated or unknown.
Stale, conflicting and unmeasured observations cannot become current measurements.
Credit expiry and native units are retained without implying subscription rights.
Funding product/account and declared eligible/excluded surfaces are independent
fields. A promotion tied to one API organization cannot fund a coding
subscription or consumer app by association. Purchase/grant receipts retain
their original amounts as receipts; balances and consumed cost stay unknown
without separate observations. Repository examples are synthetic.

The default HTTP integration projects saved profile declarations. Native usage,
funding, connection and actual cost are unknown until a host supplies already
captured public snapshots. It never calls a collector, refreshes an account,
reads an assistant session or silently probes a provider. A refresh in this view
means rereading this local projection.

Configured connections and declared Bot account references are locators, not
verified distinct provider accounts, human identities or account control.
Resource count, current-reading count and distinct configured-reference count
describe different coverage. Aliases may point to one login; matching references
do not prove equivalence, independent capacity, ownership or sharing authority.
The qualified independent-account count stays unknown without genuine
source-owned identity and equivalence evidence. The
[provider grouping contract](../src/core/resources/provider-aggregation-types.ts)
keeps these counts separate and leaves verified account coverage unknown.

The local resource-display follow-up must retain native quota `observedAt` with
its original `quotaExpiresAt`, and credit observation time with its original
`creditsExpiresAt`. Connection checks and admission checks have independent
stamps; neither refreshes usage or credit evidence. Display-age policy can
shorten validity but cannot extend the original source TTL. Exact expiry
wakeups and focus rechecks only reevaluate retained evidence: they do not fetch,
restamp, admit work or spend. Expired readings remain visibly retained with
current availability unconfirmed; a current credit reading does not refresh an
expired subscription reading. See the
[source-expiry guard](../src/core/verse/quota-freshness.ts) and
[follow-up acceptance](PROACTIVE-COORDINATION-BACKLOG.md#local-resource-display-follow-up).
This source candidate includes the resource-display slice for 3.29.15. Verify
matching published artifacts before installation; the source version alone
does not establish publication, installed behavior or provider qualification.

[Routing lab](../src/core/proactive/routing-lab.ts) saves a deterministic shadow
evaluation of one exact saved task/brief, or runs a synthetic offline benchmark.
Synthetic System One responses exercise closed choices, order changes, malformed
answers, low confidence, cancellation and timeout/429/529 fallbacks. They are
fixtures, not TypeSafe calls or evidence that the model improves production
routing. The pinned model label records the intended contract, not model use.
Only local evaluation duration is measured; provider latency remains null.

Receipts pin request, input, snapshot and policy digests. An immutable intent is
saved before evaluation, and an interrupted intent stays uncertain. Retry the
same request; it does not restart an adapter. Changed request bytes conflict.
Preference proposals and withdrawals are inspectable local records and never
change production routing or grant authority.

`GET .../planning` lists receipts. `GET .../planning/resources` projects evidence.
`POST .../planning` records a preview, benchmark, proposal or withdrawal behind
the existing operator mutation gate. The preview accepts a saved task ID; host
code resolves its scope and exact packet. The browser cannot supply another
tenant, destination or source-account set. All results retain
`executionAuthorized: false`.

## Release readiness evidence

`GET .../planning/release` reports a missing target by default. The pure
[release evaluator](../src/core/proactive/release-readiness.ts) checks an exact
channel, target, version, source revision, artifact digest and attempt against
fresh tests, qualification, provenance, commissioning, provider-state and replay
receipts. Host evidence is independently validated through a separate injected
port; browser JSON cannot commission a target. All-fixture evidence remains
simulated even when the planned checks pass.

Post-check and recovery plans are channel-specific: npm uses a corrective newer
version, websites identify a previous deployment and affected targets, and
desktop recovery names signed prior assets and the customer update path.
These are structural planning checks; a later effect consumer must verify actual
signatures, deployment ownership, acceptance and recovery execution. Readiness
never authorizes publication, deployment, installation or service changes.

## Qualification still required

See [the backlog](PROACTIVE-COORDINATION-BACKLOG.md) for account-scoped transports,
proactive event ingestion, real cancellation/results, qualified cached funding
observations, live router evaluation, bounded goal execution and commissioned release targets.
OAuth, persistent account access, paid calls and cross-client sharing require
separate authorization. The installed app and live fleet remain unchanged.


<!-- page: PULSE-BRIDGE -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/PULSE-BRIDGE.md

# ashlr pulse connect — Hub→Pulse OTLP Bridge (M62)

`ashlr pulse connect` wires your local hub usage (GenAI spans: tokens, cost,
model, provider, tier) to pulse.ashlr.ai so your cofounder/team can see the
same activity in the shared fleet view.

The underlying transport already existed (OtlpHttpSink in
`src/core/observability/telemetry-sink.ts`); this command provides the UX to
configure and verify it.

---

## Quick start

```bash
# 1. Set the endpoint (defaults to pulse.ashlr.ai)
ashlr pulse connect https://pulse.ashlr.ai/api/otlp/v1/traces

# 2. Store your Pulse PAT (hidden prompt; never printed, never in config.json)
ashlr pulse connect --token

# 3. Verify
ashlr pulse connect --status
ashlr pulse connect --test
```

---

## Commands

### `ashlr pulse connect <endpoint>`

Writes the OTLP endpoint into `cfg.telemetry.pulse` in `~/.ashlr/config.json`.
Preserves all other config fields (budgetUsd, budgetWindow, etc.).

```bash
ashlr pulse connect https://pulse.ashlr.ai/api/otlp/v1/traces
```

The default endpoint when you run `ashlr pulse connect` with no URL is:
`https://pulse.ashlr.ai/api/otlp/v1/traces`

### `ashlr pulse connect --token`

Stores the Pulse PAT. The token is **never** printed, logged, or written to
`config.json`.

Three ways to give the PAT:

- `ashlr pulse connect --token` (no value): hidden prompt when stdin is a
  terminal. Without a terminal it exits 2 and points to `--token-stdin`.
- `printf %s "$PAT" | ashlr pulse connect --token-stdin`: reads exactly one
  non-empty line from a pipe (64 KiB cap). It refuses a terminal stdin.
- `ashlr pulse connect --token <pat>`: still works for existing scripts, but
  prints a warning on stderr, because a command-line argument is visible in the
  process list (`ps`) and in shell history.

Whichever form you use, the PAT is handed to `phantom add` on stdin only and
never appears in a child process's arguments.

**PAT storage and current sending support:**

1. **Phantom vault storage** — stored as secret `ASHLR_PULSE_TOKEN` via
   `phantom add ASHLR_PULSE_TOKEN --stdin` (the token is piped on stdin, never
   passed as an argument; phantom-secrets refuses positional secret values).
   To store it yourself, run `phantom add ASHLR_PULSE_TOKEN` for a hidden
   prompt. Requires `phantom.enabled: true` in
   your config and the `phantom` CLI on PATH.

2. **Current OTLP sending route: existing environment variable.** The command
   prints instructions to set:
   ```bash
   export ASHLR_PULSE_TOKEN=<your-token>
   ```
   Add to `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc` for persistence.

OtlpHttpSink currently reads a valid existing `ASHLR_PULSE_TOKEN` environment
value at emit time. Empty values and `phm_` placeholders are unavailable. A vault
store confirms storage only; child `phantom exec` cannot return a PAT to this
parent-process sender. Vault-backed sending requires a separately qualified
transport. No vault extraction or availability subprocess runs on emission.

### `ashlr pulse connect --status`

Reports the current bridge state:

```
  ashlr pulse — bridge status

  Endpoint     configured  https://pulse.ashlr.ai/api/otlp/v1/traces
  PAT          available
  Active sink  OtlpHttpSink
```

- **Endpoint**: whether `cfg.telemetry.pulse` is set.
- **PAT**: boolean only — `available` or `not found`. The value is never shown.
- **Active sink**: `OtlpHttpSink` (bridge active) or `LocalFileSink` (local only).

### `ashlr pulse connect --test`

Builds a minimal metadata-only GenAI span and calls `OtlpHttpSink.emit` once.
Reports the returned `{ok, detail}` (e.g., `HTTP 200`). Honest on failure.

```bash
ashlr pulse connect --test
# ok     sink=otlp  detail=HTTP 200
# OR
# fail   sink=otlp  detail=PAT unavailable
```

This is the real end-to-end verification. **Requires your actual Pulse PAT.**
Without it, the result will be `fail  detail=PAT unavailable`.

### `ashlr pulse connect --disconnect`

Clears `cfg.telemetry.pulse` from config. Telemetry reverts to `LocalFileSink`
(local JSONL under `~/.ashlr/telemetry/`). Other config fields are unchanged.

```bash
ashlr pulse connect --disconnect
# ✓ Endpoint cleared (was: https://pulse.ashlr.ai/api/otlp/v1/traces)
#   Telemetry will now use LocalFileSink (~/.ashlr/telemetry/).
```

---

## What is sent

Only **metadata** — never content. Each GenAI span carries:

| Field | OTLP attribute |
|-------|---------------|
| model id | `gen_ai.request.model` |
| provider | `gen_ai.system` |
| input tokens | `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` |
| output tokens | `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` |
| estimated cost USD | `gen_ai.usage.cost_usd` |
| run id | `ashlr.run.id` |
| tier | `ashlr.tier` |
| status | `ashlr.status` |

**Never sent**: prompt text, response text, tool arguments, file contents,
project paths, or secrets.

---

## PAT security

- The PAT is stored in Phantom (`ASHLR_PULSE_TOKEN`) or as an env var.
- It is placed **only** in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` HTTP header at
  emit time.
- It is never written to `config.json`, never logged, never in `TelemetryEmitResult.detail`.
- `patAvailable()` returns a boolean only — it never reads or returns the value.

---

## Live end-to-end test

The `--test` flag sends one real span to the configured endpoint. You need:

1. A configured endpoint (`ashlr pulse connect <url>`)
2. A valid Pulse PAT stored via `--token` or `ASHLR_PULSE_TOKEN`

Without a real PAT, the test will report `detail=PAT unavailable`. This is
expected and not a bug — the OtlpHttpSink degrades gracefully when no PAT is
found.

---

## Config storage

The endpoint is stored in `~/.ashlr/config.json` under `telemetry.pulse`:

```json
{
  "telemetry": {
    "pulse": "https://pulse.ashlr.ai/api/otlp/v1/traces",
    "budgetUsd": 50
  }
}
```

`saveConfig` uses a deep-merge pattern, so existing keys (`budgetUsd`,
`budgetWindow`, `govAction`, etc.) are always preserved.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---------|-------|-----|
| `detail=PAT unavailable` | No usable environment PAT | Set the existing `ASHLR_PULSE_TOKEN` environment route; vault storage alone does not activate sending |
| `detail=no endpoint configured` | `telemetry.pulse` not set | `ashlr pulse connect <url>` |
| `detail=HTTP 401` | Wrong or expired PAT | Refresh the existing `ASHLR_PULSE_TOKEN` environment route |
| `detail=request timed out` | Network/endpoint unreachable | Check connectivity; try `--test` again |
| Vault PAT stored, sink unavailable | In-process vault transport unsupported | Use the existing environment route; enabling Secrets does not qualify transport |

---

## Implementation files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/cli/pulse.ts` | `cmdPulseConnect` — the M62 subcommand |
| `src/core/observability/telemetry-sink.ts` | `OtlpHttpSink` — the OTLP emitter |
| `src/core/observability/otlp.ts` | `buildGenAiTrace` — span→OTLP shape |
| `src/core/config.ts` | `loadConfig` / `saveConfig` |
| `test/m62.pulse-connect.test.ts` | Hermetic tests (no network, no real ~/.ashlr) |


<!-- page: QUARANTINE-LEDGER -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/QUARANTINE-LEDGER.md

# Quarantine ledger

Flaky tests are retired through the ledger, never silently. `npm run gate` runs
[scripts/check-quarantine-ledger.mjs](../scripts/check-quarantine-ledger.mjs) in
Phase A; it fails CI Gate on any untracked skip or a diff that is only
additions. A test may be silenced only when a live row in
[queue/quarantine.tsv](../queue/quarantine.tsv) covers the skip marker.

## Row format

`queue/quarantine.tsv` starts with the header `test repo lead expiry`
(tab-separated, `#` comments and blank lines are ignored) and then holds one
row per skip marker:

| Column | Rule |
|--------|------|
| `test` | `<repo-relative test file>` covers every marker in that file; `<file> > <full name>` covers one marker. Full name is the describe path joined with ` > `, as Vitest reports it. |
| `repo` | `owner/name` the row applies to. Rows for other repos are shape-checked only; they cannot cover skips in this tree. |
| `lead` | Accountable owner: a person or team handle (for example `CI-Efficiency`). |
| `expiry` | `YYYY-MM-DD` (the whole UTC day) or an ISO-8601 datetime with offset. Must be in the future and no more than 7 days out — a quarantine is a short lease, not a permanent exemption. |

## Rules the verifier enforces

- **Tracked skip only.** Adding `.skip`, `.skipIf`, `.todo`, or an `x`-prefixed
  callee (`xit`, `xdescribe`, …) to a *running* test requires a covering row.
  The marker counts as a conversion only when the unskipped call appears in the
  diff's removed lines — keep the title on the call line.
- **Only additions fail.** A skip that is only an addition — a test born
  disabled, including every marker in a new test file — fails even with a row.
  Rows added to the ledger must also cover a live marker; a diff that only
  adds rows covering nothing fails.
- **Expiry is enforced.** A skip covered only by an expired row fails
  (`expired-skip`), and any expired row left in the file fails (`expired-row`).
  To renew, replace the row and keep the marker.
- **Pairs are atomic.** Unskip the test and delete its row in the same change;
  a leftover row covering no live marker is a `stale-row` violation.
- **`.only` is never legal** (`focused-test`), and skip markers need literal
  titles (`dynamic-title`).
- **Security R8.** `secret-shape`, `gitleaks`, `cargo-deny` and `ci-gate` are
  non-quarantinable, enforced in the verifier code
  (`NON_QUARANTINABLE`): a skip inside a matching file, or a ledger row naming
  a protected check, fails the gate. Security lanes can never be silenced
  through the ledger.

## Usage

```sh
node scripts/check-quarantine-ledger.mjs --base <merge-base>   # diff vs a base
node scripts/check-quarantine-ledger.mjs --diff change.diff    # a stored diff
node scripts/check-quarantine-ledger.mjs                       # ledger hygiene only
node scripts/check-quarantine-ledger.mjs --base HEAD~1 --json  # machine-readable
```

`npm run check:quarantine` runs the ledger-only form. `npm run gate` runs the
diff form against the merge-base (untracked files count as fully added) and,
under `gate:full` where no diff exists, the ledger-hygiene form.

## Quarantining a test

1. Convert the running call to a skip marker (`it('x'` → `it.skip('x'`).
2. Add a row: `test/x.test.ts > suite > x`, this repo, your handle, an expiry
   at most 7 days out.
3. Land both together. To un-quarantine, remove the marker and its row in the
   same change; to keep it parked longer, renew the row before it lapses.

Scope note: the verifier is diff-scoped for markers — a skip committed before
this check exists is not retro-flagged, but a row can never make it valid and
removing its marker still requires removing the row. Row liveness is checked
against the whole tree, so stale and foreign rows are always re-validated.


<!-- page: QUEUE-STATS -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/QUEUE-STATS.md

# Queue statistics

`phm queue stats --json` reads the local metadata journal at
`~/.ashlr/queue/visits.jsonl` and returns station and pool aggregates for sliding
1 hour, 24 hour and 7 day windows. `--window <seconds>` selects one window.
The command is read-only and requires no service or credentials. Missing journals
produce empty groups; malformed records fail explicitly without echoing contents.

Producers can call `recordQueueVisit` from `src/core/queue/journal.ts` with an
opaque visit `id`, `station`, `pool`, and epoch-millisecond `arrivedAt`. Append a
snapshot with `startedAt` when service begins and `completedAt` when it ends.
All snapshots for a visit must retain the same arrival time, station and pool;
the last appended snapshot wins. A retry or station transfer gets a new visit ID.
Do not put prompts, credentials or task descriptions in these labels. Existing
fleet events do not contain these timestamps: producers must record visits before
the estimator can report them. The journal currently has no automatic retention.

Windows are half-open `[now - window, now)`. Arrivals divided by window seconds
are `lambda`; `mu` is completed visits divided by their total service seconds
(the observed per-worker service rate), and `rho = lambda / mu` is offered load
in worker equivalents, not a capacity-adjusted utilization percentage. No service
sample yields null `mu` and `rho`; zero-duration service alone also yields null.

`queueLength` is time-average waiting occupancy; `wip` is time-average total
occupancy, integrating overlapping visits and clipping carry-in and unfinished
visits to each window. `currentQueueLength` and `currentWip` are endpoint counts.
`wait` is mean arrival-to-start time for visits completed within the window.
Rates use seconds and wait/residence durations use seconds, while window bounds
and `windowMs` use milliseconds.

The Little's law check compares measured `L = wip` with `lambda * W`, where `W`
is mean arrival-to-completion residence for departures in the window. Relative
drift is `abs(L - lambda*W) / L`, flagged only above 20%. Two zeros have zero
drift; zero L with nonzero expectation has drift 1. No departures yields null
W, drift and flag. Short windows, changing load and censored visits can flag
legitimate boundary effects; the check is diagnostic, not an admission control.


<!-- page: QUEUE -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/QUEUE.md

# Phantom job queue

`phm queue` owns a dispatch-neutral `queue.v1` snapshot at
`~/.ashlr-runs/queue/queue.v1.json`. `--dir <directory>` selects an isolated store.
This command does not start workers, change dispatchd, push code, access vendor
authentication, call inference, or fetch credentials. dispatchd remains the
fallback until a separate, explicit cutover. Do not dispatch the same imported
jobs from both schedulers. Publication remains exclusively through publish.sh.

## Commands

```sh
phm queue import router-queue.md --json
phm queue list --json
phm queue add RQ-EXAMPLE --priority P0 --pool codex-personal --tier frontier \
  --repo phantom --scope 'Implement the feature' --acceptance 'Tests pass' \
  --deps RQ-PREREQUISITE --json
phm queue claim RQ-EXAMPLE --owner worker-1 --json
phm queue done RQ-EXAMPLE --owner worker-1 --pr-url https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/pull/123 --json
phm queue done RQ-EXAMPLE --owner worker-1 --json
phm queue block RQ-OTHER --owner worker-2 --reason 'Waiting for prerequisite' --json
phm queue export --json > queue-backup.json
phm queue export --md --json
```

`claim` requires READY and all dependencies present and DONE. Missing dependencies
fail closed. `done --pr-url` records PR-OPEN without releasing the claim; `done`
without a PR URL records DONE. These are operator-reported states, not evidence
of GitHub merge checks. `block` records BLOCKED and closes the active claim.
Completion and blocking require the last active claim's owner. This is local
coordination, not an authentication boundary. There is no automatic reclaim,
retry, promotion of HOLD/PROPOSED, dispatch, or merge.

`--help` is side-effect free. Unknown commands, flags, irrelevant options and
missing operands fail before mutation. All commands support `--json`, including
errors; failures return exit code 1. `list` and JSON export do not create files.

## Contract and interoperability

The canonical TypeScript contract and runtime validator are in
[`schema.ts`](../src/core/queue/schema.ts). A document contains `schema: "queue.v1"`
and a `jobs` array. Each job has a unique `id`, status
`READY|CLAIMED|PR-OPEN|BLOCKED|HOLD|PROPOSED|SPLIT-PARENT|FIXUP|LAND|DONE|RETIRED|DROPPED`,
`priority`, `pool`, `tier`, `repo`, `deps`, `scope`, `acceptance`, and `claims`.
Claims record `owner`, `claimedAt`, and optional `finishedAt`. Jobs optionally
carry `prUrl` and `blockedReason`. Timestamps are ISO dates, PR URLs are
credential-free HTTPS, and self-dependencies and duplicate dependency IDs are
refused. Cyclic dependencies cannot be claimed because all dependencies must be
DONE. A document may also carry `raw` (unparsed job-shaped lines kept verbatim
with a reason) and `warnings` (non-fatal import observations).

The store API is a clean seam for a future scheduler: `read`, `add`, `import`,
`claim`, `finish`, and `mirror`. No executor is imported. Status changes happen
inside the same transaction that checks readiness and dependencies.

Markdown import accepts one job per line in either direction of the live
router format: fields may sit before or after the id, and operational tokens
(timestamps, worker names, pool names) may precede the id:

```text
- READY RQ-EXAMPLE (P0 FLAGSHIP, pool=codex-personal, tier=frontier, repo=phantom, deps=RQ-A|RQ-B, EO 13:45): Scope text. Acceptance: criteria.
- CLAIMED 14:26 dispatchd codex-personal RQ-EXAMPLE (P0, pool=codex-personal, tier=frontier, repo=phantom): Scope text.
- PR-OPEN (https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/pull/123, bridge 12:23, EO 12:40) RQ-EXAMPLE: Scope text.
```

Bullets are optional; status may use brackets or Markdown bold and IDs may be
bold. Job IDs use the `RQ-` prefix; the job id is the last `RQ-*` token in the
header (everything before the first `:` that follows the first `RQ-*` token),
excluding tokens claimed by a dependency or `children`/`parent` keyword. Field
groups are balanced parentheses, so inner `(...)` pairs do not truncate them.
Fields accept comma or semicolon separators. Routing fields (`priority`, `pool`,
`tier`, `repo`, `deps`) come only from parenthesized groups; `pool` may also be
inferred from a known pool name in the pre-id tokens. Dependencies use `|`, `+`,
commas, or spaces within the field (CLI `--deps` uses commas), and are also
collected from prose (`deps=`, `depends on`, `after`, `waits for`, `blocked by`,
`needs`, `requires`) anywhere on the line. On the Mac restocker, unmet `after=`
deps become `PARKED-DEP.<lane>` rows whose prompts carry `DEPENDENCY GATE: <ids>`;
restock unparks them when every id has a `MERGED` outcome in `jobs.jsonl` (see
[Mac queue scripts](../contrib/mac/README.md)). `phm fleet dep-gate --json` is the
read-only gate over the same evidence: it scans non-PARKED `ready.tsv` rows and
exits 1 when a queued prompt's declared gate ids are not all MERGED.
`children=`/`parent=` tokens mark
related ids, never the job id or a dependency. `worker=`/`owner=` plus a
`claimed=`/`claimedAt=` ISO timestamp import as a real claim; `reason=`,
`blocked=`, `PR=` and `BASE_OVERRIDE=` text stays intact in `source`. Unknown
fields, headings, comments, whitespace, line endings, and the original text are
retained in `source`. Absent routing fields become `unspecified`, priority
defaults to P2, and absent acceptance becomes an empty string. Such jobs need
operator review before scheduler cutover. Imported CLAIMED and PR-OPEN jobs
without importable claim fields retain their status but have no invented owner
or timestamps, so they cannot be finished through this CLI; jobs that depend on
them cannot be claimed until they are resolved.

Job-shaped lines that cannot be parsed (an unknown status, no `RQ-` id, or a
duplicate id) never abort the import: each becomes a `raw` record with its
line number, verbatim text and reason, and a warning is collected on the
document and printed to stderr by `phm queue import`. Plain prose lines are
left as `source` text, not raw records. Self-dependencies are dropped with a
warning, and an unbalanced `(` is treated as literal text with a warning.
JSON import validates the same schema. Import requires an empty queue; it never
replaces live state. Use a separate directory to inspect a later snapshot.

### Tier values

A router-queue line's `tier=` must be one of `frontier`, `work`, `mid` or
`fast`. dispatchd skips any other value without an error, so the job never
runs. `queuegen` refuses to write a line with another tier, and
`router-lint` reports such an admission line as `invalid` with reason
`unknown-tier`. The refusal names the allowed values and, where one is near,
the closest match: `standard` means `work`, `medium` means `mid`, `low` means
`fast` and `high` means `frontier`. Nothing is accepted by alias; write the
tier name itself. The vocabulary lives in
[`queue-tier.ts`](../src/core/drive/queue-tier.ts). Keep it identical to
`TIERS` in `contrib/mac/dispatchd.py`.

`exportMarkdown` round-trips unchanged imports byte-for-byte. State changes
update the status while retaining original text and append a comment with claim,
PR and block metadata. JSON export is the complete backup and restore format.
`export --md` writes `queue.mirror.md` with a read-only notice and mode 0444 on
POSIX. It never overwrites `router-queue.md`; the mirror is not an input channel.

## Storage and failure behavior

Every mutation and mirror export acquires `queue.v1.lock` with exclusive file
creation, then reads and validates the snapshot under that lock. Concurrent
callers wait up to five seconds. Updates use a unique private temporary file,
fsync its contents, and atomically rename it over the snapshot. Readers observe
a whole old or new snapshot. Files use mode 0600 and newly created directories
use 0700. The existing dispatchd directory's permissions are not changed.
Corrupt snapshots fail closed instead of becoming empty queues.

## Load-aware admission

`phm pool admission [--json]` is a read-only report of the dispatchd load gate:
1-min loadavg and its limit, `ncpu`, process and live-worktree counts, the daemon
tick age, the global running cap, running jobs, the `queue/install.lock` holder and
`admit` true or false with the reason. It claims and launches nothing. The gate
logic itself lives in `contrib/mac/dispatchd.py`; see `contrib/mac/README.md`.
The global cap is adaptive (RQ-QUEUE-BATCH-1). dispatchd raises it while load,
memory, swap, disk, process count and provider rate limits have headroom, and backs
off before they run out. The report shows it as `adaptiveCap`. An operator
`hard_cap` in `slots.json` is optional; without one, `hardCap` is `null`. The same
change batches related ready tasks into one agent session. See
[adaptive concurrency and batching](../contrib/mac/README.md#adaptive-concurrency-and-batching).

`ashlr fleet admission [--json]` reads that stored verdict from `queue/status.json`
and says why each lane is waiting: held, at target, blocked by the global cap, or ok.
It does not probe the host or launch work. It exits 1 when any lane is blocked by
the global cap with 5 or more jobs queued. Other waits are `ashlr fleet lane-idle`.

`ashlr fleet lane-share [--json]` reads the same file and prints each lane's share
of the fleet: one line per lane with running of target and queued, marked `starved`
(10 or more queued and none running) or `full` (running equals target), then one
line with fleet running against the admission cap. It exits 1 when a lane is
starved while the admission reason starts with `at_cap` — queued work parked
because the whole fleet is full, the case `ashlr fleet trim` suggests a slot move for.

`ashlr fleet starved [--json]` reads the same file and prints only the lanes that
still have queued work: running of target and queued, marked `starved` when a lane
is below its target while the admission reason starts with `at_cap`, then one line
with the admission running, cap and reason. It exits 1 when any lane has 10 or
more jobs queued and none running.

Locks are never stolen on age or PID heuristics. If a writer crashes, an operator
must confirm that no writer is running before removing its orphaned
`queue.v1.lock`. A busy lock leaves the snapshot unchanged. A crash before rename
can leave an unused temporary file; it is never read as queue state. Atomicity
assumes a local filesystem with exclusive creation and atomic rename. Directory
entries are not fsynced, so sudden power loss is outside the durability guarantee.

The host dispatchd README was not accessible in the implementation workspace.
`test/fixtures/queue/router-queue-live.md` is a scrubbed snapshot covering every
status prefix and line shape observed in the live queue; the suite imports it
with zero unparsed lines and round-trips it byte-for-byte. Verifying the real
snapshot end to end remains a required cutover step, not a claimed validation.

## Replay failed attempts

`ashlr queue replay --failed --since 2026-11-02T00:00:00Z --query repair --dry-run --json`
lists proposed READY runs without writing. Remove `--dry-run` to persist them.
Failed means BLOCKED with a finished claim; `--since` filters that completion
instant inclusively and `--query` matches job ID, repo, scope, acceptance or reason
(case insensitive). Omit either filter to include all failed attempts.
`--mode replay_failed` is the default. `--mode replay_failed_and_dependents`
includes transitive dependents in dependency order and maps their dependencies
to replay runs. Active original dependents must finish before replay. Claims still require
all dependencies DONE. Each new run records `replayOf` (the original run ID)
and `replayedAt`; original runs remain unchanged. Concurrent or repeated requests
reuse active READY, CLAIMED or PR-OPEN replays. Completed replays allow a later
explicit replay. Queue snapshots persist lineage across process restarts.

## Group failed jobs by error

`ashlr issues` (also `phm issues`) reads the queue and groups failed jobs (BLOCKED
with a finished claim) by their error text. Ids, timestamps and long numbers are
ignored, so one problem counts once. Each group shows a count and a few sample
job ids. It never writes unless you add `--retry`, which queues one READY retry per
failed job using the same lineage as `queue replay` (repeats do not duplicate).
Add `--json` for `{ v, failed, groups: [{ error, count, samples, jobs }] }`, or
`{ v, retried: [{ id, retry }] }` with `--retry`. Use `--dir` to pick a queue directory.
# Lane queue counts

Run `phm fleet queue-counts --json` for ready, parked and running counts and
the oldest wait per lane. `oldestWaitSeconds` covers ready and parked jobs,
using `queued` timestamps in `~/.ashlr-runs/metrics/jobs.jsonl`. It is `null`
when there are no waiting jobs, the queue or metrics are unavailable, or any
waiting job has missing or conflicting enqueue timestamps. The command reads
at most 2 MiB of metrics and treats a larger ledger as unavailable. Without
`--json`, the same command prints a plain-language report. Use `--root /path`
to inspect a different runs directory.

# Quickstart — Phantom

Latest dated changelog release (verify promoted package availability before installing):

```sh
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom@3.29.13
phm --version
```

Phantom by AshlrAI is the everyday coding-agent workbench, formerly Ashlr Verse.
The Universe experiment kernel is a separate, bounded source-checkout path below.
Installing Phantom, enrolling a repo, starting a resident fleet and publishing
its work are distinct steps.

The primary CLI is `phm`; `ashlr` remains compatible. Current source uses
`@ashlr/phantom` in `ashlrai/phantom`. Find the current qualified release at
[GitHub releases](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/releases/latest).
This source tree targets version 3.30.24; check canonical release availability and exact matching assets before installation.
The verified 3.25.3 compatibility release remains `@ashlr/hub`.
Local routes remain `/verse/`, and the published macOS app is `Phantom.app`. See
[the product naming guide](PHANTOM-BRAND.md).

[phm.dev](https://phm.dev) introduces the Phantom workbench;
[phm.dev/secrets](https://phm.dev/secrets) introduces Phantom Secrets.
Use the qualified workbench release links below to install. Website availability
does not establish installed fleet or hosted-service readiness.

## From public Connect to your first local session

If you arrived through the public **Connect** experience, continue with the
local workbench installation below. A public page or a selected provider does
not verify local installation, account sign-in, model access or available quota.
If an advertised resource is unavailable, use another eligible resource or
finish its setup before sending work; no working hosted session is implied.

1. Install a qualified release, check `phm --version`, then run `phm verse`
   to open the local workbench. `phm doctor` checks this machine; it does not
   establish provider readiness or authorize unattended work.
2. In **Resources**, inspect the account you intend to use and its chat readiness.
   Sign in through that provider's own CLI, configure an API resource, or start
   a tool-capable local model. Missing or stale usage remains unknown, and a
   saved account or model listing does not prove entitlement or usable capacity.
   Keep subscription allowances, API credits and local hardware separate.
3. Choose **Work with me** → **New chat** and select a scratch project or a
   public repository you can edit. Confirm the selected folder before sending;
   saving a project does not enroll it for unattended fleet work.
4. Start with a small task, for example: “Fix one typo in README.md, show the
   diff and report the checks you ran. Leave the change uncommitted.” Review the
   diff and actual verification results before accepting the result. If a turn
   is held, inspect the resource's reason; connection alone is not readiness.

Use **Automatic** for an eligible resource, or **Advanced** to choose an account
or model explicitly. No eligible resource means setup is still incomplete.
Fleet activation is a separate, optional step after this first interactive task.
See the [first-session guide](VERSE.md#first-local-session) for the same checklist.

## Open Phantom

### CLI on macOS, Linux or Windows

Install Node.js 22.15+ and Git, then install the canonical package's promoted release:

```sh
node --version  # must print v22.15.0 or newer; npm only warns on older Node
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
phm --version   # report the installed version
phm verse
```

Phantom opens at `http://127.0.0.1:7777/verse/` and binds to loopback. The CLI
prints a read token for the browser and asks for a separate mutation token
before your first chat or other change. Keep both tokens private. Confirm
the installed version with `phm --version`. Browse
[GitHub releases](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/releases/latest) and select
that same version before using desktop installer artifacts.
Use `npm install -g @ashlr/phantom@latest` for current installation. To reproduce
a particular release, pin a published version and use its matching desktop
artifacts; the source candidate is not proof of publication. Package
installation, desktop installation and fleet activation are separate steps.

### Desktop app on Apple silicon Mac

Qualified releases from 3.29.8 support `phm desktop install [--apply]` for a new
Apple silicon Mac installation. Check `phm --version` and use its matching
public release. See the [consumer installation notes](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/desktop/README.md#consumer-first-install).
Clean-Mac acceptance remains unverified; command publication does not establish
that acceptance.

The [current qualified macOS release](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/releases/latest)
provides the signed `Phantom_<version>_aarch64.app.tar.gz` archive and paired
[`latest.json`](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/releases/latest/download/latest.json),
rather than a DMG. Match these artifacts to the installed CLI version.
Use the qualified signed-update flow in an eligible installed app, or the
maintainer artifact path in the
[desktop installation guide](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/desktop/README.md#install).
Downloading or unpacking the archive alone is not qualified installation.
The [3.27.0 DMG](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/releases/download/v3.27.0/Phantom_3.27.0_aarch64.dmg)
remains a historical download. The app inside the DMG is
locally signed; the DMG is unsigned. Neither is Apple Developer ID notarized.
Do not install the old 3.25.2 DMG, whose updater
client reproduced a startup abort. Publication and installed startup acceptance
remain separate. The desktop includes the CLI and the same console. The current
app is locally signed, not Apple Developer ID notarized;
macOS may require **Open Anyway** on first launch.
For a source build and local signing, follow [Releasing locally](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/RELEASING-LOCALLY.md).
There is no Linux or Windows desktop package in this release; use the CLI above.

### Complete your first readiness check

1. Open **Resources** in `phm verse` and connect an account or configure a local
   model. Check **chat readiness**: a connected badge alone does not mean the
   resource is usable. Resolve signed-out, unknown usage, exhausted quota or
   capacity holds before starting; follow the resource's displayed recovery step.
2. Select your project and workspace. Confirm the repository path so the task
   uses the project you intended.
3. In **Work with me**, ask: “Read the README and name one test command with its
   source path. Do not change files.” Verify the cited file and command in your
   project. This is done when the answer checks out; a waiting task or connection
   alone does not pass. If it waits, return to Resources and resolve the hold.

`phm doctor` checks the machine and `phm onboard` checks activation prerequisites;
neither result proves a connected resource can complete your task. Check **fleet
readiness** separately before unattended work: a successful chat does not establish
fleet authority. The first task above does not require enrolling the repository.

### Read the workbench before starting work

- In the desktop top bar, expand **Automatic awake** to inspect the idle-sleep
  request and choose **Automatic during local work**. A browser reports host
  power unavailable; display sleep, locking and lid closure remain separate.
- Expand **Resources** for dated usage and Devin organization consumption.
  Consumed ACUs are distinct from the tracked budget and do not show remaining
  subscription or purchased credits.
- Subscription allowances, API credits and local hardware are separate readings.
  Saved Grok Bot profiles do not inherit Grok Build usage. Promotional API credits
  remain held until their balance, expiry and funding boundary are verified;
  purchased credits are excluded from automatic reset spending. Read
  [resource evidence](RESOURCE-EVIDENCE.md) for context, slot and speed provenance.
- Open **Growth** for source-qualified adoption readings. Retrievals, traffic
  and downloads use different windows and do not count active engineers.
- In Fleet or Resources, inspect **Use allowance before resets**. Saving On
  does not establish execution eligibility. Current unbound producers retain
  the saved reserve; Off disables both reset priority and reserve shrinking.
  Read [the reset guide](RESET-AWARE-SCHEDULING.md) before changing the setting.

### Choose how to work

**Work with me** is a conversation you steer: Automatic picks an eligible
resource; Advanced pins an explicit account or model. Choose **Manager** in the
Auto seat menu when you want planning, delegation and review in one conversation.
It uses the resident fleet and its existing authority.

**Work for me** is a durable outcome: the Leader refines priorities and ready
tasks, while you inspect progress and answer decisions in Phantom or configured
Telegram. Enabling a Manager on an outcome adds its coordination and review path.
Saving an outcome or changing workspaces does not start the fleet.

Supported CLI accounts, configured APIs and tool-capable local models share the
workbench, but keep their own billing and limits. In **Resources**, check both
chat and fleet readiness. Signed out, missing usage, exhausted quota, reserved
capacity or missing authority can hold work; connection alone is not readiness.
See [Automatic work](AUTOMATIC-OUTCOMES.md) for resource boundaries and recovery.

To give Claude Code, Codex or Cursor the tools of Phantom Secrets, Locus and
Ashlr MD through one MCP connection, see
[One connection for every agent](COMPANIONS.md#one-connection-for-every-agent).

### Troubleshoot account setup and return to the tour

- If no account appears, open **Apps & Accounts** under the gear. Sign in to
  the supported provider's own CLI, or start Ollama for local models. For
  separate native accounts, follow [seat commissioning](RESOURCE-POOLS.md#commission-native-accounts-and-local-capacity);
  preparing a profile alone does not sign in or enroll it.
- If a seat is signed out, choose **Reconnect** where offered and finish the
  provider's sign-in in Terminal. Opening sign-in from Phantom is supported on
  macOS; otherwise use the provider's own CLI. Choose **Check again** where
  offered to refresh health. For a spent or unavailable seat, inspect its
  reported reason and reset in **Resources**; a connection does not guarantee
  available quota or permission to run.
- If you closed or skipped the tour, open **Settings → Onboarding** and choose
  **Replay**. Closing the tour card folds it back to its chip; **Skip setup**
  or the chip's × dismisses it. Opening Settings does not complete the tour.
- If the workbench itself is closed, run `phm verse` to open it again. Keep
  the printed tokens private. See [Automatic work](AUTOMATIC-OUTCOMES.md) for
  readiness and recovery, and [the Phantom guide](VERSE.md) for the interface.

### Make your first useful turn

1. Choose **Work with me**, open **New chat** and choose a scratch project or
   public repository for your first task. Saving a folder as a project does not
   enroll it for unattended fleet work.
2. Use provider CLIs you are already signed in to, or start Ollama with
   a tool-capable local model. **Automatic** chooses an eligible resource;
   open **Advanced** if you want to pin an account or model. For separate Claude Code, Codex and Grok accounts,
   follow [seat commissioning](RESOURCE-POOLS.md#commission-native-accounts-and-local-capacity).
   Each vendor signs in through its own CLI; Phantom does not take its password.
   Providers may have their own costs; check the selected resource and budget
   before starting the turn.
3. Ask for a small, checkable change. Inspect reported tools, context and
   sources, then review the diff and verification results before accepting it.
   When sharing setup feedback, include the task and checks, and keep private
   code, credentials and unredacted logs out of the report.
   Usage can be reported, estimated or unknown; a producer's success message
   alone does not prove delivery. Use **⌘K** to find actions and **⌘J** for
   **Needs you**. The full interface is in the [Phantom guide](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/VERSE.md).

Choose **Work for me**, open Fleet and select **New outcome**. Describe the
result, select enrolled repositories and add observable acceptance criteria.
The Leader refines the work; expand its tasks to inspect runs, proposals and
verified merge evidence. Edit, pause or resume the outcome as it evolves.
See [Automatic work](AUTOMATIC-OUTCOMES.md). Standing instructions also guide
the Leader's fleet planning. Changing workspaces only navigates; it does not start the fleet or
change your permission mode. Optional planning, CI and spend settings are under
**Options** when creating an agent.

Several available seats can receive the same task, each in its own workspace.
There is no preset six-seat fan-out ceiling. Workspace retention defaults to
25; `ASHLR_VERSE_AGENT_CAP=none` disables retention-driven automatic archiving,
or use a positive safe-integer count. Capacity and provider quotas still govern
execution. This environment setting applies when the Phantom process starts and
does not widen fleet authority.

The optional phone gateway is a separate, Access-protected and Mac-approved
surface; [set it up](REMOTE-PHONE.md) rather than exposing the main loopback
console. Resident autonomy is macOS-only and starts dormant. Inspect the
**installed** release with `ashlr authority status` and
`ashlr authority setup --dry-run --json`, then use the
[autonomy setup guide](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/AUTONOMY-SETUP.md) if you want to sign a standing grant.
A source checkout or a static guide cannot establish the current service state
on your Mac.

## Run a bounded Universe experiment

This path is for evaluating the local experiment kernel from a trusted source

|--------------------|----------------|
| Run reproducible code experiments without model credentials | [Current Universe kernel](#run-the-current-universe-kernel) |
| Inspect one experiment store and its evidence graph | [Scoped Universe console](ASHLR-UNIVERSE.md#observe-one-universe-store) |

## Run the current Universe kernel

Prerequisites: a trusted source checkout, Git and Node.js 22.15+. Current Universe
experiment execution additionally requires macOS `sandbox-exec`; Linux isolation
and Windows execution are not yet supported for that path. Building the CLI and
reading supported console evidence are separate from executing experiments.

1. In the repository root, install the locked dependencies and build the CLI and
   web assets. Installation and build execute trusted repository scripts locally:

   ```sh
   npm ci
   npm run build
   node bin/ashlr universe help
   ```

2. Choose a new absolute private experiment root, outside the source checkout,
   with an existing physical parent. Run the demonstration only in that selected
   root; it creates a seed repository and performs bounded local code execution:

   ```sh
   node bin/ashlr universe demo --root /absolute/private/experiments --json
   ```

   Expect tested code variants, rejected candidates and later-generation parent
   references. This deterministic example proves the experiment mechanism, not
   model capability or accepted product value. No provider account is required.

3. Inspect the same root without starting another experiment:

   ```sh
   node bin/ashlr universe status --root /absolute/private/experiments --json
   node bin/ashlr universe archive --root /absolute/private/experiments --json
   ```

4. Start its foreground, read-only loopback console:

   ```sh
   node bin/ashlr universe console --root /absolute/private/experiments --json
   ```

   Open the printed URL, enter its private read token and inspect campaigns,
   trials and the evidence graph. Keep the terminal running; Ctrl-C stops this
   console. Never share its startup token or put it in a URL. If records appear
   missing, compare the console's displayed root with the command above before
   creating more state. See the [operator guide](ASHLR-UNIVERSE.md) for failure
   recovery and campaign controls.

The demonstration can be replaced with explicitly configured local-model
generation or the opt-in [resource generation bridge](ASHLR-UNIVERSE.md#generate-candidates-through-an-enrolled-resource-pool).
The bridge uses enrolled native or local workers through Resource Pools; it needs
an explicit private runtime binding, fresh observations and resource limits
before dispatch. The fleet map does not create accounts or evidence. Follow the
commissioning guide above before authorizing generation.

## General Phantom and legacy fleet setup

`ashlr init`, `ashlr serve`, `ashlr enroll` and `ashlr daemon` remain compatibility
surfaces beneath the workbench. For their command and safety contracts, use the
[Phantom reference](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/HUB-REFERENCE.md). The current first-run console is
`ashlr verse` at `/verse/`; older `/` and `/next/` dashboard guidance should not
be used as a Phantom onboarding path.

To inspect resident authority, use the **installed** binary, not an unbuilt
source checkout:

```sh
ashlr authority status
ashlr authority setup --dry-run --json
ashlr authority resident status --json
```

A grant, service installation and live resident process each require their own
verification. The [autonomy setup guide](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/AUTONOMY-SETUP.md) covers signing,
starting, stopping and scope. The [phone guide](REMOTE-PHONE.md) covers the
separate protected gateway. Neither path makes the main loopback server public.

Workspace retention does not reserve infinite hardware. Creation refuses an exhausted dedicated-port range before archiving or creating a workspace; restore refuses an occupied original range. Create and restore admissions serialize across repositories in the owning Phantom process. Separate Phantom processes do not share that reservation lock. A repository needing no dedicated ports may configure `ports: 0` in `.ashlr/verse/workspace.json`.

# Docs Radar

Radar records changes to public documentation and package metadata. It makes
read-only HTTPS GET requests without credentials and saves normalized observations
locally. A change is evidence of different source content, not proof that a
feature is available or that a model capability works.

## Commands

Copy and paste:

```sh
phm radar list --json
phm radar run --json
phm radar diff --json
```

`list` validates and displays the catalogue without network access. `run` visits
verified sources sequentially, independently reporting each outcome. Unverified
sources remain visible but are never fetched. `diff` reads local state only and
compares the last two successful observations. The first observation is a
`baseline`, not a report that every entry was newly added.

All verbs accept `--json`. Help supports `phm radar --help --json`. List emits
`{ok,sources}`; run emits `{ok,results,warnings}` and diff emits `{ok,results}`.
A run reports individual fetch or parse failures as warnings and exits 0 unless
every source errors or the catalogue is invalid. Diff reports unavailable, stale
or missing evidence as an error. Invalid arguments exit 2. A throttled run exits 0 and includes `retryAt`; it does
not claim to have refreshed the source.

## Source catalogue

Each entry has exactly `id`, `product`, `url`, `kind`, and `verified`.
Kinds are `page`, `atom`, `rss`, `npm`, `pypi`, or `json`. IDs are unique lowercase
letters, digits and hyphens, up to 80 characters. `verified` is a boolean and
means a maintainer checked the public endpoint, not that the content is trusted.

The catalogue covers Claude, Codex, Grok, Cursor, Devin, GLM, Gemini,
Antigravity, MLX, Qwen, GitHub CLI, Vercel CLI, Supabase CLI, Wrangler,
Context7 and the MCP SDK. Grok Bot and Grok Build use their RSS feeds for
fetching their changelogs.

Only public HTTPS URLs on port 443 are accepted. Credentials, query strings,
fragments, IP literals, local hostnames and extra configuration such as headers
are refused. Runtime DNS answers are checked against private and reserved IPv4
ranges and pinned to the request. IPv4 DNS connectivity is required. Redirects
are refused, including redirects to another public URL; update the catalogue to
the verified final endpoint instead. No auth headers, cookies, proxy credentials,
provider accounts or browser sessions are used. Responses must be HTTP 200 and
uncompressed. The entire read, including DNS, has a 15-second deadline and a
2 MiB body limit. Errors use fixed diagnostics without response bodies.

## Observations and diffs

- Atom: entry IDs and titles, sorted by ID. XML namespaces, character references,
  CDATA and text/HTML/XHTML titles are supported. DTDs, duplicate IDs, malformed
  feeds and entries without identity/title are refused. Diffs report added and
  removed IDs and changed titles. Removal means absence from this fetched feed
  window, not deletion from the provider's complete history.
- RSS 2.0: item GUIDs, or links when GUIDs are absent, and titles. The same
  XML safety rules and added, removed and changed title diffs apply as for Atom.
- npm: `dist-tags.latest`, or `version` for a version-specific endpoint.
- PyPI: `info.version`.
- Page: SHA-256 of whitespace-normalized visible text and an ordered heading
  list. Scripts, styles, comments and tag markup are excluded. Common and numeric
  character references are decoded. This is a static HTML observation, with no
  browser execution or JavaScript-rendered content.
- JSON: SHA-256 of canonical JSON with sorted object keys and preserved array
  order. Unrelated key ordering does not trigger a change.

No raw page body is retained. Remote text is untrusted data; it never becomes
instructions, queued work, routing changes, notifications or outbound messages.
Machine output escapes source text as JSON, following the offline modelcaps
report's approach. Existing `scripts/radar-modelcaps.ts` remains an independent,
offline comparison of complete model inventories. Ecosystem changelog collection
and curated cross-repository links remain separate evidence streams.

## Storage and recovery

State lives at `~/.phantom/radar/snapshots/<id>.json`, with directory creation mode
0700 and atomic file writes at mode 0600. Symlinked directories or state files
are refused. A file contains the latest attempt time, the last two successful
snapshots, and a failure marker. Failed fetches or normalization leave successful
observations intact and mark subsequent local diffs `stale`.

Every source attempt is recorded before network access. A source cannot run
again for six hours, including after failures or an interrupted attempt. A clock
rollback conservatively extends the wait. There is no force or cooldown-bypass
flag. Changing the source URL or kind under an existing ID refuses comparison;
use a new ID to establish a new baseline.

An exclusive `<id>.lock` prevents concurrent runs. A normal exit removes it. If
a process crashes, the lock remains and reports `busy`. Its local JSON records
`pid` and `startedAt`. Confirm that process has exited before removing that one
lock file. Do not remove snapshot JSON to bypass the cooldown. Corrupt state is
reported as an error rather than silently reset to an empty successful baseline.

## Offline verification

All test responses are synthetic. With a temporary test home:

```sh
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/radar-sources.test.ts test/radar-diff.test.ts test/radar-cli.test.ts test/radar-modelcaps.test.ts --bail 1
```

The CLI's `universe help`, `resources pool --help` and `runtime help` describe
the command surface in the exact binary you are running. A source guide may
describe features not present in an older registry or desktop release.

The generated [CLI reference](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/CLI-REFERENCE.md)
records the source checkout's overview and full command table.

## For coding agents

Start with the selected command registry from the binary you intend to use:

```sh
ashlr docs --agent --json
```

From a trusted, built source checkout, use `node bin/ashlr` in place of `ashlr`.
The registry returns command usage, descriptions, safety classifications and JSON
shape references. It is discovery metadata, not a complete schema or permission
to execute. Consult the selected command's help and the owning guide; do not
infer current provider readiness or mutation authority from a safety label.

For an already configured store, these commands inspect evidence without starting
campaigns or contacting model providers. Replace `ID`, `ABS_ROOT` and `ABS_RUNTIME`
with the assigned experiment/campaign ID and explicit private absolute paths;
keep the same root throughout a task.

| Question | Read-only command | Interpret the result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What experiments and outcomes are recorded? | `ashlr universe status --root ABS_ROOT --json` | Check `sourceState`, run status and measured usage; unknown values are not zero. |
| What recovery state is recorded for this campaign? | `ashlr universe campaign check ID --root ABS_ROOT --json` | Check `sourceState`, `disposition` and `reasonCode`; this does not inspect current workers. |
| Is the explicit resource setup valid? | `ashlr universe resources check --resource-runtime ABS_RUNTIME --json` | Check `status`, worker eligibility and warnings; valid configuration is not authenticated account readiness. |
| Was a local artifact handoff recorded? | `ashlr universe deliveries ID --root ABS_ROOT --json` | Check `sourceState` and each receipt's `status`; `pending`, `unchanged` and `delivered` are different outcomes. |

A zero exit code alone does not mean work is ready, useful or delivered. For
example, campaign `check` returns zero for healthy held or terminal evidence.
Inspect the structured result and use each command's own exit-code contract.
Raw startup records and private JSON can contain tokens or paths; do not publish
them. The [demo exporter](DEMO.md#generate-a-shareable-evidence-graphic) is the
separate, allowlisted path for sharing the deterministic demo.

When execution is within your delegated scope, follow the existing
[experiment contract](ASHLR-UNIVERSE.md#the-experiment-contract),
[bounded campaign guide](ASHLR-UNIVERSE.md#continue-autonomously-with-a-bounded-campaign)
and [worker commissioning guide](RESOURCE-POOLS.md#commission-native-accounts-and-local-capacity).
For [supervised local delivery](ASHLR-UNIVERSE.md#deliver-supervised-campaign-results),
inspect both campaign and delivery outcomes and reconcile receipts before retrying.
A local branch is not a merge, release or production acceptance. Keep scope,
resource reserves and acceptance criteria explicit; routine execution can proceed
within them without turning discovery or a passing trial into broader authority.

For an opt-in versioned source installation, see [versioned self-swap](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/SELF-SWAP.md) (source).

To set up and operate Phantom from a cold start, see the [agent operations guide](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/AGENT-OPERATIONS.md) (source).

For the public-source review of contributor instructions across the seven repos, see the [AGENTS.md audit](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/AGENTS-MD-AUDIT.md) (source).

## What the evidence means

- **Implemented** means the code path exists; **verified** names the tests that ran.
- **Packaged** identifies exact built bytes; **published** identifies their distribution.
- **Commissioned** means a specific provider/runtime was configured and exercised.
- **Accepted engineering value** requires useful artifact-level acceptance, not
  process completion, token consumption, dashboard activity or a benchmark alone.

Universe evaluates candidates and retains evidence. Resource Pools manage explicit
worker capacity and execution receipts. These paths are not yet automatically
connected into an unattended subscription-backed product factory. Keep their
roots, budgets and acceptance evidence explicit.

## Deeper design and history

The [ecosystem design](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/AGENT-NATIVE-ECOSYSTEM.md)
describes federation across independent products. [Mission OS](MISSION-OS.md)
documents mission contracts, and [runtime activation authority](RUNTIME_ACTIVATION_AUTHORITY.md)
records the separate resident-runtime boundary. The
[milestone index](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/MILESTONE-INDEX.md)
and [historical contracts](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/contracts/README.md)
are source references, not setup instructions or current release receipts.

Update the owning guide when behavior changes. Keep exact test counts, source
hashes, artifact digests, provider observations and rollback identities in dated
release or commissioning evidence instead of duplicating them throughout the
documentation. Use focused local checks while iterating, then follow the
canonical release guide for required hosted qualification and publication.

- [Local model inventory](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/MODEL-INVENTORY.md): opt-in Mac benchmarks, admission and fleet schema.

# Release autonomy audit

The implementation is not yet wired into the top-level CLI dispatcher. Once wired, `phm release autonomy` inventories the remaining release steps and controls for the seven enrolled repositories. It reads GitHub settings and workflow evidence through `gh api` GET requests and reads the local fleet publish switch. It never changes settings, dispatches workflows, or sends messages. Authenticate `gh` with access to repository settings before running the audit. Missing permissions or incomplete evidence are reported as unknown, not as absence of a gate.

```sh
phm release autonomy --json
phm release autonomy --repo locus --md
```

Each observed item is marked `human step`, `gate (keep)`, or `ok`. The gate inventory also proposes `cut`, `automate`, or `hard-limit`, with a reason and location. These are recommendations, not authorization to change controls. Required checks and attestation remain gates. Disabled tag rulesets are reported as disabled. The auto-tag result describes the latest observed run, not proof of a successful release. The local `PUBLISH_HOLD` reading applies to this machine; missing or degraded switch evidence is unknown.

The inventory includes policy and source controls in addition to GitHub observations. Those entries identify where to investigate and do not assert that every external system was inspected. Access failures, pagination limits, and unread workflow sources limit completeness; review unknowns before drawing conclusions.
