# Zero Waste

## What "zero waste" means for the fleet

Zero waste means every provider's remaining usage is spent before its reset
deadline.  A held lane that still has budget sitting in its window is waste —
a window that resets with usage left over could have been executing useful
work.  Every lane's budget should be driven toward 100 % consumption before
the provider's scheduled reset point.

## Where to look

| Surface | What it shows | Source |
|---------|---------------|--------|
| **Resources bar** (desktop console rail foot) | Per-account battery: how much of each binding window is left, reset instant, and reserve kept for the operator. | `src/web-ui/routes/verse/resources/ResourcesBar.tsx` |
| **Fleet usage pane** (desktop console drawer) | Every window with its reset, the burn rate and projected exhaustion per lane. | `GET /api/verse/leader/resources` (`usedPct`, `creditsRemaining`, `resetAt`, `burnPctPerHour`, `projectedExhaustion` from `src/core/fleet/runs-resource-ledger.ts`) |
| **Notification bell** | Urgent and critical alerts derived from the fleet ledger — signals when a lane is approaching its reset without consuming its window. | `src/web-ui/components/notifications/NotificationBell.tsx` |
| `ashlr resources` | Table view: engine, availability, used %, cap, resets-in, cost. Flags: `--json`, `--watch`. | `src/cli/resources.ts` |
| `ashlr resources --json` | Raw JSON — full `ResourceSnapshot` of every backend. | `src/cli/resources.ts` |

## What to do when a lane is held with usage left

When a lane is held (flagged `held: true` or `held` in the slots file) while
its window still has budget, the hold is consuming time without producing work.
Unhold the lane through the normal fleet control process so that remaining
budget can be spent before the window resets.  See

* [Lane Holds](./LANE-HOLDS.md) — how holds work, how to spot a stale hold,
  and how to unhold a lane.

## Related documentation

* [Resource Ledger](./RESOURCE-LEDGER.md) — full field glossary for
  `ResourceLedgerV1` and `ResourceLaneRow`.
* [Reset-aware Scheduling](./RESET-AWARE-SCHEDULING.md) — how the fleet
  uses fresh deadlines to select useful work before a provider reset.
* [Usage Signals](./USAGE-SIGNALS.md) — event-driven usage readings that
  feed the burn-rate and exhaustion projections.


<!-- page: add-a-computer -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/add-a-computer.md

# Add a computer in 60 seconds

On the computer to add, install Node.js 22.15.0 or newer, then install Phantom:

```sh
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
```

Join with a unique node ID and the owner scope used by the jobs you want to
run. Choose capabilities for this computer's role (see below):

```sh
phm node join --node laptop --owner acme --caps build,gh --json
```

Replace `laptop` and `acme` with your own node ID and owner scope. Save the
`session` number from the output; use that number in the commands below.

## Pick a role

Roles are expressed as capabilities, not a `--role` flag. Advertise only what
this computer can actually do: use `--caps build` for build jobs, `--caps gh`
for GitHub jobs, or `--caps build,gh` for both. Jobs select nodes that advertise
all their required capabilities and share their owner scope. For `gh` jobs,
sign in locally with `gh auth login` and report that login with `--probe-auth`;
credentials stay on this computer.

## Verify and stay live

Replace `1` with the session returned by join:

```sh
phm node beat --node laptop --session 1 --probe-auth --json
phm node status --owner acme --json
```

Check that `laptop` appears live with the intended caps and, for GitHub jobs,
that its auth is `ok`. A join does not start a worker or recurring heartbeat.
Repeat the heartbeat comfortably within 30 seconds to keep the session live;
if it expires, join again and use the new session number. Omit `--probe-auth`
if this node does not need GitHub authentication.

## Leave

```sh
phm node leave --node laptop --session 1 --json
```

Use the current session number and check for `"left":true`. An expired or
replaced session cannot leave a newer one.

The current router uses a private local state directory shared by processes on
one host; joining does not connect separate computers over a network. See the
[node router guide](NODE-ROUTER.md) for routing, leases, and this limit.


<!-- page: adr/0001-projection-authority -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/adr/0001-projection-authority.md

# ADR 0001: Handle-Relative Projection Authority

- Status: accepted design, dormant implementation
- Scope: proposal persistence and the operational proposal projection
- Activation: prohibited until every gate in this ADR is satisfied by a separate reviewed change

## Decision

Ashlr will replace pathname-based projection authority with a long-lived native
single-writer service. The service will acquire the trusted storage root once,
retain directory handles for its lifetime, and perform every descendant open,
create, rename, remove, read, and durability operation relative to those held
handles.

The first production implementation will use a small Rust service and a durable
append-only commit journal with immutable content-addressed proposal blobs. A
journal root is authoritative only while it exactly matches the externally
signed monotonic CAS root; materialized proposal JSON and projection manifests
are compatibility caches. SQLite is not part of the first authority boundary.
It may replace the journal later only behind a handle-relative custom VFS or an
equivalent proven immutable-root mechanism.

This branch remains dormant. No source module outside the transaction/replay
implementation may import its coordinator until the native service, migration,
rollback, cross-platform, and external monotonic-root gates are complete.

## Problem

The current code has strong path-level checks but no object-capability boundary.
It repeatedly validates `(dev, ino)`, ownership, modes, symlink/reparse state,
and stable reads, then performs later Node.js filesystem operations by pathname.
A concurrent replacement can therefore present an approved directory during a
check and a different directory during a later open or rename. Additional
before/after checks detect many races but cannot prove that every operation was
resolved beneath the same directory object.

Keeping a directory descriptor open does not fix this by itself. The child
operation must also be relative to that descriptor. A descriptor plus a later
absolute `open`, `rename`, or `lstat` remains path-authorized.

## Current Interface And Call-Site Map

| Boundary | Current behavior | Authority gap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proposal-mutation-lock.ts` | `ProposalStoreMutationAuthority` captures home/root paths and `(dev, ino)` while a path-backed local lock is held. | It is an identity observation, not an open root capability. |
| `store.ts::persistProposal` | Creates temp/rollback files, fsyncs, links or renames, rereads, and rolls back under the store lock. It is reached by proposal creation, status/field updates, and realized-merge recording. | Temp creation, publication, reread, cleanup, and rollback all resolve pathnames independently. |
| `operational-projection.ts` | Reads proposal files and a signed projection manifest; migration writes `proposal-projection/current.json`. | Proposal enumeration, member reads, key reads, and manifest publication are independent pathname traversals. This module currently has test-only consumers. |
| `operational-projection-transaction.ts` | Persists the active phase journal and binds reads to captured home/root identities. | Journal/key reads and temp publication return to path resolution after validation. |
| `operational-projection-replay-ledger.ts` | Persists an authenticated local phase history and reconciles one-phase gaps. It explicitly reports `rollbackProtected:false` and `historicalAuthority:false`. | It has the same pathname boundary and cannot supply an external monotonic root. |
| `operational-projection-transaction-coordinator.ts` | Coordinates journal and replay-ledger phases. | It is intentionally dormant and has no non-test call site. It does not atomically mutate proposal plus projection state. |
| `private-file-write.ts` / `stable-file-read.ts` | Pin opened file identity and perform bounded I/O with extensive before/after validation. | Parent directory operations remain pathname-relative; Windows has no Node.js handle-relative child API here. |
| `foundry/provenance.ts` | Reads the host-shared key after opening and checking directory/file identities. | The key and its parents are still located by pathname. The HMAC authenticates cooperative local state, not independent history. |

The production conversion must cover all `persistProposal` callers and all
proposal readers. Converting only the projection manifest would leave proposal
bytes outside the same authority and would not close the transaction.

## Options Considered

### 1. One-Shot Native Helper

A Rust helper can use `openat`/`renameat`/`fsync` on POSIX and `NtCreateFile`
with `OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES.RootDirectory`, `FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT`, and
handle-relative rename on Windows.

This proves descendant resolution beneath the held root only for one helper
lifetime. A helper invoked independently for each phase reintroduces cross-call
root ABA. It is acceptable only if one invocation performs the complete commit
and recovery operation, and every authoritative read also goes through that
invocation. At that point it is effectively the service protocol with process
startup on every request and weaker continuity, so it is not selected.

### 2. SQLite Transactional Projection Store

SQLite is an excellent atomicity engine. One transaction can commit proposal,
projection, journal, and replay rows together, and its crash-test history is far
stronger than a new multi-file transaction implementation.

SQLite alone does not prove namespace authority. The standard API opens a
filename through a VFS, and rollback/WAL modes create sidecar files. Even
`SQLITE_OPEN_NOFOLLOW` addresses the final database symlink, not a hostile
parent replacement or all sidecar resolution. Default Node `DatabaseSync`
likewise accepts a path, not a trusted directory handle. A custom VFS could make
SQLite handle-relative, but that is a larger first slice than a bounded journal
and still requires the native service boundary.

SQLite remains the preferred later storage engine if measurements justify it
and the custom VFS passes the same root-continuity suite. It is rejected as a
standalone fix.

### 3. Native Single-Writer Service With Immutable Root Handle

This is selected. The daemon starts one native child from an immutable verified
release and retains a private anonymous inherited IPC channel. Launch admission
must bind the exact executable bytes and release identity used by the child,
pass only the intended channel and root capabilities, close all other inheritable
descriptors/handles, and construct an allowlisted environment that excludes
loader injection and language-runtime hook variables. No named pipe, Unix socket,
path-discovered endpoint, mutable `PATH`, or post-verification executable lookup
may enter the authority boundary. The child and supervisor mutually bind a fresh
session nonce, protocol version, executable digest, and release digest before any
storage request is accepted.

The child resolves the OS account home without trusting mutable `HOME`, acquires
the platform root/volume capability, opens the home and `.ashlr` hierarchy
component by component without following links/reparse points, and holds the
resulting handles until shutdown. Account lookup and initial root acquisition
remain part of launch admission rather than a guarantee supplied by the journal;
platform tests must prove that a mutable path cannot be substituted between
lookup and capability acquisition.

On POSIX, descendant operations use single-component `openat`, `mkdirat`,
`fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`, `renameat`, and `unlinkat` calls. Linux may add
`openat2` with `RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS | RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS`,
but portable POSIX behavior must not depend on Linux-only `openat2`. Files and
the exact containing directory handles are fsynced; unsupported durability is
a hard failure.

On Windows, the service uses directory handles opened without
`FILE_SHARE_DELETE`, `NtCreateFile` relative to `RootDirectory`,
`FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT`, explicit reparse-tag/DACL/owner checks, and
handle-relative rename information. File data and metadata are flushed with
documented write-through/flush APIs. Native Windows activation remains blocked
until abrupt-power-loss tests prove the exact selected filesystem semantics;
an unsupported directory-entry durability result is not downgraded.

## Authoritative Storage Model

The service owns one private `projection-authority-v1` directory beneath the
held `.ashlr` root:

```text
projection-authority-v1/
  journal.log
  blobs/
    <proposal-digest>.json
  snapshots/
    <journal-root>.json
```

- Proposal blobs are canonical, bounded, immutable, content-addressed files.
  Creation is exclusive and handle-relative. Existing bytes must match the
  requested digest exactly.
- `journal.log` is opened once by handle. Each bounded frame carries length,
  schema version, sequence, previous-root digest, transaction ID, proposal ID,
  before/after digests, canonical timestamp, checksum, and service attestation.
  Framing must distinguish a torn final frame from a malformed committed frame;
  corruption before the final candidate is a hard stop, never a truncation hint.
- A commit first makes every new blob durable, then appends and flushes one
  complete journal frame as a local candidate, then performs an externally
  signed compare-and-set from the exact previous root to that candidate root.
  The candidate becomes readable as committed, and success is returned, only
  after the signed CAS response verifies and exactly names both roots. A partial
  final frame is not committed. A complete local candidate with an unchanged
  external root is recovered only by retrying the same idempotent CAS or stopping;
  it is never exposed or discarded by local policy. An external root ahead of,
  or conflicting with, durable local history is degraded and requires explicit
  signed recovery evidence. Committed history before a malformed tail is never
  silently reinterpreted.
- The current proposal namespace and operational projection are derived views.
  They may be materialized handle-relatively for compatibility, but readers
  cannot use those files as authority.
- The request is one compare-and-commit operation. Callers provide expected
  journal root/generation and canonical next proposal bytes. The service
  computes digests, membership, and the next projection. It never accepts a
  caller assertion that verification, locking, durability, or recovery already
  occurred.

The service protocol has only `status`, bounded point/batch reads, and
`compare-and-commit`. Every bounded frame carries the session nonce, monotonically
increasing request ID, protocol version, operation, canonical request digest, and
an exact response binding; duplicate, skipped, unsolicited, truncated, or
out-of-order traffic closes the session and degrades authority. Unknown fields,
duplicate IDs, noncanonical JSON, oversized frames, stale expected roots,
unavailable keys, incomplete recovery, peer death, or any platform-assurance
failure return a typed degraded result and perform no commit. There is no path
fallback. There is no reconnect to a path-discovered endpoint.

## Guarantees

| Strategy | Actually proves | Does not prove |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current path checks | Cooperative ownership/mode checks, file identity around bounded I/O, many detectable races. | Parent object continuity for later path operations; same-root resolution for proposal and projection; rollback resistance. |
| One-shot handle-relative helper | Same-root descendant resolution during one invocation; no symlink/reparse traversal for covered calls. | Continuity across invocations; multi-file atomicity unless the whole transaction is one invocation; external history. |
| SQLite with default VFS | Serializable atomic transactions and crash recovery for records inside one database under documented filesystem assumptions. | Trusted database/sidecar namespace, root continuity, HMAC integrity, external monotonic history. |
| Selected native service and journal | One writer; object continuity for the service lifetime; handle-relative namespace confinement; a single local commit point; bounded crash recovery; no live path fallback. | Trust before root acquisition; protection from a process with equivalent OS authority; independent verification; cross-restart rollback resistance; remote/CAS availability. |
| Selected service plus external signed monotonic CAS | All above, plus detection/reconciliation of local rollback or root replacement across restarts when the CAS transport is healthy and signatures verify. | Correctness of a compromised signer/service, hardware failure outside documented guarantees, or authorization beyond the signed policy. |

The service is a storage authority, not an independent judge. It does not make
proposal quality, verification, merge, or deployment decisions.

## Incremental Dormant Implementation

1. **Protocol and native primitive harness:** add a Rust workspace containing
   no daemon integration. Implement root acquisition, relative single-component
   file operations, strict flushes, bounded framing, launch/peer binding, and a
   fake in-memory transport. Package no binary in release artifacts yet.
2. **Native platform proof:** run Linux, macOS, and Windows tests against real
   filesystems. Inject parent swaps, child swaps, symlinks, junctions, mount
   escapes, hard links, stale handles, service death, partial writes, rename
   failure, flush failure, and restart after every commit point.
3. **Shadow import:** while legacy writers are quiescent under the existing
   global store lock, the service opens the legacy inbox handle-relatively,
   ingests a complete bounded snapshot, and writes a signed genesis frame.
   Reads compare service state with legacy state but never route authority to it.
4. **External-root binding:** bind genesis and every committed journal root to
   the signed monotonic CAS coordinator. Missing, unavailable, stale, unsigned,
   or conflicting CAS evidence stops startup and mutation.
5. **Writer conversion:** route every `persistProposal` caller through one
   compare-and-commit port. Remove direct path mutation from live code. Keep the
   old files as service-produced compatibility views only.
6. **Reader conversion:** route proposal and operational-projection reads
   through the service. Require a healthy exact journal root. Missing service or
   incomplete migration is degraded, never cold-start or healthy zero.
7. **Canary and activation:** activate only on an immutable release with native
   CI, signed artifact identity, abrupt-crash evidence, canary monitoring, and a
   tested disable path. Activation is a separate reviewed change.

The smallest first code slice is steps 1 and 2 for one immutable blob plus one
journal frame. It remains unreachable from `store.ts`, the daemon, CLI, web,
automerge, and release installation.

## Migration And Rollback

- Migration is idempotent and CAS-guarded. The genesis frame binds a complete
  legacy namespace digest, projection digest, provenance-key generation, and
  external expected root. Partial or changed legacy input aborts.
- Dual-write is prohibited because it creates two authorities. Shadow mode is
  legacy-write plus service import/compare; cutover is service-write plus
  compatibility projection.
- Legacy files remain untouched through the canary and rollback window.
- Rollback means disable mutation and return to a read-only prior release that
  understands the service export. It must never resume a legacy path writer
  after service cutover. If a compatible rollback release is unavailable, the
  fleet remains stopped and exports evidence for recovery.
- Rollback to an earlier journal root requires an externally signed rollback
  permit bound to the exact before/after roots. Local HMAC state is insufficient.

## Required Tests Before Activation

- **Primitive confinement:** every operation is relative to a held handle;
  absolute paths, separators, `.`/`..`, alternate streams, device paths, and
  unknown reparse tags are rejected.
- **ABA:** swap/rename every ancestor and child before and during open, create,
  publish, read, flush, and recovery. The operation either targets the original
  held object or fails; it never targets the replacement.
- **Crash matrix:** kill before/after blob write, blob flush, directory flush,
  journal append, journal flush, CAS request, CAS apply, signed response receipt,
  and caller response. Recovery yields exactly the externally anchored before or
  after root and never a healthy ambiguous state.
- **Protocol:** malformed/duplicate/oversized/out-of-order frames, stale CAS,
  stale generation, replay, conflict, unknown fields, wrong session/executable/
  release binding, inherited-handle leakage, loader-environment injection, peer
  replacement, peer death, and partial responses all fail closed without fallback.
- **Migration:** empty, complete, oversized, changing, malformed, aliased,
  hard-linked, and legacy-unmigrated namespaces; repeated genesis is exact
  replay and different genesis is conflict.
- **Durability:** real native Windows, macOS, and Linux abrupt-process tests;
  supported filesystem matrix; injected sync errors; removable/network/
  unsupported filesystems refuse activation.
- **Import boundary:** until the activation change, no live source imports the
  transaction/replay coordinator. The contract test added with this ADR
  enforces that dormant state.
- **End-to-end:** every proposal create/update/merge-evidence path and every
  authoritative reader crosses the service; killing or impersonating the
  service cannot cause local fallback.

## Activation Gates

Production projection authority remains false until all of these are true:

1. native artifacts are reproducible, signed, and bound to the immutable Hub release;
2. all three native platform suites and the crash matrix pass;
3. the external signed monotonic CAS transport is available and writable;
4. migration is complete and exact read parity is proven;
5. every writer and reader uses the service with no path fallback;
6. the service is supervised, resource-bounded, launch/peer authenticated, and
   exposes health without raw proposal contents;
7. canary, disable, export, and signed rollback-permit procedures are exercised; and
8. a separate reviewed activation change removes the dormant import guard.

## Research Basis

- POSIX specifies directory-relative rename through
  [`renameat`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/functions/rename.html)
  and descriptor durability through
  [`fsync`](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/009695399/functions/fsync.html).
- Linux `openat2` adds explicit beneath/no-symlink resolution controls, but is
  Linux-only: [`openat2(2)`](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/openat2.2.html).
- Microsoft documents relative opens through `OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES.RootDirectory`
  and reparse-point control in
  [`NtCreateFile`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winternl/nf-winternl-ntcreatefile),
  plus handle-relative rename targets in
  [`FILE_RENAME_INFORMATION`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/ns-ntifs-_file_rename_information).
- SQLite documents its atomic-commit assumptions and crash testing in
  [Atomic Commit](https://www.sqlite.org/atomiccommit.html), while its open API
  delegates filename behavior to the selected
  [VFS](https://www.sqlite.org/c3ref/open.html).
- Microsoft recommends replacement/database patterns instead of adopting the
  deprecated TxF platform:
  [Alternatives to TxF](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/deprecation-of-txf).

# Agent first run — Phantom 3.30 CLI

A source-backed runbook for a coding agent with shell access on Mason's host.
Every command below exists in the shipped 3.30 CLI; the wire shapes quoted are
the real outputs of the implementing modules. None of these commands contacts
a provider or spends money. Only §3's optional post and §4 write anything,
and only into local stores on this host. Deeper failure semantics live in
[AGENT-CLI-CONTRACTS.md](AGENT-CLI-CONTRACTS.md).

## 1. Install or upgrade, then prove the version

Requires Node.js 22.15.0 or newer.

Fresh install:

```sh
node --version                      # must print v22.15.0 or newer
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
phm --version                       # prints the installed version, e.g. 3.30.0
```

Upgrade from 3.29.15 — same install command, same check:

```sh
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
phm --version                       # must now print a 3.30.x version
```

The whole orientation surface in this runbook is new in 3.30. Published
3.29.15 has no `phm comms bus`, no `phm comms inbox`, and no
`phm fleet runs|journal|parked|job` verbs; its `phm comms` answers
"unknown subcommand" for them. After upgrading, probe each command's help
before relying on it — help prints usage and exits 0:

```sh
phm comms bus --help
phm fleet runs --help
phm fleet job --help
phm comms inbox --help
```

`phm` and `ashlr` are the same binary; this runbook uses `phm`.

## 2. Inspect the fleet (read-only)

All fleet reads observe the host runs directory `~/.ashlr-runs` and the
`~/.ashlr` home. Exit 0 can still carry missing or degraded sources —
`missing`/`unknown` means absent evidence, not an empty fleet. Check
`sourceState`/`sources` before treating a projection as current.

```sh
phm fleet runs --json       # lanes, running vs target, queued, held, last tick
phm fleet parked --json     # parked queue: totals, ready/parked by lane, hold reasons, unmetDeps for PARKED-DEP gates
phm fleet journal --json    # leader journal: recent passes, ingest and reject rows
```

`--lane <lane>` filters lane-attributed rows on `runs` and `parked`; totals
and source health stay global.

One job and its notes (job IDs match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{2,79}`):

```sh
phm fleet job <job-id> --json        # state, lane, tier, model, publish evidence, log tail
phm fleet job <job-id> --notes       # the worker's bridge-notes artifact (scrubbed)
phm fleet job <job-id> --log --tail-lines 20
```

Job detail is artifact evidence (`fleet.job.v1`); process liveness is not
checked. `--notes` reads a scrubbed worker artifact and exits 1 when none is
recorded. `phm fleet workers --json` lists live worker processes if you also
need liveness.

## 3. Read Mason's inbox

```sh
phm comms inbox read --limit 20 --json
```

Reads `~/.ashlr-runs/leader/MASON-INBOX.md` and prints one JSON object:
`{sourceState, entries:[{at, source, priority, text}]}`. `sourceState` is
`healthy`, `missing` or `degraded`; a missing inbox is not a healthy empty
one, and `degraded` exits 1. Read selects the newest matching entries and
returns them oldest first; `at` is the entry's local time in
`America/New_York` (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`). `--source`, `--priority`,
`--after`/`--before` (RFC 3339 with zone) and `--limit 1..200` filter;
`source` is metadata, not identity.

Optionally leave Mason a plain-text note (this writes the same file; it is
not a bus envelope and is capped at 6000 characters):

```sh
printf '%s\n' 'fake note: new agent online, runbook complete' | phm comms inbox post --file - --json
```

Post answers `{ok:true, ack:{channel:"cli", status:"accepted"|"duplicate",
dedupeKey}}`; the stored entry's `source` is `cli`. The CLI adapter is
verified only as `local-operator` — see §5. Writing the file does not send
anything to Mason's phone.

## 4. Exercise the local bus

The bus is a bounded local JSON transport under
`$ASHLR_HOME/fleet/bus-inbox/messages.json` (`~/.ashlr/fleet/…` by default).
It has no delivery handlers: `posted` means retained in the local store, not
delivered, read, or acted on.

```sh
phm comms bus status
```

Status prints `{source, retainedCount, retainedBytes, maxMessages, maxBytes,
liveCount, expiredCount}` — metadata only, no bodies. `source` is `missing`,
`available`, or `unavailable` (exit 1); missing/unavailable counts are `null`,
not zero.

Post one fake envelope. The wire contract is exactly six fields — `id`,
`from`, `to`, `priority` (`P0`–`P3`), `ttl` (positive integer milliseconds),
and `body` (any strict JSON) — at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes total; `id`/`from`/`to`
are printable-ASCII tokens of 1–128 characters:

```sh
cat > /tmp/fake-envelope.json <<'EOF'
{"id":"fake-hello-1","from":"fake-agent","to":"fake-coordinator","priority":"P3","ttl":300000,"body":{"note":"first-run check"}}
EOF
phm comms bus post --file /tmp/fake-envelope.json
```

(`--file -` reads one envelope from stdin.) Post answers
`{status:"posted",id,cursor}`; the same ID with the identical envelope is a
successful `{status:"duplicate"}`, and the same ID with different content is
`{status:"conflict"}`. Other statuses: `invalid` (exit 2), `retryable`
(writer contention — retry with backoff, same ID and envelope),
`unavailable`, `full` (all exit 1).

Read the receipt back, then resume from the cursor:

```sh
phm comms bus read --after 0
phm comms bus read --after 0 --id fake-hello-1
phm comms bus read --after <nextCursor>
```

Read answers `{status:"ok", messages:[{cursor, receivedAt, envelope}],
nextCursor}`; each message row is the stored receipt — the persistent integer
`cursor`, the epoch-ms `receivedAt`, and the validated envelope. Semantics:

- The cursor starts at 0 and never resets. Process a page, then persist its
  `nextCursor` only after processing succeeds; resume with `--after` that
  value. A cursor beyond the retained end is `invalid`.
- Expired records advance the cursor but are not returned, so an empty
  `messages` with an advanced `nextCursor` is normal. `ttl` in a returned
  envelope is the *remaining* milliseconds; reads never renew it.
- `--limit` is 1–100 (default 50) and counts scanned live records before
  filtering. `--id`, `--to`, `--from`, `--exclude-from`, `--priority` are
  exact, case-sensitive, and combined.
- `phm comms bus watch` polls the same pages for a live tail.

Full store: retained capacity is 1 MiB or 1024 records, whichever is reached
first. A live record is never evicted for another; records already expired are
reclaimed by the next post, so `{status:"full"}` means live data fills the
bound — an expired-only store accepts new posts again without resetting
cursors. Detect it from `status` (`retainedCount` at `maxMessages`, or
`retainedBytes` at `maxBytes`) or from a `post` answering `{status:"full"}`;
do not retry a full store as if it were contention.

## 5. Trust boundary — local owner vs verified remote identity

- Local owner trust: every command above runs as the local OS user against
  that user's `~/.ashlr` and `~/.ashlr-runs`, and the stores enforce
  owner-only permissions (0700 directories, 0600 files). The local process
  owner is the trust boundary: running these commands proves you are a local
  operator, nothing more.
- The inbox CLI is verified only as `local-operator` — the canonical sender
  ID the adapter itself supplies; a sender ID asserted inside a message body
  is never identity. Only a trusted channel adapter that authenticated its
  remote side (for example the Telegram adapter verifying the configured bot
  chat) produces a verified remote sender; the `cli` channel does not
  authenticate internet or email senders.
- Bus `from`/`to`, inbox `source`, and `priority` are routing labels and
  metadata — exact and case-sensitive for filtering, but they confer no
  authenticated identity or authority. Any local writer can claim any label.
- Remote delivery is a separate concern with its own configuration. Nothing
  here sends to Telegram, email, or a provider: `bus post` retains a local
  record and `inbox post` appends a local file. Cloud/provider identity
  (provider CLI sign-in, a Locus pin) is established by those tools, never
  by these commands.

Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/ambitious-fleet-os-v1.md

# Ambitious Fleet OS V1

## Product thesis

Ashlr Hub should feel like an always-on engineering chief of staff, not a wall of telemetry. Its first job is to convert an operator's intent into bounded work, keep that work moving through the existing evidence gates, and surface only the exceptions that need judgment.

This slice advances that thesis in three connected places:

1. **Mission Compiler** turns a strategist briefing into at most three deduplicated, repository-bound goals. Preview is read-only; adoption is explicit and verifies exact persistence.
2. **Operator Briefing** puts `Needs you`, `Autonomous now`, and `Last proof` ahead of the detailed fleet panels, with a compact `Observed -> Decided -> Acted -> Proved` evidence chain.
3. **Crash-safe resident autonomy** makes spend authority durable across abrupt termination, midnight rollover, stale process ownership, and resident-service restart behavior.

## Operator experience

The main screen is intentionally exception-first:

```text
Mission Control
  Needs you          Autonomous now       Last proof
  [safe next action] [bounded work state] [O -> D -> A -> P]

  Evidence and telemetry (collapsed by default)
    readiness | fleet | goals | learning | dispatch | repair | evidence
```

- Every suggested command is visible and individually copyable; the browser never executes it.
- A clear/continue command is withheld unless the snapshot and readiness proof are fresh, the kill state is exactly inactive, authority is known and unblocked, and no human action is pending.
- Unknown, paused, stale, or blocked state yields a read-only inspection action.
- Polling and event-stream refreshes preserve focus, scroll position, and disclosure state.
- The settings dialog traps and restores focus and remains scrollable in mobile, short, zoomed, and safe-area viewports.

## Mission Compiler contract

- `ashlr vision preview` is non-mutating and reports selected goals plus deterministic skip reasons.
- Candidate goals must resolve to one exact enrolled repository path or one unambiguous exact basename; missing, malformed, or ambiguous targets fail closed.
- A briefing compiles at most three goals and respects goal-focus capacity.
- Exact raw objectives are reserved across all stored statuses and projects because goal filenames are objective-derived. Normalized objective/project identities are also reserved, including archived and completed history.
- Adoption reports `created`, `skipped`, or `failed` per goal and returns a failing exit status for degraded inventory, partial persistence, or write failure.
- A creation is successful only when the exact minted ID, objective, project, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt` are read back from storage.

## Durable autonomy contract

- A versioned spend guard is durably created before provider dispatch and carries the accounting identity, owner identity, budget day, budget snapshot, reserved exposure, and selected item IDs.
- State and guard transitions use file and parent-directory synchronization so success is not reported before the filesystem ordering boundary is durable.
- Startup recovery requires provably dead ownership. An exact accounting receipt permits idempotent cleanup; unknown exposure fails closed rather than reopening spend authority.
- Dispatch is capped to the guard's bounded item capacity.
- Cross-midnight recovery accounts the old budget day before establishing the new day.
- Persistence failures become terminal daemon failures. Resident service definitions must restart nonzero failures while intentional operator stop/kill remains a clean exit.

## Authority boundaries

This work does **not** expand merge, deployment, publication, provider-token, or external-mutation authority.

- Source changes remain proposal-only and subject to the existing verifier and protected-remote gates.
- Mission adoption requires an explicit CLI action; preview cannot write goals.
- Dashboard actions are copy-only.
- Unknown durability or spend exposure blocks further same-day provider authority.
- A successful build, local test, or dashboard render is not evidence that the resident daemon is installed, running, or production-authorized.

## Release gates

- [x] Independent P0/P1 reviews are clear.
- [x] Focused mission, dashboard, daemon, budget, state, and service suites pass.
- [x] Typecheck, changed-file lint, build, audit, invariants, and diff integrity pass.
- [x] Full `npm run test:ci` passes from the synchronized branch.
- [x] Desktop and constrained/mobile browser inspections pass with no console errors.
- [x] Branch is committed and pushed as draft PR #225 for protected CI.
- [ ] Resident daemon activation is separately approved and verified from the deployed artifact.

### Local evidence

- Changed-surface regression: 14 files, 799/799 tests.
- Safety invariants: 41 files, 445 passed, 5 platform-skipped.
- Full suite: 610 files passed, 2 platform-skipped; 13,950 tests passed, 42 skipped.
- Typecheck, build, dependency audit, and diff integrity passed.
- Full lint: 0 errors, 101 pre-existing warnings.
- Browser: 1440x900 and 390x844; no console errors or warnings; mobile settings containment and focus restoration verified.

Status: source-ready in draft PR #225 for protected review. Resident activation remains intentionally separate and is not claimed by this branch.

# Fleet graph v1

`GET /api/verse/fleet/graph` returns the `graph.v1` fleet registry — the
fleet's declared agents, engine/account identities, model catalogs and MCP
server identities, plus the `routes-to` and agent-relationship edges between
them. `GET /api/verse/fleet/graph?live=1` additionally joins the
`graph-live.v1` projection: per-node capacity, metered cost, quota standing
and reset times from the same evidence the dispatch gates read.

For a locally started `phm verse`, set `PHM_URL` and `PHM_READ_TOKEN`
privately from its startup JSON (the desktop manages its own credentials):

```sh
curl -fsS -H "X-Ashlr-Token: $PHM_READ_TOKEN" "$PHM_URL/api/verse/fleet/graph?live=1"
```

| Query | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `live=1` | Adds the `live` field (below). `live` is the only accepted key and `1` its only accepted value. |

Any other query key or value returns `400` with `VERSE_INVALID`. The route is
read-only: other methods return `405`.

| Fields | Meaning and source |
| --- | --- |
| `v`, `generatedAt` | Contract version and snapshot time, generated by the server. |
| `graph` | The `RegistryGraph` projection (`graph.v1`: `nodes`, `edges`, `issues`, `complete`, `sources`). See [types.ts](../../src/core/graph/types.ts). |
| `live` | Present only for `?live=1`: the `GraphLiveProjection` (`graph-live.v1`). Every registry node is repeated with a `live` field — `state`, `usedPercent`, `quota`, `resetsAtMs`, `spentTodayUsd`, `readingAgeMs`, `stale`, `reasons` — plus `counts.byState`, `budget` and `issues`. See [graph-live.ts](../../src/core/fleet/graph-live.ts). |
| `sources` | Per-source read state for `fleet` and `seats`, the same states `graph.sources` reports. |

Source states are `loaded` (the input parsed), `missing` (the file is absent
or no seat inventory is configured), `invalid` (the input parsed as JSON but
failed the allowlist contract) and `unavailable` (the file or the discovery
path could not be read). A missing or invalid source is a state, not an
error: the response is still `200`, carrying whatever projected, with
`complete: false` and the corresponding `issues` entries.

## Inputs

The route reads the same evidence the graph pipeline already reads:

- `fleet` — `$ASHLR_HOME/fleet/fleet.json`, the shared fleet document. The
  `fleet.v1` registry seed sections (`agents`, `mcp`, `edges`) live in it.
- `seats` — the public `seats` half of `discoverSeats(cfg)`, the same
  inventory the desktop console lists.

Both inputs are allowlist-parsed: only ids, engines, account ids and model
ids project. Launcher commands, environment maps, labels, notes and
credential fields are never copied into the response — a seat row carrying
`apiKey`, `env`, `command` or `launches` contributes only its public fields.

## Live node states

`live.nodes[].live.state` is an observation, never a dispatch decision —
`untracked` (no live signal applies), `ready` (fresh headroom), `limited`
(warn-level), `unknown` (a reading was expected but none qualified), `stale`
(every dated reading exceeded the staleness bound), `held` (a gate or policy
refused) or `exhausted` (provably saturated). The runtime gates
(`subscriptionAllows`, quota reservation, the router) remain authoritative.

## For agents

Read `sources` and `issues` before trusting the graph; `complete` means a
structurally complete projection of the selected inputs, not live readiness.
Treat `null` live fields as unknown, never zero. A `routes-to` edge records a
binding or catalog listing, not permission to execute.

Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/api/FLEET-RUNS-V1.md

# Fleet runs v1

`GET /api/verse/fleet/runs` returns a `FleetRunsV1` snapshot described by the
[JSON Schema](../../schema/fleet-runs.v1.schema.json). The desktop polls every
5 seconds. The server caches snapshots for two seconds. Each source can fail
independently; empty arrays can reflect unavailable data, so check `sources`.

For a locally started `phm verse`, set `PHM_URL` and `PHM_READ_TOKEN` privately
from its startup JSON (the desktop manages its own credentials):

```sh
curl -fsS -H "X-Ashlr-Token: $PHM_READ_TOKEN" "$PHM_URL/api/verse/fleet/runs"
```

| Fields | Meaning and source |
| --- | --- |
| `v`, `generatedAt` | Contract version and snapshot time, generated by the server. |
| `sources` | State of `runsDir`, `workers`, `inbox`, `codex`, and `merges`, respectively. |
| `lastTick`, `paused`, `memFreePct`, `diskFreeGb` | Last dispatch tick, pause state, free memory percent and free disk GB from `status.json` in the runs directory under the home folder. |
| `switches`, `claudeLane` | Present dispatch switch names and selected Claude lane from switch files and `claude-lane.state` in the runs directory. |
| `lanes` | Lane name, running, target and queued counts, held state and reason, tokens in the last hour, merges and merge rate over 24 hours; derived from `status.json` and `jobs.jsonl` in the runs directory. |
| `workers` | Live job, repo, lane, tier and age in seconds from the local process list. |
| `leaders`, `orchestratorAgents` | Leader labels and ages, and orchestrator agent count, from the local process list. |
| `publishesLastHour` | Job, lane, URL and time of recent publishes from `jobs.jsonl`. |
| `mergesLastHour` | Count and items (repo, PR number and title) from GitHub's merged PR search. |
| `events` | Time, kind and text from `dispatch-events.log`. |
| `codexPersonal` | Personal Codex session usage percent, reset time and observation time from local Codex session usage data. |
| `inbox` | Recent entry time, source and text from `MASON-INBOX.md`. |
| `drop` | Pending lane and file basenames and done count from the leader drop directory. |

Source states are `healthy` (reader succeeded), `degraded` (reader failed or
reported degraded), `missing` (reader reported missing or no personal Codex
session was found), and `not-landed` (reader module is unavailable). A healthy
source is not a guarantee that every underlying value is known.

## Inbox submission

With dispatch enabled, use the separate mutation token in the same header:

```sh
curl -fsS -X POST -H "X-Ashlr-Token: $PHM_MUTATION_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text":"Please review the demo","source":"Mason"}' \
  "$PHM_URL/api/verse/fleet/runs/inbox"
```

The body requires nonblank `text` (at most 6000 characters after trimming) and
allows `source` (1–40 letters, digits, spaces, dots, underscores or hyphens).
No other keys are accepted. Success is `201 {"ok":true,"at":"..."}` on the
first post and `200` with `duplicate:true` on a repost inside the dedupe
window; receipts persist under the runs dir (`ASHLR_RUNS_DIR`, else
`~/.ashlr-runs`), so the dedupe survives a Hub restart. Invalid bodies return
`400` with `VERSE_INVALID`; a refused entry returns `422` with
`INBOX_REFUSED` and a reason; an unavailable inbox returns `503` with
`INBOX_UNAVAILABLE`; an unreadable receipt store returns `503` with
`INBOX_RECEIPTS_UNREADABLE` without writing the entry. Dispatch disabled
returns `404`. The mutation gate also applies.

## For agents

Read `sources` before trusting a field; treat null as unknown, never zero. The
inbox is Mason's channel to the leaders, so agents must not post to it as if
they were Mason. A snapshot is an observation, not authority to act.


<!-- page: architecture/context-and-self-improvement -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/architecture/context-and-self-improvement.md

# Synthesized context, the constitution, and the self-improvement loop

Status: **Phase 1 shipped**: [CONSTITUTION.md](../../CONSTITUTION.md), the
evidence-scored context compiler (`src/core/teams/context.ts`), and the
draft-PR-only proposal loop (`phm improve propose`, `src/core/improve/loop.ts`).
Companion to [teams.md](teams.md).

## 1. Connectors are evidence, not truth

GitHub, chats, docs, mail, calendars, logs and metrics are **evidence
indicators**. Phantom builds its own living context from them. Each context
entry is a claim with:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `source` | provenance link back to the evidence (URL, `path@sha`, thread id) |
| `observedAt` | when the evidence was observed; drives decay |
| `importance` | 0..1 (0.5 neutral) |
| `supersedes[]` | ids of stale facts this replaces; superseded entries never surface |
| `scope` | personal / company / client:<x>, plus project and person |

Score = relevance (TF-IDF vs. the task) × recency (half-life 14 days, floor
25%) × importance. Connectors are BYO: anything that can produce a pointer and
a short summary (MCP server, CLI, API, local files, infra) is an evidence feed.
Nothing is copied wholesale; secrets are refused.

## 2. Constitution (successor to CLAUDE.md)

`CONSTITUTION.md` is versioned (`version:` front matter) and changes only via
a reviewed PR. It holds the mission (make Phantom the most useful engineering
tool; it improves itself), principles, the always-ask list (push/merge to
main, deploy, rotate credentials, external sends, spend, deletes outside the
workspace) and the self-improvement rules. Phase 2 generates AGENTS.md,
CLAUDE.md and Skills from it so per-tool files never drift.

## 3. Task-scoped context compilation

Context is compiled per task, not read from a static file:
`compileTaskContext(team, task, constitution)` returns a stable prefix (the
constitution version + always-ask list, which caches well) followed by the
evidence pack for this task's title/detail, fitted to the token budget with
provenance and dates on every line.

## 4. Self-improvement loop

```
evidence (team log, steward, tagged feedback) → proposals (why, evidence, eval, metric)
  → ranked by realized leverage of their kind → draft PR from an isolated worktree
  → register hypothesis + deterministic metric → measure at exact merge base and head
  → promotion gate (green checks + measured improvement) → merge
  → outcomes feed the next ranking and the proposer-vs-baseline comparison
```

Signals: repeated declined handoffs, steward over-quota roots, and context
tagged `feedback` / `bug` / `feature-request`. `phm improve propose` prints
proposals, ordered by the realized leverage of their kind (proven kinds first,
unmeasured kinds next, kinds with a zero or negative record last).
`--open-pr --repo <dir>` opens each as a **draft** PR
(`workplans/proposals/<id>.md`) on an `improve/*` branch and never pushes to
the default branch. `--auto-merge` is refused on proposals. GitHub evidence
links require a fresh public-repository visibility check; private or unknown
links and local measurements remain withheld.

### Measured outcomes (`src/core/improve/outcomes.ts`, `measure.ts`, `promote.ts`)

A proposal earns credit only from a metric it declares up front:

```json
{ "id": "0123456789", "title": "...", "kind": "team-feedback", "predictedDelta": 0.05,
  "source": { "kind": "model", "engine": "claude", "model": "<exact model id>" },
  "metric": { "name": "eval-pass-rate", "direction": "increase",
              "runner": { "kind": "npm", "script": "eval:memory" } },
  "pr": { "repository": "ashlrai/phantom", "number": 123 } }
```

* `phm improve register <file>` appends it to the digest-chained ledger
  `$ASHLR_HOME/improve/outcomes.jsonl` (public fields only).
* `phm improve measure <id> --repo <dir>` runs the metric in private detached
  worktrees at the PR's exact merge base and head (twice each by default). The
  command's last stdout line must be `{"metric": "<name>", "value": <number>}`.
  It runs with a minimal environment (no tokens or API keys) and a private
  empty HOME, with git hooks and fsmonitor disabled. Under a standing grant
  the metric command also runs inside the verification sandbox (writes only
  to its worktree, no network egress, HOME jailed), because the head is
  agent-written code nobody reviewed; when that sandbox cannot be built the
  measurement is unknown and the command does not run. `npm ci
  --ignore-scripts` still runs outside it, since it needs the registry and
  runs no package code. A failed run, a missing script, or two runs of one
  commit that disagree make the outcome **unknown**, never zero.
* `phm improve outcomes` lists outcomes and compares proposers. Proposals
  chosen by the deterministic rules are the baseline; each exact engine/model
  pair is a fixed-model group. A rate or comparison needs at least three
  measured outcomes on each side, otherwise it is reported as unknown.
* `phm improve promote <id> --repo <dir> [--queue-merge]` evaluates the promotion
  gate: the PR is on an improvement-owned branch (`improve/*`, `ashlr-cloud/*`),
  targets the default branch, is not from a fork, has every reported check
  green on its exact head (at least one actually passed, not only skipped), and
  its metric improved between the current merge base and that head. It also
  refuses when Stop or Pause is on; when the diff touches an owner-lane path
  (`src/core/authority/protected-paths.ts`: CI, manifests, test config, Tier-1
  code), the promotion gate itself, the autopilot, Stop/Pause or the governance
  documents; when it changes its own metric script; or when it weakens tests
  (G1b: deleted test files, removed `it`/`expect` calls, added `.skip`/`.only`).
  The ledger's numbers are claims, so the gate re-measures base and head itself
  and refuses unless its own run reproduces the recorded values and improves.
  The default branch comes from GitHub, the checkout's `origin` must be the PR's
  repository, and the PR is re-read after measuring. With `--queue-merge` and an admitted gate it queues GitHub auto-merge
  (`--squash --auto --match-head-commit <head>`) and then re-reads the PR,
  disabling auto-merge again if its head or base changed, so branch protection and
  required checks still decide the merge; it never uses `--admin`. Anything
  else is refused with reasons, and every decision is recorded in the ledger.
  Without `--queue-merge` it only reports the decision. CONSTITUTION.md v3's
  self-improvement section admits exactly this gate and nothing wider.

### Lessons from matched outcomes (`src/core/improve/lesson-trial.ts`)

Approved lessons (learn/retro knowledge notes) are only worth injecting if
runs that receive them land more often than runs that do not. That is measured
with a randomized holdout, not with hit counts:

* When a cloud launch has applicable notes, a hash of the task id picks its
  arm. A fixed share (`ASHLR_LESSON_HOLDOUT`, default 0.2, 0 turns it off, at
  most 0.5) runs without the lessons block. Both arms record which notes
  applied (`CloudTaskV1.lessons`).
* When the task's PR merges or closes, the cloud tracker records the exact
  head and merge commit, the CI rollup on that head and the review verdict
  (`CloudTaskV1.outcome`). A failed read leaves it absent, which is unknown,
  never green.
* `phm improve observe --repo <dir>` also checks merged cloud tasks for a
  later default-branch revert and records it (`outcome.revertedBy`).
* Cloud retros cite that evidence: a PR closed with failing checks becomes a
  lesson candidate naming the checks and `owner/repo#n @sha`; a review that
  asked for changes or a revert is cited as the cause. Candidates still need
  approval before any run sees them, and a reason a person wrote outranks the
  machine signals.
* `phm improve lessons [--json]` compares the landed rate (merged and not
  reverted) with and without lessons, overall and per note, with a 95%
  interval. Below three finished runs in either arm the effect is unknown.

### Nightly ONE-TEAM proposals

The Verse retro timer also checks for a nightly run after 02:00 UTC, once per
UTC day, when `foundry.selfImprove` is explicitly `true`. It shares the existing
startup delay, shutdown handling and `ASHLR_RETRO_SWEEP_TIMER=0` kill switch.
An hourly sweep being recent or busy does not suppress the nightly check. A
missed night catches up on the next eligible tick while Verse is running.

The local producer supplies two newline-terminated JSONL files under
`~/.ashlr/learn/retro-input/`. Both must exist; an empty review file is valid.
This is a versioned adapter contract because the router queue format is not
part of this repository:

* `jobs.jsonl`: `v: 1`, `id`, `repo` (`owner/repo`), `arm` (a producer-assigned,
  provider-agnostic routing arm), `status`, `updatedAt` (canonical ISO UTC),
  and optional `playbook` (string or null). Status is one of `succeeded`,
  `failed`, `running`, `blocked`, or `cancelled`.
* `review-blocks.jsonl`: `v: 1`, `id`, `jobId`, `repo`,
  `kind: "review-block"`, `updatedAt`, and `body` (at most 16,384 characters).
  Review IDs are stable across edits. Job IDs identify attempts; use a new ID
  for a retry and a newer timestamp to correct an observation.

The latest observation for each repository and ID wins. Conflicting normalized records
at the same timestamp, invalid versions, future timestamps, torn JSONL,
unsafe paths, and unreadable inputs fail the run without advancing completion.
Each input is bounded to 8 MiB and 10,000 rows. Retained jobs and reviews are
each capped at 10,000; the output is capped at 8 MiB. Exceeding a bound requires
operator attention and never silently drops deduplication evidence.

The atomic private file `~/.ashlr/learn/retro-proposals.json` contains:

* Advisory routing priors grouped by repository and arm: `alpha = 1 + successes`,
  `beta = 1 + failures`. Only explicit terminal outcomes count. Review comments
  do not add failures, and these producer observations do not establish verified
  merge credit or automatically change router policy.
* Pending playbook lessons with local job or review evidence references. Raw
  comments are classified into finite categories and discarded. A review joins
  only its exact repository and job; unmatched reviews wait for later input.
* Proposed improvement jobs derived through `fleet/self-improve.ts`, each with
  a stable ID, evaluation and target metric. These are local suggestions only.
* Retained normalized observations and the completed UTC night, committed in
  the same write so retries and process restarts cannot duplicate credit.

No queue, approved knowledge, active playbook, provider, git remote, or live
routing policy is written. Source files are read-only. The nightly path calls
no model and requires no new credentials. Rotating source files is safe after
a successful run because normalized observations remain in the proposal file.
Corrupt output fails closed instead of resetting that history.

## 5. Roadmap

* Proposals implement code (agent run in the worktree) and register their own
  metric; cloud backlog items and goal-loop milestones register through the
  same ledger so all autonomous work shares one outcome record.
* Post-merge re-measurement and revert/regression observations
  (`src/core/fleet/post-merge-observations.ts`) subtract credit.
* Leverage per unit of cost once usage receipts can be joined to proposals.

## 6. Decisions for the operator

1. Initial evidence feeds to wire first (GitHub is the obvious first).
2. Which change classes should earn auto-merge first, and on what record.

# Metrics and observability

Status: **Phase 1 shipped**: telemetry schema + local store
(`src/core/metrics/telemetry.ts`), PR significance/quality scoring, value
attribution, a UCB1 allocator (`scoring.ts`), and a first dashboard
(`phm metrics dashboard`). Feeds the self-improvement loop
([context-and-self-improvement.md](context-and-self-improvement.md)).

## 1. Primary metric

**Value-weighted PRs shipped to production per token**, also per second and
per dollar.

```
value(PR) = significance(PR) [0..10] × quality(PR) [0..1]
```

credited to the session that produced the merged PR only when
`deployedToProduction: true` is recorded explicitly. Missing deployment evidence
earns no shipment credit. Replayed event ids and duplicate PR merges do not
inflate usage or shipment totals. Secondary
metrics are tracked separately and never folded into the primary number:
session success rate, tool error rate, cache hit rate, wall time, disk/context
health.

## 2. Telemetry schema (v1)

Append-only JSONL at `$ASHLR_HOME/metrics/events.jsonl` (0600). Invalid event
kinds, unknown payload fields, credential-shaped values and nonfinite or
negative usage counts are refused before writing. Reads validate saved records
and ignore corrupt lines; logs larger than 64 MiB require rotation before reading. JSONL keeps
Phase 1 dependency-free; Phase 2 adds a DuckDB/SQLite projection with the same
columns. Every event carries attribution:

| field | |
|---|---|
| `v, id, ts` | schema version, id, ISO time |
| `sessionId, agent, model, resource, strategy, process, taskType, repo, owner` | attribution dimensions |

| `kind` | extra fields |
|---|---|
| `session.started` | none |
| `session.ended` | `outcome` (success/failure/abandoned), `wallMs` |
| `usage` | `inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedTokens?, costUsd?, wallMs?` |
| `tool.called` | `tool, ok, ms?` |
| `pr.opened / pr.merged / pr.reverted` | `pr: {repo, number, additions, deletions, files, areas[], userFacing, risk, ciPassedFirstTry, reviewFindings, followUpFixes, coverageDelta, deployedToProduction}` |
| `pr.rated` | `pr, rater: human/llm-judge, rating 1..5, rubric?` |

Record with `phm metrics record '<json>'` (or `recordEvent()` in-process).

## 3. PR scoring (lightweight, non-constraining)

Grading is an explicit caller-driven operation. The adapters support asynchronous,
sampled grading after merge; no grader runs automatically and no endpoint is
configured by this feature. Risk tolerance is high:

* **Significance (0–10), upside-weighted:** log size (no penalty cap) +
  boldness (risk 0.3/1/2 is a *bonus*) + user-facing (0.5/2.5) + critical
  area (security, auth, secrets, release, billing, core, infra: 1.5, else 0.5).
* **Quality (0–1):** starts at 0.75; +0.1 CI green first try; up to +0.1 for
  coverage gains; **only real regressions subtract** (−0.15 per follow-up fix,
  max −0.5); a revert sets it to 0. CI retries and review comments are normal
  iteration and are not penalized. When sampled ratings exist, quality =
  0.7 × quantitative + 0.3 × mean rating.

**Scale:** built for hundreds of PRs a day per person and thousands or more
per team. Scoring is O(1) per PR from metadata. Ratings use deterministic
hash sampling (`sampled(pr, rate)`, so every machine picks the same PRs) and a
bounded-concurrency async queue (`gradeBatch`). Failures are dropped.

**Pluggable raters** (`src/core/metrics/raters.ts`): `Rater { id, rate() }`.
Ships with `localModelRater(complete)` (any injected local endpoint) and a
`jevRater(ask)` adapter for Jev / TypeSafe AI ([JEV-INTEGRATION](../JEV-INTEGRATION.md)).
The caller injects the client and resolves credentials through Phantom
Secrets. Phantom ships no key and makes no network call here.

## 4. Attribution and allocation

`rollup()` aggregates value, tokens, wall time and cost by agent, model and
strategy (leaderboards sorted by value per 1M tokens), plus per-day
throughput. `recommend(taskType, arms)` is a UCB1 bandit: unseen arms are
explored first, then the arm with the best normalized value per 1M tokens
plus its confidence bonus wins. Phase 2 adds an LP allocator that respects
subscription windows, local RAM/concurrency caps and budgets.

## 5. Dashboard

`phm metrics dashboard [--out file]` writes one self-contained HTML file (no
scripts, no network). It shows a hero number (value per 1M tokens), KPIs, value
per day, a quality trend, leaderboards by agent, strategy and model, cost per
day, and context/disk health from the steward. There is **one primary action**:
`phm steward disk --apply` when disk is over quota, otherwise
`phm improve propose`. Phase 2 moves this into the Verse UI.

## 6. Privacy

Local by default. Sharing (team sync or aggregate) is opt-in. Secret-shaped
values are refused, not redacted-and-stored. The accepted schema contains counts, ids, scores and an optional rating rubric;
arbitrary prompt or response fields are refused. Metrics-based improvement
proposals withhold agent identities and measurements from public PR text.

## 7. Roadmap

* Phase 2: auto-ingest from Phantom runs and `gh` (merged PRs, CI, reverts),
  LLM-judge rubric job, DuckDB projection, Verse dashboard, team sharing.
* Phase 3: LP allocator wired into dispatch; per-process A/B experiments.
