Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/contracts/CONTRACT-M7.md

# CONTRACT-M7 — Shared Memory / Genome

Cross-project, local-first shared memory the whole ecosystem reads from and writes
to. Aggregates per-project `.ashlrcode/genome/` dirs across indexed repos plus a hub
store at `~/.ashlr/genome/hub.jsonl`. Recall ranks local-first (keyword/TF-IDF), with
optional best-effort embedding rerank via local Ollama. Never cloud. Fully offline-capable.

All shapes below are defined in `src/core/types.ts` (THE CONTRACT) and MUST NOT be
redefined downstream:

- `GenomeEntry { id: string; project: string | null; source: 'project' | 'hub'; title: string; text: string; tags: string[]; ts: string }`
- `RecallHit { entry: GenomeEntry; score: number; method: 'keyword' | 'embedding' }`
- `GenomeHealth { totalEntries: number; projects: number; hubEntries: number; sizeBytes: number; lastLearnedAt: string | null; embeddingsAvailable: boolean }`
- `LearnInput { text: string; title?: string; project?: string; tags?: string[] }`
- `AshlrConfig.genome?: { maxRecall: number; injectOnRun: boolean }` — optional top-level field; defaults `maxRecall: 5`, `injectOnRun: true`.

## EXACT SIGNATURES

### `src/core/genome/store.ts`

```ts
import type { AshlrConfig, GenomeEntry, GenomeHealth, LearnInput } from '../types.js';

/**
 * Aggregate the full genome: every indexed repo's `<repo>/.ashlrcode/genome/`
 * (manifest.json + section .md/.json files; parse defensively — formats vary)
 * PLUS the hub store at `~/.ashlr/genome/hub.jsonl`. Bounded reads (cap
 * entries/bytes). Never throws on malformed input; skip unreadable sources.
 */
export function loadGenome(cfg: AshlrConfig): GenomeEntry[];

/**
 * APPEND a single entry to `~/.ashlr/genome/hub.jsonl` (one JSON object per
 * line). NEVER overwrites/deletes existing entries. Creates the store dir/file
 * if missing. If `input.project` resolves to an indexed repo, MAY additionally
 * drop a NEW note file under that repo's `.ashlrcode/genome/` — never modifying
 * existing genome files. Returns the entry that was written (source: 'hub').
 */
export function appendHubEntry(input: LearnInput): GenomeEntry;

/** Absolute path to the hub store: `~/.ashlr/genome/hub.jsonl`. */
export function hubStorePath(): string;

/**
 * Status/health of the aggregated genome: entry counts, project coverage,
 * hub store size, staleness (lastLearnedAt), and whether a local
 * embedding-capable model is available. Never throws.
 */
export function genomeHealth(cfg: AshlrConfig, snapshot?: { ollamaModels: readonly string[] }): GenomeHealth;
```

### `src/core/genome/recall.ts`

```ts
import type { AshlrConfig, RecallHit, GenomeEntry } from '../types.js';

/**
 * Search the aggregated genome and return the top relevant hits with source +
 * score, sorted descending by score. Default ranking: local keyword/TF-IDF
 * overlap (method 'keyword'). When `opts.embeddings` is true AND a local
 * embedding-capable model is present (Ollama /api/embeddings, e.g. bge-m3),
 * OPTIONALLY rerank with embeddings (method 'embedding') — best-effort, falls
 * back to keyword on any failure, NEVER calls a cloud API. `opts.limit`
 * defaults to `cfg.genome?.maxRecall ?? 5`. Works fully offline.
 */
export async function recall(
  query: string,
  cfg: AshlrConfig,
  opts?: { limit?: number; embeddings?: boolean },
): Promise<RecallHit[]>;

/**
 * Keyword/TF-IDF overlap score for a single entry against a query. Pure,
 * synchronous, deterministic. Higher is more relevant; 0 means no overlap.
 */
export function keywordScore(query: string, entry: GenomeEntry): number;
```

### `src/cli/genome.ts`

```ts
/**
 * `ashlr recall "<query>"` — search the aggregated genome, print top hits with
 * source + score. Returns process exit code (0 success).
 */
export async function cmdRecall(args: string[]): Promise<number>;

/**
 * `ashlr learn "<text>" [--project <name>] [--tags a,b]` — APPEND a GenomeEntry
 * to the hub store (and optionally a NEW note into a resolved project's
 * `.ashlrcode/genome/`). Never overwrites. Returns process exit code.
 */
export async function cmdLearn(args: string[]): Promise<number>;

/**
 * `ashlr genome` — print genome status/health (entry count, projects covered,
 * staleness, store size, embeddings availability). Returns process exit code.
 */
export async function cmdGenome(args: string[]): Promise<number>;
```

## GUARDRAILS (binding on implementers)

- **Local-first**: embeddings ONLY via local Ollama; NEVER call a cloud API.
  Recall/learn MUST work fully offline (keyword path).
- **Append-only**: `appendHubEntry` APPENDS, never overwrites/deletes existing
  genome. Writes ONLY under `~/.ashlr/genome/` (and optionally a NEW note file
  under a project's `.ashlrcode/genome/` — never modify existing genome files).
- **Bounded**: cap entries/bytes read; recall injection into `ashlr run` is
  bounded (small k via `cfg.genome.maxRecall`, char cap) and behind `--no-memory`.
- **Privacy**: genome is the user's own notes/summaries — read/store locally;
  never exfiltrate; print no secrets.

## INTEGRATION POINTS (for owning agents — not new files here)

- `ashlr status`: surface a one-line genome summary (via `genomeHealth`).
- `ashlr doctor`: add a genome check (store reachable, counts, staleness).
- `ashlr run` orchestrator: inject top-k `recall(goal, cfg)` hits into the
  sub-agent system prompt, bounded, behind a `--no-memory` flag (gated on
  `cfg.genome?.injectOnRun ?? true`).

## RULES

Zero new runtime deps. Each agent writes ONLY its file(s). No git commit.
Build against this contract; do not redefine contract types.

`genomeHealth` accepts an optional invocation-scoped Ollama model snapshot to
reuse a completed provider probe. An empty list means unavailable/no models;
omitting the snapshot retains the standalone synchronous probe.

<!-- page: contracts/CONTRACT-MISSION-RECEIPT-V1 -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/contracts/CONTRACT-MISSION-RECEIPT-V1.md

# Mission Observation Receipt V1 Contract

Status: source contract. This document does not attest runtime installation,
daemon activation, automatic reconciliation, merge authority, release, or
deployment.

## Purpose

Mission Observation Receipt V1 records one bounded, authenticated snapshot of
what the local Hub observed after an explicit planning reconciliation. It binds
the exact briefing digest, Ecosystem Mission Graph digest, source snapshots,
node lifecycle, HMAC-obscured goal and proposal references, verification
evidence, and realized merge revisions.

The receipt is evidence, never authority. It cannot create a goal, dispatch an
agent, create or approve a proposal, merge, release, deploy, publish, access a
credential, mutate an external system, establish company truth, change policy,
or earn a learning label.

## Authority invariants

Every valid record fixes these values:

- `authority: "observation-only"`;
- planning, execution, proposal, merge, release, deployment, external-mutation,
  and learning authority are all `false`;
- `policyEligible`, `verifierIsolated`, `humanDecisionEvidenceComplete`, and
  `outcomeEvidenceComplete` are `false`;
- `businessOutcomeStatus` is `"not-observed"`; and
- `attestationAuthority` is `"host-shared-hmac"`.

The HMAC proves that a process with the existing local provenance key recorded
the bytes. It is not independent verification and does not prove that the host
or current operating system is uncompromised.

## Input and source quality

The receipt writer accepts evidence-normalized input. All four sources—the
briefing, enrollment, goals, and linked proposals—must report a complete bounded
read with a lowercase SHA-256 source digest. The briefing source digest must
equal `missionObservationBriefingDigest()` for the supplied briefing.
Missing-but-complete empty operational sources are valid. A degraded or
incomplete source returns `source-degraded` and writes nothing.

The shared `missionObservationBriefingDigest()` canonicalizes a plain JSON-like
briefing with NFC string normalization, code-unit key ordering, finite numbers,
data properties only, cycle/depth/node/byte bounds, and domain-separated
SHA-256. The briefing itself is never persisted in the receipt.

V1 accepts no human-approval boolean and no external outcome assertion. Those
require later, separately authenticated protocols. A graph's engineering status
may be complete while its business outcome remains unobserved.

## Bounded evidence

A receipt contains 1–24 unique mission nodes. Each node has no more than eight
unique blockers and 64 milestones; the complete receipt has no more than 512
milestones and 256 KiB of canonical serialized data.

Local goal, milestone, and proposal identifiers are converted to
domain-separated HMAC references. Receipts do not persist objectives,
rationales, repository paths, diffs, verification commands/output, PR URLs,
provider payloads, credentials, or raw business evidence.

A work milestone is engineering-realized only when all of these are bound:

1. proposal status is `applied`;
2. passing verification has a SHA-256 evidence digest;
3. realized merge source is `local-default-branch` or `github-host`;
4. the exact lowercase 40-hex merge revision is present; and
5. a SHA-256 realized-merge evidence digest is present.

A work node is complete only when it has at least one non-skipped milestone and
every non-skipped milestone is engineering-realized. Human gates cannot be
complete in V1; they are blocked or awaiting an authenticated human receipt.

## Identity, replay, and authentication

The canonical identities are domain separated:

- `snapshotDigest` hashes every semantic observation field except `recordedAt`
  and authentication fields;
- `receiptId` hashes the graph digest and snapshot digest;
- `receiptDigest` hashes the complete unsigned record, including `recordedAt`;
- `attestation` is HMAC-SHA-256 over the receipt digest and unsigned body.

An identical semantic retry therefore selects the same immutable slot even when
it observes a later wall clock. The earliest valid persisted record is returned
as `replayed`. A different semantic snapshot receives a different receipt ID.

## Persistence

Receipts live under `~/.ashlr/mission-receipts/` through the shared
`ImmutablePrivateRecordStore`. The writer uses the existing provenance key and
never creates one. Readers use the read-only key loader and do not create keys,
directories, locks, or cleanup writes.

The store supplies exact-private directories and files, identity pinning,
no-clobber hard-link publication, cooperative writer locking, authenticated
crash recovery, post-write point verification, bounded aggregate reads, and
explicit missing/healthy/degraded source state. Aggregate consumers must use
`requireComplete: true`. A point read authenticates only one slot and makes no
claim about ledger completeness.

## Lifecycle use

The first integration point is `ashlr vision shadow [--json]`. It reads bounded
briefing, enrollment, goal, and proposal snapshots, records one immutable
observation receipt, and emits at most one all-false `would-create` or `hold`
suggestion. It never calls goal adoption, proposal creation, agent dispatch,
merge, release, deployment, publication, external mutation, policy, or budget
APIs. A receipt failure returns nonzero and emits no trusted suggestion.

The ordinary `ashlr vision reconcile` command remains an explicit planning
mutation and does not yet write this receipt. Post-effect capture, a shared
CLI/daemon reconcile lease, and an independently activated automatic mode are
separate future integrations.

Receipts must not be read by mission readiness projection. A future shadow
reconciler may require a healthy complete receipt source as an additional audit
gate, but it must still recompute readiness from current authoritative sources
and exact current graph/briefing digests.

<!-- page: contracts/CONTRACT-OUTCOME-LEARNING -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/contracts/CONTRACT-OUTCOME-LEARNING.md

# Outcome learning

Status: source-complete. The dispatch log is the memory. There is no operator
setting for the weights, the exploration rate, or the failure threshold.

## What it records

`learnOutcomes` reads a dispatch event log. A finished job is an `ASSIGN` or
`LAUNCH` (with resource, model, job type, and repo) followed by an `OUTCOME`
(`merged`, `closed`, `dirty`, or `fixup`, plus usage, optional minutes, and
`breakage=0|1`). The same facts may arrive as JSON lines. Legacy
`LAUNCH job repo lane tier` rows are ignored. For each
(resource, model, job type, repo) the view reports merge rate, time to merge,
usage, and breakage rate.

## How it routes

`routeLearnedJob` draws a Thompson sample from a Beta success posterior and a
Gamma cheapness posterior. Success is a merge that did not break main.
Cheapness is the inverse of usage, so the draw favors the cheapest resource
that ships. A cold resource still wins some draws; that is the exploration.

When a resource's observed time to merge is longer than the time left before
its allowance resets, it cannot take the job. Among resources that can finish,
one whose allowance resets sooner gets a higher score, which is the
usage-before-reset balance. A critical job never returns `wait`: if something
can take it now, it is sent there; if nothing can, the action is `nowhere`.

The plain-language reason names the constraint that decided the assignment,
for example `Sent to Devin because CMP Codex resets in 40 min with 5% left.`

`learnedSeatPenalty` turns the same posterior means into seat-router penalties.
Omitting the penalty leaves `routeSeat` unchanged.

## Improvement jobs

A failure pattern becomes an improvement job when it has happened at least
three times and, for a low merge rate, good merges are the minority. The jobs
are data. This module does not enqueue them, spend, or merge.

## Surfaces

`phm fleet outcomes` and `phm fleet outcomes route` print the view. `--json`
is the same object the desktop imports from
`desktop/outcome-learning-view.ts`.


<!-- page: contracts/CONTRACT-SELECTOR -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/contracts/CONTRACT-SELECTOR.md

# Selector

Status: source-complete. A standing ranker above the job queue. It reads
candidates, scores them with what the dispatch log has learned, and funds the
top few as `READY` lines. Source: `src/core/routing/selector.ts`; CLI:
`src/cli/select.ts`.

## Score

`score = value x leverage / (minutes + usage x 60)`

- `value` and `leverage` come from the candidate. `leverage` defaults to 1.
- `minutes` and `usage` come from the candidate (`estMinutes`, `estUsage`), else
  from the outcome-learning cells for the same repo and job type
  (`learnOutcomes`, the router from #2775), else 30 minutes and 0.3 usage.
  Each pick reports which one it used as `basis`.
- `predictedValue = value x leverage x merge rate`, where merge rate is the
  smoothed good-merge rate of the same cells (prior 0.5, weight 2). It is what
  funding the pick is expected to return, and is what the picks log records so
  a later run can compare it with the real outcome.

Ties break by id. There is no tuning setting.

## Candidates

`<runs-dir>/selector/candidates.jsonl`, one object per line: `id` (`RQ-*`),
`scope`, `repo`, `value` (> 0), and optional `acceptance`, `jobType` (default
`work`), `pool` (default `claude`), `tier` (default `work`), `priority`
(`P0`..`P3`, default `P2`), `leverage`, `estMinutes`, `estUsage`. A malformed or
duplicate row is counted as `rejected`, never fatal. Scope and acceptance are
untrusted text: control characters and parentheses are removed so a candidate
cannot add fields, jobs, or dependencies to the line it produces.

## Funding

`phm select` takes the top `--top` (default 5) candidates that are not already
in `picks.jsonl`, prints each as a `READY` line the queue importer reads
(`docs/QUEUE.md`), appends `{at, rank, id, repo, jobType, score, predictedValue,
mergeRate, minutes, usage, basis}` to `<runs-dir>/selector/picks.jsonl`, and posts
a `selector.picks` envelope (`from: selector`, `to: planner`, P2, one hour TTL)
to the local bus inbox. `--dry-run` writes and posts nothing. `--json` prints the
whole result including `bus` (the post status) and each pick's `ready` line.
The selector does not enqueue, claim, spend, or merge; a planner appends the
lines to the queue.

## Hourly on the Mac

`phm select schedule` previews the launchd agent `ai.ashlr.phm.selector`
(`StartInterval` 3600, runs `phm select --json`); `--write` installs the plist
and prints the `launchctl bootstrap` command. It does not load it.

# CONTRACT-XREVIEW: Cross-model review and SHA-bound merge decision v1

Status: source-complete. This contract adds no merge authority. It never runs
gh and never merges. Host custody supplies scoped GitHub access for CI reads.
It produces a review record and a decision. The supervisor that holds merge rights acts on them.
Operator guide: [Cross-model review](../CROSS-REVIEW.md).

## Exports

`src/core/fleet/cross-review.ts`. All exports are pure, with no IO.

- `parseCrossReviewPolicy(raw)` and `parseCrossReviewRequest(raw)` return
  `{ ok: true, … } | { ok: false, errors }`. Both fail closed: one invalid
  reviewer rejects the whole policy.
- `reviewerLaunchProblem(reviewer): string | null` gives the launch rules.
  A claude reviewer needs the restricted argv, `-p`, a stdin prompt and text
  output. A local reviewer must be a tool-less runner. Only the family's
  model credential is passed, and `FORBIDDEN_CREDENTIAL_ENV_RE` names are
  never passed.
- `selectCrossReviewer(producer, reviewers)` picks a reviewer on another
  pool from an independent family.
- `scanSensitiveChange({ diff, repo, policy, codeowners }): SensitiveScan`,
  together with `diffPathsForReview`, `codeownersGlobs`,
  `isSelfRepoTarget` and `CROSS_REVIEW_ESCALATE_PATTERNS`.
- `buildCrossReviewPrompt(request, diff)` is the only sink for job text.
  `parseReviewVerdict(output)` accepts the closed schema
  (`REVIEW_REASON_CODES`) and nothing else.
- `decideCrossReview(input): CrossReviewDecision` and `diffSha256`,
  `isCommitSha`, `prUrl`. The optional `checks` evidence binds `headSha` to a
  hold code or `null` for success; omitted evidence holds with `checks-unreadable`.

`src/core/fleet/cross-review-process.ts`:

- `runReviewerProcess(reviewer, prompt, { parentEnv?, onScratch? }): Promise<ReviewerRun>`
  never throws.
- `buildReviewerEnv(reviewer, scratch, parentEnv)`.
- `REVIEWER_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES`.

`src/core/fleet/cross-review-run.ts`:

- `runCrossReview(request, policy, deps?)` and
  `decideCrossReviewAtHead(request, policy, head, { pauseFile?, now? })` both
  return promises. Before approval they read live required checks and exact-SHA
  results through host custody, then re-read the PR head and stop states.
- `latestCrossReview(repo, pr)` and `loadCrossReviewPolicy(path?)`.
- `crossReviewPolicyPath`, `crossReviewLogPath`, `crossReviewPauseFile` and
  `readBoundedFile`.

`src/cli/cross-review.ts` exports `cmdFleetCrossReview(args)`, which backs
`phm fleet xreview run|decide`.

## Invariants (each covered by `test/cross-review*.test.ts`)

1. `enable-auto-merge` requires every one of the following:
   - an approve verdict;
   - recorded at exactly the head SHA the caller passes now;
   - over the same diff sha256;
   - a clean sensitive scan;
   - a reviewer on another pool and an independent family;
   - an allowed repo;
   - KILL off and PAUSE absent;
   - nonempty required checks, all completed successfully on the current head
     with matching App identities. Missing, pending, failing, stale or unreadable
     evidence holds with a structured reason; API error bodies are never logged.

   Only then is `matchHeadCommit` set.
2. If the head moved or the diff changed, the action is `re-review`. A stale
   verdict is never reused.
3. The reviewer process inherits no GitHub, git, ssh, cloud or `ASHLR_*`
   env. Its HOME, cwd and TMPDIR are a fresh 0700 scratch that is removed
   afterwards. The prompt goes to stdin, with `shell: false` and no job text
   in argv.
4. The review log and audit log hold structured fields only. They never hold
   diff text, job text, model output, env values or file paths.
5. Any malformed reviewer output, non-zero exit, timeout, oversize output or
   refused launch escalates.

# Milestone contracts

Per-milestone **contracts-first** build specifications. Each milestone (M*/H*) was built by an
agent fleet against a contract authored in its scaffold phase: module boundaries, the hard safety
invariants, and how each is verified. They are a historical/design record — the code is the source
of truth; these capture the intent and the safety reasoning at build time.

Not every shipped milestone has a standalone contract file — many were delivered as part of a
batched CHANGELOG entry instead. For a complete ID → subject → status lookup across every
milestone (including which numbers were spec'd for one thing and shipped as another), see
[`docs/MILESTONE-INDEX.md`](../MILESTONE-INDEX.md) — check it before assigning the next milestone
number.

- [`CONTRACT-M566.md`](./CONTRACT-M566.md) — private, default-off execution-capacity reservation ledger.
- [`CONTRACT-M567.md`](./CONTRACT-M567.md) — source-complete, default-off local Docker observation broker.
- [`CONTRACT-M568.md`](./CONTRACT-M568.md) — version-general, authority-free stopped-selection broker permit.
- [`CONTRACT-M570.md`](./CONTRACT-M570.md) — strict, authority-free release-successor policy evidence schema and verifier.
- [`CONTRACT-M571.md`](./CONTRACT-M571.md) — exact-source local production gate and canonical no-authority receipt.
- [`CONTRACT-XREVIEW.md`](./CONTRACT-XREVIEW.md) — cross-model review on another pool and the SHA-bound auto-merge decision.

<!-- page: daemon-tick-phases -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/daemon-tick-phases.md

# Daemon tick phases

Every awaited stage of a resident daemon tick now runs inside a bounded
**phase**. A phase has a deadline, an `AbortSignal`, exception capture, a
degrade path and a log line — so one wedged await can never freeze
`lastTickAt` again. This page is the operator reference for reading and
tuning that behavior.

## Read the phases

```sh
phm daemon status --json | jq .tick.phases
```

```json
[
  { "name": "tick hooks", "status": "ok", "durationMs": 412 },
  { "name": "mirror-prep", "status": "ok", "durationMs": 8031 },
  { "name": "backlog-refresh", "status": "ok", "durationMs": 96 },
  { "name": "self-heal", "status": "ok", "durationMs": 210 },
  { "name": "invent", "status": "skipped", "error": "no-frontier", "durationMs": 3 },
  { "name": "capacity", "status": "ok", "durationMs": 87 },
  { "name": "dispatch-plan", "status": "ok", "durationMs": 12 },
  { "name": "dispatch", "status": "timeout", "durationMs": 305004,
    "error": "phase exceeded its 5 min deadline; cancelled and left running detached" }
]
```

`.tick` also carries `lastTickAt`, `outcome` and `lastError`. While a tick is
in flight `tickInProgress` names the phase currently running.

## Phase statuses

| status      | meaning                                                        |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `ok`        | the stage settled inside its deadline                          |
| `degraded`  | the stage threw or rejected; the tick continued and completed  |
| `timeout`   | the stage exceeded its deadline; cancelled, then left detached |
| `skipped`   | intentionally not run (`error` says why, e.g. `no-frontier`)   |
| `running`   | in-progress snapshot only — never persisted                    |

## Tick outcomes

`.tick.outcome` folds the phases plus whole-tick failure into one word:

- `ok` — every phase settled clean.
- `degraded` — at least one phase threw.
- `timeout` — at least one phase hit its deadline, or the whole tick was
  abandoned at the resident deadline.
- `failed` — `tick()` threw before it could produce a record.

`lastTickAt` advances on every outcome — including `failed` and `timeout`.
A frozen `lastTickAt` was the original incident shape: one never-settling
await inside `tick()` kept `recordTick` unreachable forever. `runDaemon` now
wraps each `tick()` call in a 60-minute backstop (`DAEMON_TICK_DEADLINE_MS`)
and persists the outcome in a `finally`, whatever `tick()` did.

## Deadlines

| phase            | default deadline | what bounds it                                          |
|------------------|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| `tick hooks`     | ~26 min          | `boundedBeforeTick` (25 min + grace)                    |
| `mirror-prep`    | prep + abort grace + 30 s | wraps the existing per-repo mirror deadline      |
| `backlog-refresh`| 5 min            | `TICK_PHASE_BACKLOG_REFRESH_MS`                         |
| `self-heal`      | 5 min            | `TICK_PHASE_MAINTENANCE_MS`; verify subprocesses ≤15 min|
| `invent`         | 3 min            | `TICK_PHASE_INVENT_MS`; frontier probe ≤30 s            |
| `ancillary`      | 5 min            | `TICK_PHASE_MAINTENANCE_MS`                             |
| `reflection`     | 3 min            | `TICK_PHASE_REFLECTION_MS` (nested inside `ancillary`)  |
| `auto-merge`, `proposal-repair` | 5 min | `TICK_PHASE_MAINTENANCE_MS`                   |
| `capacity`       | 30 s             | `TICK_PHASE_CAPACITY_MS`; internally probed             |
| `dispatch-plan`  | 60 s             | `TICK_PHASE_DISPATCH_PLAN_MS`                           |
| `dispatch`       | worst-case turns | `tasks / slots` × (turn watchdog + grace)               |
| `dispatch-hook`  | 60 s             | per-item `afterDispatch` hooks                          |

At a deadline the phase's `AbortSignal` fires; it then gets a 5-second grace
(`TICK_PHASE_GRACE_MS`) to wind down. Still-running work is left **detached**
and its late rejection is swallowed — never an unhandled rejection, never a
record leaking into the next tick's ledger.

## Dispatched runs never block the tick

`superviseFleetTurn` bounds every turn — not just llama-server ones — at
`localFleet.taskTimeoutMs` (default 20 min, config
`daemon.localFleet.taskTimeoutMs`). Past that the turn is detached with a
`turn-deadline` outcome and the dispatch phase completes. The detached run
keeps its own engine backstops and stall monitor; the tick does not kill it.

A second resident tick refuses to start while a previously abandoned tick is
still open (`refused-open`), so two ticks can never race over shared state.

## Child processes on the tick path

Verification subprocesses (typecheck / test / build via
`runVerifyCommandAsync`) already run with hard timeouts, SIGTERM → SIGKILL
process-group escalation, and bounded drain. A phase deadline now also flows
into them as an `AbortSignal` — cancellation terminates the child process
group instead of waiting on it.

`log stream` denial watchers are file-polled, lifecycle-managed and never
awaited for exit: start blocks ≤ `STREAM_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` (3 s), the
end-of-run barrier waits ≤ `BARRIER_TIMEOUT_MS` (3 s), and `finish()` /
`abort()` stop the watcher with `SIGTERM`. Run disposal always aborts the
watcher, so it cannot leak past the run.

## No frontier client ⇒ invent is skipped

`invent` probes `resolvePlanningClient` against a 30-second bound. `null`
records `skipped: no-frontier`; a wedged probe records `timeout`. Neither
holds the tick open, so "no frontier client available" can never freeze
`lastTickAt` again.

## Mirror prep

`hooks.beforeTick`'s mirror preparation is wrapped as one `mirror-prep`
phase whose bound is the per-repo mirror deadline plus abort grace plus 30 s
of slack. The per-repo mirror internals (each git call bounded at 10 min,
the bounded repo lease, dependency installs) keep their own guarantees; this
phase only ensures the whole stage cannot outlive the tick.

## Budget

`phm daemon status` labels `--budget` "legacy --budget metered cap": it gates
metered USD spend only. $0 subscription and local-model work continues under
their own admission checks; the metered cap is not a stop for them.


<!-- page: design/plugins -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/design/plugins.md

# Phantom features as plugins

Status: proposal, not implemented. Scope: package existing Phantom features behind a common registry while preserving every public CLI contract. This builds on [the existing plugin system](../PLUGINS.md); it does not replace its trust model. The requested research source `/workspace/phantom-work/research/bbide.md` was unavailable in this worktree environment.

## Boundary and manifest

Keep the CLI bootstrap, argument parsing, configuration, policy, audit, kill switch and plugin loader in the host. A feature owns its implementation and declares its commands and dependencies; the host owns routing and safety decisions. Core features ship with Phantom and are trusted as part of the installed release. Third-party plugins remain default-off, explicitly enabled and integrity-checked; they run in-process with the host's OS privileges, not in a sandbox. Capability declarations constrain host registration, not arbitrary Node access.

Extend the existing `manifest.json` schema in a versioned API revision, retaining `name`, `version`, `apiVersion`, `entry` and `capabilities`. A bundled feature additionally declares `commands` (full command paths, aliases, help and supported options) and `requires` (feature IDs and compatible version ranges). Example proposal:

```json
{"name":"backlog","version":"1.0.0","apiVersion":"^2.0.0","entry":"./index.js","capabilities":["command"],"commands":[{"path":["backlog"],"aliases":[],"help":"Manage the work queue"}],"requires":[]}
```

The host validates names, paths, versions, capability declarations and dependency ranges before importing code. Bundled manifests are generated or checked against the release inventory; they cannot be shadowed by user plugin directories. Existing v1 external manifests and `phm x <name>` continue through the current loader unchanged until a separately specified migration. No automatic installation, network fetch or dependency execution occurs during discovery.

## Discovery and load order

1. Read the bundled inventory and external manifests without executing plugin code. Apply the existing external disable switch, kill switch, enablement, API compatibility and integrity gates before import.
2. Validate the entire bundled command inventory and dependency graph. A duplicate ID, command path or alias, missing/incompatible dependency, or cycle is a deterministic startup error naming the conflict; never choose a winner by filesystem order. An invalid external plugin is skipped and audited under existing behavior; it cannot claim a builtin path.
3. Topologically sort bundled features by dependency, breaking ties by ASCII feature ID. Lazily activate only the selected command's transitive dependencies in that order; cache successful activation per process. Help, version, completion and manifest inspection use metadata and execute no feature code.
4. Register only declared contributions. A bundled dependency or activation failure fails the requested command with a nonzero exit and an actionable error; unrelated commands remain available. External failures retain the existing isolated, audited behavior. No silent fallback to another implementation.

Dependencies express initialization order, not implicit authority. A feature accesses other features through narrow versioned host interfaces; cycles are rejected rather than resolved through globals. The external kill switch must not disable bundled commands needed for recovery.

## CLI parity and rollout

The host dispatches existing `phm` and `ashlr` names to the same feature handlers. Preserve command paths, aliases, argument validation, defaults, stdout/stderr, JSON shapes, exit codes, help, completion, lazy side effects and authorization gates. Unknown commands and conflicting registrations fail deterministically. External commands stay under `x`; a plugin cannot override a builtin. Management commands remain host-owned so recovery works even if a feature fails.

First inventory current dispatch, help, completions and machine-readable commands, including aliases and error cases. Add a registry in shadow mode and compare its routing and metadata against that inventory without changing execution. Migrate one low-risk feature behind a reversible internal switch, then migrate feature by feature; keep the old dispatcher until parity is demonstrated. Rollback restores the prior dispatch path without changing user config or external plugin pins. Publish an API compatibility and deprecation plan before changing external manifests.

Acceptance requires fixture-driven old/new CLI comparisons for successful and invalid invocations, JSON, streams, exit codes, help and completions; dependency ordering, collisions, cycles, missing dependencies and activation failure tests; and tests proving discovery/help do not import code, external gates still apply, and recovery commands work with plugins disabled. Measure cold startup and command latency against the existing CLI before expanding rollout. No feature is removed until its parity and safety tests pass.

Open decisions before implementation: choose the API v2 schema and interface ownership, define bundled artifact integrity and release packaging, identify the first migration candidate, and set measured startup budgets. The unavailable research should be reviewed before approving the design.


<!-- page: doctrine/FRICTION-LOOP -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/doctrine/FRICTION-LOOP.md

# Friction loop doctrine

Mason's operating pattern for the fleet: delegate everything, find where delegation breaks, and build the tool that removes the break safely. This page is doctrine — it describes how autonomy work is chosen. It grants no runtime authority and changes no gate; [Security GATES v3 and the hold list](../../AGENTS.md#article-1-full-autonomy-always-forward) stay exactly as they are.

## The pattern

The default is that an agent does the work. When a task stops for a human, that stop is a signal, not an annoyance to route around. Repeated stops of the same shape mean the harness is missing a capability, and the highest-leverage fix is usually not a better prompt — it is a tool, an interface, or a custody boundary that makes the human step unnecessary without removing the protection it was pretending to provide.

The loop has four phases. It is a loop, not a pipeline: measurement feeds the next round of identification, and a fix that did not move its signal is reopened, not celebrated.

## 1. Identify — collect friction signals

A friction signal is any point where delegated work had to stop for Mason, or where Mason did the step himself because delegation could not. Signals already observable in this ecosystem:

- **Needs-you items.** Every row in the needs-you drawer ([NEEDS-YOU.md](../NEEDS-YOU.md)) is a residual human step; each recurring row class is a candidate.
- **Holds and gates.** The hold list, lane holds, dispatch switches, parked dependency gates (`phm fleet parked --json`), and stuck-PR quarantine rows are all places work waits on a person or a pin.
- **Stalls in the job ledger.** `metrics/jobs.jsonl` shows queue wait, checkout, model, CI and merge time per attempt (`phm fleet job-latency --jobs jobs.jsonl --json`); a phase that consistently outruns the others is friction with a number on it.
- **Direct reports.** The desktop *Flag UI friction* action appends to `~/.ashlr/router/feedback.jsonl` (see the router README's desktop friction queue); Mason naming a repeated annoyance in chat is the same class of evidence.
- **Hard-limit escalations.** Passwords, 2FA, device approvals, payments and outside sends are the four kept human steps. Each recurring *kind* of escalation is a signal to make the safe path easier, never to remove the limit.
- **Red-main streaks and silent red tests.** A main branch that is red, or a check that has been failing so long nobody reads it, is delegation breaking on verification.

Record the shape of the break — what delegated task stopped, on what missing capability — not just that it stopped.

## 2. Select — score by autonomy unlocked, not ease

Score each candidate on how much delegation it unlocks across fleet work *and* client work:

- **Breadth.** Does it unblock one lane or every lane? A fix used by every agent on every repo outranks a fix used by one worker on one task.
- **Depth.** Does it remove a whole class of human steps (all secret handling) or one instance (this one API key)? Class-removals compound; instance-fixes recur.
- **Safety cost.** The fix must keep the protection while removing the step. A fix that removes friction by removing a gate is a regression, not a win — it is rejected under Article 1.
- **Measurability.** A signal that can be counted before and after beats one that can only be described.

Explicit anti-targets: do not score on ease, speed, or how interesting the tool is. Choosing the easy fix optimizes the fleet's activity metrics, not Mason's leverage. A hard fix that deletes a daily human step beats ten easy fixes that each delete a step nobody takes.

## 3. Solve — design, place, build, verify, ship

- **Design the boundary first.** What does the agent see, what does it never see, and where does custody live? The worked examples below all share one shape: the agent holds a reference, the trusted edge holds the value.
- **Prefer an existing repo over a new tool.** The default is a change inside Phantom or the repo that owns the capability. A new tool is justified only when the friction is a custody boundary the existing repos cannot hold — secret values, identity scope, personal voice data each became a separate tool for exactly that reason.
- **Build through the normal path.** Branch, PR, affected-only checks, merge, release through the sanctioned workflow — same as any other change. Doctrine does not create a shortcut around the merge path.
- **Verify end-to-end.** Run the real delegated task that used to stop and confirm it completes without the human step. A build that cannot be exercised is not done.

## 4. Measure — did the signal drop

Name the signal before building, then check it after shipping:

- The class of needs-you item stops appearing, or its rate drops.
- Human touches per merged PR in that area fall toward zero.
- Jobs no longer stall on the removed step; the ledger shows the phase shrinking.
- The escalation to Mason happens less often, or disappears.

If the signal did not drop, the loop repeats: either the fix missed the real break, or the signal was misread. Unmeasured is not fixed — if the signal cannot be counted, instrument it first and treat the instrumentation as part of the fix.

## Worked examples

### Phantom Secrets — the credential boundary

- **Break.** Every secret a delegated task needed was a Mason step: paste a key, reveal a value, approve an environment. Delegation stopped at every credential.
- **Fix.** A secrets layer where agents carry `phm_` references and `phantom_*` tool calls while real values are injected at the network edge. Values never enter config, logs, or model context — the protection got *stronger* as the step disappeared.
- **Signal that dropped.** Secret-paste steps and "reveal this key" asks per task, to zero.

### Locus — the identity boundary

- **Break.** Agents acting on infrastructure had no scoped identity: "which account, project, org" questions became human steps, and ambient unscoped identity was the unsafe alternative.
- **Fix.** An identity plane with hard-scoped pins — `locus pin`/`locus enter`, frozen scopes, and `whoami`/`doctor` surfaces an agent can read before mutating. The agent can act inside the pin; it can never widen it.
- **Signal that dropped.** Account-scope stalls and ambient-identity workarounds.

### Lexicon — the voice-input boundary

- **Break.** Mason dictates, and speech-to-text mangled the same names every time; each mangled proper noun was a manual correction — voice input, the cheapest delegation channel, was the least reliable one.
- **Fix.** A personal voice lexicon: canonical spellings, `normalize_transcript`, and `learn_correction` so each name is corrected once, permanently.
- **Signal that dropped.** Repeated corrections of the same names across sessions.

### Phantom — engineering work itself

- **Break.** The largest friction was engineering work itself: every repo task needed Mason driving it — queueing, reviewing, merging, watching.
- **Fix.** This workbench: a queue of well-scoped jobs, isolated worktrees, one merge path, fleet lanes, and a needs-you surface that makes the remaining human steps visible and countable.
- **Signal that dropped.** Mason-driven task flow. The needs-you drawer is the residual measure — every item on it is the next loop's input.

## Applying the loop to queue picks

Any job or self-improvement proposal that claims to reduce friction should name, in its description: the signal it addresses, the class of human step it removes, where the change belongs (existing repo or new tool and why), and the metric checked after merge. Proposals scored on ease rather than autonomy unlocked are deprioritized; proposals that remove a gate instead of the human step are rejected.

## Non-goals

- **Not a license to remove gates.** The four hard limits — secrets, money, outside sends, destruction of Mason's data — are kept human steps, not friction to optimize away.
- **Not a license for new tools.** A new repo is the exception and must justify itself by a custody boundary; otherwise the fix goes into the existing repo.
- **Not telemetry for its own sake.** Signals exist to find the next fix, not to produce dashboards. No measurable signal, no claimed win.

# fleet lane-hold — bounded, self-expiring lane hold

`ashlr fleet lane-hold <lane> --minutes <n> --reason <text> [--runs-dir <abs>] [--json]`
places a hold on a lane through the same guarded slots.json temp+rename path
releaseLaneHold uses — nobody hand-edits queue/slots.json when a lane is
burning jobs on dead credentials.

- `--minutes` is required, an integer 1..1440: a Phantom hold always
  expires. dispatchd enforces `held_until`; the cap is 24 h.
- `--reason` is required, printable ASCII, at most 120 chars. It lands in
  `held_reason`, the lane-target-changes.log audit line and the
  dispatch-events.log narration.
- `held_by` stamps `phantom <changed-by> <iso>` and may be refreshed. A row
  held by anyone else — `held_by` not `autobackoff`, not `phantom…` — is
  refused `manual-hold`: a hold a person placed is never overwritten.
- releaseLaneHold still treats a phantom hold as manual; a follow-up
  relaxes that once runs-lane-hold.ts is free.

# Main Health — is the default branch safe?

A **red main** means a PR landed, the main guardian ran post-merge
verification, and one or more CI checks **failed** on that merge commit.
The guardian writes `state: "red"` into `~/.ashlr-runs/guardian/state.json`
along with a `red_first` timestamp so every fleet member can see how long
each repo has been red. Red mains never auto-revert — they surface through
`main-health-needs-you` for an agent or human to act on.

## Check a repo in four seconds

```
ashlr fleet main-red-age
```
Reads `state.json` (or `--state <file>`) and prints each repo's state,
minutes red, attempt count and the current job driving repair. Exit `0`
when the state file is readable; `1` when it is missing or invalid.

## Read it over HTTP

`GET /api/verse/fleet/main-red-age` serves the same projection as
`main-red-age --json`: `{v, generatedAt, known, repos}` where each repo
carries `repo`, `state`, `redSince`, `redMinutes`, `attempts` and
`currentJob`. A missing or unreadable state file answers `200` with
`known: false` and no repos — unknown is never green. The Fleet surface
(⌘2) shows one compact row per repo under "Main health"; agents read the
typed route.

## How many merges rode red checks?

```
ashlr fleet red-merges [--hours 24] [--root <dir>] [--json]
```
Rolls up per-hour merge counts by red/green/other check state across
every lane from `metrics/jobs.jsonl`. Read-only — never dispatches or
mutates anything. Pass `--json` for machine-parseable output.

## Is the build clean right now?

```
npm run typecheck
```
Runs the full type-check suite; `0` means the tree compiles, `1` means
it does not. Pair with `ashlr fleet red-merges --hours 1` to spot
regressions the guardian has not yet caught.

## Guardian reference

Full guardian docs:
https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/docs/main-guardian.md

Source — `main-red-age`:
https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/src/cli/fleet-main-red-age.ts

Source — `red-merges`:
https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/master/src/cli/fleet-red-merges.ts


<!-- page: fleet/pr-hygiene -->

# Fleet pr-hygiene — open-PR triage audit

`ashlr fleet pr-hygiene [--repo <owner/name>] [--stale-days <n>] [--limit <n>] [--json]`
audits every open pull request on one repo and emits a `fleet.pr-hygiene.v1`
triage report for the merge cockpit. It is read-only: the only GitHub calls
are `gh pr list` for open and merged PRs — it never closes, updates or merges
a PR and never reads a PR body.

Each PR is flagged and then triaged into one advisory lane:

| Lane | Meaning | Flag precedence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `close-candidate` | A merged fleet job's prompt named this PR (`PR #n`) — superseded work a host-side closer may reap | `superseded` |
| `refix` | GitHub reports a merge conflict (`mergeable: CONFLICTING` or `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`) | `conflicted` |
| `review` | Idle at least `--stale-days` days (`stale`), or shares files with other open PRs (`overlap`) — a conflict waiting to land | `stale`, then `overlap` |
| `ok` | No hygiene signal | — |

Informational flags that never escalate a PR on their own: `behind`
(`mergeStateStatus: BEHIND`) and `draft`.

## Usage

```sh
phm fleet pr-hygiene --json              # audit ashlrai/phantom, machine-readable
phm fleet pr-hygiene --stale-days 14     # human summary, older stale threshold
phm fleet pr-hygiene --repo org/repo     # audit another enrolled repo
```

Defaults: `--repo ashlrai/phantom`, `--stale-days 7`, `--limit 500` (max 5000).
Exit codes: 0 audit produced (findings are data, not a verdict), 1 the open-PR
list could not be read, 2 bad usage.

## Report shape (`fleet.pr-hygiene.v1`)

    { schema: 'fleet.pr-hygiene.v1', v: 1, repo, generatedAt, staleDays, limit,
      complete,                       // false when the open page filled the limit
      reads: { open: 'ok' | 'failed',
               merged: 'ok' | 'failed' | 'skipped',
               prompts: 'ok' | 'unavailable' },
      counts: { open, unreadable, flagged,
                triage: { 'close-candidate', refix, review, ok },
                flags:  { superseded, conflicted, stale, overlap, behind, draft } },
      items: [{ number, title, url, headRef, isDraft, mergeStateStatus,
                createdAt, updatedAt, ageDays, idleDays, flags, triage, reason,
                supersededBy?: { number, title, jobId },
                overlap?: { count, prs } }],
      error?: string }                // fixed token when reads.open is 'failed'

`items` covers every audited PR, flagged lanes first, then oldest-idle first.
`reason` is one machine token: `superseded-by-merged-pr`, `merge-conflict`,
`stale-no-update`, `file-overlap` or `ok`.

## Evidence honesty

- A failed open read still emits the versioned shape (exit 1) with
  `reads.open: 'failed'`, empty `items` and an `error` token — never a
  fake-clean backlog. gh's stderr is not echoed.
- The superseded leg degrades alone: a failed merged-PR read
  (`reads.merged: 'failed'`) or a missing local prompts directory
  (`reads.prompts: 'unavailable'`) skips supersession matching; the other
  flags are still computed. Supersession is never inferred from titles —
  it needs the same prompt evidence `ashlr fleet superseded` uses.
- Timestamps GitHub did not send parseably leave `ageDays`/`idleDays` null;
  a PR with unknown activity is not flagged `stale`.
- Rows gh could not describe are counted in `counts.unreadable`, not dropped.

The report grants no close, merge or dispatch authority; consumers re-verify
before acting.


<!-- page: fleet/superseded-route -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/fleet/superseded-route.md

# Fleet superseded route

`GET /api/verse/fleet/runs/superseded` serves the `ashlr fleet superseded`
answer to the Merges pane and the phone. Pinned wire (`SupersededReadV1`):

    { v: 1, generatedAt: string, source: 'ok' | 'unavailable',
      pairs: [{ open, openTitle, openState, mergedBy, mergedTitle, jobId }],
      openDirty: number }

Each `pairs` row names an open PR superseded by merged PR `mergedBy`; `jobId`
is the `RQ-…` id the merged title carries; `openDirty` counts open PRs GitHub
reports DIRTY. The last good read is cached for 60 seconds, and every read is
side-effect free: it never mutates git, GitHub or disk.

Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/fleet/telegram-ship.md

# Ship a Phantom release from Telegram

Send `/ship` in the configured private Telegram chat.
Phantom replies with the open release PR and its checks.
Only the configured owner can use this command.
If the PR is green and mergeable, it is armed for 10 minutes.
Reply `/ship confirm` within that window to request the merge.
Confirmation is single use, even if the request fails.
Phantom checks the PR again and refuses changed or blocked releases.
If the window expires, send `/ship` again to start over.
Merging the release PR triggers release-please release tagging.
The desktop self-update picks up the release on its next check.

<!-- page: fleet-health -->
Source: https://verse.ashlr.ai/docs/fleet-health.md

```sh
ashlr fleet doctor
```

Start here. Doctor checks whether each worker engine is installed, signed in
and ready. Then use the matching read-only check below to investigate a problem.
For agents, run `ashlr fleet doctor --json`; every example below also uses `--json`.
`phm` is an alias for `ashlr`.

# Fleet health

Read results in plain words:

- **ok**: the available evidence looks healthy.
- **warn**: something needs attention, or evidence is missing, stale or unknown.
  Unknown does not mean healthy.
- **red**: a reported failure or blocked engine needs fixing.

These are reading guidelines, not shared JSON values. Each verb keeps its own
fields and thresholds. Doctor currently returns engine readiness rows (`ready`,
`installed`, `authed`), not an `ok`/`warn`/`red` report. Read the result,
not just the exit code: several report commands exit 0 even with problems.

| Check | Example command | What to read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engines | `ashlr fleet doctor --json` | `ready: true` is ok; unknown authentication is warn; a missing or blocked engine is red. Does not start workers. |
| Fleet overview | `ashlr fleet status --json` | Daemon, queue and engine evidence; inspect missing or degraded sources before trusting totals. |
| Lanes | `ashlr fleet lanes --json` | Lane capacity, queue depth and live jobs; unknown readings need attention. |
| Idle lanes | `ashlr fleet idle-lanes --json` | Ok: a readable report with no listed lanes. Warn: queued work is held. Red: queued work is not held and `running < target`; exits 1. A red lane with no ledger event for at least 30 minutes is marked `stuck` when a usable event exists. Missing lane age is unknown, not proof that a lane is healthy. Missing or invalid evidence exits 2, not ok. |
| API pools | `ashlr fleet api-pools --json` | No color status or health thresholds. Ok: pacing figures and `slot_target` are known. Warn: any figure is unknown (`null`); missing cost or ceiling can leave the target unknown. Red: observations cannot be read; exits 1. Reports open Claude API pools only; a readable empty list is not proof of healthy pools. |
| Host load | `ashlr fleet load --json` | Ok: all measurements are known and there are no warnings. Warn: load exceeds `load_max`, worktrees exceed 40, measurements are unknown or admission warnings exist. Red: load exceeds twice `load_max`, the daemon tick is over 1800 seconds old or admission data is unavailable; exits 1. Red takes priority over warn. |
| Admission | `ashlr fleet admission --json` | Ok: no lane is blocked by the global cap with 5 or more queued. Red: a lane has queued work, is under its target, is not held, and global running is at the cap, with 5 or more queued; exits 1. Missing or invalid evidence exits 2. For other waits, use `ashlr fleet lane-idle`. |
| Lane share | `ashlr fleet lane-share --json` | Ok: each lane prints running of target and queued against the admission cap. Mark `starved`: 10 or more queued and none running. Mark `full`: running equals target. Red: a starved lane while the admission reason starts with `at_cap`; exits 1. Missing or invalid evidence exits 2. |
| Leader | `ashlr fleet leader-health --json` | Failures in a row, hours since success, last bet and cause. Unknown means no evidence; exits 1 at two consecutive failures. |
| Queue and supervisors | `ashlr fleet heartbeat --json` | `stale: false` is fresh. Older than 30 minutes, missing or unreadable is stale; exits 1 if any source is stale. |
| Default branches | `ashlr fleet main-health --json` | Repo `state`, failing check and fix jobs. Red means failing checks; also inspect `stale`, `source` and `guardianOff`. Add `--strict` for exit 1 on red, stale or unavailable evidence. |
| Guardian freshness | `ashlr fleet health-age --json` | `fresh` means at most 30 minutes old. Stale, missing or invalid evidence exits 1. |
| Sign-in holds | `ashlr fleet login-health --json` | Expired-login holds and whether a later nonempty finish was observed. Top-level `status: ok` means the ledger was read, not that all logins work. |
| Stuck PRs | `ashlr fleet stuck-prs --json` | Lists PRs still recorded open after 60 minutes. An empty list with an error is unknown, not healthy. |
| PR hygiene | `ashlr fleet pr-hygiene --json` | Triage audit of open PRs: `close-candidate` (superseded), `refix` (conflicting) and `review` (stale or file-overlapping) lanes. `reads.open: 'failed'` (exit 1) means the backlog could not be read — unknown, not clean. |
| Wasted runs | `ashlr fleet waste --json` | Last six hours of skips, empty finishes, pool errors and runs without a PR. Counts overlap; unavailable totals stay unknown. |
| Old worktrees | `ashlr fleet worktree-stale --json` | Lists cleanup candidates, oldest first. This example only lists; do not add `--apply` for a health check. |
| Brain activity | `ashlr fleet brains --json` | Last recorded action; stale after 90 minutes, missing log is unknown. |
| Disk | `ashlr fleet disk --json` | Free-space trend and largest runs folders; unknown readings are not zero. |
| Memory | `ashlr fleet memory --json` | Recorded free memory, swap and memory guard state; check the sample age. |
| Judge | `ashlr fleet judge-health --json` | Recorded calibration, verdict distribution and warnings. Leave out `--degradation` to avoid running new judge evaluations. |
| Evidence source | `ashlr fleet evidence doctor decisions --json` | Source state and reason; healthy, cold-start and recovered retry exit 0. Other states exit 1; cold-start still means little evidence. |

Follow the reason in the affected result, fix that problem, then rerun that check.
Idle-lane ages come from pooled, dated events in `~/.ashlr-runs/queue/jobs.jsonl`.
If the ledger is missing, unreadable, oversized or has no usable pooled event,
age fields are omitted. A lane without a matching event has null age and is not
marked stuck; this does not establish that it is healthy.
These commands inspect health; they do not authorize dispatch, cleanup or merge.
See [all fleet verbs](FLEET-VERBS.md) for other fleet tools.
