# Unified cross-vendor agent network

Research date: 2026-11-04. Status: proposed contracts, docs only. No adapter is
commissioned by this document. No credential resolution, outbound send, paid
service, TCC change, or deployment was performed.

## Decision and evidence boundary

Use the Phantom durable agent bus as the native source of work and receipts.
Use an internal shared Slack channel as the human-visible coordination surface,
with Socket Mode ingress. Add Telegram long polling, Gmail drafts, and a strictly
Mac-local iMessage adapter behind the same policy boundary. A2A provides optional
peer interoperability; MCP exposes bounded tools and resources. Neither protocol
provides a universal, trusted identity directory or permission to act.

The requested first step, reading every matching handoff file, is blocked:
listing `/Users/masonwyatt/.ashlr-runs/handoff/inbox` returned `Operation not
permitted`. An initial Python existence probe produced no files; that is not
evidence of an empty inbox. No handoff contents were read, copied, or inferred.
In particular, Ashlr.'s design has not been reviewed. Reconciliation below is
provisional against the queue requirements and repository evidence, not a claim
of agreement with the unseen design. Before implementation, list the inbox,
read all files whose filename or title mentions network, bus, Slack, iMessage,
or adapter, and replace this limitation with a file-by-file decision record.
Do not bypass host permissions to obtain it.

| Comparison available now | Agree | Difference and reason | Merged recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Queue's shared Slack plus four adapters | One shared coordination surface and native Phantom bus | A shared Slack channel must be internal, not Slack Connect; an external audience violates default deny | Internal private channel, explicit team identity allowlist |
| Queue's A2A/MCP identity and message layer | Both are useful interoperability standards | Neither authenticates a vendor persona merely from its name | Local verified principal registry, protocol bindings at the edge |
| Existing agent-to-agent design | Bilateral consent, disabled default, local iMessage, draft approval | Team sends requested by the queue are broader than the current own-handle exception | Preserve stricter draft approval until a reviewed policy explicitly reconciles it |
| Existing bus v2 | Reuse participants, body kinds, work feed and claim rules | Contract presence does not mean resource-claim runtime exists | Implement missing coordination storage separately before channel execution |
| Ashlr. handoff | Unknown | Access denied; no defensible comparison possible | Reconcile before treating recommendation as final |

Checkout evidence: HEAD `e9e50be39`; local `origin/master` was `2c718fdd6`.
No fetch, checkout reset, or merge was performed. This report is not represented
as rebased onto current remote master. PR #3431's requested A2A shape is assessed
from the checked-in schema and guide, not from an independently retrieved PR.

## Existing components to extend

- [Native bus](../AGENT-BUS.md): six-field `BusEnvelope`, authenticated cursor
  reads at `/api/verse/agent-bus`, mutation-gated POST, bounded retention of
  1024 messages and 1 MiB. Same id and different bytes is a conflict, not an edit.
- [A2A consent configuration](../AGENT-TO-AGENT.md) and
  [`a2a-schema.ts`](../../src/core/agents/a2a-schema.ts): `enabled` defaults false;
  each counterpart requires `localOptIn: true`, `remoteOptInEvidence`, channel
  and scope. Current channels are email, Slack and iMessage; Telegram is absent.
  Nonblank evidence is shape validation, not proof of consent.
- [`bus-v2-schema.ts`](../../src/core/agents/bus-v2-schema.ts): participants and
  provider enum, seven body kinds, resource overlap rules, maximum one-hour
  leases and work feed shape. These are pure schemas, not runtime wiring.
- [`bus-work-claims.ts`](../../src/core/fleet/bus-work-claims.ts): local
  message-receipt claims keyed by id, cursor and receivedAt, lock-protected
  mutations, random token checks, expiry and terminal completion. This does not
  fence a remote provider or provide distributed consensus.
- [Existing provider adapters](../../src/core/fleet/bus-adapters/README.md):
  reuse Codex's host ports and Devin/Grok file adapters. Provider adapters run
  agents; channel adapters carry messages. Do not conflate these two boundaries.
- [`channel-bus-publish.ts`](../../src/core/fleet/channel-bus-publish.ts): existing
  Mason interjection projection has stable ids and best-effort append. Do not
  invent a second interjection format or treat best effort as durable delivery.
- Desktop Durable bus and the retired console
  [`FleetBusMapPane.tsx` prototype](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/blob/e4a9e781440cc3006de8efe3be2ee94fbb412361/src/web-ui/routes/verse/fleet-bus-map/FleetBusMapPane.tsx)
  illustrate projections of existing receipts. Real iMessage must never enter
  a cloud-readable bus projection, including bodies, handles or attachments.

No runtime CLI/API surface is added here. Future surfaces require JSON output,
a plain-English section in `docs/AGENT-NETWORK.md`, a copy-paste example, and
entries in `docs/llms.txt` and `AGENTS.md`. Existing safe contract inspection:

```sh
npm run dev -- agents bus contract --json
```

## A2A and MCP mapping

Pin the [A2A 1.0 specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/v1.0.0/specification/)
for the initial interoperability target and negotiate supported versions rather
than following a floating latest schema. Agent Cards advertise skills, endpoints
and security requirements; messages, tasks and artifacts carry peer interaction.
An advertised card is not proof of team membership. Authenticate its endpoint,
bind its key to a locally enrolled principal, and constrain discovery URLs to
trusted destinations to prevent SSRF. No public listener is required for our
outbound client; push notifications remain disabled.

| A2A concept | Phantom mapping | Required constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent Card | Participant capabilities plus verified local endpoint binding | Card text cannot enroll itself or expand scope |
| Message id | Namespaced native envelope id | Persist wire mapping; retries keep identical bytes |
| Context id | Topic registry, Slack thread binding | Not an authorization boundary |
| Task id | `work.post.jobId`, subsequent `work.status` | Map lifecycle explicitly; do not pretend enum values match |
| Artifact | Local bounded reference or approved sanitized output | No automatic remote URL fetching or attachment transfer |
| Security requirements | Trusted launcher identity and request-time broker | Consent references are additional checks, not credentials |

Map submitted/working/input-required/completed/failed/canceled semantics to a
reviewed Phantom transition table. Preserve original state and task id in the
edge journal; input-required becomes blocked with a reason, cancellation requires
an explicit supported action. Streaming reconnect does not imply task restart.
Keep the six bus envelope fields unchanged. Use a separately versioned signed
network object inside opaque v1 `body` initially, projecting valid v2 bodies only
after verification. The strict v2 union rejects invented `kind` values.

Proposed state projection, with the original A2A state retained locally:

| A2A TaskState suffix | Phantom work status | Local detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SUBMITTED | queued | Task accepted, execution not confirmed |
| WORKING | running | Remote task active |
| INPUT_REQUIRED | blocked | Needs scoped input, not permission to send |
| AUTH_REQUIRED | blocked | Request-time broker/consent check; never relay credentials in chat |
| COMPLETED | done | Remote result recorded, channel delivery tracked separately |
| FAILED | failed | Sanitized failure code |
| REJECTED | failed | Preserve rejection as terminal reason |
| CANCELED | terminated | Confirmed remote cancellation |
| UNSPECIFIED | blocked | Unknown state, reconcile before new execution |

[MCP authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization)
is transport-scoped. HTTP clients use resource-bound authorization; stdio has a
separate local trust model. Expose tools for read, draft and policy inspection
separately from send. Phantom's stricter secret custody overrides examples that
use ambient credentials: only `phm_` references in persistent configuration;
resolve through `phantom exec` or the broker at request time. Do not pass provider
tokens between MCP and A2A audiences. MCP tool access cannot mint a team identity,
a work lease or send approval. Do not claim Codex, Claude, Devin, Grok Bot or
Cursor natively implement A2A without a tested provider-specific binding.

## Slack

Choose [Socket Mode](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/events-api/using-socket-mode/):
an outbound WebSocket receives Events API payloads without a public inbound URL.
HTTP Events API delivery instead needs a reachable request URL and verification
of Slack's signed HTTP request. Socket Mode still needs Web API calls for replies.
Persist each event before acknowledging its envelope; acknowledgments and
reconnections do not confer execution authority. Use one active ingress owner,
expect reconnects and duplicate delivery, and do not equate a socket with an agent.

Start mention-only in one private, internal channel where the bot is invited:

| Credential | Minimum scope for proposed baseline | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App-level reference | `connections:write` | Open Socket Mode connection |
| Bot reference | `app_mentions:read` | Receive explicitly addressed messages |
| Bot reference | `chat:write` | Team reply path, absent from read-only deployment if unnecessary |
| Bot reference | `groups:read` | Inspect private channel and paginated membership |
| Bot reference | `users:read` | Resolve member ids and membership attributes |

The [app scope](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/scopes/connections.write/),
[mention event](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/app_mention/),
[conversation inspection](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/conversations.info/)
and [membership method](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/conversations.members/)
define these permissions. Add `channels:read` only for a public-channel pilot;
`groups:history` or `channels:history` only if ordinary messages or recovery
history are required. A mention-only bot does not receive every thread reply.
Avoid DMs initially; they otherwise require their corresponding read/history
permissions and explicit routing. No `users:read.email`, `chat:write.public`,
admin scopes, file upload, channel creation or automatic joins.

Map `(workspaceId, channelId, root thread_ts)` to a stable opaque bus topic id;
store timestamps as strings. Replies use the root `thread_ts` with broadcast
disabled. Human messages become untrusted notes, never executable claims.
A shared bot signs as the bridge and records the verified human actor separately;
it cannot assert that a Slack display name proves a particular agent authored it.

[Slack Connect](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/slack-connect/) joins organizations.
Refuse externally shared, pending-shared and unknown conversations. Before each
send, inspect channel state and enumerate all membership pages. Compare immutable
user ids, workspace and enterprise bindings with the explicit team allowlist;
reject guests, deleted users, unknown bots and members whose membership cannot be
proved. The [user object](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/objects/user-object/)
includes membership attributes; email domains and display names are insufficient.
Invalidate cached evidence on membership/share changes and fail closed on lookup
errors. Even fresh checks have a membership-change race with posting: Slack offers
no atomic check-and-send audience lock. Use a locked-down internal channel and
retain drafts-only if the hard boundary cannot be assured. Confirmation never
overrides the no-outside-send allowlist.

Budget per method and workspace; handle 429 with `Retry-After`, jitter and bounded
queues. Slack's [rate limits](https://docs.slack.dev/apis/web-api/rate-limits/)
include about one message/second/channel and 30,000 event deliveries/hour/workspace.
History and replies have special limits for certain commercially distributed,
non-Marketplace apps, including one request/minute and small pages; internal
customer-built apps differ. Verify installation classification before choosing
recovery cadence. Avoid history polling as the primary ingress and reserve
capacity for recipient checks. Unknown API outcomes enter reconciliation, not
blind resend. [Posting documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.postMessage/)
defines reply routing; a successful post is not an end-to-end agent completion.

## Telegram

Choose outbound long polling over webhook, so no inbound listener is needed.
[Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api) delivery modes are mutually exclusive;
updates are retained at most 24 hours. Persist each update transactionally before
advancing `offset` past its `update_id`; one poller owns a bot. Restrict
`allowed_updates`, use positive long-poll timeouts, track gaps and report downtime
beyond retention as loss requiring operator reconciliation. Preserve ids as decimal
strings at adapter boundaries and handle group migrations explicitly.

Allowlist bot identity, numeric chat id and numeric sender id together. Group
membership alone is not team identity. Treat membership uncertainty as deny,
refuse forwarding as identity evidence, and disable inline/business paths unless
separately reviewed. Keep privacy mode enabled and avoid making the bot an admin.
The [Bots FAQ](https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq) explains that privacy limits group
visibility to addressed interactions, replies and selected events; bots do not
normally see other bots' messages. Telegram is consequently a human interaction
adapter, not a reliable vendor-bot mesh. Bot chats are not a local private data
store. Never bridge iMessage into them. Respect 429 retry instructions; paid
broadcasts are forbidden. Webhook fallback, if ever approved, needs HTTPS and its
secret-token verification plus its own security review.

## iMessage and macOS locality

Propose a Mac-only, read-only reader of `~/Library/Messages/chat.db`, then a
separately reviewed AppleScript sender through Messages. The database is an
unsupported internal interface, not a stable Apple API. Do not write to it,
assume `text` contains every message, or assume schemas and attributed bodies are
stable. Inspect only synthetic databases in automated tests. Use a WAL-aware
read-only connection and short snapshots, never copy just the live database or
mark a changing database immutable. [SQLite WAL documentation](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html)
describes why committed records may live in sidecar files.

[TCC controls](https://support.apple.com/en-ca/guide/security/secddd1d86a6/web)
protect file access and Automation separately. The actual signed reader/launcher
may need Full Disk Access; controlling Messages requires Automation consent.
Accessibility is not a substitute. Mason handles consent dialogs. No TCC database
edits, permission resets, profiles or bypasses. Verify exact permissions on the
supported macOS version. Apple announced further [Full Disk Access controls](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=p6zjojqw)
in October 2026, so legacy permission assumptions need revalidation.

Apple documents [inspecting an application's scripting dictionary](https://support.apple.com/guide/script-editor/view-an-apps-scripting-dictionary-scpedt1126/mac),
but that page returned 429 during this review. The installed Messages dictionary
and an approved synthetic-account exercise must establish supported send commands;
no runnable send example or successful delivery is asserted here. Construct
AppleScript parameters as data, not interpolated script or shell source. Resolve
an exact allowlisted handle and reject groups with unknown members, ambiguous
contacts, attachment commands and automatic SMS fallback. API return is not a
recipient delivery receipt; ambiguous outcomes require local reconciliation.

Real bodies, handles, contact graphs, attachments, database copies, derived
summaries and embeddings stay on the Mac. Only local oMLX at `127.0.0.1` may
process real content, with no cloud fallback, remote telemetry or shared-bus
projection. The private local journal and local-only drafts are excluded from
cloud agents, sync and CI artifacts. Any health counter exported must be content
free and separately approved; opaque ids can still reveal activity patterns.
Synthetic fixtures must use invented identities and text, never scrubbed real
messages. This research did not open the live database.

## Email

Prefer Gmail API for Gmail accounts: bounded OAuth scopes, provider ids and a
native drafts resource are easier to constrain than a combined mail client.
Use metadata-only access for routing where sufficient, `gmail.readonly` only if
body processing is required. Do not grant modify or full mailbox scope merely
to fetch messages. Poll with cursors initially; avoid a new push infrastructure.
Use history recovery and bounded resync when cursors expire, not guessed delivery.

[Gmail draft creation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/reference/rest/v1/users.drafts/create)
accepts `gmail.compose`, which also permits sending. There is no drafts-only OAuth
boundary here. Put the credential behind a method-allowlisting broker that exposes
only draft create/update/get, rejects `messages.send` and `drafts.send`, and
cannot be bypassed by raw HTTP tools. Local draft files are safer before that
broker exists. Gmail-hosted drafts still disclose contents to Google, so never
use them for real iMessage-derived data.

The [draft guide](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/drafts)
explains stable draft ids and replacement of underlying message ids. Persist draft
id, revision and digest; changes to content or To/Cc/Bcc invalidate approval.
Never treat a draft being absent as proof it was sent. Validate parsed MIME
recipients, aliases, Bcc and reply-all expansion; do not trust From/Reply-To or a
matching domain as team membership. Reject header injection and auto-replies.

IMAP/SMTP is a portability fallback, not the default. IMAP APPEND to Drafts does
not require SMTP sending, but mailbox conventions and UIDVALIDITY handling vary.
Keep SMTP credentials and execution unavailable in drafts-only mode. Gmail's
[IMAP/SMTP OAuth mechanism](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/imap/xoauth2-protocol)
uses the broad `https://mail.google.com/` scope, a disadvantage against API
scoping. RFC Message-ID is useful for correlation, not a provider-enforced
idempotency guarantee. Never send email automatically, even to team, until the
local `comms.toml` has `confirmedByMason=true` and all other approvals pass.
This work must not set that flag. Non-team messages remain local drafts only;
confirmation is necessary but cannot override the team-only hard limit.

## Identity, signatures and bridge loops

Issue a stable organization-owned agent id independent of vendor account or
session, for example synthetic `ashlr:agent:research`. Bind Codex, Claude, Devin,
Grok Bot and Cursor launcher identities to that id through locally enrolled
bindings; each active incarnation has a distinct session id and signing key id.
Two unrelated agents using the same vendor must never share identity. Reuse
v2 `participantId` for stable ids and the existing provider enum for bindings.
Display names, mailbox headers and claimed `from` values are untrusted labels.
Revocation disables bindings, queued sends and key verification as policy dictates.

Sign a domain-separated, versioned object using Ed25519 per
[RFC 8032](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032), canonicalized with
[JCS RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785). Include organization,
message id, origin, actor, intended audience, topic, creation and expiry,
causation, classification and payload digest. Resolve signing keys through the
broker; never store private key material in channel configuration. Pin enrolled
public keys, support rotation/revocation, reject expiry and excessive clock skew,
and store replay keys for at least accepted message lifetime plus skew.
A bridge-attested human message is explicitly different from an agent signature.

Preserve the origin id across channel projections. Each bridge adds a separately
signed hop receipt binding the origin digest, previous receipt digest and
provider event id. Never rewrite the signed origin to append a route. Enforce
bounded hop count, no repeated bridge id, audience checks, echo suppression by
provider message id, and one outbox row per `(originId, destinationBinding)`.
Do not dedupe by text: identical text can represent distinct work. Channel edits
become new revisions with causation links; they cannot silently mutate an already
signed work order. Strip mentions, unfurls and executable markup from projections.

## Claims and delivery guarantees

Exactly-once external delivery cannot be promised across these providers. A
process can crash after a remote send succeeds and before recording its receipt.
Leases prevent concurrent local ownership but do not retract a remote side effect.
Use at-least-once intake with durable dedupe, exactly-once local acceptance within
the retained journal horizon, and explicit unknown outcomes for external sends.

1. Validate provenance, bounds, consent and classification; persist normalized
   source event plus dedupe index before acknowledging or advancing a cursor.
2. Append deterministic envelope bytes to the existing bus. On duplicate, accept;
   on conflicting bytes quarantine. Persist projection status so a crash between
   journal commit and bus append is recoverable. Do not recompute TTL on replay.
3. Acquire the existing message claim for work execution. Resource claims remain
   a separate v2 concern; implement their missing runtime with existing overlap
   rules before claiming distributed exclusion. Claims confer no send authority.
4. Atomically reserve an outbox item under a destination-specific idempotency key.
   A monotonic fencing epoch must be checked by the single sending authority;
   the current random local claim token alone cannot fence a remote call.
5. Recheck audience and approval against exact bytes immediately before sending.
   Record provider receipt and terminal state durably. Complete the work claim
   only after durable result recording; claim completion is not send completion.
6. Retry known pre-send failures and explicit throttles. For timeout after request
   transmission, mark unknown and reconcile using provider ids where possible.
   If no proof exists, require local review rather than automatic resend.

Journal/dedupe retention must exceed replay windows; the bounded native bus alone
cannot provide permanent dedupe. On disk pressure, key-store loss, exhausted caps
or uncertain state, stop intake/sends with an explicit health reason. Multi-Mac
operation needs one fenced leader per channel or a reviewed shared coordinator;
replicating local claim JSON does not make it distributed. The Desktop Durable tab
should show draft/blocked/unknown receipt states without displaying local data.

## Threat model against the four hard limits

All inbound text, attachments, cards and tool results are untrusted data. They
cannot enroll identities, grant consent, change policy, select secrets or trigger
spending. No new paid services or automatic upgrades. Every new diagnostic path
must be covered by `scrub.pl` before activation, with synthetic regression cases.
Prefer allowlisted metadata logging: never log bodies, auth headers, socket URLs,
Telegram token-bearing URLs, MIME, signing material or provider responses raw.

| Channel | Secrets | Money | Outside sends | Mason's data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native bus/A2A/MCP | Forged card/tool requests cannot select arbitrary vault refs; scoped broker, pinned principals | Work/claim is no billing authority; no purchasable tools | Authenticate origin and exact audience; no arbitrary discovery/wake URLs | Bounded payloads, private stores, ACLs; no real iMessage projection |
| Slack | Stolen bot/app refs or diagnostic URLs; request-time resolution, redact transport errors | No admin or paid provisioning capability | Connect/guests/unknown bots, membership races; deny shared channels, paginate checks, keep drafts when uncertain | Limit invited channel, no attachments/unfurls or broad history crawl; Slack receives permitted projected text |
| Telegram | Token appears in endpoint path; redact URL before all logging and retry traces | Paid broadcasts disabled, bounded rate queue | Numeric chat plus actor allowlist, migration review, refuse unknown group audience | Privacy mode, no contact upload, no iMessage; Telegram cloud sees permitted bot messages |
| iMessage | No key/handle leakage via AppleScript errors or subprocess argv | No purchases, no SMS fallback or paid relay | Exact local recipient binding and group audience check; local drafts until approved | Entire data path and inference local; no database export, sync, cloud logs or fixtures |
| Email | OAuth custody only in broker; no broad IMAP access by default | No paid relay or subscription changes | Draft-only broker, all recipient fields checked, header injection denied; confirmation never bypasses allowlist | Minimize mailbox scope; local drafts for sensitive data; no iMessage to Gmail |

Residual risks: compromised enrolled team accounts can inject malicious requests;
recipient membership may change at send time; provider outages exceed retention;
Mac-local privileged processes can access plaintext. Mitigate with least privilege,
read/draft defaults, bounded work admission and explicit uncertain delivery states.
A signature proves possession of an enrolled key, not that an instruction is safe.

## Recommended build order and acceptance gates

No downstream build-line names were supplied, so the stages below define concrete
scope without inventing queue ids. All remain proposed and disabled by default.

1. Reconcile every matching Ashlr. handoff and current origin/master. Record
   conflicts and the selected policy, especially the existing own-handle approval
   rule versus proposed team sends. Do not call reconciliation complete beforehand.
2. Pure contract and synthetic tests: identity bindings, consent evidence,
   signature vectors, classification, recipient allowlist, draft policy,
   canonicalization, origin dedupe and hop rules. Add Telegram to consent schema
   only through a reviewed compatibility change; no silent enum widening.
3. Journal and native bus integration: transactional inbox/outbox, cursors,
   bounded retention, crash recovery and fenced sender ownership. Reuse existing
   HTTP bus, provider ports and Durable tab, then implement missing resource-claim
   runtime separately. Test concurrent claims and stale-owner rejection.
4. Slack receive-only Socket Mode adapter for one internal channel, synthetic
   membership snapshots and local drafts. Test reconnect, duplicates, membership
   pagination, Connect/guest denial, event storage before ack and 429 recovery.
5. Telegram receive-only long polling and local drafts. Test cursor commit crashes,
   duplicate updates, chat migrations, unallowlisted actors and retention gaps.
6. Gmail local draft generation, then broker-isolated Gmail draft methods. Test
   To/Cc/Bcc, MIME injection, revised drafts and rejection of both send methods.
7. Mac-only iMessage reader and local draft builder after Mason grants required
   OS permissions. Test synthetic WAL databases and permission denial, with a
   network tripwire proving real-data routes cannot use cloud ports. Validate
   Messages scripting separately with synthetic accounts; no real-data CI.
8. Credential injection or send-capable implementation belongs in a separate PR
   on `codex-bridge/RQ-AGENTNET-RESEARCH-1-sec`, titled
   `[SECURITY REVIEW] RQ-AGENTNET-RESEARCH-1`, with no auto-merge. Add scrub coverage
   for each log path. Keep `confirmedByMason` unchanged, spending disabled and
   outside identities denied. This report creates neither that PR nor credentials.

Acceptance must include crash-after-send becoming unknown, stale lease failure,
revoked key/consent rejection, forged origin and repeated-hop rejection, a bot echo
loop, capped-store exhaustion and inability to send with missing confirmation.
Use affected-only tests with temporary homes and `--bail 1`; never weaken controls.

## Concrete TypeScript interfaces for implementation

These are proposed documentation contracts, not exported or runnable code.
Import existing types rather than duplicating provider or claim enums. Runtime
validators must reject unknown fields, enforce bounded lengths, verify bindings
and return scrubbed reason codes. `LocalMessageRef` is an opaque Mac-local journal
handle, never a path or permission to retrieve its contents remotely.

```ts
import type { BusBody, Participant } from '../../src/core/agents/bus-v2-schema.js';
import type { BusEnvelope } from '../../src/core/fleet/bus-envelope.js';
import type { BusClaimRequest, BusClaimResult } from '../../src/core/fleet/bus-work-claims.js';

type AgentId = Participant['participantId'];
type Channel = 'native' | 'slack' | 'telegram' | 'imessage' | 'email' | 'a2a';
type SecretRef = `phm_${string}`;
type LocalMessageRef = string & { readonly localOnly: unique symbol };
type Classification = 'team' | 'mac-local';

interface IdentityBinding {
  agentId: AgentId;
  provider: Participant['provider'];
  sessionId: string;
  bindingId: string;
  channel: Channel;
  tenantId: string;
  subjectId: string; // immutable provider id, never a display name
  keyId: string;
  consentEvidenceRef: string;
  allowedScopes: readonly string[];
  revoked: boolean;
}

interface SignedOrigin {
  version: 'agent-network.v1';
  orgId: string;
  id: string;
  actor: { kind: 'agent' | 'bridge-attested-human'; bindingId: string };
  audienceBindingIds: readonly string[];
  topicId: string;
  createdAt: number;
  expiresAt: number;
  causationId?: string;
  classification: Classification;
  payloadDigest: string;
  keyId: string;
  signature: string; // excludes this field from canonical signing input
}

interface HopReceipt {
  bridgeId: string;
  originDigest: string;
  previousReceiptDigest?: string;
  providerEventId: string;
  keyId: string;
  signature: string;
}

type NetworkMessage =
  | { origin: SignedOrigin; hops: readonly HopReceipt[];
      classification: 'team'; body: BusBody }
  | { origin: SignedOrigin; hops: readonly HopReceipt[];
      classification: 'mac-local'; localRef: LocalMessageRef };
// Validate classification equals signed origin.classification.
// mac-local variants are rejected by all cloud/channel serialization ports.

interface InboundEvent {
  channel: Channel;
  bindingId: string;
  eventId: string;
  cursor: string;
  message: NetworkMessage;
}

interface AudienceProof {
  destinationBindingId: string;
  policyRevision: string;
  observedAt: number;
  expiresAt: number;
  teamOnly: true;
  memberIds: readonly string[];
  evidenceDigest: string;
}

type OutboundDecision =
  | { kind: 'deny'; reason: string }
  | { kind: 'draft'; reason: string; localOnly: boolean }
  | { kind: 'send'; audience: AudienceProof; approvalDigest: string };

interface Draft {
  id: string;
  revision: number;
  messageId: string;
  destinationBindingId: string;
  contentAndRecipientsDigest: string;
  localOnly: boolean;
}

type DeliveryResult =
  | { status: 'accepted'; providerMessageId: string }
  | { status: 'retryable'; retryAfterMs: number; definitelyNotSent: true }
  | { status: 'unknown'; reconciliationId: string }
  | { status: 'denied'; reason: string };

interface ChannelAdapter {
  channel: Channel;
  receive(after: string | undefined, signal: AbortSignal): AsyncIterable<InboundEvent>;
  acknowledge(eventId: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<void>;
  inspectAudience(bindingId: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<AudienceProof>;
  draft(message: NetworkMessage, destinationBindingId: string): Promise<Draft>;
}
// Implement this capability only in the separately security-reviewed sender.
interface SendPort {
  send(request: { draftId: string; revision: number; digest: string;
    decision: Extract<OutboundDecision, { kind: 'send' }>;
    idempotencyKey: string; fenceEpoch: number },
    signal: AbortSignal): Promise<DeliveryResult>;
}

interface NetworkJournal {
  // Atomic local accept and cursor checkpoint; conflict on same id/different digest.
  accept(event: InboundEvent): Promise<'accepted' | 'duplicate' | 'conflict'>;
  // Native projection always uses the existing strict six-field envelope.
  project(eventId: string, envelope: BusEnvelope): Promise<void>;
  claim(request: BusClaimRequest): Promise<BusClaimResult>;
  reserve(messageId: string, destinationBindingId: string): Promise<{
    idempotencyKey: string; fenceEpoch: number;
    state: 'reserved' | 'accepted' | 'unknown';
  }>;
  record(idempotencyKey: string, fenceEpoch: number,
    result: DeliveryResult): Promise<void>;
}

interface SecretBroker {
  // No method returns a secret value to adapters or models.
  sign(ref: SecretRef, canonicalBytes: Uint8Array): Promise<string>;
  createEmailDraft(ref: SecretRef, draft: Draft): Promise<{ providerDraftId: string }>;
}
```

Broker draft input in implementation must carry an opaque content handle bound to
the approved digest, resolved inside the broker. It must not fetch arbitrary paths
or URLs. The draft type above represents identity and revision, not complete MIME.
SendPort must revalidate policy, audience freshness, confirmation and exact bytes
inside the fenced sender; possession of a serialized `send` decision is not a
capability. Keep claims, broker references and private local refs out of public
channel projections. These constraints are part of the interface contract.

# RQ-OSS-A2A-ORCH-1 — open-source agent-to-agent communication and orchestration

Research date: 2026-11-06. Job: RQ-OSS-A2A-ORCH-1 (lane: devin, tier: work).
Status: research findings and recommendations only. No code, configuration,
queue, dispatchd, or credential change was made. No model calls, paid
resources, or network mutations were performed. Web research only.

## Scope and method

The slice covers agent-to-agent wire protocols, durable orchestration
runtimes, and subagent pattern libraries that could improve Phantom's fleet:
dispatchd, bus relays, multi-lane work, and director/subagent patterns.
Projects were found by web search (2025–2026 projects, comparison guides,
CNCF/Linux Foundation notes, GitHub topics `multi-agent`,
`agent-orchestration`, `a2a`) and checked against the Phantom needs in the
job spec: durable job handoff, priority, non-live async replies,
auditability, low model cost, and a fleet of one Mac plus hosted Linux box
workers.

Every `license (SPDX)` cell was verified on 2026-11-06 by reading the LICENSE
file on the repository's default branch (`license_url` column). Three rows
surfaced non-obvious licenses this way: **Inngest is SSPL-1.0**, **Restate is
BUSL-1.1**, and **multica is a modified Apache-2.0 with commercial
conditions** — none are OSI open source. AutoGen's root LICENSE is CC-BY-4.0
(docs); code is MIT in `LICENSE-CODE`. Mastra ships `ee/` directories under a
separate license.

## Decision summary

Adopt two things, in sequence. First, align the unimplemented agent-bus v2
contract with the A2A v1.0 object model (Task, Message, Artifact, AgentCard)
and use the Apache-2.0 TypeScript SDK when an external endpoint is wanted —
this buys a neutral, inspected wire shape instead of a Phantom-private one.
Second, run a spike between Hatchet (MIT) and DBOS Transact TS (MIT) as the
durable backend for cross-host job handoff, because the node router's lease
and fencing model is currently confined to one host's state directory while
the fleet already spans the Mac and a hosted Linux box. Everything else is
inspiration for patterns Phantom already half-owns, or a skip.

## Phantom gap analysis

What Phantom already covers well: an implemented bounded append-only bus
with cursor reads, auth-gated mutation, P0–P3 priority and TTL ([AGENT-BUS
v1](../AGENT-BUS.md)); a lease+fencing node router with capability and owner
scoping, local auth and secret names only ([NODE-ROUTER](../NODE-ROUTER.md));
a file-based queue with READY/deps and operator claims
([QUEUE](../QUEUE.md)); dispatchd's lane targets, tick budgets and route
hysteresis; swarm planner/runner phased fan-out; and a locked-down remote
gateway for off-Mac read/steer.

Where OSS is ahead, concretely:

1. **Cross-host durability.** The node router's lease/fencing state lives in
   a single-host directory (`~/.ashlr/nodes`); the hosted box is reached over
   SSH remote dispatch ([NODES](../NODES.md)). A Postgres-backed durable
   queue (Hatchet or DBOS) gives the box the same one-claim-per-job
   guarantees the Mac enjoys locally, with lease expiry and redelivery
   replacing manual reap passes. This is the largest real gap.
2. **Bus v2 is contract-only.** The claim table and work feed are "not yet
   implemented" per the docs' own ownership table. A2A's Task state machine
   is a proven superset of `work.post`/`work.status`; adopting its shape now
   (before the runtime lands) avoids inventing and later un-inventing a
   private protocol, and `a2a-inspector` gives free conformance checking.
3. **Interop boundary.** Today every provider needs a bespoke adapter
   (`src/core/fleet/bus-adapters/{codex,devin,grok}.ts`). An A2A JSON-RPC
   edge would let external agents — including non-TS providers — speak one
   neutral protocol, replacing per-provider file adapters at the boundary.
   Phantom's own `a2a-schema.ts` name also now collides with the industry
   term; worth noting in docs.
4. **Push/wake.** The bus is poll-only and the webhook relay is explicitly
   "not built". A2A push notifications, Hatchet event triggers and NATS
   deliver-now consumers are three proven patterns for waking a
   `wake.kind=webhook` participant without polling latency.
5. **Identity.** `from`/`to` are routing labels, explicitly "not identities".
   Inside one owner+LAN trust domain that is fine; ANP (DID+HTTP signatures)
   and Dapr's crypto agent identity are the references if counterparts ever
   go cross-org — inspire-only until then.
6. **Retry/dead-letter.** The queue has "no automatic reclaim, retry,
   promotion". aden-hive's tracker+DLQ and Hatchet retries are the two
   patterns worth porting for failure recovery.
7. **Auditability.** The append-only bus is a good base. Temporal/Restate
   journals show the bar: replayable per-job history. A durable backend
   (Hatchet/DBOS) buys most of that incidentally.
8. **Model cost.** All recommended adoptions are infrastructure and schema
   alignment — zero inference spend, consistent with the low-Grok-cost
   constraint.

Not recommended anywhere: heavyweight control planes (Temporal server, Dapr
sidecars, k8s runtimes), non-OSI runtimes as dependencies (Restate BUSL-1.1,
Inngest SSPL-1.0, multica conditions), and roleplay frameworks (MetaGPT,
ChatDev) which solve coordination, not dispatch.

## Proposed READY implementation one-liners

For the adopt items only, in dependency order:

1. `RQ-A2A-SCHEMA-MAP-1 (P2, pool=codex-cmp, tier=work, repo=phantom): Map agent-bus v2 bodies (work.post, work.status, work.claim, participant) onto the A2A v1.0 Task/Message/Artifact/AgentCard object model; ship zod validators + round-trip tests + a docs diff of incompatibilities. Acceptance: pure-schema change, no endpoint, no dep.`
2. `RQ-DURABLE-HANDOFF-SPIKE-1 (P1, pool=codex-cmp, tier=work, repo=phantom): Spike Hatchet Lite vs DBOS Transact TS as the durable store for node-router job handoff between Mac and the hosted box — fence a claim across two hosts, prove lease expiry redelivery, compare ops weight. Acceptance: hermetic dockerized PoC + decision doc; no dispatchd or live queue cutover.`
3. `RQ-BUS-V2-CLAIMS-IMPL-1 (P2, pool=codex-cmp, tier=work, repo=phantom, deps=RQ-DURABLE-HANDOFF-SPIKE-1): Implement the bus v2 claim table and work-feed endpoints from docs/AGENT-BUS.md on the backend chosen by the spike. Acceptance: acquire/renew/release/complete + feed per the contract's overlap rules, token-bound mutation, existing caps kept.`
4. `RQ-A2A-EDGE-ENDPOINT-1 (P2, pool=codex-cmp, tier=work, repo=phantom, deps=RQ-A2A-SCHEMA-MAP-1): Expose the durable bus as a loopback A2A JSON-RPC endpoint via @a2a-js/sdk with an AgentCard per bus participant. Acceptance: a2a-inspector validates the card; mutation gate and draft-approve boundaries preserved; loopback only.`

## Limitations

- Licenses verified 2026-11-06 against each default branch; projects can
  relicense (this survey already caught SSPL-1.0, BUSL-1.1 and a custom
  source-available license hiding behind "open source" marketing).
- The GitHub API was rate-limited from this host; repo metadata (stars,
  activity, maintenance status) comes from search-result snapshots dated
  ~2026-11-04 and repo pages, not a fresh API pull.
- aden-hive/hive is months old and was rewritten ground-up at v0.10; its
  patterns are recommended as design references, not as a dependency.
- No benchmark of Hatchet/DBOS on Phantom's real workload exists; the
  adoption call is deliberately a spike, not a cutover.
- MCP is intentionally out of scope per the job spec (sibling job
  RQ-OSS-MCP-SKILLS-1); nothing here depends on MCP internals.

# RQ-OSS-AGGREGATE-1 — ranked OSS adoption and build handoff

Checked 2026-11-06. **Dot/Core: please relay the executive summary below to Mason.** This file is the handoff; no message was sent and no queue was edited.

## A. Executive summary

There are open-source desktop agent examples: [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) is a coding-agent desktop, [Hope Agent](https://github.com/shiwenwen/hope-agent) presents persistent agent workflows, and [Jan](https://github.com/janhq/jan) is a local-model desktop. They demonstrate pieces of a Grok-Bot-like experience, not verified feature or security equivalence. Phantom already has a Tauri shell, MCP gateway, local inference integration, and multi-node lease/fencing. Extend these rather than replace the product.

Top five bets: (1) MCP gateway lifecycle and conformance; (2) local inference measurement against existing llama-server and oMLX; (3) safe Agent Skills compatibility; (4) desktop streaming and tool-state clarity; (5) restart-safe fleet handoff and status. They are proposed product outcomes, not claims of installed or production acceptance.

License bottom line: bounded adoption of the five explicitly marked candidates below has a re-opened upstream LICENSE; MCP's current root license is a MIT-to-Apache transition, not simply Apache. Licenses of pinned versions, packages, assets, dependencies, model weights, datasets and converted artifacts require separate checks. Preserve applicable notices. Proprietary products are inspiration only. No fork is recommended here.

**Coverage:** Only the local-speed worker report was available on the required recheck, as an uncommitted sibling-worktree file. Desktop, A2A, MCP and multinode reports were not accessible; the queue parent returned EPERM, exact-ID GitHub searches found no PRs, issues or branches, and unrelated PR comments were not exhaustively searchable. The ranking below combines that one table with independent primary-source research, **not a completed five-worker synthesis**. Reconcile the four missing reports before treating the ranking as final. Candidate READY build rows are bounded, independently actionable proposals, not evidence that all research dependencies finished. Check Core's queue for duplicates under lock before appending.

Scoring: impact and strategic fit each 1–5, composite = 0.6 × impact + 0.4 × fit; estimated effort S/M/L and license clarity break ties. Scores are judgments, not measurements. `adopt` means scoped use of a specific candidate, not deployment; `inspire` means independent implementation with no code copied; `evaluate` is deferred.

## D. Explicit skips

- Grok Bot, Cursor and other proprietary products: behavior inspiration only; no code reuse.
- Open WebUI: current license has branding conditions and historical distinctions; do not fork or adopt without reviewing the exact version and conditions ([LICENSE](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/blob/main/LICENSE)).
- Gemma and Llama-derived weights: custom terms, not blanket Apache or MIT; defer until exact terms and intended use are cleared. Avoid assuming rights from a runtime or distillation repository.
- AGPL, SSPL, BUSL and other source-available components: no adopt/fork absent specific prior clearance. Avoid selecting an abandoned project solely to fill a ranking; activity and maintenance are not assessed here.
- TensorRT-LLM: NVIDIA-specific stack is a poor fit for the Mac-first local slice and carries separate dependency terms.

# RQ-OSS-DESKTOP-UX-1 — Desktop app UX + OSS “Grok Bot–like” local agent hunt

- **Date:** 2026-11-06 · **Lane:** devin (non-Grok) · **Tier:** frontier · **Status:** complete
- **Mission:** survey OSS desktop agent UIs for Phantom's workbench; answer whether an
  open-source local re-implementation of the Grok Bot app (or close cousins) exists and what
  its license allows. Proprietary products (Grok Bot, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf,
  Conductor, Codex app, LM Studio, Devin UI) are **design inspiration only** — no code,
  assets, or reconstructed source is reused.
- **Method:** web search (GitHub, HN, r/LocalLLaMA, Product Hunt, reviews) followed by
  direct LICENSE-file verification on each repo's default branch. Licenses were read from
  the checked-in `LICENSE` / `LICENSE.md` / `LICENSE.txt` / `LICENSE-*` files (raw text),
  not from README claims. ~50 candidates reviewed; every `adopt`/`fork` below is a
  permissive OSI license.

## 2. Grok-Bot-like subsection

**Does a credible OSS local desktop agent app exist that is a reimplementation or close
functional peer of Grok Bot / the Cursor Chat shell?**

- **A literal reimplementation: no.** The one attempt found,
  `b-nnett/grok-bot-0.18-reconstructed` (3.6k★, archived 2026-08-28), is a source-oriented
  reconstruction of a shipped proprietary binary. It carries **no LICENSE at all** (default
  copyright = all rights reserved), its bootstrap downloads and extracts the proprietary
  app, and its provenance makes any copy legally unsafe. Recommendation: **do not clone,
  do not read its "source", do not reuse manifests or UI text.** Treat it as radioactive
  and as proof that "OSS Grok Bot" is marketing bait, not a real thing.
- **Close functional peers: yes, and they are legitimately open source.** The honest OSS
  answer to "Grok Bot at home" is the *parallel coding-agent desktop* genre that matured in
  2025–2026 — Electron/Tauri shells that orchestrate local CLI agents on git worktrees —
  plus the chat shells. Best candidates for Phantom:
  1. **Emdash (Apache-2.0)** — orchestrates multiple coding agents in parallel across
     worktrees; the closest structural peer to Phantom's own dispatchd + queue model.
  2. **Paradev / ex-Superset (MIT)** — Conductor/Codex-app alternative; agent grid +
     embedded terminal + worktrees.
  3. **Goose desktop (Apache-2.0)** — the most mature *single-agent* local desktop shell:
     MCP-native, sessions/recipes, permission prompts, provider-agnostic.
     Honorable mentions: Vibe Kanban (Apache-2.0, kanban of agent runs), Crystal (MIT,
     small Electron session multiplexer), liaan/grok-desktop (MIT, thin GUI over the Grok
     Build CLI via ACP — pattern reference only).
- **What Phantom may legally reuse:** MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-3 code may be copied, modified and
  vendored with license notices preserved (Apache-2.0 additionally requires retaining
  NOTICE and marking modifications; it carries a patent grant). **AGPL/GPL/LGPL projects
  (Cherry Studio, Witsy, claudia, opcode, Chatbox, Zed editor, PI-Desktop) and
  source-available projects (Open WebUI, LobeChat, Crush, GPT Pilot, 5ire, screenpipe) yield
  ideas and UX flows only — no code.** For FSL-1.1 code (Crush, GPT Pilot), each release
  converts to MIT two years after publication; older releases are technically re-usable but
  cold.
- **Clear statement:** Grok Bot, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Conductor, the Codex
  app, LM Studio and similar proprietary products are **inspiration only**. Phantom must
  not copy, reimplement from leaked/reconstructed source, or paste proprietary code or
  assets. When in doubt about a repo (no LICENSE, custom license, reconstructed source):
  `license=UNVERIFIED` ⇒ **skip**.

## 3. Desktop UX patterns worth stealing (ideas only)

Mapped to Phantom's workbench (`phm serve` console, Fleet/Home surfaces, Verse, COS API,
dispatchd, lanes, router-queue, worktrees). No code copied.

- **Global ask bar → queued job.** One pinned natural-language box everywhere (header /
  tray / hotkey) that turns text into a structured job card (title, lane, tier guess) and
  returns an ack chip linking to the run. Phantom already has the seam:
  `POST /api/verse/fleet/cos/ask` + `phm queue`. (Seen in: Conductor, Devin UI, agent-ui.)
- **Multi-agent sidebar with live status.** Left rail listing each running agent: status
  dot, lane/branch/worktree badge, model, burn/quota meter, "needs you" flag. One click =
  jump to that run's timeline. (emdash, Paradev, Crystal.)
- **Unified run timeline.** A single collapsible event stream per job — prompt, plan,
  tool calls, terminal runs, file diffs, test output, retries, permission prompts,
  checkpoints — with timestamps and deep-linkable entries. Phantom's job-latency
  boundaries (queued → launch → checkout_complete → finish → ci_start → ci_complete →
  merged) are a ready-made spine. (OpenHands, Emdash, Modus.)
- **Plan-mode card with a Build button.** Read-only exploration phase writes a reviewable
  `plan.md` rendered as a card; approving it starts execution. Fits Phantom's RQ/plan →
  READY line hand-off. (OpenHands, agent-ui, Origin, Dyad.)
- **Diff-first review surface.** Per-file diff tabs, inline stage/commit/push, branch +
  upstream status, "what changed since you looked" — the review step is a first-class
  panel, not a git command. (Vibe Kanban, Emdash, Dyad.)
- **Permission-prompt rail, not modal spam.** Approvals as queued first-class objects with
  risk tiers (read vs. write vs. network vs. spend), remember-this-rule, and a visible
  audit trail — aligned with Phantom's Security GATES rather than raw shell asks.
  (Cline/Roo, Origin, Goose.)
- **Checkpoints and one-click rollback.** Pre-run snapshot + undo button so an agent run
  is never a commitment. (Dyad, claudia, bolt.diy.) Pairs naturally with Phantom's
  worktree-per-job model.
- **Needs-you inbox + digest notifications.** Completions and blocks surface as a small
  inbox/tray badge with a digest, mirroring Phantom's needs-you/drafts concepts — approval
  required before any outbound send. (Vibe Kanban, OpenHands, Phantom drafts.)
- **Session resume + CLI-history import.** Import prior agent sessions, resume mid-thread,
  compact-context affordance when history gets long. (agent-ui, Crystal, OpenHands.)
- **BYOK/provider catalog with keychain storage.** Model/provider picker that reflects
  exactly what the underlying agent reports — never a silent fallback; keys in the OS
  keychain, usage totals per provider. (Jan, Origin, Dyad, grok-build-desktop's honest
  model selector.)
- **In-app update/feed rail.** Release notes + update status as a quiet rail, not a
  startup modal; plus a fleet feed ("what shipped in the last 24h") matching Phantom's
  recorded-merges Home view. (Zed, Cherry Studio.)

   obligations listed; no production changes.
2. **RQ-JOB-TIMELINE-1** — Unified job-run timeline component in `src/web-ui` rendering
   the queued→launch→checkout→finish→ci→merged event spine per job, with collapsible
   tool/terminal/diff entries. *Acceptance:* component + unit test against fixture
   `jobs.jsonl`; real runs render end-to-end.
3. **RQ-ASK-BAR-1** — Global ask bar in the console (and tray entry) posting to
   `POST /api/verse/fleet/cos/ask`, rendering the ack/status chip and needs-you state.
   *Acceptance:* happy path + `VERSE_INVALID`/`COS_REFUSED` handling; mutation-gate
   respected; tests added.
4. **RQ-PERMISSION-UX-1** — Permission-prompt model spec for agent actions (risk tiers,
   remember-rule, audit trail) mapped onto Security GATES v3. *Acceptance:* proposal doc
   + JSON schema; Security review requested; no implementation yet.
5. **RQ-OSS-LICENSE-POLICY-1** — Vendor/derivative policy page capturing this report's
   adopt/fork/inspire-only/skip lists and NOTICE obligations for Apache-2.0 imports.
   *Acceptance:* `docs/` page + checklist wired into PR template.

# RQ-OSS-SPEED-LOCAL-1: local inference speed and efficiency

No weights are committed, caches deleted, or models downloaded by this study.

## Evidence and caveats

- The 2026 [vllm-mlx paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19139) reports 21–87% higher text throughput than llama.cpp and up to 4.3× aggregate throughput at 16 concurrent requests on its tested configurations. These are author measurements, not 8/16 GB Phantom measurements; compare versions, chips, context, quantization and concurrency.
- A 2026 [Apple Silicon optimization study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31479) reports that all tested speculative decoding methods reduced throughput on its Apple workloads. llama.cpp [supports several methods](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/speculative.md); test draft acceptance, latency and total memory against no speculation. Do not assume GPU-server gains transfer.
- [AWQ](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/llm-awq/blob/main/LICENSE) (MIT) reports [6.39 vs 17.07 ms/token](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/llm-awq/blob/main/tinychat/README.md) for W4 vs FP16 Llama-3-8B on RTX 4090 with four context tokens. This is CUDA evidence, not a Mac prediction. [GPTQ](https://github.com/IST-DASLab/gptq/blob/main/LICENSE) is Apache-2.0; compare MLX-native quantization and llama.cpp GGUF quantization before adding a conversion pipeline. Each converted artifact inherits or adds its own weight terms.
- Small MoE active parameter counts do not establish resident-memory fit: total weights, KV, runtime, OS and concurrent work matter. 4-bit file sizes are lower bounds, not allocations. [Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B) has Apache-2.0 weights per its model card; use only with a supported embedding endpoint, and evaluate retrieval recall.
- For quality, use a pinned, isolated subset of [SWE-bench](https://github.com/SWE-bench/SWE-bench) plus representative Phantom tasks: patch applies, tests pass, regressions, escalation rate and human-reviewed merge readiness. Passing tests are a proxy, not proof of merge quality. [HELM](https://github.com/stanford-crfm/helm) and lm-eval subsets can supplement, with dataset licenses and resource limits checked per task. Avoid executing generated code outside an appropriate sandbox.

## Mac / oMLX practical shortlist

These are alternatives, not simultaneous resident models. Fit is unverified; start with one request, short context and the existing memory guard, then measure real peak memory, swap and thermal behavior. Use exact checkpoint revision, hash, quantization, license and runtime version in a local pin; never check weights into Git.

| memory | stack | role and license |
|---|---|---|
| 8 GB | oMLX + Qwen3-0.6B 4-bit | draft/router experiment; Apache-2.0 code and weights |
| 8 GB | mlx-lm + Qwen3-4B MLX 4-bit | bounded worker candidate; MIT code, Apache-2.0 weights; admission may refuse |
| 8 GB | llama.cpp + Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B GGUF | embedding candidate; MIT code, Apache-2.0 weights; verify exact converted artifact license |
| 16 GB | oMLX + Qwen3-4B MLX 4-bit | worker candidate; Apache-2.0 code and weights |
| 16 GB | llama.cpp + DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B GGUF | reasoning/router comparison; MIT code and model weights; verify conversion provenance |
| 16 GB | oMLX + Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | embedding candidate; Apache-2.0 code and weights; verify endpoint and artifact compatibility |

An 8B model or MoE is deliberately not promised to fit at useful context. Model cards are upstream starting points, not guarantees that a particular community quantization is licensed or supported.

## READY jobs

- READY RQ-LOCAL-CODING-BENCH-1: extend the existing inventory with sandboxed, pinned coding tasks and record patch/test success, escalation and latency alongside three cold samples; compare 8/16 GB hosts without evicting caches.
- READY RQ-LOCAL-CACHE-AB-1: compare bounded cold/warm prefix reuse and speculation on/off across pinned oMLX, mlx-lm and llama.cpp, recording TTFT, decode tok/s, peak memory, swap and draft acceptance.
- READY RQ-LOCAL-LANE-CAPS-1: enforce measured per-host context, concurrency and memory admission caps with fail-closed loopback routing and regression tests; do not alter live queue configuration.
- READY RQ-LOCAL-MODEL-PINS-1: define local-only model manifests with source revision, hash, quantization, code/weight license and provenance; keep weights outside Git and reject unverified conversions.

# Research topics

The offline restock source reads bullets in the form `- STABLE-ID | question`.
Keep IDs stable: they become part of daily queue IDs. Other Markdown is ignored.
Use one question per line. Hold-list entries are case-insensitive literal phrases
or IDs; matching candidates are excluded. Unsafe topics are ignored.

- SOURCE-FRESHNESS | How should an engineering agent measure source freshness and preserve provenance?
- RETRIEVAL-QUALITY | Which reproducible evaluations best measure retrieval quality for repository research?
- LOCAL-RESEARCH | Which local retrieval approaches support useful offline engineering research?
- RESEARCH-HANDOFF | How can research findings become small testable engineering proposals?
- EVIDENCE-CONFLICTS | How should an agent report conflicting primary evidence and uncertainty?
- RESEARCH-COST | Which measurements reveal research usefulness per unit of compute?
- PROVIDER-USAGE-PROBES | Which provider usage-percent and reset-time signals can the fleet read itself?

## Restock contract

`src/core/driver/restock.ts` is the DRIVER-3 integration seam. Pass the topic
file contents, full queue contents, explicit hold list and current time to
`restockQueue` under the queue writer's existing lock, then persist its returned
queue. DRIVER-3 is absent in this checkout; this module does not install a timer
or dispatch jobs. The driver should invoke it on each restock tick.

The default target is three lines per UTC day, configurable to two through four.
IDs have the form `RQ-RESEARCH-YYYYMMDD-TOPIC-ID`. Existing daily IDs count toward
the quota, including completed jobs. Retain IDs in the input queue or its history
when pruning completed work. Repeated ticks fill only the remaining quota.
Topics rotate daily; later days may revisit a question with fresh evidence.
If holds or invalid topics leave too few candidates, return fewer lines instead
of bypassing exclusions. Hold input is required; pass an empty list explicitly
when no items are held. Callers must not persist a stale snapshot concurrently.

Each line uses `ID (P2, pool=codex-personal, tier=work, repo=phantom): Research
question. Acceptance: ...` and includes the exported research acceptance tail.
The tail requires dated primary sources, alternatives, recommendations and
limitations, with findings confined to this directory and no code changes.
No provider, token, network access or Grok Bot is needed to generate lines.

# Agent swarms and recursive self-improvement

Research date: 2026-10-26. Job: RQ-RESEARCH-SWARMS. Status: research and
experiment specifications, not measured Phantom performance or launch approval.

## Decision

Prioritize a budget-matched topology benchmark, then trace-driven lesson trials.
Keep one writer per task worktree and independent verification. Archive-based
search is promising after those measurements exist. Editable improvement
strategies belong in an offline experiment, outside the promotion mechanism.

A swarm distributes work across agents. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) changes
the mechanism that produces future improvements. Adding workers, retrying a
failed task, and accumulating lessons do not by themselves demonstrate RSI.
None of the evidence below establishes unbounded improvement, production
reliability, or a reason to relax Phantom's authority boundaries.

## Dated primary evidence

Versions are pinned so later revisions cannot silently change these claims.
Numbers describe the authors' experiments, not forecasts for Phantom.

| Source | Dates and version | Finding and limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.08296v3) | Submitted 2025-12-09; v3 2026-04-08 | Across 260 configurations and six benchmarks, relative changes span +80.8% on decomposable financial reasoning to -70.0% on sequential planning. Task structure and coordination matter; this is not a coding-specific sizing rule. |
| [How we built our multi-agent research system](https://www.anthropic.com/research/multi-agent-research-system) | Engineering report 2025-06-13 | Internal research evaluation reports 90.2% improvement over a single Opus 4 agent. Multi-agent usage was about 15 times chat usage, not 15 times the single-agent baseline. Different models and larger compute make this insufficient evidence for equal-budget swarm gains. |
| [Darwin Godel Machine](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.22954v3) | Submitted 2025-05-29; v3 2026-03-12 | Maintains an archive of agent variants and empirically evaluates code changes. Reports SWE-bench improvement from 20.0% to 50.0%. This is benchmark-specific empirical selection, not a proof that arbitrary self-modification is beneficial. |
| [GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.19457v2) | Submitted 2025-07-25; v2 2026-02-14 | Uses trajectory reflection and a Pareto frontier to evolve prompts. Reports up to 35 times fewer rollouts than GRPO across its experiments. Prompt optimization is useful evidence for bounded adaptation, not evidence of autonomous weight improvement. |
| [Hyperagents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461v1) | Submitted 2026-03-19, v1 | Makes both task behavior and the meta-level modification procedure editable; reports cross-domain transfer of improvements to the improvement process. Research evidence does not establish safe production self-editing or indefinite acceleration. |

## Phantom starting point

- The [swarm planner](../../src/core/swarm/planner.ts) asks for independent
  build tasks with phased dependencies, at most six tasks per phase and eighteen
  overall. A prompt claiming independence is not evidence that edits are disjoint.
- The [swarm runner](../../src/core/swarm/runner.ts) already slices budgets using
  spent and reserved usage. Any experiment must count coordinator, workers,
  retries and verification within the same total, rather than add worker budgets.
- [Improvement discovery](../../src/core/improve/discover.ts) carries evidence,
  an evaluation plan and a metric into proposals. Extend that workflow instead
  of creating a second autonomous proposal channel.
- [Lesson trials](../../src/core/improve/lesson-trial.ts) already assign a
  deterministic holdout and count merged, unreverted work. Its minimum of three
  finished tasks per arm is a reporting threshold, not statistical power for
  the experiments proposed here.
- [Exact-commit measurement](../../src/core/improve/measure.ts) and
  [promotion](../../src/core/improve/promote.ts) are existing boundaries to
  preserve. A successful model evaluation alone must never authorize a merge.

## Experiment protocol shared by every idea

These are proposed experiments. No model calls, paid resources, new credentials,
or production changes are required by this research change. First implement
fixture-based runners; execute model trials only within separately authorized
capacity. Never print credentials or include private raw traces in reports.

Freeze task IDs, repository SHAs, model versions, tool versions, scoring commands,
timeouts and total token ceilings before comparing arms. Record candidate and
parent hashes, seed, task class, outcome, wall time, measured tokens, verifier
result and failure reason. Unknown usage stays unknown, not zero. Include failed
and timed-out attempts in denominators; record launch failures separately.

Use disjoint development, selection and final holdout tasks, split by issue family
to reduce near-duplicate leakage. Candidate agents cannot edit evaluators or read
final holdout solutions. Select on the selection split, then evaluate the chosen
candidate once on the frozen holdout. Rotate the holdout for subsequent rounds.
Run paired trials on the same tasks with randomized arm order and three seeds.
Bootstrap paired differences by task, not by individual seed, with a fixed
bootstrap seed and 10,000 resamples. Report 95% intervals and all strata, including
negative results. The sample sizes below are bounded pilots, not power claims;
an interval spanning zero means inconclusive and does not justify rollout.

Primary quality is the fraction of tasks passing independent functional checks.
Report tokens per verified success, total tokens including failed attempts,
p50/p95 elapsed time and conflict or verifier-disagreement rate. A zero-success
arm has undefined cost per success. Missing usage prevents cost-based acceptance.
Keep the incumbent whenever evidence is incomplete. Later online validation must
also track merged-and-unreverted outcomes over a fixed seven-day observation window.

IMPACT-SCORE is an ordinal priority from 1 to 10, not a measured effect size:
score = expected value (1-5) + evidence fit (1-3) + ease of bounded testing (1-2).
The numeric targets below are hypotheses chosen for engineering usefulness.

## Idea 1: Match swarm topology to task dependencies

**IMPACT-SCORE: 9/10** (value 4 + fit 3 + testing 2).

**Evidence:** Scaling Agent Systems and Anthropic's 2025 report above support
selective parallelism. **Expected impact:** at least 20% lower median latency
on independent tasks without lower success, while avoiding wasted fan-out on
sequential work. This is an inference to test, not a published Phantom result.

**Experiment design:** collect 60 historical, reproducible tasks, twenty each
independent, shared-file and sequential. Compare one agent, two workers plus
coordinator, and four workers plus coordinator at identical total token and
wall-time ceilings. Give each arm the same tools and model. Freeze dependency
labels before execution. Use isolated worker worktrees and a single integration
writer. Count integration failures as failures. Compare against an equal-budget
single agent with retries so additional search is not mistaken for coordination.

**Acceptance:** independent-task median latency improves at least 20%, its paired
95% interval excludes zero, and quality difference has a nonnegative lower
confidence bound. Require no quality loss in other strata before general use;
otherwise restrict any later rollout to the validated class. Abort on budget
violation. **Landing:** a source-only benchmark adjacent to the existing planner;
no dispatch or permission changes. Start with offline fixtures in READY item 1.

## Idea 2: Evolve lessons from failure traces with a held-out comparison

**IMPACT-SCORE: 8/10** (value 4 + fit 2 + testing 2).

**Evidence:** GEPA above motivates reflection over trajectories rather than
scalar scores alone. **Expected impact:** five percentage points more verified
success at equal inference budget through concise, task-specific lessons.

**Experiment design:** develop candidate lessons on 30 sanitized failure traces;
select on 30 separate tasks; freeze one lesson set and compare it with no lessons
on 60 final tasks. Ablate reflection by comparing a same-length generic checklist
on the selection split. Account for lesson generation and serving tokens, and
report optimization cost separately from inference cost. Treat retrieved lessons
as untrusted task data. Adapt the existing lesson-trial assignment for later
online validation, without changing current eligibility or promotion decisions.

**Acceptance:** final quality gain at least five points with a positive lower
confidence bound, total inference tokens no greater than baseline, and no new
verifier failures. Otherwise retain existing lessons. **Landing:** a fixture-based
trial report and candidate lesson artifacts; no automatic knowledge activation.

## Idea 3: Preserve diverse candidate lineages instead of only the latest winner

**IMPACT-SCORE: 7/10** (value 4 + fit 2 + testing 1).

**Evidence:** DGM above supplies the archive mechanism. **Expected impact:** ten
percent more verified improvements per fixed search budget by retaining useful
alternatives that a greedy chain would discard.

**Experiment design:** compare a greedy incumbent-only chain with an archive of
at most eight candidates across ten historical failure families. Cap each search
at twenty proposals and identical total tokens. Keep parent hashes and behavioral
coverage signatures; select diverse candidates on development/selection tasks
only. Freeze winners before testing on sixty held-out tasks. Repeat with three
seeds. Ablate diversity using an equally sized random-parent archive.

**Acceptance:** at least 10% relative gain in accepted improvements per budget,
positive paired interval across failure families, no final-holdout regression,
and reproducible lineage records. If baseline finds zero improvements, report
absolute counts instead of a relative percentage. **Landing:** offline archive
simulation consuming redacted proposal evidence. Do not change live proposal
selection until the evaluation establishes value.

## Idea 4: Evaluate changes to the improvement strategy itself

**IMPACT-SCORE: 5/10** (value 3 + fit 1 + testing 1).

**Evidence:** Hyperagents above distinguishes an editable improvement procedure
from a fixed search loop. **Expected impact:** ten percent fewer proposal attempts
to obtain the next independently verified improvement on unseen task families.

**Experiment design:** freeze the task agent and compare a fixed proposal strategy
with an editable strategy artifact restricted to reflection templates and parent
selection parameters. Train on ten failure families and evaluate on ten disjoint
families, three seeds, twenty proposals maximum per family and equal total token
ceilings. Record improvement yield per generation, not just best final score.
Treat capped runs without success as censored; report success-at-cap alongside
attempts-to-success to avoid rewarding strategies that succeed rarely.

**Acceptance:** at least 10% reduction in attempts with a positive paired interval,
no lower success-at-cap, and transfer to the untouched families. Any attempted
evaluator, permission, protected-path or budget modification rejects the candidate.
**Landing:** offline simulation only. The experiment cannot modify its own scoring,
promotion or execution boundary. Defer live recursive modification even if this
pilot succeeds; that requires a separate design and authority review.

## Delivery and validation

implementation links and detects a broken implementation reference. Existing

## Ranked ideas — highest gain for merge speed or autonomy

1. Compact-and-retry on context overflow (S8, reinforced by S1's idle
   compaction): turns a whole class of dead runs into finished work —
   `src/core/run/agent-loop.ts` plus `src/core/run/context-window.ts`.
2. Prepared-attempt engine split (S6): core resolves policy once, engines
   only execute, so new backends cannot weaken authority —
   `src/core/run/engine-registry.ts`.
3. Parallel read-only tool batching (S2): fewer model round-trips per step
   shortens every dispatched job — `src/core/run/agent-loop.ts`.
4. Structured plugin load report (S3): silent skips are the top cause of
   "why didn't my skill run" debugging loops —
   `src/core/plugins/registry.ts`.
5. Scoped and self-fixing doctor (S2 --network-only, S6 doctor --fix, S3
   retired-key warnings): faster triage and less config debt before dispatch —
   `src/core/doctor.ts` plus `src/core/doctor-fix.ts`.
