# Provider usage probes — resets and spare usage the fleet can read itself

Checked 2026-10-31, the day the fleet was ordered to detect provider resets and spare usage
itself. For each provider: the documented or observable used-percent and reset-time signal,
where Phantom reads it, how fresh it is, and how it fails. Claims cite a public page or a
repo file; the unconfirmed is marked unverified. No credential or auth file was opened.

## Claude Code subscription

- Signal: rolling `five_hour` and weekly `seven_day` windows with `used_percentage` 0–100
  and `resets_at` Unix epoch seconds; per-model weekly scopes (Sonnet/Opus/Fable) may also
  appear. Wire shape: [status-line JSON](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline)
  `rate_limits.*`; the limits: [Claude support](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753).
- Read from: `claude -p /usage` (non-inference local command, version-pinned builds only)
  parsed by [claude-account-usage.ts](../../src/core/resources/claude-account-usage.ts);
  the fleet reads `~/.ashlr/routing/capacity.json` via
  [subscription-usage.ts](../../src/core/fleet/subscription-usage.ts).
- Freshness: seats carry `observedAt`; older than `HEADROOM_READING_MAX_AGE_MS` (15 min,
  [headroom.ts](../../src/core/routing/headroom.ts)) is stale = unknown. The `usage_report`
  frame is the fresh reply; legacy text may be header-seeded (`quotaFresh: false`).
- Fails: signed-out or unpinned CLI → no reading; missing or stale snapshot →
  `subscriptionAllows` fails closed. A rate-limited `/usage` endpoint yields last-known
  bars ~60 min ([costs doc](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs)); the upstream endpoint
  behind the bars is unverified — do not probe it.

## Anthropic API

- Signal: per-response headers `anthropic-ratelimit-{requests,tokens,input-tokens,
  output-tokens}-{limit,remaining,reset}`; reset is RFC 3339, `retry-after` rides on 429s
  ([rate limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits)). Org usage/cost
  history: `/v1/organizations/usage_report/messages` and `cost_report` under an Admin key
  or `org:admin` scope ([usage-cost API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api)).
- Read from: Phantom does not call these today. Its only Anthropic-API fact is the grant
  ledger — recorded billing observations (`remainingUsdMicros`/`totalUsdMicros`,
  `capturedAt`, `expiry`) in [claude-api-grant.ts](../../src/core/resources/claude-api-grant.ts)
  — plus a display-only `claude-api` seat with `windows: []` in
  [budget-store.ts](../../src/core/routing/budget-store.ts). No public API returns a
  prepaid balance — a live balance read is unverified.
- Freshness: headers are exact at response time; reports are hourly/daily delayed
  buckets; the ledger is as old as its last verified observation.
- Fails: a tier spend-cap 429 carries no `retry-after` and does not self-reset; headers
  are absent on non-2xx; grant rows are `automaticAdmission: 'held'` — evidence, never
  spend authority.

## Codex CLI

- Signal: a `rate_limits` snapshot per account — `primary`/`secondary` windows
  `{used_percent, window_minutes, resets_at}` (5h and weekly), `credits`, `plan_type`,
  `rate_limit_reached_type`, filled from `x-codex-*` response headers
  ([rate_limits.rs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-api/src/rate_limits.rs)).
- Read from (local, auth never opened): `~/.codex*/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`
  `event_msg`/`token_count` rows — [codex-session-usage.ts](../../src/core/fleet/codex-session-usage.ts)
  covers both homes, [codex-source.ts](../../src/core/observability/codex-source.ts) the
  default. Live: `codex app-server --stdio` JSON-RPC `account/rateLimits/read` →
  `rateLimits`/`rateLimitsByLimitId` ([schema](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/v2/GetAccountRateLimitsResponse.ts)),
  probed by [readers/codex-usage.ts](../../src/core/fabric/readers/codex-usage.ts).
- Freshness: session rows are per-turn while runs are active; older than
  `CODEX_USAGE_STALE_MS` (24 h) is stale. The app-server read is live but needs ChatGPT
  auth inside an 8 s deadline.
- Fails: no session files → `unavailable`, never 0%; the app-server call requires chatgpt
  auth; malformed windows → null. Weekly `resets_at` can re-anchor to "now + 7d" rather
  than a fixed expiry ([issue #36313](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36313),
  community-observed) — treat a reset instant as a provider claim.

## Devin

- Signal: org ACU consumption, not a native percent — `GET /v3/organizations/{org}/consumption/daily` returns `total_acus` and
  `consumption_by_date[].{date,acus,acus_by_product.devin}`; needs `ViewOrgConsumption`;
  day boundary is midnight PST = 08:00 UTC
  ([consumption-daily](https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/consumption/organizations-consumption-daily));
  cycle edges: `enterprise/consumption/cycles` ([cycles](https://docs.devin.ai/api-reference/v3/consumption/consumption-cycles)).
- Read from: [devin-usage-worker.ts](../../src/core/fabric/readers/devin-usage-worker.ts)
  in `phantom exec` custody; it also reads `enterprise/consumption/acu-limits/devin` —
  used in-repo but absent from the published docs index (unverified). It emits `{acuUsed,
  acuLimit, pctUsed, resetAt: cycle.before}` as `devin-api-v3-org-cycle`, cached by
  [devin-usage.ts](../../src/core/fabric/readers/devin-usage.ts) and
  [consumption.ts](../../src/core/devin/consumption.ts).
- Freshness: 5-min TTL, 30 s on failure; consumption is daily-grained, so intra-day
  movement is approximate. `resetAt` is the enterprise cycle end.
- Fails: 401/403/429 → `unauthorized`/`forbidden`/`rate-limited` (honours `retry-after`);
  missing key or org → `missing-*`; schema drift → `malformed-body` = unknown, never zero.

## Local oMLX

- Signal: no subscription quota exists — spare usage is resident memory and model
  occupancy, and nothing resets. `GET /admin/api/models` lists `loaded`/`is_loading`/
  `virtual`, `estimated_size`, `model_context_length`, `quantization`, `model_type`;
  `/v1/tokenize` and `/v1/completions` return `usage`. oMLX is internal with no public doc
  — the wire shape is observable only through this repo (unverified externally).
- Read from: [model-inventory.ts](../../src/core/resources/model-inventory.ts)
  (loopback-verified fetch to 127.0.0.1:8000); the OpenAI-compatible default base URL is
  in [local-inference.ts](../../src/core/run/local-inference.ts); ceilings are planned
  offline by [omlx/config.ts](../../src/core/local-runtime/omlx/config.ts). The
  `local-omlx` `capacity` bucket is declared capacity-only in
  [pool-budget.ts](../../src/core/fleet/pool-budget.ts).
- Freshness: live HTTP during measurement; an inventory older than `RESOURCE_MAX_AGE_MS`
  (35 min, [resource-view.ts](../../src/core/fabric/resource-view.ts)) is unknown.
- Fails: refused or timed-out loopback → `unavailableEngines`; a busy engine (models
  resident) refuses measurement rather than evicting work.

## Smallest fleet changes

The three smallest `src/core/fleet` changes that would use these signals:

1. `subscription-usage.ts`: answer `subscriptionUsage('claude')` from the
   `readCapacitySnapshot()` seats already imported for `_budgetVerdict` — a ~20-line map
   of `SeatCapacity.windows` to `{usedPercent, windowLabel, resetsAt}` so displays stop
   reporting Claude as permanently unknown. No new I/O or trust boundary.
2. `codex-session-usage.ts`: export a reader adapter mapping the collected
   `CodexAccountResource` windows into `UsageReading`-shaped rows for `codex-personal`,
   `terra`, and a session-file fallback for `codex-cmp`. `fleet.readings` belongs to
   [usage-signal-writer.ts](../../src/core/fabric/usage-signal-writer.ts), so the adapter
   feeds its `readers` seam (`() => Promise<unknown>`), not the file — no subprocess, and
   covers the seat the app-server probe misses.
3. `pool-budget.ts` / `pool-budget-store.ts`: one producer turning the newest
   model-inventory or machine reading into `addBudgetReadings({pool:'local-omlx',
   bucket:'capacity', remaining})` — `parseBudgetOutput` already accepts `capacity
   remaining: <n>` lines, so the local pool stops reporting permanently unknown with no
   parser work.

# Speculative execution, bounded parallelism and agent memory

Research date: 2026-10-26. Repository inspected: `a6f3c323`.
Status: research and offline evaluation tooling, with READY implementation experiments below.
No runtime behavior, provider calls, credentials, paid resources or token allowances change.

## Decision

Prioritize provenance-aware memory selection, then selective read speculation, then
parallel task selection. Phantom already implements bounded best-of-N and offline
memory recall. The opportunity is to spend the existing allowance better, not
multiply workers or add another memory service. Run each experiment independently
before a combined treatment, so a memory improvement cannot conceal a parallelism
regression. The scores below are engineering estimates, not measured outcomes.

This change includes an offline paired-results evaluator and adversarial tests.
The evaluator does not run agents, authenticate observations, grant execution
permission or promote a proposal. No performance benefit has been measured here.

## Verified primary sources

Dates below are submission and revision dates from the linked primary records,
checked on the research date. Claims are the authors' reported results, not
independent replications. Versioned links pin the evidence used in this brief.

| Source | Date and version | Finding and transfer limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04371v2) | Submitted 2025-10-05; v2 2026-04-23 | Predicts future actions and commits matching predictions. Reports up to 55% prediction accuracy and up to 20% latency reduction across evaluated settings. Its operating-system extension is lossy. The title is not proof that arbitrary shell commands can be speculated safely. |
| [TomasuLLM: Out-of-Order Speculative Execution for LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38201v2) | Submitted 2026-09-22; v2 2026-10-01 | Uses isolated copy-on-write execution, dependency/effect tracing and ordered validation. Reports 1.31x on 100 SWE-bench Verified tasks, 1.35x on 28 Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks, and no false accepts in 4,010 audited validation records. These samples do not establish safety for Phantom's host tools. |
| [Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.08296v3) | Submitted 2025-12-09; v3 2026-04-08 | Tests 260 configurations across six benchmarks. Reports gains on decomposable reasoning and losses on sequential planning, with overhead on tool-heavy tasks. Architecture must match task structure; its predictive model is not a ready-made Phantom routing policy. |
| [Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19413v1) | Submitted 2025-04-28; v1 | Extracts, consolidates and retrieves salient conversational information. Reports 91% lower p95 latency and over 90% token savings against full-context processing on LOCOMO. That baseline is much larger than Phantom's existing bounded recall; do not forecast those savings here. |
| [A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12110v11) | Submitted 2025-02-17; v11 2025-10-08 | Organizes structured notes with links and updates their contextual representations. Motivates testing relational recall, but does not establish that generated memory links are reliable evidence or appropriate authority. |

## Existing implementation and constraints

| Surface inspected | Existing behavior | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Best-of-N policy](../../src/core/run/best-of-n-policy.ts) and [execution](../../src/core/run/best-of-n.ts) | Hard limits of eight candidates and two concurrent workers; per-candidate budget splitting; real-judge availability is distinguished from fallback. | Compare against the current bounded implementation. Increasing fan-out is not a new contribution. These are protected Tier-1 paths and are not edited by this work. |
| [Genome recall](../../src/core/genome/recall.ts) | Eligibility filtering, keyword ranking, memory-tier weighting, configurable result count, and explicitly opt-in embedding reranking. | Keep the default offline path and compare within the same context allowance. |
| [Genome consolidation](../../src/core/genome/consolidate.ts) and [store](../../src/core/genome/store.ts) | Consolidation preserves provenance metadata such as source timing and merge count. | Build on existing records rather than replace the store or silently rewrite evidence. |
| [Firm memory](../../src/core/universe/firm-memory.ts) | Immutable daily/master records, source digests and expected-prior checks. | Reuse the provenance design where applicable; do not conflate firm memory with genome recall or claim they are already integrated. |
| [Genome playbooks](../../src/core/genome/playbook.ts) | Synthesis from recalled entries with bounded prompt text. | Count synthesis and maintenance work in any future memory experiment. |

All proposals retain one writer per task/branch, existing sandboxing, enrollment,
Stop/Pause and independent verification. Memory is untrusted task data, never
permission. A synthetic fixture must not enter a production memory store.

## Scoring and shared experiment protocol

`IMPACT-SCORE` is an ordinal 1-10 prioritization tag: expected recurring benefit
(0-4), direct applicability to inspected code (0-3), and feasibility of a bounded
offline pilot (0-3). It is not a probability, ROI estimate or paper metric.

For each idea, freeze 100 task instances, grouped by repository/task family and
split before tuning: 40 development, 60 held-out. Repeat with three paired seeds
for model-backed trials only after separate authorization; do not manufacture
independent samples by treating repeated seeds as new tasks. Use the same source
revision, inputs, model/version, tools, deadline and total token ceiling per pair.
Randomize arm order, record cache warmth and machine load, and include all attempts,
failed branches, cancellation time, judging, retrieval and memory maintenance.
A timeout is a failed task at the full elapsed deadline, not a removed row.
Unknown token accounting makes the comparison incomplete, never zero cost.

Initial work is deterministic fixture replay with no model calls. Any later trial
must fit an already authorized resource allowance; this task authorizes no new
spend or tokens. Freeze task IDs, seeds, cohort labels, code/input digests and raw
observations in a private experiment manifest. Avoid transcripts or secrets in
public reports. Maintain the full task inventory so missing pairs are visible.

Report task success, paired lost/gained successes, p50 and p95 end-to-end latency,
total elapsed time, all tokens per success, CPU time, cancellation waste, and
unsafe/stale accepts. Bootstrap paired differences by task cluster with 10,000
resamples and 95% intervals. Inspect each cohort, especially sequential tasks.
A pilot needs zero unsafe/stale accepts, no observed success-rate decline, at
least 10% p95 improvement, no total elapsed-time increase and no token increase.
Before runtime adoption, require a positive held-out latency improvement interval
and a success-rate lower confidence bound above a preregistered -2 percentage
point noninferiority margin. Expand the sample if inconclusive; 100 tasks is a
screen, not a power claim. Existing policy and review remain necessary.

## Idea S: reuse speculative read results only after exact validation

**IMPACT-SCORE: 8/10** (benefit 3, applicability 2, pilot feasibility 3).
Evidence: Speculative Actions and TomasuLLM above. Adopt the narrow mechanism of
prediction plus validation, not their headline speedup as a forecast.

**Expected impact:** target 10-20% lower p95 on runs dominated by repeated repository
reads, with unchanged model token totals. Reject the idea if hashing, invalidation
and contention consume the saved latency. In a simple model, expected latency
saved is `p*S - (1-p)*R - V`, where `p` is acceptance probability, `S` is overlap
saved, `R` is rejection/replay penalty and `V` is validation overhead. Estimate all
four from traces; this is a heuristic, not a concurrency correctness proof.

**Experiment design:** compare serial reads against one deterministic predicted
read on the same immutable snapshot. Use fixture-derived transitions, not an extra
predictor model. Key reuse by tool/version, normalized arguments, repository and
worktree identity, base revision, dirty-content digest and relevant configuration.
When input completeness cannot be proven, miss the cache. Validate before exposing
the observation and re-read on mismatch. Repository HEAD alone is insufficient.
Fixtures include dirty edits, rename/delete, symlink escape, configuration changes,
identical arguments in another worktree, cancellation, and prediction misses.
Use 50 repeat-read, 25 changed-input and 25 no-predictability tasks.

**Boundary and decision:** whitelist only snapshot file reads and searches. Shell
commands, tests, package managers, network calls and writes are excluded: a test
can mutate state despite being described as verification. No speculative write
can escape, and no result from a rejected branch enters durable memory. Measure
acceptance, wasted reads and digest overhead alongside the shared gates. Retain
serial execution as the fallback. The first READY task is an offline simulator;
any integration touching Tier-1 code requires a separately authorized owner lane.

## Idea P: allocate bounded parallelism by dependency structure

**IMPACT-SCORE: 7/10** (benefit 3, applicability 2, pilot feasibility 2).
Evidence: Scaling Agent Systems above. Independent subtasks and multiple competing
solutions are different experiments; neither justifies concurrent branch writers.

**Expected impact:** target 10-15% lower p95 for decomposable tasks at equal total
tokens, with no benefit assumed for sequential edits. Amdahl's bound limits the
upside: at parallel fraction `f=0.5` and two workers, ideal speedup is only
`1 / ((1-f) + f/2) = 1.33`, before orchestration and verification.

**Experiment design:** 40 independent inspection tasks, 30 dependency-chain tasks
and 30 competing-solution tasks. Compare (A) single execution, (B) current bounded
best-of-N, (C) offline selection of single versus two-way execution using declared
read/write sets and observed critical path. Preserve the current candidate cap,
concurrency cap and total budget. Include controller and independent judge tokens;
an unavailable judge cannot count as accepted success. Treat task-graph metadata
as untrusted: missing dependencies, conflicting paths or unknown effects force
serial execution. No test in this change launches workers.

**Boundary and decision:** inspect in parallel, serialize final edits and proposal
assembly. For separate candidates use isolated worktrees and choose one verified
diff; never concatenate conflicting diffs. Measure makespan, merge conflict rate,
judge disagreement and cancellation waste. Reject policies that help independent
tasks but regress the sequential cohort. Keep recommendations offline until an
owner-lane change can preserve current admission and cancellation gates.

## Idea M: retrieve compact memory with evidence and temporal validity

**IMPACT-SCORE: 9/10** (benefit 4, applicability 2, pilot feasibility 3).
Evidence: Mem0 and A-MEM above. Combine compact retrieval with explicit source links;
do not introduce a graph service or automatic trust in model-generated relations.

**Expected impact:** target 15-25% less recalled context at equal or better task
success, and at least 10% lower p95 end-to-end time. The existing keyword recall is
the primary baseline; full transcript replay is only a diagnostic upper-cost arm.
Any offline indexing, synthesis or consolidation costs belong in the treatment.

**Experiment design:** compare existing recall against a bounded selector over a
fixture memory corpus. Each candidate note has source record ID/digest, repository,
observed revision, validity interval, evidence kind and explicit supersession links.
Retrieve only eligible notes at the query's time; add at most one directly cited
neighbor inside the same fixed token allowance. Missing provenance means abstain.
Leave original entries immutable and represent corrections as new records. Apply
the same source validation to summaries and linked neighbors, not just first hits.
Use 40 recurring-fix tasks, 30 changed-fact tasks and 30 adversarial tasks covering
cross-repository collisions, injected instructions, contradictory summaries,
unsupported links, revoked sources and facts dated after the query.

**Boundary and decision:** split by task family and time before memory construction;
held-out outcomes must never become training memories. A speculative observation is
ephemeral until its branch and source state are accepted. Measure evidence precision,
correct abstention, stale retrieval/acceptance, source coverage and context size in
addition to shared gates. If links do not improve held-out performance over compact
flat recall, retain flat recall. No provider-backed embedding or synthesis is
required for the fixture pilot; no credentials or storage migrations are added.

## Reproducible accounting delivered here

Run the [offline evaluator](../../scripts/research/paired-results.mjs) on JSON:

```sh
node scripts/research/paired-results.mjs /path/to/paired-results.json
```

Input schema, shown with one explicitly synthetic pair:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "evidence": "synthetic",
  "pairs": [{
    "id": "fixture-read-001",
    "baseline": {"elapsedMs": 100, "tokens": 10, "success": true, "unsafeAccepts": 0, "staleAccepts": 0},
    "candidate": {"elapsedMs": 80, "tokens": 9, "success": true, "unsafeAccepts": 0, "staleAccepts": 0}
  }]
}
```

Each arm records the whole attempt, including rejected work and verification.
`elapsedMs` is positive; counters are nonnegative safe integers. `success` must be
a boolean. Pair IDs must be unique task/seed identifiers. Missing arms, unknown
counters, duplicate IDs and overflowing totals are rejected. A zero-success arm
has null tokens-per-success. The tool reports nearest-rank p95, aggregate ratios
and paired success transitions, retaining failed attempts in all denominators.

Exit 0 means `pilot-screen-pass`; 1 means `hold`; 2 means invalid input or invocation.
Synthetic evidence always holds. Even measured evidence with 100 pairs passing the
numeric screen is only a candidate for deeper review. The tool cannot authenticate
labels, detect omitted tasks, enforce cohort balance, calculate confidence intervals
or certify independence. Those remain manifest/review obligations in the protocol.
The [tests](../../test/research-paired-results.test.ts) exercise failed-attempt cost,
unsafe acceptance, tail versus total latency, unknown counters and misleading data.


# Resource pacing core

[Source](../src/core/resources/pacing.ts) implements a pure advisory planner for
one pool's current reset window. It performs no file, network, provider,
dispatch or merge operations. It is not wired into worker drain or the fleet
router. Eligibility, reading freshness, shared-pool accounting, metered opt-in,
Stop and all existing authority checks remain the caller's responsibility.

This is the independent pacing slice of
[PR #938](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom/pull/938). It does not require that
PR's #933 base, CLI changes, account defaults, learning pipeline or HiGHS
dependency. The optional LP adapter is supplied explicitly by the caller.

## Planning a window

`paceWindow({ poolId, used, windowStartMs, nowMs, resetAtMs, knobs, stamp? })`
returns periods, fractional spends, a first-period allowance, and a derived
pace series. Times are explicit safe-integer epoch milliseconds; usage is a
finite fraction from 0 to 1. Invalid inputs throw `RangeError`. At or after
reset, the allowance is zero: the caller must supply a new window and usage
reading before planning another cycle.

The even plan follows the reset window's pace line. A pool ahead of that line
waits. Remaining quota is placed into later periods subject to cumulative
ceilings, targeting full utilization at reset. Unused allowance remains in the
next plan's remainder. The caller must include all consumers' usage and
outstanding reservations in its budget and must not independently spend several
plans for the same shared pool.

`HorizonKnobs` supplies:

- `periodMs` and `maxPeriods`: tick length and horizon size (1 to 256 periods).
  Long horizons coarsen the periods to stay bounded.
- `bufferFraction`, `reserveFraction`, `bufferWindowMs`: safety and optional
  consumer reserve fractions, each held until the final buffer window and then
  released linearly. Their sum must be at most 1.
- `flex`: pace slack, from 1 to 100, relative to the original tick.
- `deviationWeight`, `flexPenalty`, `landingWeight`: nonnegative LP penalties
  for deviation from the even plan, spending above the natural flex amount,
  and unspent quota at reset.

Only the first period may inform the next tick. Its allowance also respects
the hold in force **now**. Future spends assume future hold release and are
projections, not immediately available quota. Multiple consumer plans (such as
an orchestration plan and a cloud plan with a reserve) must share a single total
budget at admission.

## Optional LP

`planHorizon` takes the same input plus optional `values`, `solver` and
`solverBudgetMs` (default 100; valid range 1 to 60,000). Varying per-period
values produce a maximization LP with cumulative quota constraints, absolute
deviation and flex penalties, and a terminal landing constraint. Missing
trailing values repeat the last supplied value. Flat values or an absent
adapter use the even plan without invoking a solver.

The `PaceSolver` callback receives the LP string and its budget. It returns a
status and a map of primal variables, with every `s0` through `sN` present for
an optimal solution. Returned spends must be finite, nonnegative, within every
cumulative ceiling and within 1e-8 of full utilization. Tiny numerical
overshoots are removed before returning a plan. Malformed, infeasible, failed,
timed-out or materially incomplete solutions fall back to the even plan.

An asynchronous deadline bounds waiting for an adapter. A blocking synchronous
solver must enforce its own budget or run in a worker; JavaScript cannot
preempt it. The adapter owns cancellation and cleanup of its underlying solve.
The core installs no solver dependency and claims no HiGHS runtime acceptance.

## Reading provenance

Every series has `projection: 'derived'` and `isReading: false`. An optional
`stamp` carries `source` (manual or config), `atMs`, exact `ageMs`, `stale`, and
`uncertainty`. Actual points retain their reading timestamp; projected current
and future points are not readings. Without a stamp the actual value and source
are unknown, uncertainty is 1, and the series is marked stale.

Staleness is preserved, not refreshed by planning. A stale series can still be
used for an advisory simulation; it does not establish dispatch eligibility.
The caller must apply its existing freshness and reset-provenance gates.

Run focused verification with an isolated home:

```sh
HOME=$(mktemp -d) npx vitest run test/resource-pacing.test.ts
```

# Coding pool cost feed (#933)

The #933 spend extension is a version 1 metadata contract in
`src/core/observability/coding-cost-feed.ts`. It complements the existing coding-pool routing event contract and dashboard. Producers supply one `spend` record per
**incremental** usage observation, with a stable `recordId`, logical `taskId`,
`attemptId`, `repo`, `pool`, `taskClass`, `engine`, `model`, UTC `timestamp`,
`tokensIn`, `tokensOut`, `costUsd`, and `costBasis`. Set unavailable counts and
cost to `null`; costBasis is `reported`, `estimated`, or `unknown` (null cost).
Never infer a model, task class, token count or subscription dollar charge.
Use `unknown` as an explicit dimension when attribution is unavailable.

Supply a `merged` record with `repo`, `prNumber`, UTC `timestamp`, and all
contributing `taskIds` when a trusted merge observation arrives. Both record
types require `schemaVersion: 1` and `kind`. Include failed/retried attempts,
review and repair usage in the task's spend. Do not send cumulative snapshots
as incremental spend. Task IDs are scoped to a repo and may belong to one PR;
split work into separate task IDs when it produces multiple PRs.

Run the offline adapter against a complete JSONL snapshot:

```sh
npx tsx src/cli/coding-cost-feed.ts /path/to/spend-events.jsonl > /tmp/coding-cost-feed.json
```

Output includes `byTaskClass` (repo/pool/class/engine/model), `byMergedPr`
(repo/PR plus dimension groups), and `posthogEvents`. Totals are known
subtotals, accompanied by missing-token, missing-cost and estimated-cost
counts. `missingTasks` identifies merged tasks with no spend records. Reward
consumers must inspect coverage before treating a subtotal as complete cost;
this feed does not grant routing or merge authority. No time filter runs before
the PR join, so historical attempts remain in the cost of a newly merged PR.

Identical replay records collapse. Conflicting record IDs or PR observations,
and a task attributed to multiple PRs, fail the entire feed. The JSONL adapter
prints only a fixed error on invalid input. Records reject extra fields.
Do not put prompts, responses, paths, user identities or credentials in metadata.

`coding_spend_recorded` events account for total spend;
`coding_merged_pr_spend` events attribute each spend observation to a PR at its
merge timestamp. Do not add these event families together. Stable top-level `uuid`
values deduplicate replay at capture; persist sent IDs in a durable uploader
outbox rather than relying on indefinite server deduplication. Late spend adds
new events without replacing cumulative snapshots. Corrections to previously
sent records require reconciliation, not a new record ID for the same spend.
See [PostHog's duplicate-event contract](https://posthog.com/docs/data-pipelines/troubleshooting#why-am-i-seeing-duplicate-events).

[posthog-coding-spend.json](posthog-coding-spend.json) is a dashboard recipe:
create each tile as a saved insight, then attach it to a dashboard. It contains
[PostHog SQL query nodes](https://posthog.com/docs/sql), with a 30-day display
window and explicit coverage columns. It is not an API dashboard-create payload.
Its [JSON Schema](posthog-coding-pools.schema.json) is validated in Vitest using
the existing MCP SDK validator; no new dependency is needed.

The adapter performs no network calls and reads no keys. A separately authorized
uploader must use **Phantom Secrets `phantom exec -- <uploader> ...`** for all
PostHog credentials and Locus for account access. Never resolve a raw key into
this process, a file, shell substitution, CLI argument, or report. No live
capture or dashboard provisioning is required to compute or test the feed.

# Router calibration

`phm router-calibration --jobs jobs.jsonl [--posthog runs.json] [--json]` reads local files and prints Markdown by default or JSON with `--json`. It makes no network requests. Each JSONL record has `event` (or `type`) and `job_id` (also `jobId` or `id`). Recognized events are `launch`, `finish`, `publish`, and `outcome`. There must be exactly one launch per job ID; its `arm` identifies the routing arm. A job ID identifies one attempt, including retries. Unrecognized events are ignored, but a nonempty ledger with no recognized events is rejected.

Use numeric `predicted_merge_rate` (probability from 0 to 1), `predicted_tokens`, and `predicted_wall_time_ms` for predictions. Actual usage is `tokens` or `total_tokens` and `wall_time_ms` or `duration_ms`. Camel-case equivalents are accepted. A finish and launch with ISO timestamp fields `timestamp`, `at`, or `time` supply wall time if it is otherwise absent. An outcome of `merged` is positive; `closed`, `rejected`, `failed`, or `not_merged` is negative. A boolean `merged` is also accepted. Publishing, unknown outcomes and missing outcomes are not evidence of a merge or failure.

The optional PostHog export is a JSON array or an object with a `results` array; each row is a run or has a `properties` object. Join by `job_id` or `jobId`, using the same numeric fields. Unmatched rows are counted. Conflicting values and duplicate launches are rejected rather than silently double-counted. PostHog export input must represent one run per job or contain consistent duplicate observations.

Each predicted / actual average uses only jobs with both values, with the paired count shown alongside it. Brier is the mean squared difference between each recorded merge probability and its binary resolved outcome for that same population. `resolved` counts all known outcomes, including jobs without predictions. Missing pairs produce null in JSON and `n/a` in Markdown. These are descriptive statistics of recorded evidence, not proof that the sample is representative. The files supplied by the operator determine schema compatibility and coverage.

# Codex 0.165 follow-ups

RQ-RADAR-CODEX-0165 fixed the unknown-model path: a `model_not_found` / `Unknown model` failure now drops the model into `probed_bad`, retries the job without `--model`, and reroutes a codex job to the next account pool when the default is rejected too. The pool is no longer marked dead, because an unknown model is not an auth failure — `auth-failed` classification now defers to model-rejection detection, since Codex 0.165 fails fast and preserves the provider message, which can carry login guidance.

This note records the follow-ups that were deliberately left out of that change.

## Cross-vendor effort changes

Codex 0.165 enables mid-conversation reasoning-effort changes by default for supported models and adds the Vertex provider. The router models effort only indirectly through tiers (`frontier`/`workhorse`/`cheap` map to configured model names); there is no effort axis in `state.json`, the ledger, or `router_invoke_cli` argv.

Design questions for a future change: whether effort belongs on the tier, on the model record, or on the job row; how `phantom route --json` should express an effort preference; whether a rerouted job keeps the original effort or the new pool's default; and how quota accounting should treat effort (higher effort burns allowance faster, so `accountHeadroom` and `budgetScores` may need an effort multiplier). Cross-vendor parity matters: Claude and Grok expose different effort knobs, so the config schema should normalize a small enum rather than pass vendor strings through.

## Memory export/import

Codex 0.165 enables memory v2 by default for fresh profiles and supports importing memories from other agents. Router jobs run `codex exec --ephemeral`, but account-level memory under `CODEX_HOME` is shared state across jobs and across pools (`~/.codex` work, `~/.codex-2` personal).

Open questions: whether jobs should see pool memory at all (a memory written by one job could steer or leak into another job's context, including imported memories containing instructions or secrets); whether `plant_auth`-style pool setup should seed or snapshot memory files; whether keepalive should rotate or scrub memory state like it does not-touch auth files; and how imported external-agent memories interact with the forbidden-flag and protected-path guardrails. Any import path needs an audit story — memory is instruction-shaped input, so it belongs in the same review surface as prompt construction.

## Thread forks

The app-server API in 0.165 supports experimental attached thread forks. Today a reroute or failover restarts the job from the prompt on the new pool; the failed attempt's context is discarded. A fork could carry the conversation to the next pool instead, preserving partial progress and reducing duplicated spend.

Open questions: fork lifecycle versus the router's attempt model (attempts are process-scoped; a forked thread is account-scoped state that would need a lease, heartbeat, and cleanup story); whether forks honor `--ephemeral` expectations; how to bound fork fan-out so failover does not multiply concurrent context; and where fork references would be recorded (ledger `pool`/`account` fields, `meta.json`, or `state.json`). This likely wants a spike on the app-server API surface before any router integration is sized.

# Router eval harness

`phm eval router --dataset jobs.jsonl [--policy NAME] [--decisions] [--json] [--write report.json] [--check baseline.json]` replays a router or prompt policy over a frozen set of past router lines with known outcomes and reports merge rate, cost per merged PR and wall time with confidence intervals. It reads local files only and makes no network requests. `--policy list` prints the builtin policies (`logged`, `strict-pool`, `cheapest`, `hold-all`); any other policy is supplied through the `RouterPolicy` seam in `src/core/eval/router-eval.ts`.

The dataset is router-eval.v1 JSONL. An optional first `{"v":1,"kind":"meta"}` line carries the arm catalog (`catalogCostUsd`, `tier`, `label`) — decision-time knowledge only. Each job line records the job id, the router-time fields (`repo`, `pool`, `tier`, `priority`, `task`), the recorded eligible `candidates`, the `chosen` arm (null only for `held`), the `outcome` (`merged`, `closed`, `failed`, `held`, `pending`), and measured `costUsd`, `tokens`, `wallTimeMs`. An `arms` object may freeze per-candidate counterfactual outcomes for benchmark lines; an entry for the arm that ran must agree with the recorded outcome. Duplicate ids, chosen arms outside `candidates`, non-terminal counterfactuals and contradictory records are rejected with a line number — never silently replayed.

A replayed decision matching the recorded arm observes the recorded outcome; a changed decision observes its frozen counterfactual when one exists and is otherwise *unobserved* — never estimated or credited. Held and pending lines stay out of the terminal cohort, and a decision outside the recorded candidates is rejected and counted. Merge rate carries a Wilson score interval; cost-per-merged-PR and wall-time means carry seeded percentile bootstrap intervals (the seed is pinned in the report so a baseline reproduces byte for byte). Intervals describe sampling noise over the frozen set, not counterfactual certainty.

`--check` exits 1 when the replay drifts from a baseline report, naming the metric that moved. `benchmarks/router-eval/` holds the committed frozen day, baseline report and regeneration commands; `test/router-eval-harness.test.ts` runs the gate in the daily master run.

# Changed-files verification (`scripts/verify-changed.mjs`)

Run the local pre-merge check from the repository root:

```
node scripts/verify-changed.mjs
```

Pass `--force` (or set `PHANTOM_VERIFY_FORCE`) to rerun a state that already passed.

## What it does

0. **Skips already-passed states** — before any check it fingerprints the working tree (see "Pass dedupe" below) and exits 0 with `SKIP verify-changed` when that exact state previously passed.
1. **Collects changed paths** — committed, staged, unstaged, and untracked files diffed against `origin/master`.
2. **Selects lintable files** — existing `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.cts`, `.mts`, `.tsx`, `.jsx` files still on disk.
3. **Runs ESLint** on the changed files (skipped silently if `node_modules/eslint` is absent — CI Merge Gate handles this).
4. **Takes one machine-wide typecheck slot** (default 3, `PHANTOM_TSC_SLOTS` overrides) before running `tsc --noEmit` with incremental build-info caching and a **shared atomic cache** (works through a unique temporary file to avoid readers seeing partial writes).
5. **Runs `tsc --noEmit` on `src/web-ui/tsconfig.json`** only when a path under `src/web-ui/` is changed.
6. **Runs two lane/integrity scripts**: `scripts/check-realio-lane-membership.mjs` and `scripts/check-verse-sync-io.mjs`.
7. **Records the pass** — on success the fingerprint is written as a marker so a later identical state skips the run.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PHANTOM_TSC_CACHE_DIR` | `<git-common-dir>/phantom-tsc-cache` | Directory that holds the shared incremental build-info cache across worktrees. |
| `PHANTOM_TSC_SLOTS` | `3` | Machine-wide cap on concurrent typechecks, shared across worktrees through the git common dir. |
| `PHANTOM_TSC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `900` (15 min) | Hard timeout (seconds) for `tsc --noEmit`; writes that exceed it are killed with `SIGKILL`. |
| `PHANTOM_VERIFY_PASSED_DIR` | `<git-common-dir>/phantom-verify-passed` | Directory holding one marker file per passed state, shared across worktrees. |
| `PHANTOM_VERIFY_FORCE` | unset | Truthy (`1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`) reruns verify instead of skipping an already-passed state; identical to `--force`. |

## Pass dedupe

The fingerprint combines the real git tree hash of the working state (a private copy of the index is updated with `git add -A` and hashed by `git write-tree`, so committed, staged, unstaged and untracked non-ignored content all count and the real index is untouched), the `origin/master` merge-base (changed-file selection depends on it), and the installed checker identities (eslint/typescript versions, tsgo presence, Node version, platform) whose drift can change a verdict on an identical tree.

Each pass stores `<sha256-of-inputs>.json` under the marker directory — shared across worktrees through the git common dir — and markers are pruned to the newest 256. A corrupt marker counts as a miss; `--force` and `PHANTOM_VERIFY_FORCE` bypass the skip (a forced pass still records). If fingerprinting fails (for example a repo without `origin/master`), verify runs normally and nothing is recorded.

## Where the shared cache lives

The shared cache file path is derived from a SHA-256 hash of the `package-lock.json` length + `package-lock.json` content + `tsconfig.json` content:

```
<PHANTOM_TSC_CACHE_DIR>/<sha256>.tsbuildinfo
```

If `PHANTOM_TSC_CACHE_DIR` is unset, the cache lives under the repository's git common directory (accessible via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), i.e. `.git/phantom-tsc-cache/<hash>.tsbuildinfo` in a normal single-repo checkout.

## Typecheck slots

A typecheck takes one slot by atomically creating `phantom-tsc-slots/slot-<n>` beside the shared cache root and writing its pid inside. Worktrees of the same repo share the slots through the git common dir, so at most `PHANTOM_TSC_SLOTS` typechecks run machine-wide at once. When every slot is held the check polls until one frees — bounded by `PHANTOM_TSC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` — and a slot whose recorded pid no longer exists is reclaimed. The slot is always released: success, failure, timeout, and signal exits all free it.
